name: SayCan
resolvedTitle: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
org: Robotics at Google; Everyday Robots
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: LLMs can break down long-horizon instructions but are not grounded in what a particular robot can do in its current scene, so their plans may be infeasible.
keyIdea: Score each skill in a fixed library by the product of the LLM's probability that the skill's text is a useful next step and a learned value function's probability that the skill succeeds from the current state; execute the argmax and repeat.
architecture: Frozen PaLM 540B scores skill descriptions; language-conditioned skills: BC-Z-style policies (FiLM-conditioned ResNet-18, USE sentence embeddings) and MT-Opt RL Q-functions (trained in sim with RetinaGAN sim-to-real) used as affordances; scripted navigation and place.
inputs: High-level user instruction; RGB image / robot state for value functions
outputs: Sequence of skill selections (natural-language plan) executed by low-level policies
actionRepr: Planner outputs discrete skills; low-level policies output end-effector 6-DoF pose, gripper open/close, base x-y and yaw delta, terminate
trainingData: 551 skills over 7 skill families and 17 objects proposed; BC on 68000 teleop demos (11 months, 10 robots) + 12000 success-filtered autonomous episodes (from 276000); RL value functions via MT-Opt in simulation

headlineResults.comparedTo: No LLM: BC NL 0%, BC USE 9%

parents: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners (Huang et al.)
whatChangedVsParent: Instead of letting an LLM generate or score plans alone, multiplies LLM skill likelihoods by learned value-function affordances so plans are feasible in the current scene.
limitations: Inherits LLM biases; the main bottleneck is the range and capability of the underlying skills; cannot easily react when a skill fails despite reporting a high value.
notes: Open-sourced a simulated tabletop version (Colab) only. Tested with 15 objects, 5 locations, Everyday Robots 7-DoF mobile manipulator. Chain-of-thought variant handles negation; multilingual queries (Chinese, French, Spanish) show almost no planning drop. Surveys often summarize it as 'LLM x value function'; that matches the paper.

keyEquations.meaning: Pick the skill that is both useful for the instruction (LLM) and likely to succeed now (affordance).
LLM scores the next skill given instruction and previously chosen skills.

algorithmSteps: Given instruction i and state s_0, start empty plan
For every skill, compute LLM probability of its description given i and plan so far
For every skill, compute value-function probability of success from current state
Multiply the two and pick the argmax skill
Execute the skill's policy; observe new state
Append the skill text to the prompt
Repeat until the 'done' skill is chosen
ablations: Removing affordances: plan success drops from 84% to 67% (No VF) or 74% (generative + USE projection).
Removing the LLM: BC with raw NL instruction 0%, with USE-projected instruction 9% execution.
LLM scale (generative, no VF): PaLM 540B 74%, 62B 72%, 8B 38%, FLAN 137B 43%.
hyperparams: Sparse 0/1 rewards rated by 2-of-3 humans; RL: 16 TPUv3 ~100 h, 3000+3000 CPU workers; BC: 16 TPUv3 ~27 h; eval episodes end at 50 actions.

name: Inner Monologue

org: Robotics at Google
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: LLM planners like SayCan produce open-loop plans that assume every step succeeds, so they cannot retry or replan after failures or scene changes.
keyIdea: Close the loop in language: continually inject textual feedback (success detection, passive scene/object descriptions, answers to the LLM's own questions from humans) into the LLM prompt so it can retry, replan and interact, with only few-shot prompting and no training.

outputs: Next skill in natural language (or a question to the human); 'done' to terminate
actionRepr: Discrete language skills executed by pretrained primitives (e.g. pick-and-place pixel/3D locations)
trainingData: No LLM training (few-shot prompts). Sim CLIPort primitive: 20000 demos. Kitchen: SayCan policies (68000 teleop demos + 12000 autonomous successes); success detector fine-tuned from CLIP on offline teleop + autonomous data.

headlineResults.benchmark: Real kitchen mobile manipulation, 120 evals (with and without disturbances)
Real tabletop (block stacking + fruit/bottle sorting, 10 runs)
Sim Ravens, unseen task 'put blocks in matching bowls' (50 episodes, noise)
Sim Ravens, unseen 'put blocks on mismatched bowls'

parents: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners (Huang et al.)
whatChangedVsParent: SayCan plans open-loop; Inner Monologue appends success, scene and human feedback to the LLM prompt after every step so the plan can be retried or revised.
limitations: Feedback modules introduce their own failure modes (noisy detectors, e.g. ViLD misses objects 28.0% of the time); object feedback in kitchen was human-provided; success is bounded by low-level skill quality.
notes: No defining equation in the paper; it is a prompting framework. Emergent behaviours shown: adapting to changed goals mid-task, self-proposing goals under infeasibility, multilingual instructions, answering scene questions. ViLD vs MDETR object feedback: precision 85.7% vs 39.6%, recall 72.0% vs 87.5%.
algorithmSteps: Put instruction and few-shot examples in the LLM prompt
Add passive scene description (visible objects / achieved sub-goals)
LLM generates next skill or, optionally, a question to the human
Execute skill with low-level policy (kitchen: grounded by SayCan affordances)
Run success detector and append result as text
Append new scene description / human answer
Repeat until LLM outputs done (or step limit k=15 in sim)
ablations: Kitchen with disturbances: SayCan 12.5/0.0/0.0% (manipulation/mobile/drawers) vs IM Object+Success 33.3/75.0/44.4%.
Real tabletop: Object-only 45%, Success-only 40%, Object+Success 90% total; the two feedback types are complementary.
Sim: Object+Scene beats Object+Success on most tasks (e.g. 'stack all blocks' 26% vs 10%) because it tracks achieved sub-goals.
hyperparams: Sim noise: N(0,3) pixels, N(0,2.5) heatmaps, N(0,0.02 m) place; max k=15 steps; real success thresholds 3 cm (stacking) / 10 cm (sorting); real policy noise sigma 1.5 cm / 0.7 cm.

name: Code as Policies

org: Robotics at Google
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: LLM planners only sequence a fixed set of pre-trained skills, so they cannot express feedback loops, spatial-geometric reasoning or precise parameters like 'a bit to the left' or 'faster' without new skill data.
keyIdea: Few-shot prompt a code-writing LLM to turn language commands into Python 'language model programs' that call perception APIs, use NumPy/Shapely for spatial reasoning, and parameterize control primitives; undefined functions are generated recursively (hierarchical code-gen).

inputs: Natural-language command (as code comment), perception API outputs (object names, positions, boxes)
outputs: Executable Python policy code that calls control APIs (pick/place, waypoints, velocities, say)
actionRepr: Calls to control primitives (e.g. put_first_on_second, goto_pos, set_velocity, waypoint trajectories); can also generate reactive PD/impedance controllers
params: Codex (size not public); GPT-3 6.7B and InstructGPT 175B compared
trainingData: None (few-shot prompting). CLIPort baseline trained on 30k demos.

headlineResults.benchmark: Sim tabletop, unseen attributes + unseen instructions, long-horizon
Sim tabletop, unseen attributes + unseen instructions, spatial-geometric

whatChangedVsParent: Rather than choosing among fixed skills in natural language, the LLM writes code that composes perception and control APIs, loops and arithmetic, and defines new functions on the fly.
limitations: Limited by what perception APIs can describe and which control primitives exist; struggles with commands much longer or at a different abstraction level than the examples; assumes instructions are feasible and cannot tell a priori whether code is correct.

algorithmSteps: Format instruction as a code comment appended to the few-shot prompt
LLM (temperature 0) generates Python code
Find functions called but not yet defined; recursively prompt a function-generation LMP to write them
Check code is safe (no import, no __, no exec/eval)
Run with exec using API globals; perception calls return object info
Control primitives move the robot; say() gives spoken feedback
Keep the session in the prompt so later commands can refer back ('undo that')

name: PaLM-E

org: Robotics at Google; TU Berlin; Google Research
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: LLM planners like SayCan only see text, which is insufficient when scene geometry matters, and off-the-shelf VLMs trained on VQA cannot solve robot reasoning tasks.

outputs: Text: answers, or plan steps / subgoal instructions for low-level policies
actionRepr: High-level language subgoals or skill names (not low-level actions); executed by RT-1 (mobile manipulation) or Lynch et al. Language-Table policies
trainingData: 'Full mixture' mostly web VLM data (WebLI 52.4%, VQ2A, CC3M, VQG, Object Aware, OK-VQA, VQAv2, COCO, Wikipedia); robot data 8.9% (mobile manipulator real 3.1%, Language-Table sim+real 4.2%, TAMP sim 1.6%). TAMP: 96,000 scenes (1% = 320 examples per planning task); mobile manipulation: 2912 SayCan sequences.
controlRateHz: Language-Table: PaLM-E subgoals at 1 Hz, low-level policy 5 Hz

headlineResults.benchmark: NLG tasks, relative drop vs base PaLM

name: VoxPoser

org: Stanford University; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: LLM-based robot systems still rely on pre-defined motion primitives, which are a bottleneck; LLMs cannot directly output high-frequency control.
keyIdea: Have an LLM write code that calls a VLM perception stack and NumPy to compose 3D voxel value maps (affordance, avoidance, rotation, velocity, gripper) in the robot's observation space, then use them as the cost for a model-based planner that synthesizes 6-DoF end-effector trajectories zero-shot in closed loop.
architecture: GPT-4 language model programs (planner, composer, per-map LMPs, following Code as Policies prompting) + perception: OWL-ViT detector -> Segment Anything masks -> XMem tracking -> point clouds from RGB-D; greedy-search motion planner in MPC loop with known robot dynamics (optionally heuristic or learned environment dynamics).
inputs: Free-form language instruction, multi-view RGB-D observations
outputs: Dense sequence of 6-DoF end-effector waypoints with velocity and gripper action
actionRepr: Dense end-effector waypoints (6-DoF pose, velocity, gripper) tracked by an operational space controller; replanned at 5 Hz
trainingData: None for the zero-shot system (5-20 prompt examples per LMP); optional MLP dynamics model learned from under 3 minutes of online interaction for contact-rich tasks

headlineResults.benchmark: Sim, unseen instructions + unseen attributes, object interaction
Sim door opening with learned dynamics

whatChangedVsParent: Code as Policies has the LLM parameterize fixed primitives; VoxPoser has the LLM compose dense 3D value maps that a motion planner optimizes, removing the need for primitives in most tasks.
limitations: Relies on external perception modules (holistic or fine-grained geometric reasoning is hard); contact-rich tasks need a general dynamics model; plans only end-effector (not whole-arm) trajectories; requires manual prompt engineering.
notes: Code released (simulation in RLBench); uses GPT-4 via API, no trained weights. Simulated block-world has 13 tasks with 2766 unique instructions, 20 episodes per task. Error breakdown: VoxPoser has lowest 'specification error'; real-world errors mostly from perception. Planar pushing uses a heuristic dynamics model with a pushing primitive.

keyEquations.meaning: Per sub-task trajectory optimization: complete the instruction with low control cost under dynamics constraints.
Task cost is the negative accumulated value-map score along the entity's path.

symbols.meaning: voxel value map in R^{w x h x d}
discretized position of entity of interest at step j
trajectory of the entity of interest

keyEquations.meaning: Value map produced by executing LLM-written code on the current observation.

algorithmSteps: Planner LMP splits instruction into sub-tasks
Composer LMP calls value-map LMPs with language parameters
LMPs call detect() (OWL-ViT -> SAM -> XMem) to get object/part point clouds
LMPs write NumPy code filling 100x100x100 affordance, avoidance, rotation, velocity and gripper maps

name: ReKep

org: Stanford University; Columbia University
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: Constraint-based manipulation needs constraints that are versatile across multi-stage, in-the-wild, bimanual and reactive tasks, free of manual labeling, and solvable in real time by off-the-shelf optimizers; rigid-pose constraints need object models and fail on deformables, while learned constraints need combinatorial data.
keyIdea: Represent each task as a sequence of Relational Keypoint Constraints: Python functions mapping 3D semantic keypoints to a cost (<=0 means satisfied), automatically written by GPT-4o from a keypoint-marked image, then solved hierarchically (sub-goal then path) for SE(3) end-effector poses in a closed loop.
architecture: Keypoint proposal: DINOv2 patch features + SAM masks, k-means (k=5) per mask, centroids lifted to 3D via calibrated RGB-D. ReKep generation: GPT-4o visual prompting outputs number of stages plus sub-goal and path constraint functions. Solver: SciPy Dual Annealing + SLSQP (first iteration ~1 s), then local-only re-solves at ~10 Hz; DINOv2 point tracker at 20 Hz; nvblox ESDF for collision; AnyGrasp for grasp selection.
inputs: Free-form language instruction; RGB-D observations (multiple calibrated cameras)
outputs: Sequence of 6-DoF end-effector poses in SE(3) (12-D for bimanual) executed by position control
actionRepr: dense SE(3) end-effector pose trajectory from spline-fit optimized waypoints (not a learned policy)
params: n/a (training-free; uses GPT-4o and DINOv2/SAM off the shelf)
trainingData: None task-specific (zero-shot); no demonstrations or environment models
controlRateHz: ~10 Hz solve loop; 20 Hz keypoint tracking and position control

headlineResults.benchmark: 7 real-world tasks (mobile single-arm + dual-arm), 10 trials each

headlineResults.metric: success on unseen poses / unseen objects

whatChangedVsParent: Unlike VoxPoser's 3D value maps, the VLM writes keypoint-relation constraint code that a numerical optimizer solves for full 6-DoF (up to 12-DoF bimanual) poses, with within- and across-stage replanning.

notes: Training-free system; no model weights of its own (depends on proprietary GPT-4o). Init stage i=1
If any path constraint of stage i is violated, backtrack i<-i-1

name: MOKA

resolvedTitle: RoboPoint: A Vision-Language Model for Spatial Affordance Prediction for Robotics
org: University of Washington; NVIDIA; Allen Institute for AI; Universidad Catolica San Pablo
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: VLMs can say what to act on but cannot precisely say where, especially for relational references and object-free regions ('place the cup next to the plate'); prior approaches rely on action primitives, external detectors, coarse boxes or iterative prompting.
keyIdea: Instruction-tune a VLM to point: output a set of normalized 2D image points satisfying a spatial language query, trained on an automatically generated synthetic dataset (including free-space affordances) co-mixed with real VQA and LVIS data.
architecture: LLaVA-style VLM: CLIP ViT-L/14 336px image encoder (frozen), 2-layer MLP projector, Vicuna-v1.5-13B language model; projector and LLM weights fine-tuned autoregressively.
inputs: RGB image + language instruction
outputs: List of 2D points (x, y) normalized to [0,1]; projected to 3D with depth for downstream use
actionRepr: 2D image keypoints as text tokens (target/placement/waypoint points), converted to 3D targets + motion planner
trainingData: Object reference 347K + free-space reference 320K (synthetic, ~660K image-relation pairs from 10K procedurally generated scenes, ACRONYM objects >8K instances / 262 categories) + VQA 665K + LVIS 100K
whatChangedVsParent: Adds point-output spatial-affordance instruction tuning with a synthetic free-space data pipeline to LLaVA-1.5, keeping VQA performance on par (e.g. GQA 63.28 vs 63.24).
limitations: Provides no confidence estimates for point predictions, and the number of output points is not controllable.
notes: Described as an open-source VLM. Training: 40 hours on 16 A100s, batch 16/GPU, LR 4e-5. Synthetic data rendered in CoppeliaSim-style procedural scenes with colored-box visual prompts during training only (not at test). Navigation (CoppeliaSim, YouBot): beats PIVOT and GPT-4V in 2 of 3 scenes. Also demonstrated for AR assistance. Surveys group it under VLM planning; it is more precisely a spatial-affordance/pointing VLM used as a mid-level interface.

keyEquations.meaning: Spatial affordance prediction: set of image-space target points satisfying the language relation.

symbols.meaning: normalized image coordinates of an action point

algorithmSteps: Procedurally generate scenes (layouts, ACRONYM objects, cameras)
Compute pairwise spatial relations from camera view
Sample 1-50 GT points on referenced objects (object reference)
For free space: remove target, re-render, sample points in target-mesh / support-surface intersection
Co-finetune projector + LLM on synthetic + VQA + LVIS mix
At test: predict 2D points from image + instruction, project to 3D, plan motion
ablations: Removing free-space reference data drops WHERE2PLACE from 46.77 to 13.21
Removing VQA data: 28.28; removing LVIS: 34.27; removing object reference: 42.23
Using only 10% of the data: 15.71
hyperparams: Frozen vision encoder and tokenizer; LR 4e-5; batch 16 per GPU on 16 A100s; 40 h; points normalized to [0,1]

name: CLIPort
resolvedTitle: CLIPort: What and Where Pathways for Robotic Manipulation
org: University of Washington; NVIDIA
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: End-to-end manipulation networks such as Transporter are spatially precise but learn from scratch with no semantics, so each new goal needs new demos or goal images; web-pretrained vision-language models have semantics but lack spatial precision for manipulation.
keyIdea: A two-stream language-conditioned imitation agent: a frozen CLIP semantic ('what', ventral) stream fused laterally with a Transporter spatial ('where', dorsal) stream, predicting dense pick and place affordances as SE(2) pick-and-place actions.
architecture: Three fully convolutional two-stream networks (f_pick, Phi_query, Phi_key). Semantic stream: frozen CLIP ResNet50 on RGB (to 7x7x2048) with upsampling decoder conditioned by tiled CLIP sentence embedding (1024-D) via Hadamard product at three layers, plus skip connections. Spatial stream: tabula-rasa Transporter ResNet on RGB-D; lateral 1x1-conv fusions into semantic stream.
inputs: Top-down orthographic RGB-D heightmap + English instruction
outputs: Pick pose T_pick and place pose T_place in SE(2) (pixel + discrete yaw)
actionRepr: two-step pick-and-place primitive: argmax over dense pixelwise affordance maps, place rotation from k=36 discrete angles
trainingData: Ravens/PyBullet: 10 language-conditioned tasks, 1/10/100/1000 demos per task; real Franka: one multi-task model for 9 tasks from 179 image-action pairs

headlineResults.benchmark: Ravens 10 language tasks, seen splits (avg, Fig. 3)
headlineResults.value: CLIPort (single) >90%; 86% on most tasks with 100 demos

headlineResults.metric: fraction of evaluations where multi beats single

headlineResults.benchmark: Real Franka, 9 tasks, one multi-task model
headlineResults.value: 55.0-75.0 per task (e.g. Stack Blocks 70.0, Pick Cherries 75.0, Fold Cloth 57.0)

whatChangedVsParent: Adds a frozen CLIP semantic stream and language conditioning to Transporter's FCNs, enabling one policy for many language-specified goals and tasks.
limitations: Restricted to SE(2) two-step pick-and-place primitives with open-loop execution (quasi-static tasks, sensitive to hand-eye calibration); struggles with multi-object relations and counting, relies on balanced datasets and on an expert to signal task completion.
notes: Benchmark, code and pre-trained models released (cliport.github.io). Sim: UR5e with suction gripper, 3 cameras 640x480. Trained 200K iterations single-task (600K multi-task), batch size 1, LR 1e-4, SE(2) augmentation. CONFLICT: surveys list CLIPort under 'high-level planning with LLMs and VLMs', but it is an end-to-end language-conditioned imitation policy with no LLM planner; it uses only CLIP's encoders.

keyEquations.meaning: Language-conditioned policy outputs a pick pose and a place pose.
Pick at the pixel with the highest pick affordance.

symbols.meaning: dense pixelwise pick action-values from f_pick

keyEquations.meaning: Place values by cross-correlating features of a crop around the pick with full-scene features.

symbols.meaning: c x c crop centered at pick

keyEquations.meaning: Cross-entropy imitation loss on softmaxed pick and place affordance maps.

symbols.meaning: one-hot pixel (and rotation) encoding of expert action

algorithmSteps: Build top-down RGB-D heightmap and encode instruction with CLIP
Run two-stream f_pick; take argmax pixel as T_pick
Crop c x c around T_pick, rotate k=36 times, run Phi_query
Run Phi_key on full input; cross-correlate to get Q_place
Take argmax (pixel, rotation) as T_place
Execute pick and place primitive; repeat until expert signals completion
ablations: One-stream Language Transporter (language fused into Transporter bottleneck) scores ~0 on stack-block-pyramid and packing tasks
Removing CLIP skip connections: stack-block-pyramid-seq-seen 1000 demos 3.3 vs 98.8
RN50-BERT semantic stream reaches 97.5 at 1000 demos but only 5.3/35.0 at 1/10 demos vs CLIPort 28.3/64.7
hyperparams: Crop c=64, rotations k=36 (place; k=1 pick in sim), feature dim d=3; language conditioning at 3 decoder layers; 200K iters single-task / 600K multi-task; batch 1; LR 1e-4

name: World Models (Ha & Schmidhuber)
resolvedTitle: World Models
org: Google Brain; NNAISENSE; IDSIA (USI & SUPSI)
problem: Model-free deep RL agents with large networks face hard credit assignment; the paper asks whether a compact, unsupervised generative model of the environment can supply features for a tiny controller and even serve as a training environment.
keyIdea: Split the agent into a VAE vision model (V), an MDN-RNN memory/predictive model (M) and a tiny linear controller (C) evolved with CMA-ES; C can be trained entirely inside the 'dream' generated by M and transferred to the real environment.
architecture: V: convolutional VAE compressing each frame to z (32-D CarRacing, 64-D Doom). M: LSTM (256 / 512 hidden) with a 5-component diagonal Gaussian mixture density output predicting next z (and done for Doom). C: single linear layer on [z_t, h_t].
inputs: Raw RGB frames; previous action
outputs: Continuous action vector (tanh-bounded)
actionRepr: single-step continuous action from a linear controller
params: CarRacing: VAE 4,348,547; MDN-RNN 422,368; controller 867. Doom: VAE 4,446,915; MDN-RNN 1,678,785; controller 1,088
trainingData: 10,000 random-policy rollouts per environment (CarRacing-v0, VizDoom Take Cover)

headlineResults.benchmark: VizDoom Take Cover, trained in dream (tau=1.15)

headlineResults.comparedTo: shows controller exploiting model at low temperature

parents: Schmidhuber's RNN-based world model / controller work (1990-2015)
whatChangedVsParent: Combines a VAE + MDN-RNN generative world model with an evolved tiny controller and shows policies learned purely inside the model transfer back to the real environment.
limitations: The controller can exploit imperfections of the approximate world model (adversarial 'cheating' policies); the standalone VAE may encode task-irrelevant details and miss task-relevant ones; the LSTM world model has limited capacity and suffers catastrophic forgetting; iterative data collection needed for harder environments.
notes: Separate training stages (V, then M, then C), each under an hour on one GPU for V/M. Temperature tau of M's sampling is a key knob: higher tau makes the dream harder and reduces exploitation. Interactive article at worldmodels.github.io. Not a robotics paper; foundational for later world-model agents (PlaNet, Dreamer).

keyEquations.meaning: MDN-RNN predicts a mixture-of-Gaussians distribution over the next latent.
Linear controller maps latent and memory state to action.

symbols.meaning: controller weights and bias (optimized by CMA-ES)

algorithmSteps: Collect 10,000 rollouts from a random policy
Train VAE (V) to encode frames into z
Train MDN-RNN (M) to model P(z_{t+1}|a_t,z_t,h_t) (plus done for Doom)
Define linear controller a_t = W_c[z_t h_t] + b_c
Evolve W_c, b_c with CMA-ES in real env or inside M's dream
Deploy learned policy in the actual environment
For harder tasks, iterate: collect with current C, retrain M and C
ablations: CarRacing controller with z only: 632 +/- 251; adding a hidden layer: 788 +/- 141; full z+h: 906 +/- 21
Low temperature (0.10, 0.50) yields high virtual but ~193-196 actual scores (model exploitation)
hyperparams: z dim 32 (CarRacing) / 64 (Doom); LSTM 256 / 512 units; 5 Gaussian mixtures; MDN-RNN 20 epochs; CMA-ES population 64, 16 rollouts per agent; Doom done threshold 50%

name: PlaNet
resolvedTitle: Learning Latent Dynamics for Planning from Pixels
org: Google Brain; University of Toronto; DeepMind; Google Research; University of Michigan
problem: Planning with learned dynamics from images was limited to simple tasks because models were not accurate enough over multiple steps, failed to capture multiple futures and were exploited by planners.
keyIdea: Deep Planning Network: learn a Recurrent State-Space Model (deterministic + stochastic latent paths) from pixels and plan purely in latent space with the cross-entropy method in an MPC loop, with no policy or value network.
architecture: RSSM with GRU (200 units) deterministic path and 30-D diagonal-Gaussian stochastic state; conv encoder/deconv decoder from Ha & Schmidhuber; reward model and other functions as 2x200 FC layers; CEM planner over action sequences.
inputs: 64x64x3 pixel observations; actions; rewards (for training)
outputs: Continuous action (first action of CEM plan), replanned every step
actionRepr: online CEM over horizon-12 action sequences, execute first action with action repeat R
trainingData: Self-collected online: 5 random seed episodes, then one episode per 100 update steps; about 1,000 episodes per DMC task

headlineResults.benchmark: DMC Cartpole Swing Up / Reacher Easy / Finger Spin

headlineResults.value: 40x to 500x+ per task; ~200x fewer episodes on average vs A3C/D4PG

whatChangedVsParent: Jointly learns an RSSM with both deterministic and stochastic paths and uses latent CEM planning, rather than a two-stage VAE+RNN with an evolved controller.
limitations: Online planning over a fixed short horizon (H=12) with rewards only inside the horizon; finger task remains below D4PG; latent overshooting did not help the final RSSM; action repeat must be tuned per domain.
notes: Code and videos at danijar.com/planet. Training 10-20 h per task on one V100. A single agent trained on all six tasks solves them, learning more slowly. Latent overshooting helps other models (e.g. DRNN) but slightly reduces RSSM performance, so the final agent does not use it; 3 free nats KL clipping used.

keyEquations.tex: h_t = f(h_{t-1}, s_{t-1}, a_{t-1}),\quad s_t\sim p(s_t\mid h_t),\quad o_t\sim p(o_t\mid h_t,s_t),\quad r_t\sim p(r_t\mid h_t,s_t)
keyEquations.meaning: Recurrent state-space model splits state into deterministic and stochastic parts.

keyEquations.tex: \ln p(o_{1:T}\mid a_{1:T}) \ge \sum_{t=1}^{T}\Big(\mathbb{E}_{q(s_t\mid o_{\le t},a_{<t})}[\ln p(o_t\mid s_t)] - \mathbb{E}_{q(s_{t-1}\mid o_{\le t-1},a_{<t-1})}\big[\mathrm{KL}[q(s_t\mid o_{\le t},a_{<t})\,\|\,p(s_t\mid s_{t-1},a_{t-1})]\big]\Big)
keyEquations.meaning: Variational bound: reconstruction minus KL between filtering posterior and one-step prior.

keyEquations.tex: \frac{1}{D}\sum_{d=1}^{D}\ln p_d(o_{1:T}) \ge \sum_{t=1}^{T}\Big(\mathbb{E}_{q(s_t\mid o_{\le t})}[\ln p(o_t\mid s_t)] - \frac{1}{D}\sum_{d=1}^{D}\beta_d\,\mathbb{E}_{p(s_{t-1}\mid s_{t-d})q(s_{t-d}\mid o_{\le t-d})}\big[\mathrm{KL}[q(s_t\mid o_{\le t})\,\|\,p(s_t\mid s_{t-1})]\big]\Big)
keyEquations.meaning: Latent overshooting: trains multi-step latent predictions of all distances up to D.

edges: first action + noise, repeated R times

algorithmSteps: Initialize dataset with S=5 random seed episodes
For C update steps: sample B sequence chunks of length L and update model on the variational bound
Reset environment; infer belief q(s_t|o<=t,a<t) by filtering
Plan with CEM: sample J=1000 action sequences over H=12, roll out in latent space, sum predicted rewards
Refit Gaussian to top K=100 for I=10 iterations; take first mean action
Add N(0,0.3) exploration noise, repeat action R times
Append episode to dataset and repeat
ablations: Purely stochastic SSM or purely deterministic GRU transition models perform worse than RSSM on all tasks; without the stochastic component the agent does not learn
Random data collection instead of planning-based collection hurts all tasks and fails on cartpole, finger and walker
Picking best of 1000 random sequences instead of iterative CEM lowers performance on all tasks
hyperparams: GRU 200 units; 30-D stochastic state; Adam LR 1e-3, eps 1e-4, grad clip 1000; B=50, L=50; 3 free nats; 5-bit images; CEM H=12, I=10, J=1000, K=100; S=5, C=100; action repeat cartpole 8, reacher 4, cheetah 4, finger 2, cup 4, walker 2

name: Dreamer
resolvedTitle: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination
org: University of Toronto; Google Brain; DeepMind
problem: Agents using learned world models either plan online or maximize rewards only within a fixed imagination horizon (shortsighted), and often use derivative-free optimization rather than the model's analytic gradients.
keyIdea: Learn an actor and a value model purely on trajectories imagined in the RSSM latent space, training the actor by backpropagating analytic gradients of lambda-return value estimates through the learned dynamics, so rewards beyond the horizon are accounted for.
architecture: World model = PlaNet RSSM with conv encoder / transposed-conv decoder and reward model (30-D stochastic latents); action model outputs tanh-transformed Gaussian; value model; other functions 3 dense layers of 300 ELU units.
inputs: 64x64x3 images, actions, rewards
outputs: Continuous (tanh-Gaussian) or discrete (categorical) actions from the action model
actionRepr: single-step action from a learned latent-space policy (action repeat R=2)
trainingData: Self-collected online; 5 random seed episodes then 1 episode per 100 training steps; evaluated at 5x10^6 environment steps on 20 DMC visual tasks

headlineResults.comparedTo: PlaNet 11 h; D4PG 24 h to similar performance

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces PlaNet's online CEM planning with an actor-critic learned in imagination via analytic value gradients through the RSSM, using lambda-returns to see beyond the horizon.
limitations: Depends on the representation-learning objective (reward-only prediction was insufficient; contrastive solved about half the tasks); the paper notes scaling latent imagination to higher visual complexity requires better representation learning.
notes: Source code at danijar.com/dreamer. Also applied to Atari and DeepMind Lab with discrete actions (straight-through gradients) and early termination (predicted discount). Dreamer outperforms alternatives on 16 of 20 tasks with 4 ties at horizon 20. Robotics relevance: ancestor of DreamerV2/V3 and DayDreamer.

keyEquations.meaning: Exponentially weighted mix of k-step value estimates balancing bias and variance.

symbols.meaning: k-step return bootstrapped with learned value v_psi

keyEquations.meaning: k-step imagined return plus bootstrapped value.
Actor maximizes imagined lambda-returns via backprop; critic regresses them.
Reparameterized tanh-Gaussian actions allow gradients through sampling.

nodes: RSSM world model (representation, transition, reward, decoder)
edges: RSSM world model (representation, transition, reward, decoder)
RSSM world model (representation, transition, reward, decoder)

algorithmSteps: Initialize dataset with S=5 random episodes
Sample B sequences; compute posterior states; update world model by representation learning
Imagine trajectories of horizon H from each posterior state using the action model
Predict rewards and values; compute V_lambda targets
Update action model by gradient ascent on sum of V_lambda (backprop through dynamics)
Update value model by regressing V_lambda (stop-gradient targets)
Interact with env using action model + exploration noise; add episode to dataset; repeat
ablations: Learning a value model makes performance robust to imagination horizon; 'no value' (V_R) and PlaNet degrade on long-horizon tasks (Fig. 4)
Pixel reconstruction beats contrastive estimation on most tasks; contrastive solves about half; reward-only prediction insufficient
Dreamer beats no-value and PlaNet on 16 of 20 tasks (4 ties) at horizon 20
hyperparams: H=15; gamma=0.99; lambda=0.95; B=50 sequences of length L=50; Adam LR 6e-4 (model), 8e-5 (actor), 8e-5 (value); grad norm clip 100; KL beta=1 with 3 free nats; action repeat R=2; S=5, 100 train steps per episode; Normal(0,0.3) exploration; discrete: H=10, beta=0.1

name: DreamerV3
resolvedTitle: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
org: Google DeepMind; University of Toronto
problem: RL algorithms need substantial per-domain hyperparameter tuning; robustly learning and exploiting world models across very different domains with one configuration was an open problem.
keyIdea: Learn an RSSM world model with discrete latents and train actor-critic purely in imagined latent rollouts, made robust across domains by normalization, balancing and transformation tricks (symlog, free bits, unimix, percentile return normalization, symexp twohot).
architecture: RSSM: CNN/MLP encoder to categorical latents z_t, block-diagonal GRU sequence model h_t, dynamics/reward/continue predictors and decoder; separate MLP actor and distributional critic. RMSNorm + SiLU, LaProp optimizer with adaptive gradient clipping.
inputs: Images and/or vector observations, reward, continuation flag
outputs: Actions sampled from actor (no lookahead planning at execution); world model predicts latents, rewards, continuation, reconstructions
actionRepr: Single-step discrete or continuous action from a stochastic actor (Reinforce estimator for both)
trainingData: Online RL, 150+ tasks across 8 domains (Atari 200M steps, ProcGen 50M, DMLab 100M, Minecraft 100M, Atari100k 400K, Proprio Control 500K, Visual Control 1M, BSuite); single A100 per agent

headlineResults.value: All Dreamer agents discover diamonds within 100M env steps
headlineResults.comparedTo: IMPALA, Rainbow, PPO: none discover a diamond

whatChangedVsParent: Adds robustness techniques (symlog, KL balance + free bits, 1% unimix, percentile return normalization, symexp twohot) plus block GRU, RMSNorm, AGC/LaProp so one fixed configuration works across all domains.
limitations: Uses a block-breaking simplification for Minecraft; DMLab evaluated only at 100M steps; each robustness technique helps only a subset of tasks. Actor acts without lookahead planning.

keyEquations.meaning: World model loss: prediction + dynamics + representation terms (weights 1, 1, 0.1).
KL balancing with free bits (clipped below 1 nat).

keyEquations.tex: R^\lambda_t \doteq r_t + \gamma c_t\big((1-\lambda)v_t + \lambda R^\lambda_{t+1}\big),\quad R^\lambda_T \doteq v_T
keyEquations.meaning: Bootstrapped lambda-return target for critic and actor.
Actor Reinforce loss with percentile return normalization and fixed entropy scale.

algorithmSteps: Act in environment by sampling a_t from actor on model state s_t=(h_t,z_t); store in replay (with latent states).
Sample batch 16 x 64 from replay (online queue + uniform).
Train world model: prediction (symlog/twohot), dynamics and representation KL with free bits.
From replayed posterior states, imagine H=15 steps with actor and dynamics predictor.
Compute lambda-returns from predicted rewards, continuation flags and critic values.
Train critic (twohot categorical) on imagined and replay returns, regularized to its EMA.
Train actor with Reinforce on normalized returns plus entropy bonus eta=3e-4.
ablations: All robustness techniques help on a 14-task mean; KL objective (balance + free bits) matters most, then return normalization and symexp twohot.
Stopping reconstruction gradients hurts much more than stopping reward/value gradients: performance rests mainly on the unsupervised world-model loss.
Larger models (12M to 400M) monotonically raise score and reduce env steps needed; higher replay ratio also improves data efficiency.
hyperparams: Imagination horizon 15; batch 16 x 64; lr 4e-5; beta_pred=1, beta_dyn=1, beta_rep=0.1; free nats 1; 1% unimix; gamma 0.997 (horizon 333); lambda 0.95; eta 3e-4; critic EMA 0.98; AGC 0.3; LaProp eps 1e-20; replay 5e6.
notes: Latent: vector of categoricals with codes per latent = d/16 (e.g. 64 at 200M). Not a robot-manipulation policy per se; surveys cite it as the canonical latent-imagination world model. In DINO-WM's offline goal-reaching comparison DreamerV3 got 0.30 SR on PushT (DINO-WM paper numbers).

name: TD-MPC2
resolvedTitle: TD-MPC2: Scalable, Robust World Models for Continuous Control
org: UC San Diego
problem: Existing continuous-control RL needs per-task tuning and naive scaling of TD-MPC hurts performance; generalist embodied agents rely on near-expert BC data rather than uncurated multi-task data.
keyIdea: Implicit (decoder-free) control-centric world model trained by latent joint-embedding prediction, discrete-regression reward/value and TD learning, used for MPPI planning with a terminal value bootstrap and a max-entropy policy prior; made robust and scalable with SimNorm, LayerNorm, Q-ensembles and task embeddings.
architecture: Five MLPs (LayerNorm + Mish): encoder h, latent dynamics d, reward R, ensemble of 5 Q-functions, policy prior p; latent normalized with SimNorm (simplices of dim 8); learnable task embedding e (norm <= 1); action masking with zero-padding for multi-embodiment.
inputs: Proprioceptive state (or 64x64 images with conv encoder), learnable task embedding
outputs: Continuous action (first action of MPPI-optimized sequence)
actionRepr: Continuous action vector (up to 39-D) chosen by MPPI over horizon-3 Gaussian action sequences, executed one step at a time
trainingData: Online RL on 104 tasks (DMControl 39, Meta-World 50, ManiSkill2 5, MyoSuite 10); multitask agents trained on 80-task offline mixed-quality datasets

headlineResults.value: outperforms SAC, DreamerV3, TD-MPC with one hyperparameter set

headlineResults.comparedTo: policy only 42.2; no norm 46.8; continuous regression 49.6

whatChangedVsParent: vs TD-MPC: SimNorm latent, LayerNorm+Mish, 5-Q ensemble with dropout, discrete log-space reward/value regression, max-entropy policy prior, learnable normalized task embeddings, action masking, no MPPI momentum; 5M vs 1M params.
limitations: Continuous actions only (extending to discrete actions is open, MPC is designed for continuous spaces); finetuning to new tasks and zero-shot generalization to unseen embodiments remain open problems.

keyEquations.meaning: World model loss: latent joint-embedding prediction + reward and value discrete regression.
Max-entropy policy prior objective in latent rollouts.
SimNorm: project latent into L softmax simplices.
MPPI planning objective with terminal-value bootstrap.

algorithmSteps: Encode observation to SimNorm latent z_t (conditioned on task embedding e).
Warm-start MPPI Gaussian from previous step's solution shifted by 1.
Sample 512 action sequences of horizon 3 (24 from policy prior), roll out in latent space.
Score each by sum of predicted rewards + gamma^H * Q terminal value.
Refit mean/std from top 64 elites (temperature-weighted), repeat 6 iterations.
Execute first action; store transition in replay.
Update model (Eq. 3) and policy prior (Eq. 4) with batch 256, UTD 1.
ablations: Actor (80-task, 19M): planning + policy 54.2 vs planning only 53.7 vs policy only 42.2.
Normalization: LN + SimNorm 54.2 vs SimNorm only 51.0 vs none 46.8.
Discrete regression 54.2 vs continuous 49.6; Q-functions 2/5/10 give 53.5/54.2/57.0.
hyperparams: Horizon 3; 6 MPPI iterations (+2 if action dim >= 20); population 512; 24 policy-prior samples; 64 elites; temperature 0.5; 5 Q-functions; 101 reward/value bins; SimNorm V=8; latent 512 (5M model); batch 256; lr 3e-4; gamma via episode-length heuristic clipped to [0.95, 0.995].
notes: Default model 5M params vs TD-MPC 1M. Trained 317M model ~33 GPU days on one RTX 3090 (per alphaXiv summary; not re-verified in page text). In DINO-WM's offline reward-free goal-reaching setting TD-MPC2 scores 0.00 SR because it relies on reward signal to shape latents (DINO-WM paper).

name: V-JEPA 2
resolvedTitle: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
org: FAIR at Meta; Mila / Polytechnique Montreal
problem: Interaction data for world models is scarce, and video-generation world models are expensive to plan with and focus on unpredictable pixel details.
keyIdea: Pretrain a JEPA video encoder by mask-denoising in representation space on 1M+ hours of internet video, then freeze it and post-train a small action-conditioned latent predictor (V-JEPA 2-AC) on <62 h of unlabeled Droid video, planning with CEM toward image-goal embeddings.
architecture: ViT encoder up to ViT-g (~1B) with 3D-RoPE, tubelets 2x16x16; ViT predictor for masked features; V-JEPA 2-AC: ~300M, 24-layer block-causal transformer predicting next-frame 16x16x1408 feature maps from interleaved action, end-effector state and frame tokens.
inputs: Monocular RGB frames (256x256, 4 fps), 7-D end-effector state, image goal
outputs: Predicted next-frame representation; planned 7-D end-effector delta action
actionRepr: 7-D end-effector delta (xyz, Euler orientation, gripper) chosen by CEM each step, constrained to L1-ball radius 0.075 (~13 cm), receding-horizon, planning horizon 1
trainingData: Pretraining: VideoMix22M (>1M hours video + 1M images: SSv2, Kinetics, HowTo100M, curated YT-Temporal-1B, ImageNet). Post-training: <62 hours / ~23k Droid trajectories (left camera, successes and failures, no rewards or task labels).
whatChangedVsParent: Scales V-JEPA data (to VM22M), encoder size (300M to 1B), training length and resolution via progressive training, uses 3D-RoPE, and adds an action-conditioned post-trained predictor for planning.
limitations: Sensitive to camera positioning since action axes are inferred implicitly from uncalibrated monocular video; long-horizon planning limited by error accumulation and search size (pick-and-place needs image sub-goals); goals must be images, not language.

keyEquations.meaning: Mask-denoising in representation space; EMA target encoder prevents collapse.
Next-frame feature prediction from actions, states, frames (T=15).
Autoregressive rollout loss (T=2) to reduce error accumulation.

keyEquations.tex: \mathcal{E}(\hat a_{1:T}; z_k, s_k, z_g) := \|P(\hat a_{1:T}; s_k, z_k) - z_g\|_1
keyEquations.meaning: Goal-conditioned energy minimized by CEM for planning.

algorithmSteps: Pretrain encoder+predictor with masked feature prediction on VM22M (progressive resolution/length).
Freeze encoder; train 300M block-causal AC predictor on Droid clips (16 frames @4 fps) with teacher-forcing + 2-step rollout L1 losses.
At test time encode current frame and goal image.
CEM: sample 800 action candidates (L1 ball r=0.075), roll out predictor, score L1 energy to goal.
Refine 10 iterations from top-10 samples; horizon 1.
Execute first action (blocking control), observe, replan; switch sub-goals for pick-and-place (4/10/4 steps).
ablations: Cooldown at higher crop raises IN1K from 84.6 (256) to 85.1 (384).
Evaluating on longer clips (up to 64 frames) boosts average probe accuracy by up to +9.7 points.
Training AC predictor on both Droid left and right views without camera conditioning degraded performance.
hyperparams: Pretrain: 16 frames @4 fps, crop 256, batch 3072, tubelet 2, patch 16, EMA 0.99925; cooldown 64 frames, crop up to 384/512. AC: 24 layers, 16 heads, dim 1024, batch 256, 4 s clips @4 fps, T=15 teacher forcing, T=2 rollout. CEM: 800 samples, 10 iters, top-10, horizon 1, ~16 s/action on RTX 4090.
notes: VidQA SOTA at 8B class (PerceptionTest 84.0, TempCompass 76.9) after LLM alignment. Octo baseline fine-tuned on full Droid with hindsight image goals; Cosmos baseline = Cosmos 7B latent diffusion fine-tuned action-conditioned on Droid (first reported use of Cosmos for robot control per authors).

name: DINO-WM
resolvedTitle: DINO-WM: World Models on Pre-trained Visual Features enable Zero-shot Planning
org: New York University (Courant); Meta AI
problem: Online world models are task-specific and offline ones usually need rewards, expert demos or inverse models; learning observation encoders from scratch is inefficient.
keyIdea: Freeze DINOv2 patch features as the observation space and train a causal ViT to predict future patch embeddings from offline trajectories; plan to arbitrary image goals by MPC/CEM minimizing latent MSE to the goal embedding.
architecture: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 encoder (14x14 patches x 384); ViT transition model (depth 6, 16 heads, MLP 2048, ~19M params) with frame-level causal attention; actions (and proprio) MLP-encoded and concatenated to every patch; optional transposed-conv decoder trained separately for visualization.
inputs: RGB image history (224, resized to 196), actions, optional proprioception, goal image
outputs: Predicted next-frame DINOv2 patch embeddings; planned action sequence
actionRepr: Environment-native low-level actions (embedded to 10-D), sequence optimized by CEM with frameskip 5 in most envs; MPC executes first k actions
trainingData: Offline trajectories per environment, no rewards: PointMaze 2000, Reacher 3000, Push-T 18500, PushObj 20000, Wall 1920, WallRandom 10240, Rope 1000, Granular 1000
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces learned reconstruction/reward-driven latents with frozen pretrained DINOv2 patch features and frame-level causal prediction, trained purely offline without rewards.
limitations: Needs offline data with sufficient state-action coverage; assumes ground-truth actions are available (cannot train on action-free internet video); plans directly in action space without hierarchy.

keyEquations.meaning: Latent consistency loss: predict next DINOv2 patch features.

keyEquations.tex: C = \|\hat z_T - z_g\|^2,\quad \hat z_t = p(\hat z_{t-1}, a_{t-1}),\ \hat z_0 = \mathrm{enc}(o_0),\ z_g = \mathrm{enc}(o_g)
keyEquations.meaning: Planning cost: latent MSE between rolled-out final state and goal.
Optional decoder loss, trained independently for visualization only.

algorithmSteps: Encode frames with frozen DINOv2 into patch embeddings.
Train causal ViT predictor with teacher forcing on H+1 segments (latent MSE).
At test time encode current observation o_0 and goal o_g.
CEM: sample N action sequences, roll out predictor in latent space.
Score by ||z_T - z_g||^2, refit Gaussian on top-K, iterate.
Execute first k actions; re-encode new observation and repeat (MPC).
ablations: Encoder: DINO patch 0.90 PushT SR vs DINO CLS 0.44, R3M 0.42, ResNet 0.20.
Causal mask: with mask SR 0.76/0.88/0.92 for h=1/2/3 vs without 0.76/0.36/0.08.
Adding decoder reconstruction loss to predictor drops PushT SR 0.92 to 0.80; data scaling 200 to 18500 trajectories raises SR 0.08 to 0.92.
hyperparams: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 features (14x14, 384); predictor depth 6, 16 heads, MLP 2048; history H=3 (Maze/Reach/PushT) or 1; frameskip 5 (1 for Rope/Granular); action emb dim 10; batch 32, 100 epochs; CEM 100 samples x 10 iters takes 53 s; inference 0.014 s per step (A6000).
notes: Baselines IRIS, DreamerV3, TD-MPC2 were retrained offline without reward and then used with MPC, which is not their native use (TD-MPC2 in particular). Success rates are simulated goal-reaching tasks, not real-robot.

name: UniSim
resolvedTitle: Learning Interactive Real-World Simulators
org: UC Berkeley; Google DeepMind; MIT; University of Alberta
problem: Datasets for learning a real-world simulator are each rich along only one axis (objects, actions, motions, language), so no single source can teach interactive action-conditioned simulation.
keyIdea: Orchestrate heterogeneous datasets into a unified action-in-video-out interface (T5 text embeddings + discretized low-level controls) and train a history-conditioned video diffusion model that is rolled out autoregressively as an interactive simulator.
architecture: 3D video U-Net diffusion (interleaved spatial/temporal attention and conv) base model at 16x24x40, plus two spatial super-resolution models to 192x320; conditioned on 4 previous frames concatenated channelwise and action embeddings via classifier-free guidance.
inputs: History frames (4 recent), action = T5 text embedding concatenated with discretized control values (language instruction, robot delta, camera motion)
outputs: Next video segment (16 frames); rolled out autoregressively
actionRepr: Not a policy; conditions on language actions and discretized low-level controls (e.g. delta x, delta y)
trainingData: Habitat HM3D, Language Table (sim + real), Bridge, RT-1 data, Ego4D, EPIC-KITCHENS, SSv2, Matterport3D panoramas, LAION/ALIGN image-text, internet video; 512 TPU-v3 for 20 days, 1M steps
parents: Imagen Video / video diffusion (Ho et al.)
whatChangedVsParent: Turns text-to-video diffusion into an action-conditioned, history-conditioned observation prediction model trained on a unified action space across many datasets, enabling autoregressive interactive rollouts.
limitations: Hallucinates for impossible actions; limited memory (conditions on a few recent frames); limited out-of-domain generalization (e.g. unseen robot morphologies); visual only (no sound, force, touch).

keyEquations.meaning: Classifier-free guidance on the action; eta controls action conditioning strength.
Epsilon-prediction denoising loss for observation prediction p(o_t|h_{t-1},a_{t-1}).
Reduction in distance to goal metric for long-horizon policy eval.

algorithmSteps: Convert each dataset's labels into text actions (T5) plus discretized controls; images treated as 1-frame videos.
Train history-conditioned video diffusion (eps-prediction) with CFG on actions; add dataset identifier prefix for low-data domains.
Simulate: given current frames and an action, sample 16 frames (256 steps), upsample twice.
Feed last frames back as history for the next action (autoregressive long-horizon).
Use rollouts for hindsight-relabeled VLM policy data or for REINFORCE RL of a PaLI-3B VLA with a learned steps-to-completion reward.
Deploy trained policy zero-shot on real Language Table robot (inverse dynamics recovers actions from generated video for the VLM policy).
ablations: Conditioning on 4 recent frames: FID 34.63 / FVD 211.3 vs 1 frame 59.47 / 315.69.
Removing internet data worsens FVD to 307.80 vs 211.30 for full mixture.
Domain-identifier prefixes improve low-data domain generation but hurt cross-domain generalization; FVD gains plateau with model size.
hyperparams: Base 16 frames at 24x40; SR to 48x80 then 192x320; 4 conditioning frames; 256 sampling timesteps; cosine noise schedule; eps prediction; batch 256; lr 1e-4; 1M steps on 512 TPU-v3; conditioning token length 64.
notes: Simulator is cited by surveys as a precursor to world foundation models; RL success rates in Table 3 were assessed qualitatively from simulated rollouts (48 tasks), not on the real robot. Video-captioning application (PaLI-X fine-tuned on UniSim videos) also reported but numbers not captured here.

name: Cosmos world foundation models
resolvedTitle: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
org: NVIDIA
problem: Physical AI lacks scalable, safe interaction data; there was no open, general-purpose pretrained world model that can be post-trained for specific robots, driving or camera control.
keyIdea: A platform: curated 20M-hour video pipeline, Cosmos tokenizers, and open-weight pretrained world foundation models (latent diffusion and autoregressive) that are post-trained into specialized world models (camera-, action-, instruction-, trajectory-conditioned).
architecture: Diffusion WFMs: DiT-style latent diffusion (EDM) on CV8x8x8 continuous tokens with 3D patchify, FPS-aware 3D RoPE + learnable APE, T5-XXL cross-attention, QK-norm, AdaLN-LoRA. Autoregressive WFMs: Llama3-style decoder on DV8x16x16 FSQ discrete tokens with 3D RoPE (YaRN) + sinusoidal APE, T5 cross-attention, plus a 7B diffusion decoder.
inputs: Text prompt and/or conditioning video frames; post-trained variants add camera poses, 7-D robot actions, instructions, or ego trajectories
outputs: Future video (up to 121 frames at 720p for diffusion models)
actionRepr: Not a policy; action-conditioned variant takes 7-D action vectors (Bridge) through added action-embedding modules for next-frame generation
trainingData: ~100M clips (2-60 s) curated from 20M hours of raw video, ~10M for fine-tuning; 10,000 H100 GPUs over three months. Robotics post-training on Bridge (action) and Cosmos-1X (instruction); driving on internal RDS (~20,000 hours, 6 cameras).
whatChangedVsParent: Packages general video generators as a pretrain-then-post-train world-model platform for Physical AI, with physics-oriented data curation, dedicated tokenizers, and robot/driving/camera-conditioned post-training.
limitations: Still fails at physics: object permanence, contact-rich dynamics, gravity and fluids; larger models do not necessarily adhere to physics better; physical-fidelity evaluation is hard; AR Text2World does not benefit from prompt upsampling.

keyEquations.meaning: EDM denoising score matching at noise level sigma.
Noise-level weighted loss with learned uncertainty weighting u(sigma).
Autoregressive next video-token prediction loss.

algorithmSteps: Curate video: shot detection, transcode, filter (motion, quality, text overlay), VLM caption, semantic dedup, shard.
Train Cosmos tokenizers (continuous AE and FSQ discrete) jointly on images and video.
Pretrain diffusion Text2World progressively 512p/57 frames to 720p/121 frames, then high-quality fine-tune; derive Video2World by adding frame conditioning.
Pretrain AR models on next-token video prediction, then add T5 cross-attention for Video2World.
Post-train on target domain: add action/camera/trajectory embeddings and fine-tune.
Generate with guardrails (Aegis text pre-guard, video safety classifier + face blur post-guard).
ablations: Action-conditioned 7B diffusion (FVD 190) outperforms 5B AR (434) and IRASim-Action (593) on Bridge.
Medusa speculative decoding accelerates AR inference; 320x512 variant reaches real-time 10 FPS (per paper summary).
14B diffusion generates richer detail and more stable motion than 7B (qualitative).
hyperparams: Diffusion tokenizer CV8x8x8 (8x temporal, 8x8 spatial), patchify 2; stages 512p x 57 frames (context 10,240) then 720p x 121 frames (context 56,320); AR tokenizer DV8x16x16 FSQ (~64K vocab); T5-XXL text encoder.
notes: Released as Cosmos-Predict1 (open weights, permissive license); the 2025-07 v3 of the arXiv paper uses 'Predict1' naming, earlier versions called them Cosmos-1.0-Diffusion/Autoregressive. V-JEPA 2 paper reports Cosmos-7B fine-tuned on Droid needed 4 min per action for CEM planning and got 0% on pick-and-place (Lab 2). Some speedup/PSNR figures in ablations come from the alphaXiv summary rather than page text.

name: Genie Envisioner
resolvedTitle: Genie Envisioner: A Unified World Foundation Platform for Robotic Manipulation
org: AgiBot Genie Team; LV-NUS Lab; Beihang University (BUAA)
problem: Robot manipulation pipelines are a patchwork of separate data collection, policy training and evaluation stages; VLAs map vision into a language-centric space that loses spatiotemporal detail and have no internal world model.
keyIdea: One video-generative world model (GE-Base) trained on ~3,000 h of AgiBot-World robot video serves as the backbone for a policy (GE-Act, a parallel flow-matching action branch), a neural simulator (GE-Sim, action-conditioned generation) and an evaluation benchmark (EWMBench).
architecture: GE-Base: multi-view (head + 2 wrist) instruction-conditioned autoregressive video DiT built on LTX-Video 2B or COSMOS2 2B, with sparse memory frames, view embeddings, sparse cross-view self-attention and T5-XXL cross-attention. GE-Act: 160M action DiT mirroring GE-Base depth with smaller hidden dim, cross-attending to visual tokens per block. GE-Sim: GE-Base plus Pose2Image and motion-vector action conditioning and CLIP reference.
inputs: Three camera views (initial frame + 4 sparse memory frames at 5 Hz), language instruction, optional robot state
outputs: GE-Base: next multi-view video chunk; GE-Act: 54-step action chunk; GE-Sim: action-conditioned video
actionRepr: Chunk of 54 continuous actions at 30 Hz via flow matching (5 denoising steps), dual-arm AgiBot G1
params: GE-Base ~2B (LTX-Video 2B or COSMOS2 2B base); GE-Act action decoder 160M
trainingData: AgiBot-World-Beta: ~1M real dual-arm episodes, 2,967 h, multi-view with instructions. GE-Base-MR 32 A100 x 7 days; GE-Base-LF 32 A100 x 3 days; GE-Act action pretrain 16 A100 x 3 days. Cross-embodiment: 250 demos (~1 h) per task.

headlineResults.benchmark: AgiBot G1 5 real tasks (sandwich, tea, table, microwave, conveyor)
Agilex Cobot Magic box/cloth folding (1 h data)
headlineResults.value: outperforms pi0; UniVLA and GR00T N1 at 0%

whatChangedVsParent: Adapts general video DiTs to multi-view robot video with sparse memory and adds a parallel flow-matching action branch plus action-conditioned simulator in one platform, instead of separate VLA/simulator stacks.
limitations: Pretrained action decoder cannot be reused across embodiments (a new action DiT is trained per new platform); adding robot state to a general-video-pretrained model hurt via shortcut learning; GE-Sim is purely visual with no explicit physics.

keyEquations.meaning: GE-Base predicts next multi-view video chunk from initial, memory tokens and instruction.

symbols.meaning: initial frame tokens for view i

keyEquations.meaning: Parallel video and action DiT blocks; action tokens cross-attend to visual features.

algorithmSteps: Stage I (GE-Base-MR): train video DiT on 57-frame clips at 3-30 Hz with 4 memory frames on AgiBot-World-Beta.
Stage II (GE-Base-LF): fine-tune on 9-frame 5 Hz clips (2 latent frames) to match control abstraction.
GE-Act pretrain: freeze GE-Base-LF, train action branch to predict 54 actions at 30 Hz from 4 memory frames at 5 Hz.
Task adaptation: video adaptation on task data upweighted 10x, then full-model action specialization.
Inference (slow-fast): one video denoising step at 5 Hz, cache visual tokens, 5 action denoising steps at 30 Hz.
New embodiment: fine-tune video DiT, train new action DiT from scratch on ~1 h teleop data.
ablations: Pretraining: GE-Base init + task video adaptation reaches E2E 0.89 / SR 0.76 vs from scratch 0.15 / 0.05 and general LTX-Video init ~0.
Robot state input helps with GE-Base init (E2E 0.81 vs 0.49) but hurts general-video init due to shortcut learning.
Fast (asynchronous) mode matches or beats standard mode, notably on conveyor packing; COSMOS2-based GE-Sim has higher fidelity than LTX-based.
hyperparams: Action chunk 54 steps at 30 Hz; video at 5 Hz (1:6 ratio); 4 sparse memory frames; 1 video + 5 action flow-matching steps at inference; 3 camera views; LTX-Video 2B or COSMOS2 2B backbone; 250 demos (~1 h) for cross-embodiment adaptation.
notes: Most real-robot comparisons are reported only as bar charts (exact per-task SR not in text). Paper states code, models and benchmarks 'will be released'. EWMBench rankings reported to align with human judgment better than VBench. Surveys may describe GE as a WAM (world action model) - consistent with the paper's own 'world action model' term for GE-Act.

name: IRASim
resolvedTitle: IRASim: A Fine-Grained World Model for Robot Manipulation
org: HKUST; ByteDance Seed (ByteDance Research)
problem: Existing action-conditioned video world models overlook precise alignment between each action and its corresponding frame, so they fail to capture fine-grained robot-object interaction needed for manipulation.
keyIdea: Trajectory-to-video generation with a latent Diffusion Transformer whose spatial blocks are conditioned per frame on the matching action via adaptive LayerNorm (Frame-Ada), enforcing action-frame alignment.
architecture: Frozen SDXL VAE encodes frames to latents; a DiT with memory-efficient spatial-temporal attention denoises future-frame latents while historical-frame tokens are kept clean as context. Each action is linearly embedded, added to the diffusion-timestep embedding, and regresses per-frame AdaLN scale/shift for spatial blocks; temporal blocks share a trajectory-level embedding.
inputs: Historical frame(s) I_{t-h:t} (1 frame for RT-1/Bridge/Language-Table, 2 for RoboNet) + action trajectory a_{t:t+n} (7-DoF delta EE + gripper for RT-1/Bridge; 2-DoF for Language-Table; 5-D for RoboNet)
outputs: Predicted future video frames I_{t+1:t+n+1} (15 frames per pass; autoregressive rollout for long horizons, 150+ frames)
trainingData: RT-1, Bridge, Language-Table, RoboNet (4-second 16-frame clips); LIBERO and Push-T rollouts (expert + post-trained policy rollouts) for evaluation/planning, initialized from OpenSora in those experiments

headlineResults.metric: Pearson correlation with MuJoCo simulator success rates

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces video-level (text-style) conditioning with frame-level per-action AdaLN conditioning inside each DiT spatial block.
limitations: Video generation is not real-time (a 16-frame ~4 s clip takes ~30 s on an A100); authors plan diffusion distillation and using IRASim as a dynamics model for RL.
notes: v1 June 2024; v2 (July 2025) adds policy evaluation and model-based planning experiments. Human preference study: Frame-Ada beats VDM 100% on all three datasets. Uses PNDM sampler, 50 steps. Training ~2,370 GPU-hours per dataset on 32 A800/A100. Real-robot planning with MSE cost: Close Drawer 0.87, Place Mandarin (green) 0.80, (red) 0.87 vs random 0.20/0.07/0.13. Survey often frames it as action-conditioned world model / 'simulator'; paper's primary metrics are Latent L2 and PSNR (FID/FVD judged misaligned with human preference).

keyEquations.meaning: Trajectory-to-video task: predict future frames from history frames and an action trajectory.
DDPM noise-prediction loss, computed only on predicted-frame latents.

symbols.meaning: noised latents z^{t+1:t+n+1} at diffusion step t
DiT noise predictor conditioned on history and actions

keyEquations.meaning: Frame-level AdaLN in spatial block: frame i modulated by parameters from action i.

symbols.meaning: scale/shift regressed from c_S^i = action-i embedding + timestep embedding

algorithmSteps: Encode history frames with frozen SDXL VAE; keep their tokens noise-free.
Sample Gaussian noise for n future-frame latents.
Embed each action; add diffusion-timestep embedding to get per-frame conditioning.
Denoise with DiT (spatial blocks per-frame AdaLN, temporal blocks shared) using PNDM, 50 steps.
Decode latents to frames; for long horizons, use last generated frame as next history and repeat.
Planning: sample K trajectories from policy, unroll each in IRASim, score final frame, execute best.
ablations: Frame-Ada vs Video-Ada, RT-1 short traj.: PSNR 26.048 vs 25.446, Latent L2 0.2099 vs 0.2191.
Push-T with no post-trained rollouts (P=0): IoU degrades as K grows (0.679 K=5 -> 0.418 K=50); with P=1000 it rises to 0.961.
Scaling 33M -> 679M consistently lowers Latent L2 on RT-1, Bridge, Language-Table.
hyperparams: 1 history frame + 15 actions -> 15 frames (RoboNet: 2 + 10 -> 10); XL: 28 layers, hidden 1152, 16 heads, patch 2; AdamW lr 1e-4, batch 64, grad clip 0.1, EMA 0.9999; PNDM 50 steps; resolution up to 288x512.

name: UniPi
resolvedTitle: Learning Universal Policies via Text-Guided Video Generation
org: MIT; Google DeepMind; UC Berkeley; Georgia Tech; University of Alberta
problem: MDP-based agents cannot share knowledge across environments with different state/action spaces and need hand-designed rewards; internet video/text knowledge is hard to use for control.
keyIdea: Cast decision making as text-conditioned video generation (a Unified Predictive Decision Process): a video diffusion planner synthesizes the future frames of the task from the current image and instruction, and a small inverse-dynamics model extracts actions.
architecture: Imagen-Video-style Video U-Net diffusion with first-frame conditioning (first frame tiled across time and concatenated channel-wise), temporal convolutions, and a cascade of temporal super-resolution models (coarse-to-fine hierarchical planning); T5-XXL text encoder (4.6B). Separate small CNN inverse-dynamics model maps frames to 7-D controls.
inputs: Initial image x_0 + text task description c
outputs: H-step video plan; actions via inverse dynamics
actionRepr: 7-dim continuous controls per frame regressed by an inverse-dynamics model from generated frames; executed open-loop in experiments
params: 1.7B first-frame-conditioned video model + 1.7B temporal super-resolution (sim); real-world cascade 1.7B/1.7B/1.4B/1.2B; T5-XXL 4.6B text encoder
trainingData: Sim: 200k scripted videos (combinatorial blocks), 200k videos across 10 CLIPort tasks; real: pretrain on 14M video-text + 60M image-text pairs + LAION-400M (Imagen Video data), finetune on Bridge 7.2k video-text pairs; inverse dynamics on 20k action-annotated videos (combinatorial)
whatChangedVsParent: Diffuses future image frames (a video plan) conditioned on text instead of diffusing state-action trajectories, decoupling a universal planner from an environment-specific inverse-dynamics model.
limitations: Video diffusion is slow (about a minute for photorealistic videos; distillation gave a 16x speed-up); environments are fully observed, and in partial observability video models may hallucinate objects or motion.
notes: NeurIPS 2023. Trained 2M steps, batch 2048, on 256 TPU-v4 chips. Original models/code are proprietary (SuSIE states not publicly available); SuSIE and others use re-implementations, which perform poorly on real Bridge scenes. CONFLICT: AVDC paper says UniPi 'requires over 256 TPU pods'; UniPi's own appendix says 256 TPU-v4 chips. Real-world results are video-quality/success-classifier metrics, not physical robot rollouts.

keyEquations.meaning: UPDP: images as states, text as task, a conditional video generator as the planner.
Trajectory-task conditioned policy (inverse dynamics) maps a video plan to actions.

keyEquations.tex: \hat{s}(\tau_k, k \mid c, x_0) = (1+\omega)\, s(\tau_k, k \mid c, x_0) - \omega\, s(\tau_k, k)
keyEquations.meaning: Classifier-free guidance on text and first-frame conditioning during sampling.

symbols.meaning: noisy video at noise level k

algorithmSteps: Encode instruction with T5-XXL.
Tile current frame x0 across time as conditioning context.
Sample a temporally sparse video plan with first-frame-conditioned video diffusion (classifier-free guidance).
Refine with temporal super-resolution diffusion into a dense plan.
Apply inverse-dynamics model to consecutive frames to infer H actions.
Execute actions open-loop (closed-loop MPC possible but not used).
ablations: No frame condition/consistency/hierarchy: Place 13.2, Relation 12.4 vs full UniPi 59.1 / 53.2 (seen tasks).
Adding frame conditioning alone: Place 52.4, Relation 34.7; + consistency: 53.2 / 39.4.
Internet pretraining on Bridge: FID 17.75 -> 14.54, success classifier 72.6% -> 77.1%.
hyperparams: Sim: 10x48x64 base videos (every 8th frame) + 20x48x64 temporal SR; real cascade up to 32x320x192; 2M steps, batch 2048, lr 1e-4; log-SNR noise schedule [-20, 20].

name: AVDC
resolvedTitle: Learning to Act from Actionless Videos through Dense Correspondences
org: National Taiwan University; MIT CSAIL / BCS / CBMM
problem: Video-as-policy methods (e.g., UniPi) still need action labels to train inverse-dynamics or action-conditioned models, and video diffusion training is prohibitively expensive.
keyIdea: Generate a video of the task, estimate optical flow between generated frames, and use flow plus the first frame's depth to solve for SE(3) rigid transforms of the object (or camera), converted into robot commands with off-the-shelf primitives, so no action labels are needed.
architecture: Text-conditioned video diffusion U-Net (Dhariwal & Nichol style) with factorized spatial-temporal convolutions in each ResNet block, initial frame concatenated channel-wise, CLIP-Text embedding; off-the-shelf GMFlow for optical flow; rigid-transform optimization + grasp/push primitives; replanning loop.
inputs: Initial RGB-D observation + text goal
outputs: Synthesized video (T=8 future frames) -> object/camera SE(3) trajectory -> robot subgoal poses or discrete navigation actions
actionRepr: No learned action head: sequence of SE(3) end-effector subgoals from inferred object transforms (manipulation) or discrete MoveForward/RotateLeft/RotateRight/Done (navigation)
trainingData: Meta-World 165 videos; iTHOR 240 videos; Visual Pusher 198 human videos; Bridge (paper cites 33,078 demos; training details list ~40,000 Bridge videos) + 20 human videos for real Panda
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces UniPi's action-labeled inverse-dynamics model with label-free action regression from optical flow and depth, and uses an efficient factorized U-Net trainable on 4 GPUs in a day.
limitations: Main failures come from optical-flow tracking errors (off-the-shelf flow not trained in-domain, low resolution hurts small objects), and in the real world from wrong or discontinuous generated videos; assumes rigid motion and relies on heuristic grasp/contact sampling without force.
notes: ICLR 2024. Open-source codebase (flow-diffusion.github.io). Replanning triggers when robot moves <1 mm over 15 steps; up to 5 replans (18-108 s planning per Meta-World episode on RTX 3080Ti). Video generation ~10.57 s per video. Only initial-frame depth needed, so trainable on RGB-only video. Using Language-SAM masks instead of GT masks drops Meta-World to 34.5% (from report, not verified in read pages).

keyEquations.meaning: Video diffusion noise-prediction loss conditioned on text (and first frame).

keyEquations.tex: \mathcal{L}_{Trans} = \sum_i \left\| u^i_t - \frac{(KT_t x_i)_1}{(KT_t x_i)_3} \right\|_2^2 + \left\| v^i_t - \frac{(KT_t x_i)_2}{(KT_t x_i)_3} \right\|_2^2
keyEquations.meaning: Solve rigid transform T_t so projected 3D object points match flow-tracked pixels.

symbols.meaning: rigid SE(3) transform at time t
flow-tracked pixel of point i in frame t

algorithmSteps: Synthesize 8 future frames from current RGB and text with video diffusion.
Predict optical flow between consecutive frames with GMFlow.
Lift masked object pixels to 3D using first-frame depth; RANSAC inliers.
Optimize rigid transforms T_t matching projected points to tracked pixels.
Sample grasp/contact point; decide grasp vs push (>10 cm vertical displacement => grasp).
Apply transforms to get subgoals; reach them with a position controller.
If movement <1 mm over 15 steps and task unfinished, replan from current observation.
ablations: No replanning: 19.6% vs full 43.1% on Meta-World.
Directly diffusing flow (AVDC-Flow): 13.7% vs 43.1%.
Using a learned inverse-dynamics model (AVDC-ID): 6.1%.
hyperparams: T=8 frames; Meta-World 128x128, iTHOR 64x64, Bridge 48x64; 100 denoising steps (DDIM 10 viable); max 5 replans; 500 sampled mask points.

name: SuSIE
resolvedTitle: Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation with Pretrained Image-Editing Diffusion Models
org: UC Berkeley; Stanford; Google DeepMind
problem: Language-conditioned policies trained on robot data fail on novel objects/scenes and lack low-level precision; internet-pretrained models don't directly give low-level actions.
keyIdea: Finetune the InstructPix2Pix image-editing diffusion model to 'edit' the current frame into a near-future subgoal image given the instruction, then reach it with a language-agnostic goal-conditioned diffusion policy, re-generating subgoals periodically.
architecture: High level: InstructPix2Pix (latent diffusion UNet) finetuned on robot + human video, classifier-free guidance on image and text. Low level: goal-conditioned diffusion policy with ResNet-50 encoder on channel-stacked observation and goal images, 3x256 residual MLP denoiser, predicting 4-action chunks with temporal ensembling.
inputs: Current image (256x256) + language command
outputs: Subgoal image k_min..k_max steps ahead; low-level actions
actionRepr: chunks of 4 continuous actions from a goal-conditioned diffusion policy, temporally ensembled (mean of last 4 predictions)
trainingData: Real: BridgeData V2 (60k+ trajectories, 45k language-labeled) + Something-Something (~75k filtered clips), 60/40 SSv2/Bridge mix for subgoal model; Sim: CALVIN play data (35% language-labeled)
whatChangedVsParent: Generates a single near-future subgoal image with a pretrained image-editing model instead of a full video (UniPi), and replaces inverse dynamics with a goal-conditioned diffusion policy.
limitations: Subgoal model and low-level policy are trained separately, so the diffusion model is unaware of the policy's capabilities; performance is often bottlenecked by the low-level policy.
notes: ICLR 2024. Subgoal model: 40k steps, batch 1024, one v4-64 TPU pod (17 h); policy: 445k steps on v4-8 (15 h). Uses 60k robot trajectories vs >1.1M for RT-2-X (55B). DDIM 50 steps; image guidance 2.5, text guidance 7.5. k_test=20 subgoal refresh interval. Code released at rail-berkeley.github.io/susie (checkpoint availability not verified here).
