name: GR-1
resolvedTitle: Unleashing Large-Scale Video Generative Pre-training for Visual Robot Manipulation
org: ByteDance Research
problem: Robot data is scarce and multimodal; it was unclear whether generative video pretraining on large non-robot video helps multi-task visual manipulation.
keyIdea: A single GPT-style causal transformer is pretrained on language-conditioned future-frame prediction on Ego4D, then finetuned to jointly predict the next action and a future image from language, image history and robot state.
architecture: Frozen CLIP text encoder; frozen MAE-pretrained ViT image encoder (CLS + Perceiver-resampled patch tokens); linear state encoder; 12-layer, 12-head, hidden-384 causal transformer with learnable [OBS] and [ACT] tokens; MAE-style transformer image decoder; MLP action heads for arm and gripper.
inputs: Language instruction, sequence of 10 timesteps of observation images (static + gripper cameras) and robot states (6D EE pose + binary gripper)
outputs: Next action a_t (delta XYZ + delta Euler + binary gripper) and future image o_{t+Δt}
actionRepr: single-step continuous 6-D delta EE arm action (Smooth-L1) + binary gripper (BCE)
trainingData: Pretraining: Ego4D, 800,000 3-s clips (8M frames) with narrations; finetuning: CALVIN (language-annotated ~1% of play data, >20k trajectories) and real Kinova Gen2 data
whatChangedVsParent: Adds large-scale video-prediction pretraining and a joint future-image prediction objective to a GPT-style language-conditioned policy.
limitations: Authors point to future work on mixing video with and without language, studying relevance of pretraining videos, and scaling robot data; real-robot failures include incompletely closing the drawer and missing the handle; generalization to unseen categories remains weak.
notes: ICLR 2024. Code and checkpoint released (github.com/bytedance/GR-1; PAD paper initializes GR-1 from the authors' open-source checkpoint). Pretrain Δt = 1/3 s between frames; finetune Δt=3. Real-robot results (0.79 seen objects vs RT-1 0.27, drawer 0.75) reported in AI summary only, not verified from read pages.

keyEquations.meaning: Pretraining: language-conditioned future frame prediction on video.
Finetuning: jointly predict future image and current action.
Smooth-L1 arm, BCE gripper, MSE pixel video reconstruction losses summed.

algorithmSteps: Pretrain on Ego4D clips: tokens (l, o, [OBS]) per step, predict frame 1/3 s ahead.
Finetune on robot data with tokens (l, s, o, [OBS], [ACT]) per step over 10 steps.
Optimize L_arm + L_gripper + L_video with frozen CLIP and MAE encoders.
At inference, read [ACT] output each step and execute the predicted delta action.
ablations: ABCD->D avg len: no pretrain & no video prediction 3.33; video prediction only 3.82; full 4.21.
10% data avg len: 1.04 -> 1.52 -> 2.00 with video prediction then pretraining.
Future step for video prediction: 1 step 3.61, 3 steps 3.82, 5 steps 3.67 (no pretrain).
hyperparams: Sequence length 10; 12 layers/12 heads/hidden 384; Δt = 1 sampled frame (1/3 s) in pretraining, 3 in finetuning; pretrain batch 1024, lr 3.6e-4, 50 epochs; finetune batch 512, lr 1e-3, 20 epochs.

name: GR-2
resolvedTitle: GR-2: A Generative Video-Language-Action Model with Web-Scale Knowledge for Robot Manipulation
org: ByteDance Research
problem: GR-1's 0.8M-clip pretraining and single-step actions limited generalization to new backgrounds, environments, objects and tasks.
keyIdea: Scale GPT-style video generative pretraining to 38M curated text-video clips (~50B tokens) with VQGAN tokens, then finetune to jointly predict future multi-view frames and an action trajectory via a conditional VAE.
architecture: Frozen text encoder (CLIP); frozen VQGAN tokenizer (trained on internet + in-domain robot data) for image frames; GPT-style transformer decoder autoregressively predicting future image tokens; linear robot-state encoders; cVAE action-trajectory head; Whole-Body Control trajectory optimizer for deployment.
inputs: Language instruction, multi-view image sequence (head + wrist cameras), robot state sequence (EE position/rotation + binary gripper)
outputs: Future frames o_{t+1} per view and Cartesian action trajectory a_{t:t+k}
actionRepr: action trajectory (chunk) a_{t:t+k} in Cartesian space generated by a conditional VAE, tracked by WBC
trainingData: Pretraining: 38M clips (~50B tokens) from HowTo100M, Ego4D, SSv2, EPIC-KITCHENS, Kinetics-700, RT-1, Bridge, with hand filtering and re-captioning; finetuning: ~40,000 teleop trajectories over 105 tasks (Kinova Gen3), ~94,000 bin-picking trajectories of 55 objects, CALVIN ABCD

headlineResults.comparedTo: GR-1 (lower; exact value in figure only)
about double GR-1; w/ data aug. 87.0% Unseen Env.

whatChangedVsParent: Scales pretraining from 0.8M to 38M clips, switches to discrete VQGAN image tokens with multi-view support, and outputs cVAE action trajectories instead of single-step actions.
limitations: Generalization to unseen manipulation (novel object shapes, wrong-object selection with unseen objects) remains weakest at 55.8%; authors aim to improve robustness of action prediction.
notes: Tech report, authors alphabetical. With 50 trajectories/task: 73.9% Simple. Data augmentation via diffusion object insertion + SAM background inpainting + video generation model. Scaling: frozen pretrained params during finetune; success scales with size. CONFLICT: an AI summary of the paper lists GR-2 sizes as 1.1B/1.9B/3.5B/6.8B and GR-1 bin-picking avg as 35.9%; the paper text states 30M/95M/312M/719M trainable (230M default total) and GR-1 bin-picking 33.3%. Pretraining loss equations in the AI summary are generic, not from the paper.

keyEquations.meaning: Universal language-conditioned policy outputs an action trajectory end-to-end.
Finetuning jointly predicts next frames and the action trajectory.

algorithmSteps: Pretrain transformer to predict future VQGAN frame tokens from text + frames on 38M clips.
Finetune on robot data with multi-view images and states to predict future frames and a cVAE action trajectory.
At deployment, generate Cartesian action trajectory from current observation and instruction.
Optimize trajectory for smoothness; WBC converts to joint actions executed at 200 Hz.
ablations: Data scarcity: 50 traj/task gives 73.9% Simple vs 97.7% with ~400 traj/task.
Data augmentation lifts Unseen Environments to 87.0% and average across 3 generalization settings to 74.7%.
Model scaling 30M -> 719M trainable lowers video val. loss and raises real-robot success (figure).
hyperparams: Default 230M params (95M trainable); VQGAN discrete image tokens; cVAE action trajectory of length k (value not stated); WBC at 200 Hz.

name: PAD
resolvedTitle: Prediction with Action: Visual Policy Learning via Joint Denoising Process
org: IIIS Tsinghua University; Shanghai Qizhi Institute; Shanghai AI Lab; UC Berkeley
problem: Two-stage predict-then-act methods (UniPi, SuSIE) separate prediction from action and do not share pretrained representations, while diffusion policies ignore future prediction.
keyIdea: Denoise future images and future robot actions jointly in one Diffusion Transformer, so image prediction and action generation share representations; missing modalities are masked so video-only data can be co-trained.
architecture: DiT initialized from ImageNet class-conditional DiT; frozen SD VAE for RGB latents; MLP encoder for robot poses (1 token); optional downsampled depth tokens; frozen CLIP text embedding for conditioning; current-observation latents concatenated channel-wise with noisy future latents; masked multi-head attention handles missing modalities.
inputs: Current RGB image (256x256), robot pose, optional depth, language instruction
outputs: k=3 future RGB frames (and depth) plus k future robot poses; only first pose executed
actionRepr: k=3 future end-effector poses (7-D real, 4-D Metaworld) denoised jointly with images via DDIM; first pose executed then replan (closed-loop)
trainingData: Pretrain 200k steps on BridgeData-v2 (60,000 trajectories, video-only co-training); adapt 100k steps on Metaworld (50 demos/task, 50 tasks) or real Panda (200 teleop trajectories per task)
whatChangedVsParent: Unifies image prediction and action denoising in one DiT joint denoising process, instead of Diffusion Policy's action-only denoising or UniPi/SuSIE's two-stage image-then-action pipeline.
limitations: Only three modalities tested (RGB, pose, depth); control frequency is not high because images and actions must be jointly denoised; future work could use intermediate latents rather than pixel-space predictions.
notes: NeurIPS 2024. Pretraining 2 days + adaptation 1 day on 4 A100. Loss weights: lambda_I fixed 1.0; lambda_A, lambda_E ramped linearly 0 -> 2.0 over 100k adaptation steps. Scaling with GFLOPs: XL/2 72.5%, XL/4 64.5%, XL/8 48.2%, L/2 68.4%, B/2 62.4%. RT-2* is a re-implementation on InstructBLIP-7B. The AI summary's loss equation is paraphrased; verbatim eqs used here.

keyEquations.meaning: Per-modality DDPM noise-prediction loss, conditioned on current observations and instruction.
Joint objective balancing image, action and depth denoising.
Conditional reverse denoising step used for joint sampling.

algorithmSteps: Encode current RGB (VAE), pose (MLP), optional depth; encode instruction with CLIP.
Initialize k=3 future image/pose/depth latents as Gaussian noise; concatenate with current latents channel-wise.
Tokenize (patchify images, 1 token for poses) and run joint DiT denoising with 75 DDIM steps.
Decode predicted future frames; take first predicted pose.
Move to pose with linear-interpolation planner; repeat closed-loop.
ablations: No image prediction (PAD w/o img): Metaworld 43.6% vs 72.5%.
No video co-training: 59.2% vs 72.5%.
Patch size / compute: XL/2 72.5% vs XL/8 48.2% (119.1 vs 7.7 GFLOPs).
hyperparams: k=3 future steps, frame interval 4; 75 DDIM steps; 256x256 input, latent 32x32x4; XL/2: 28 layers, hidden 1152, 16 heads, 257 tokens; lr 1e-4, batch 256; pretrain 200k + adapt 100k steps.

name: VPP
resolvedTitle: Video Prediction Policy: A Generalist Robot Policy with Predictive Visual Representations
org: Tsinghua University (IIIS), Shanghai AI Lab, Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute, RobotEra, UC Berkeley
problem: Standard vision encoders for robot policies (single-image reconstruction or two-image contrastive pretraining) capture mostly static information and neglect the dynamics that matter for embodied control; denoising full future videos for control is too slow and can become open-loop.
keyIdea: Fine-tune a video diffusion model into a text-guided video prediction (TVP) model on human+robot manipulation video, then use a single forward pass of it as a 'predictive' vision encoder whose internal up-sampling features already encode the rough future; a policy learns an implicit inverse dynamics model on top of these features.
architecture: Stable Video Diffusion (1.5B) augmented with CLIP language cross-attention, predicting 16x256x256 videos; features from multiple up-sampling layers are interpolated and stacked, compressed by a Video Former (learnable tokens with spatial then temporal attention, 6 layers), and fed via cross-attention into a DiT diffusion policy head (4 encoder + 4 decoder layers, latent 384).
inputs: Current RGB image(s) (third-view and wrist camera, each predicted independently), language instruction (CLIP embedding)
outputs: Action chunk (e.g., 10 steps of 7-DoF on CALVIN/Franka; 10x18 for the Xhand dexterous hand)
actionRepr: chunk of 10 continuous actions (7-DoF arm; 18-dim for arm+12-DoF Xhand) generated by a DiT diffusion policy with 10 sampling steps
params: 1.5B TVP backbone (SVD); policy head size not stated
trainingData: TVP fine-tuning on 375,192 trajectories total: Something-Something-v2 (191,642, ratio 0.30), RT-1 (87,212), Bridge (23,377), BC-Z (43,264), Taco-Play, Jaco-Play, CALVIN-ABC (18,033), MetaWorld (2,500), self-collected Panda arm (2,000) and dexterous hand (2,476); policy trained on CALVIN / MetaWorld / real-robot data.
controlRateHz: 7-10 Hz on an RTX 4090 (TVP encoder pass <160 ms; ~140 ms latency)
whatChangedVsParent: Unlike UniPi/SuSIE (denoise a full goal image/video, then act) or GR-1 (predict frames autoregressively), VPP never finishes denoising: it reads predictive features from one forward pass of a fine-tuned video diffusion model and conditions a diffusion policy on them.
limitations: The paper does not have a dedicated limitations section in the retrieved text; the design trades explicit video quality for speed (one-step features are blurry), and the TVP model is frozen during policy learning.

Predictive representation: interpolated up-sampling-layer features stacked along channels.

aggregated predictive visual representation, T x (sum C_m) x W_p x H_p

algorithmSteps: Stage 1: fine-tune SVD with CLIP text cross-attention on mixed human/robot manipulation videos (Eq. 3-4); freeze it.
At each control step, concatenate current image s_0 with a fully-noised latent and run ONE forward pass of the TVP model per camera view.
Collect features from up-sampling layers, interpolate to a common size and stack along channels.
Video Former compresses features across space, time and views into fixed learnable tokens.
DiT diffusion policy denoises an action chunk (10 steps) conditioned on tokens and CLIP language.
Execute the 10-step action chunk, then repeat.
ablations: Replacing the VDM encoder with Stable-VAE / VC-1 / Voltron drops CALVIN Avg. Len from 4.33 to 2.58 / 1.23 / 1.54.
Removing internet data 4.33->3.97; also removing SVD pretraining ->1.63; removing CALVIN video pretraining ->3.31.
No Video Former 4.33->3.86 with latency ~140 ms->~450 ms; final-layer features only (no aggregation) ->3.60; 2-step denoising gives 4.19 (no gain, ~2x slower).
hyperparams: TVP predicts 16 frames at 256x256 (8 for MetaWorld); one denoising step for encoding (diffusion time-step 20 best: 4.33 vs 4.21 @10, 4.25 @30); action chunk 10x7 (Xhand 10x18); Video Former 6 layers, 8 heads, latent 512; DiT latent 384, 4+4 layers, 10 sampling steps; for visualization 30-step denoising with CFG 7.5.
notes: Venue: ICML 2025. CONFLICT: the v2 abstract claims an 18.6% relative improvement over the previous SOTA on CALVIN ABC-D (consistent with 3.65->4.33), while the main text says it 'improved the previous state-of-the-art result from 3.35 to 4.33'; the alphaXiv summary cites a 41.5% improvement over GR-1 (3.06->4.33, which is ~41.5% arithmetically) - surveys may quote either figure. Abstract also claims 31.6% increase in success rate on complex real-world dexterous tasks. TVP achieves FVD 41.4 on Bridge vs 246.3 for the earlier 'Seer' TVP model (Gu et al. 2023, a different 'Seer' from the PIDM Seer). Franka Panda real-world results were reported in the paper but not verified here.

name: Seer
resolvedTitle: Predictive Inverse Dynamics Models Are Scalable Learners for Robotic Manipulation
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Peking University, Chinese University of Hong Kong
problem: Scalable manipulation policies either do naive behavior cloning on large robot data ('action' view) or pretrain vision/world models used in a decoupled two-stage pipeline ('vision' view); neither closes the loop between visual prediction and action during training and inference.
keyIdea: An end-to-end Predictive Inverse Dynamics Model (PIDM): a transformer predicts a future RGB frame via a foresight token and predicts the intermediate actions via an action token that attends to that foresight latent, trained jointly on large robot data (DROID) and fine-tuned downstream.
architecture: Frozen MAE ViT-B image encoder + Perceiver Resampler, frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 text encoder, MLP robot-state encoder; 24-layer GPT-2-style transformer backbone (hidden 384, 12 heads) with appended [FRS] (foresight) and [INV] (action) readout tokens under a unidirectional mask ([INV] can attend to [FRS]); MLP action decoder and ViT image decoder (MAE-style with mask tokens).
inputs: RGB from eye-on-hand and eye-on-base cameras (history of m steps), robot state (6D EE pose + gripper), language instruction (or future robot state as goal during pretraining)
outputs: Predicted future RGB images at t+n and a short sequence of 7-DoF actions
actionRepr: 3-step chunk of 7-DoF actions (6D arm delta via Smooth-L1 regression with Tanh, 1D gripper via BCE); deterministic regression, not diffusion
params: Seer: 316M total, 65M trainable (251M frozen encoders); Seer-Large: 315M trainable
trainingData: Pretraining: DROID (76K successful trajectories) for real world; LIBERO-90 for LIBERO-LONG; CALVIN unannotated play data for CALVIN ABC-D. Fine-tuning: 100 demos per real task (15 Hz), LIBERO-LONG, CALVIN annotated data.
controlRateHz: Demonstrations recorded at 15 Hz; inference rate not stated

headlineResults.benchmark: Real Franka, 6 tasks incl. precision (DROID vs OXE pretraining)

whatChangedVsParent: Two-stage PIDMs (SuSIE/UniPi/CLOVER) train a goal-image generator and an inverse dynamics policy separately; Seer fuses them in one transformer so the action token attends to the foresight latent and both are optimized end-to-end from large robot data.
limitations: Only six downstream real tasks were evaluated, leaving broader high-precision and contact-rich tasks unexplored; cross-robot (cross-embodiment) capability still needs evaluation.

keyEquations.meaning: Conditional visual foresight: predict the RGB image n steps ahead, pixel MSE.

symbols.meaning: goal: language instruction or future robot state
history of m RGB images and robot states

keyEquations.meaning: Inverse dynamics conditioned on the predicted future latent rather than the true future image.

symbols.meaning: latent foresight representation from the [FRS] token
inverse dynamics head via the [INV] token

keyEquations.meaning: Total loss: Smooth-L1 arm + BCE gripper, plus weighted foresight loss.

algorithmSteps: Pretrain on a large robot dataset (DROID / LIBERO-90 / CALVIN play) with L = 0.5 L_fore + L_inv; if language is missing, the future robot state at t+n+1 serves as the goal.
Fine-tune on downstream demonstrations with the same objectives.
At inference, tokenize history images, robot states and instruction; append [FRS] and [INV] tokens per timestep.
[FRS] attends to history + language to form the foresight latent (image decoding is optional for control).
[INV] attends to inputs and [FRS]; MLP decodes a 3-step 7-DoF action chunk.
Execute first action or temporally ensemble multi-step predictions; repeat.
ablations: Fine-tuning objectives on CALVIN (no pretraining): plain BC 3.31 -> +L_fore 3.41 -> +L_fore+L_inv 3.64 Avg. Len.
Pretraining objectives: none 3.64 -> L_fore only 3.73 -> L_fore+L_inv 3.98 Avg. Len.

With 10% of downstream data, pretraining gives +187% relative success on LIBERO-LONG and +150% relative Avg. Len on CALVIN vs scratch; real-world DROID pretraining beats OXE pretraining (71.1 vs 56.7 avg SR).
hyperparams: History length 7 (LIBERO, real) / 10 (CALVIN); action chunk 3; foresight steps 3 (real world); 3 [INV] tokens; alpha=0.5, lambda=0.01; transformer 24 layers x 384 hidden x 12 heads; images 224x224.
notes: Not to be confused with 'Seer: Language instructed video prediction with latent diffusion models' (Gu et al. 2023), which VPP cites. Venue: ICLR 2025 (per general knowledge; not verified in retrieved text). OpenVLA baseline in real world used a 7B model fully fine-tuned (text also mentions '3B here' - internal inconsistency in the paper).

name: UVA
resolvedTitle: Unified Video Action Model
org: Stanford University
problem: Video-generation-based policies are slow and propagate video errors into actions, while action-only policies ignore scene-dynamics supervision and overfit to action history; prior joint models (e.g., PAD) cannot predict actions without generating the future images.
keyIdea: Learn a joint video-action latent with a transformer, then decode video and actions with two separate lightweight diffusion heads so video generation can be skipped at policy inference; masked training over inputs/outputs lets one model act as policy, video model, forward or inverse dynamics model.
architecture: Built on MAR-B (masked autoregressive image generation with continuous tokens): history frames encoded by a pretrained VAE (kl-f16) into N tokens, action chunks repeated and projected to N tokens, concatenated channel-wise with (masked) future-frame tokens; a Transformer fuses them into joint latents Z; a per-token video diffusion head and an action diffusion head (conv + MLP aggregation) decode outputs; CLIP text via cross-attention for language tasks.
inputs: History image observations (third-person only in Libero10), history action chunks, optional language (CLIP); masked future-frame tokens
outputs: Future action chunks and/or future video frames (either can be masked out)
actionRepr: action chunks of L continuous actions per observation frame via a lightweight diffusion head; 16 action steps inferred, 8 executed
trainingData: Per-benchmark training (no large pretraining): PushT, ToolHang, PushT-M, Libero10 (sim); UMI datasets (Cup Arrangement, Towel Folding, Mouse Arrangement; 500 episodes each for multi-task) for real world on ARX X5 arm. Initialized from pretrained MAR-B.
controlRateHz: Not stated as Hz; 0.23 s per action trajectory in sim (100 denoising steps), 95 ms in real world (16 denoising steps)

headlineResults.comparedTo: UniPi IDM 1.92 cm / 2.21 deg; SLAM 0.41 cm / 0.30 deg

whatChangedVsParent: Versus PAD/UniPi, UVA decouples video and action decoding from a shared latent so actions are produced without generating video; versus Diffusion Policy, diffusion is restricted to small heads and training adds video supervision.
limitations: UVA does not yet exploit large action-free video (web-scale pretraining is future work); it fails when background color matches objects; slightly slower than DP-UMI in real world because attention takes half the inference time; less able to use failure-recovery data due to long history.

keyEquations.meaning: Action diffusion head loss conditioned on the joint video-action latent.

symbols.meaning: noisy action chunk at diffusion step k

keyEquations.meaning: Per-token video diffusion loss; each latent token decodes one image patch.

symbols.meaning: i-th noisy visual token of the future frame

keyEquations.meaning: Total loss, summed over the h-step horizon; terms applied selectively per masked task.

algorithmSteps: Encode history frames with VAE+FC into N tokens each; repeat and project each history action chunk into N tokens.
Concatenate with future-frame tokens (randomly masked in training; fully masked/empty at inference) and temporally stack across h steps.
Transformer fuses into joint latents Z (language via cross-attention if present).
Training: randomly choose one of five input/output masking configurations (policy, video model, forward dynamics, inverse dynamics, policy+planner) and apply L_action and/or L_video.
Policy inference: skip the video head; run only the action diffusion head (16 steps real / 100 steps sim) to get a 16-step chunk; execute 8.
Video generation: run the video head autoregressively over masked tokens for 1 or more steps (8 steps improves quality).
ablations: UVA-action (no video generation/supervision) drops to 0.45 PushT, 0.62 ToolHang, 0.46 PushT-M, 0.86 Libero10 vs full UVA 0.98/0.88/0.88/0.90.
Visual disturbances on PushT: UVA 0.35 BgColor, 0.31 BgObject, 0.64 GoalColor vs DP-C 0.12/0.21/0.17.
As a forward-dynamics model guiding DP-C in block pushing, success rises from 38% to 60%.
hyperparams: 16 action steps inferred / 8 executed; 100 action denoising steps in sim, 16 in real world; MAR-B diffusion heads (base size); h = h' (history = future horizon); video FVD on Libero10 51.10 with 8 autoregressive steps vs UniPi 56.55.
notes: Uses only third-person images on Libero10 and no external data, yet beats pi0 (3.3B) and pi0-FAST (3.0B) that were fine-tuned from pretrained checkpoints on the entire Libero dataset. Venue: RSS 2025 (general knowledge, not verified). Code released per paper ('check out our code'); weights not confirmed.

name: UWM
resolvedTitle: Unified World Models: Coupling Video and Action Diffusion for Pretraining on Large Robotic Datasets
org: University of Washington, Toyota Research Institute
problem: Imitation learning needs expensive action-labeled demos and does not capture temporal dynamics, while world models trained on video are hard to turn into controllers; joint video-action diffusion with a shared timestep (PAD) limits flexible inference.
keyIdea: One diffusion transformer jointly denoises actions and future observations with independent diffusion timesteps per modality; setting a timestep to T marginalizes that modality and to 0 conditions on it, so the same model is a policy, forward dynamics, inverse dynamics and video predictor, and can co-train on action-free video by fixing the action timestep to T.
architecture: Diffusion Transformer with AdaLN conditioning on ResNet-18 features of current observations and sinusoidal embeddings of both timesteps; token sequence = MLP-embedded noisy action chunk + patchified SDXL-VAE latents of noisy future frames (spatiotemporal patch 4x4x2) + 8 register tokens; shallow MLP decoders for action and image noise.
inputs: Current multi-view RGB frames (2-frame stack, 224x224), noisy action chunk, noisy future-frame latents, two diffusion timesteps
outputs: Noise predictions for actions and future observations -> action chunk and/or future frames
actionRepr: chunk of 16 continuous delta-EE + gripper actions via DDPM-trained / DDIM-sampled diffusion (10 inference steps), 8 executed
params: Not stated (DiT with embed dim 768, depth 12, 12 heads)
trainingData: Real: 2,000-trajectory DROID subset for pretraining + another 2,000 DROID trajectories with actions removed for video co-training; 50-150 teleop demos per downstream task. Sim: LIBERO-90 pretraining, LIBERO-10 fine-tuning. Internet-video ablation: Kinetics-400 + Something-Something-v2.

headlineResults.benchmark: LIBERO-10 subset under distribution shift (5 tasks)

whatChangedVsParent: PAD jointly diffuses actions and future frames with one shared timestep and raw-pixel concatenation; UWM decouples the two timesteps (enabling marginal/conditional inference and video co-training) and conditions via encoder features + AdaLN with register tokens.
limitations: Does not yet learn from large-scale human videos across the embodiment gap; forward-dynamics predictions often contain artifacts that may hurt planning; denser video prediction is left for future work.
