name: Visual Dexterity
resolvedTitle: Visual Dexterity: In-Hand Reorientation of Novel and Complex Object Shapes
org: MIT (Improbable AI Lab, CSAIL), Tsinghua University, Meta AI
problem: Prior in-hand reorientation systems assumed simple or specific objects, limited rotation range, quasi-static motion, simulation-only results, costly sensor suites, or an upward-facing hand, making them unsuitable for real deployment and tool use.
keyIdea: Train a privileged-state RL teacher across 150 objects in Isaac Gym, then distill it into a point-cloud student via DAgger in two stages (fast synthetic complete point clouds, then rendered occluded ones), and deploy zero-shot with a single depth camera on a low-cost downward-facing D'Claw hand.
architecture: Teacher: MLP (512-256-256, ELU) trained with PPO on privileged state. Student: sparse 3D CNN (Minkowski Engine; residual blocks, channels 64-128-256) on a merged exteroceptive depth + proprioceptive point cloud with the goal-orientation object point cloud stacked in, followed by a GRU; auxiliary head predicts rotation distance to goal for stopping.
inputs: Single Intel RealSense D415 depth point cloud + proprioceptive point cloud from joint encoders (forward kinematics on cached link points) + goal as object point cloud in target orientation
outputs: Relative joint position changes for 3- or 4-finger D'Claw (3 joints per finger)
actionRepr: Continuous relative joint position deltas a_t in R^{3G}, EMA-smoothed (alpha=0.8), q_tgt = q_t + a_bar_t, at 12 Hz
trainingData: Simulation only (Isaac Gym): 150 training objects ('Big' dataset from internet sources), 12 ContactDB objects ('Small' dataset) for evaluation; teacher 32000 envs

headlineResults.benchmark: Real 3-finger, table support, rigid fingertips, 7 train objects
Real 3-finger, table support, rigid fingertips, 5 OOD objects

parents: A System for General In-Hand Object Reorientation (Chen, Xu, Agrawal 2021)
whatChangedVsParent: Extends the prior simulation-only, per-object visual teacher-student reorientation to a single cross-object point-cloud policy trained in two stages and transferred zero-shot to a real downward-facing hand with one depth camera.
limitations: Precision and drop rate need improvement; 12 Hz feedback may be too slow to catch slips, and the policy lacks explicit contact/force/slip information (touch sensing suggested); the rotation-distance predictor used for stopping is inaccurate below ~0.4 rad.
notes: Hardware under $5,000, open-source D'Claw with custom soft elastomer fingertips; system identification of joint stiffness/damping/velocity limits via CMA-ES in parallel Isaac Gym. In-air reorientation emerges only with the 4-finger hand and a table-contact penalty: with penalty 87% in-air success vs 4.1% without. CONFLICT (internal): the paper says the two-stage pipeline makes training '5x' faster on p.5 but calls stage 1 a '7x speedup' on p.31; full single-stage vision training took 20+ days on a V100, total training < 400 h on one V100. Summary report's '79% in-distribution with soft fingertips' could not be verified in the extracted page text, so the 81% rigid-fingertip figure is used. Code and data released per acknowledgments. Published in Science Robotics 2023.

keyEquations.tex: r_{1t} = c_1 \mathbb{1}(\text{success}) + c_2 \frac{1}{|\Delta\theta_t| + \epsilon_\theta} + c_3 \sum_{i=1}^{G} \|p_t^{f_i} - p_t^{o}\|_2^2 + c_4 |\dot{q}_t|^T |\tau_t| + c_5 \mathbb{1}(\|p_t^o\|_2^2 > \bar{p})
keyEquations.meaning: Teacher reward: sparse success, dense orientation, fingertip proximity, energy, push-away penalty.

keyEquations.tex: r_{2t} = r_{1t} + c_6 \mathbb{1}(\text{object contacts table}) + c_7 \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathbb{1}(p_{t,z}^{f_i} > \bar{p}_z)
keyEquations.meaning: In-air reward adds table-contact and penultimate-joint penalties.
EMA-smoothed relative joint targets (alpha=0.8).

algorithmSteps: System-identify D'Claw joint dynamics with CMA-ES in parallel Isaac Gym
Train teacher with PPO on 150 objects using privileged state, domain randomization, disturbance forces and shaped reward (plus table-contact penalty for in-air)
Stage 1: DAgger student on synthetic complete point clouds sampled from meshes (no rendering)
Stage 2: finetune student with rendered, occluded, noise-injected depth point clouds
Deploy zero-shot: depth + proprioceptive point cloud -> sparse CNN + GRU -> EMA actions at 12 Hz
Stop when predicted rotation distance below threshold and action norm small
ablations: Table-contact penalty: 87% in-air success vs 4.1% without
Two-stage student: stage 1 under 3 days vs 20+ days for rendered-only training on a V100
Soft vs rigid fingertips on OOD objects: 55% vs 45% success at 0.4 rad (from report; 45% confirmed in paper text)
hyperparams: Teacher: 32000 envs, batch 64000, 8 rollout steps, 12 epochs, GAE 0.95, discount 0.99, actor lr 3e-4, critic lr 1e-3, PPO clip 0.1; reward c1=800, c2=1, c3=-1, c4=-20, c5=-100, c6=-1, c7=-2, eps_theta=0.4 rad. Student: 400/260 envs (stage 1/2), 500 pts per CAD model, 6000 rendered pts, voxel 0.005 m, lr 3e-4. EMA alpha=0.8; 12 Hz; P gain 200, D gain 10

name: In-hand object rotation (Qi et al.)
resolvedTitle: In-Hand Object Rotation via Rapid Motor Adaptation
org: UC Berkeley; Meta AI
problem: Generalizable in-hand manipulation with multi-fingered hands remains unsolved; domain-randomized sim-to-real policies are robust but conservative and do not adapt to objects of different shape, size and mass.
keyIdea: Extend Rapid Motor Adaptation (RMA) to fingertip in-hand z-axis rotation: train a base policy conditioned on an 8-dim 'extrinsics' embedding of privileged object properties, then train an adaptation module to estimate that embedding online from proprioception/action history only.
architecture: Base policy: 4-layer MLP [512,256,128,16] (ELU) on 3-step joint/action history (96-d) plus 8-d extrinsics. Extrinsics encoder mu: 3-layer MLP [256,128,8] on 9-d privileged vector (position, size, mass, friction, CoM). Adaptation module phi: per-step 2-layer MLP (32-d) then three 1-D temporal convs over 30 steps, then linear to z-hat.
inputs: Allegro Hand joint positions q_{t-2:t} and previous actions a_{t-3:t-1} (proprioception only; no vision or touch); 30-step proprioception+action history for the adaptation module.
outputs: 16-dim PD-controller joint position targets.
actionRepr: single-step 16-DoF absolute joint position targets at 20 Hz, converted to torque by PD (Kp=3.0, Kd=0.1) at 300 Hz
trainingData: Pure sim RL in IsaacGym, 16,384 parallel envs, trained only on cylinders of varied aspect ratio with randomized mass/CoM/friction/scale/PD gains and external disturbances; ~500M agent steps per paper summary (few hours).
whatChangedVsParent: Moves RMA from legged locomotion (terrain extrinsics) to dexterous in-hand rotation, estimating object properties instead of terrain from proprioceptive history.
limitations: Only single-axis (z) fingertip rotation (multi-axis is preliminary and needs ~1.5x training); proprioception alone struggles with small objects, cubes, and objects needing precise contact placement, where failures come from incorrect contact positions.
notes: Commonly called HORA (project site haozhi.io/hora). Code released per paper ('Code and more videos are available'). Follow-up by same first author: RotateIt (General In-Hand Object Rotation with Vision and Touch, CoRL 2023) — if a survey cites 'Qi et al.' with vision+touch, it may mean RotateIt instead. Rotation reward clipped to [-0.5, 0.5]; no finger-gaiting heuristics — gaits emerge from pose/energy penalties.

keyEquations.tex: r \doteq r_{rot} + \lambda_{pose} r_{pose} + \lambda_{linvel} r_{linvel} + \lambda_{work} r_{work} + \lambda_{torque} r_{torque}
keyEquations.meaning: Composite PPO reward: clipped rotation reward plus pose, velocity, energy and torque penalties.

symbols.meaning: \max(\min(\omega\cdot\hat{k}, r_{max}), r_{min}), clipped angular velocity about z

keyEquations.meaning: Base policy conditioned on 8-d extrinsics encoded from privileged object properties.
Adaptation module regresses extrinsics from proprioception/action history.

algorithmSteps: Stage 1: train base policy pi and encoder mu jointly with PPO in IsaacGym using privileged object properties on randomized cylinders.
Freeze pi and mu.
Stage 2: roll out pi with predicted z-hat from phi, store ground-truth z_t; train phi with L2 loss iteratively until convergence.
Deploy: every 20 Hz step, phi estimates z-hat from last 30 steps of joint positions and actions.
pi outputs 16 joint targets from current proprio + z-hat; PD tracks at 300 Hz.
ablations: No physical randomization: in-distribution RotR 171.96 vs 222.27, OOD RotR 88.02 vs 160.60.
Proprioceptive history length: T=10/20/30 give OOD RotR 150.58/157.22/160.60 (saturates at 30).
Explicit SysID (regressing exact parameters) is worse than 8-d extrinsics: real heavy-object TTF 0.61 vs 0.98; NoAdapt (frozen z-hat) fails in real world.
hyperparams: Extrinsics dim 8; privileged vector 9-d; history 30 steps (1.5 s); control 20 Hz, sim 120 Hz; episode 400 steps (20 s); 16,384 envs; rotation reward clip [-0.5,0.5]; lambda_pose=-0.3, lambda_torque=-0.1, lambda_work=-2.0, lambda_linvel=-0.3 (signs as printed in paper).

name: HATO
resolvedTitle: Learning Visuotactile Skills with Two Multifingered Hands
org: UC Berkeley
problem: Bimanual imitation learning mostly uses parallel-jaw grippers because there was no affordable teleoperation system for two arms with multifingered hands and few multifingered hands with touch sensing.
keyIdea: HATO: a low-cost VR (Meta Quest 2) hands-arms teleoperation system with simplified hand mappings, on repurposed Psyonic Ability prosthetic hands with fingertip touch sensors, used to collect visuotactile demos for a Diffusion Policy.
architecture: Diffusion Policy (CNN-based DDPM) conditioned on concatenated features: per-camera ResNet-18 (GroupNorm, 32-d out, unshared) for RGB/depth from 2 wrist + 1 third-view cameras; 2-layer ReLU MLPs (hidden 256, out 64) for end-effector proprioception and touch.
inputs: RGB (and optionally depth) from three RealSense cameras (240x320), end-effector poses of both UR5e arms, 60 touch readings total (6 sensors per fingertip x 5 fingers x 2 hands); observation horizon 1.
outputs: Sequence of 24-dim actions: 6 absolute joint positions per UR5e arm + 6 normalized joint positions per Ability hand.
actionRepr: chunk of 16 x 24-DoF absolute joint-position actions via DDPM (100 train / 15 inference steps), temporally ensembled with asynchronous inference
trainingData: Own HATO teleop data: 100 demos each for Slippery Handover and Block Stacking; 300 each for Wine Pouring and Steak Serving (30 min to 2 h per task), recorded at 10 Hz.
whatChangedVsParent: Applies Diffusion Policy to bimanual multifingered hands with added tactile input, a single-step observation, and asynchronous inference with temporal ensembling of action chunks.
limitations: Teleop mapping (grip button for 4-finger power grasp, thumbstick for thumb) sacrifices finger gaiting; no haptic feedback to operator; policies are task-specific and sensitive to appearance changes; depth input is noisy and did not help.
notes: HATO = Hands-Arms Tele-Operation; the paper title does not contain 'HATO'. Authors commit to open-sourcing hardware, software and datasets. Touch: paper says 'sixty touch sensor readings from both hands h in R^60' (6 per fingertip); secondary summaries saying '60 per hand' are wrong. Table I: Handover and Pouring used image+proprio only; Stacking and Serving used image+proprio+touch. Concurrent: Wang et al. (DexCap-style bimanual dexterous) without touch.
algorithmSteps: Teleoperate with Quest 2: controller pose -> EEF pose via IK; grip button -> 4-finger flexion; thumbstick -> 2-DoF thumb.
Record proprio, 3x RGB-D, 60 touch readings and 24-d joint actions at 10 Hz; normalize to [-1,1].
Train DDPM Diffusion Policy (100 steps, cosine schedule) to predict 16 future actions from one observation.
Deploy: local process streams latest observation to remote server each control step.
Server continuously denoises (15 steps) and returns timestamped action chunks.
Local process averages overlapping predictions (temporal ensemble) and executes.
ablations: Steak Serving: full 5/10; w/o touch 0/10 despite similar ActionMSE (0.08 vs 0.07); w/o vision 0/10 (cannot pick up).
Steak Serving camera config: all cams 5/10; +depth 1/10; only wrist 1/10; only 3rd view 0/10.
Data size: ActionMSE saturates at ~75 demos (Stacking), ~100 (Serving), ~200 (Pouring).
hyperparams: Obs horizon 1; action horizon 16; DDPM 100 train steps (square cosine), 15 inference steps; AdamW lr 1e-4, wd 1e-5, batch 128, EMA weights; images 240x320; 24-d action.

name: DeformerNet
resolvedTitle: Learning Visual Shape Control of Novel 3D Deformable Objects from Partial-View Point Clouds
org: University of Utah; NVIDIA
topicName: Deformable, bimanual, mobile and soft manipulation
problem: 3D volumetric deformable shape control relied on hand-crafted features and object-specific models, and no method chose the grasp (manipulation) point conditioned on the goal shape.
keyIdea: Learn a closed-loop shape-servo controller: embed current and goal partial-view point clouds with a shared PointConv encoder, take the feature difference, and regress the end-effector displacement that moves the object toward the goal; pick the manipulation point with a keypoint-displacement heuristic.
architecture: Feature extractor g: three PointConv layers (64x512, 128x256, then 256-d vector) on 1024-point FPS-downsampled clouds, applied to current and goal clouds; deformation controller F: FC layers 128-64-32 then linear 3-d output; ReLU + GroupNorm. Manipulation point from Transporter-style unsupervised 3D keypoints (K=200).
inputs: Partial-view point cloud of current object shape and of goal shape (from depth camera).
outputs: 3-D Cartesian end-effector displacement (delta x, delta y, delta z), executed via resolved-rate control.
actionRepr: single 3-DoF end-effector position delta per step (closed-loop visual servo)
trainingData: Isaac Gym (FEM) with simulated dVRK: per object type 300 initial-config/manipulation-point pairs x 10 goals = 3000 trajectories, sampled into 10,000 (P_t, P_g, delta x) pairs; separate model per each of 9 object types (3 primitives x 3 stiffnesses: 1, 5, 10 kPa).

headlineResults.benchmark: Real Baxter + laparoscopic tool retraction (3 planes x 5 trials)
Sim box shape servo vs baselines
headlineResults.value: Beats model-free RL (PPO+HER with 10x data) at all tolerances; beats RRT at tight tolerances

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces hand-crafted extended-FPFH features with learned PointConv shape embeddings, generalizes across object geometry and stiffness, and adds goal-conditioned manipulation-point selection.
limitations: Greedy visual-servoing approach without explicit long-horizon planning; main failure source is the heuristic manipulation-point predictor choosing an unreachable grasp; single grasp point and one end fixed; slight performance drop on the real robot.
notes: Code and data released at sites.google.com/view/deformernet per paper. Published at ICRA 2022 (arXiv v2 Apr 2022). Chamfer distances in the paper are reported in metres but values (0.18–0.39 m) appear to be in an unnormalized unit; quote carefully. Later extension: DeformerNet for bimanual / 6-DoF (Thach et al., T-RO) may be what some surveys cite.

keyEquations.meaning: Shape-servo policy maps feature difference of current and goal clouds to EE displacement.

symbols.meaning: current and goal partial point clouds

keyEquations.meaning: Chamfer distance used as evaluation metric / goal tolerance.

algorithmSteps: Detect keypoints on initial and goal clouds; match pairs.
Set manipulation point to displacement-weighted average of the keypoints that move most; grasp there.
Observe current partial cloud; FPS-downsample current and goal to 1024 points.
Encode both with PointConv; compute feature difference.
Regress EE displacement; convert to joint velocities with resolved-rate control.
Repeat until Chamfer distance below tolerance.
ablations: Model-free RL (PPO+HER, same architecture, 100,000 samples = 10x data) has significantly lower success than DeformerNet across goal tolerances.
RRT matches success at loose tolerances (both 100% at 0.4) but fails more at tight ones and takes mean 38.7 min per plan.
Primary failure in generalization tests: heuristic manipulation point unable to achieve goal shape.
hyperparams: 1024 input points (FPS); 256-d shape feature; FC 128-64-32-3; MSE loss; Adam lr 1e-3 decayed x0.1 every 50 epochs; K=200 keypoints; Young's modulus 1/5/10 kPa.

name: DexDeform
resolvedTitle: DexDeform: Dexterous Deformable Object Manipulation with Human Demonstrations and Differentiable Physics
org: MIT; UC San Diego; Tsinghua University; Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute; UMass Amherst; MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab
topicName: Deformable, bimanual, mobile and soft manipulation
problem: RL is too sample-inefficient for multi-fingered manipulation of soft bodies, while differentiable-physics trajectory optimization gets stuck in local optima due to the explosion of hand-object contact modes.
keyIdea: Abstract dexterous skills from a few teleoperated human demos into a latent skill model for planning in imagination, then use differentiable physics to refine skill-planned trajectories toward augmented novel goals and feed successes back as new demos.
architecture: ConvONet encoder on point clouds -> 2D feature planes -> VAE latent scene s_t (occupancy decoder). Skill model: skill encoder f over K-step (s,a) sequences -> z; skill dynamics T(s_{t+K}|z_t,s_t); skill action decoder pi(a_t|z_t,s_t). Planning by gradient optimization over latent skill sequences; refinement with PlasticineLab (MLS-MPM) gradients.
inputs: Full point cloud of scene (hands + object, position and color); goal shape point cloud.
outputs: Joint/position targets for simulated Shadow Hand(s) (28 DoF each incl. movable base).
actionRepr: latent skill z decoded into K-step low-level action sequences for 28-DoF Shadow hand(s)
trainingData: 10 teleop demos per task variant (Leap Motion, ~$100 setup) across 6 tasks (Folding has 4 variants): ~60,000 env steps (~2 h), plus self-generated refined trajectories from goal augmentation. Simulation only.
parents: Skill-based latent planning (Shi et al. 2022, SkiMo)
whatChangedVsParent: Combines demo-derived latent skill planning with differentiable-physics refinement to escape local optima, bootstrapping the dataset on augmented goals for multi-fingered soft-body manipulation.
limitations: Assumes full point-cloud observation and runs only in simulation (no real-robot deployment); soft-body simulation speed limits RL-scale learning.
notes: ICLR 2023. Claims first learning-based dexterous deformable manipulation. Metric: normalized decrease in EMD (approximated by Sinkhorn divergence), clipped at 0. Partial point cloud (4 RGBD cams) drops Flip from 0.842 to 0.683.

keyEquations.tex: \arg\min_{z_1, z_K, \dots, z_H} C(g, z) = L_{occ}\big(g, T(z_H, T(z_{H-K}, \dots T(z_1, s_1)))\big)
keyEquations.meaning: Plan latent skill sequence so predicted final scene occupancy matches goal shape.

symbols.meaning: cross-entropy occupancy loss of goal points in decoded scene

keyEquations.meaning: Skill VAE: decoder reconstructs K actions from skill latent; KL regularizes encoder.

keyEquations.tex: L_{Dyn} = \mathbb{E}\Big[\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\big\|T(z_{iK+1}, s_{iK+1}) - s_{(i+1)K+1}\big\|_2^2\Big],\quad L_{skill} = L_{sVAE} + L_{Dyn}
keyEquations.meaning: Skill dynamics predicts latent scene K steps ahead; trained jointly with skill VAE.

algorithmSteps: Collect 10 teleop demos per task variant in PlasticineLab with Leap Motion + IK retargeting.
Train scene representation (ConvONet + VAE) and skill model (f, T, pi) on dataset D.
Sample a goal from D and augment (xz translation, y rotation).
Optimize a batch of Gaussian-initialized skill latent sequences via Eq. 1 through T; pick best.
Decode skills to actions with pi; refine with differentiable-physics gradients.
If final EMD to goal below threshold, add refined trajectory to D.
Repeat training and exploration for N iterations.
ablations: Skill-Only (no differentiable-physics exploration): Folding 0.908, Rope 0.914, Bun 0.820, Dumpling 0.725 vs DexDeform 0.970/0.972/0.874/0.888.
Giving baselines the same latent scene embedding does not close the gap (e.g., BC w/ latent Folding 0.672, PPO w/ latent 0.630).
Partial point cloud (4 RGBD cams) instead of full: Flip 0.683 vs 0.842, Folding 0.954 vs 0.970.
hyperparams: Shadow hand 28 DoF; 50-step samples split into N=5 skill abstractions (K=10 implied); batch of J initial skill sequences from standard Gaussian; refinement within tens of gradient iterations; one new trajectory per original demo per iteration.

name: Deep Whole-Body Control (Fu)
resolvedTitle: Deep Whole-Body Control: Learning a Unified Policy for Manipulation and Locomotion
org: Carnegie Mellon University
topicName: Deformable, bimanual, mobile and soft manipulation
problem: Legged manipulators are usually controlled with decoupled hierarchical arm and leg controllers, which coordinate poorly, propagate errors and produce slow unnatural motion; naive RL on the 19-DoF whole body gets stuck in local minima.
keyIdea: Train a single RL policy for legs and arm together, using Advantage Mixing (per-limb advantage weighting with a curriculum) to ease credit assignment and Regularized Online Adaptation (joint one-phase training of privileged encoder and adaptation module) for sim-to-real.
architecture: MLP policy: input state s_t (75-d) + extrinsics z_t (20-d); shared 128-d layer then two heads of 2x128 layers outputting 12 leg and 6 arm joint targets. Privileged encoder mu (body/EE mass, CoM, friction, arm/leg strength) and adaptation module phi on last 10 steps of state/action history.
inputs: Base, leg and arm joint states, previous action, EE position/orientation command (spherical coords), base velocity command; onboard proprioception history for adaptation.
outputs: Target joint positions for 12 leg joints and 6 arm joints (PD-tracked); gripper open/close not part of policy.
actionRepr: single-step 18-DoF joint-position targets at 50 Hz (12 leg + 6 arm)
trainingData: IsaacGym RL with 5000 envs on fractal-noise rough terrain; 10,000 iterations = 2 billion samples, 200k gradient updates.
whatChangedVsParent: RMA's two-phase teacher-student becomes a single-phase jointly trained regularized encoder/adaptation module (RMA is the lambda=0 special case), applied to a unified leg+arm policy.
limitations: Gripper is scripted, not learned; perception is AprilTag-based and failures come from tag/object mismatch; tasks limited to EE pose/base velocity command following rather than learned task policies.
notes: CoRL 2022. Hardware: Unitree Go1 + 6-DoF Interbotix WidowX 250s, RealSense D435, fully untethered; policy and adaptation run at 50 Hz on Raspberry Pi 4. Often called DeepWBC in later papers (e.g., HOMER cites it as DeepWBC). Real-world failures of baseline MPC+IK from IK singularity and self-collision.

keyEquations.meaning: Advantage Mixing: arm actions credited mainly by manipulation advantage, legs by locomotion, mixed via curriculum.

symbols.meaning: advantages from manipulation and locomotion rewards

keyEquations.meaning: Regularized Online Adaptation: privileged latent regularized toward adaptation estimate, which imitates it online.

algorithmSteps: Sample EE (spherical) and base velocity commands; roll out in 5000 IsaacGym envs.
Every H=20 iterations roll out with z_phi and update phi toward sg[z_mu]; otherwise roll out with z_mu.
Update pi and mu with PPO on the advantage-mixing objective plus lambda-regularization toward sg[z_phi].
Anneal beta (advantage mixing) and lambda (regularization) linearly from 0 to 1.
Deploy pi + phi onboard at 50 Hz with commands from joystick, AprilTag visual servoing or demo replay.
ablations: Without Advantage Mixing the policy stays in a local minimum following only EE commands; velocity error stays high.
Regularized Online Adaptation vs RMA: realizability gap 2e-4 vs 0.31, EE error 0.21 vs 0.26 (~20% reduction), survival 97.4 vs 95.2.
Adding regularization to the expert costs almost nothing: survival 97.8 vs 98.3, EE error 0.21 both.
hyperparams: Control 50 Hz, sim 200 Hz; leg Kp 50/Kd 1, arm Kp 5/Kd 0.5; extrinsics 20-d; state 75-d; history 10 steps; H=20; lambda = clip((itr-5000)/5000, 0, 1); PPO lr 2e-4, gamma 0.99, GAE 0.95, clip 0.2, 5000 envs x 40 steps per batch.

name: HOMER
resolvedTitle: HoMeR: Learning In-the-Wild Mobile Manipulation via Hybrid Imitation and Whole-Body Control
org: Stanford University; University of Cambridge
topicName: Deformable, bimanual, mobile and soft manipulation
problem: Mobile manipulation policies must coordinate base and arm and mix long-range reaching with fine manipulation; dense policies struggle with long horizons and spatial generalization, while hybrid keypose/dense methods were limited to tabletop arms.
keyIdea: Delegate base-arm coordination to a fast kinematic whole-body IK controller operating in end-effector space, and learn a hybrid imitation policy (extending SPHINX) that switches between absolute keypose predictions from point clouds and dense delta actions from images.
architecture: Keypose sub-policy: SPHINX-style point-cloud Transformer (6 layers, 512-d, 8 heads) predicting per-point saliency + offsets, with learnable tokens for rotation, gripper and next mode; optional VLM (MolMo 7B-D) keypoint conditioning (HoMeR-Cond). Dense sub-policy: Diffusion Policy on third-person + wrist RGB. WBC: MuJoCo + mink QP IK.
inputs: Third-person point cloud (keypose mode); third-person and wrist RGB + EE pose (dense mode); optional VLM 3D keypoint.
outputs: 6-DoF EE target pose (absolute keypose or relative delta), gripper state, next control mode {keypose, dense, terminate}; WBC converts to base (x,y,theta) + 7-DoF arm joint commands.
actionRepr: hybrid: absolute 6-DoF EE keypose (interpolated) or diffusion chunk of 16 relative 6-DoF EE deltas (execute 8) + 1-DoF gripper, mapped by IK whole-body controller
trainingData: 20 teleoperated demos per task (iPhone WebXR whole-body teleop on TidyBot++, recorded at 10 Hz), post-hoc annotated with salient points and modes (~15 min per 20 demos).

headlineResults.comparedTo: next best HoMeR (B+A) by 29.17% on average

whatChangedVsParent: Extends SPHINX's tabletop hybrid keypose/dense policy to mobile manipulation by acting in a whole-body EE action space via an IK controller, with optional VLM keypoint conditioning.
limitations: WBC ignores collisions with the external environment; fixed hand-chosen camera viewpoints (no active perception); no navigation; single-task policies only.
notes: Robot: TidyBot++ (holonomic base + 7-DoF Kinova arm). Fig. 4 per-task counts read from bar-chart labels in order DP(B+A), DP(WBC), HoMeR(B+A), HoMeR; sum of HoMeR = 95/120 = 79.17% and HoMeR(B+A) = 60/120 = 50%, consistent with the abstract. Dishwasher 13/20, Pillow 16/20 for HoMeR. Generalization (Fig. 5) numbers not extracted. Paper title stylized HoMeR; code at homer-manip.github.io.

keyEquations.tex: \min_{\dot q}\ \|J_{ee}(q_t)\dot q - e_{ee}\|^2_{W_{ee}} + \|q_t + \dot q\,\Delta t - q_{retract}\|^2_{W_{posture}} + \|\dot q_{base}\|^2_{W_{damping}}
keyEquations.meaning: Whole-body IK QP: track EE twist, stay near tucked posture, damp base motion; subject to velocity, position, collision limits.
Mode-switching execution: each sub-policy predicts the next action and the next mode.

algorithmSteps: Start in keypose mode.
Keypose mode: predict per-point saliency and offsets on point cloud; target position = highest-saliency point + offset; add predicted rotation, gripper and next mode.
Interpolate from current EE pose to keypose, each step solved by the WBC.
Dense mode: Diffusion Policy predicts 16 relative EE deltas from RGB + EE pose, executes 8, plus next mode.
WBC solves QP IK (up to 20 iterations) to get base+arm joint commands.
Switch sub-policy according to predicted mode until 'terminate'.
ablations: Hybrid actions without WBC (HoMeR B+A) is the strongest baseline (60/120 = 50%) but fails when smooth base-arm coordination is needed (Cabinet, Dishwasher, Sweep Trash).
WBC without hybrid actions (DP WBC) only slightly beats DP (B+A) overall; dense deltas veer off course when reaching.
Without VLM conditioning or point-cloud augmentations, performance drops with distractors and novel cube colors (HoMeR-Cond keeps high success; exact numbers in Fig. 5 not extracted).
hyperparams: 20 demos/task; dense horizon 16, execute 8; keypose Transformer 6 layers, 512-d, 8 heads, 2000 epochs Adam; temporal augmentation alpha=0.2; spatial aug 5 cm; WBC weights W_ee=1.0, W_posture=2e-3, W_damping=1.5; base vel cap (0.5,0.5,pi/2); QP LM damping 1.0, <=20 iterations, tol 1e-4.

name: MoManipVLA
resolvedTitle: MoManipVLA: Transferring Vision-language-action Models for General Mobile Manipulation
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications; Nanyang Technological University; Tsinghua University
topicName: Deformable, bimanual, mobile and soft manipulation
problem: VLA models generalize well but are built for fixed-base arms, while mobile manipulation methods lack large-scale data and generalize poorly; nothing produced coordinated base-arm motion from VLA outputs.
keyIdea: Use a fine-tuned fixed-base VLA (OpenVLA-7B) to predict end-effector waypoints, then generate physically feasible base and arm trajectories between waypoints by bi-level optimization of reachability, smoothness and collision costs.
architecture: OpenVLA-7B (LoRA fine-tuned) as waypoint generator; trajectory optimizer with Dual Annealing global search + SLSQP local refinement; upper level searches base poses, lower level searches arm/EE poses; Pinocchio IK; nvblox ESDF for collision.
inputs: RGB (and depth for ESDF) observations, camera/base poses, EE proprioception, language instruction.
outputs: Base poses (translation+rotation) and arm joint trajectories reaching VLA-predicted EE waypoints; 10-DoF search space (7 arm + 3 base).
actionRepr: VLA EE waypoint deltas [delta x, delta theta, delta G] converted to whole-body trajectories by optimization
trainingData: 200 pick-and-place expert episodes from OVMM heuristic baseline for sim fine-tuning (LoRA, 10K epochs, 4x RTX 3090); 50 samples for real-world fine-tuning.

headlineResults.benchmark: Real: Put in Bowl / Stack Block / Open Drawer (10 trials each)

whatChangedVsParent: Keeps a fixed-base VLA as waypoint predictor and adds a ReKep-inspired whole-body trajectory optimization so the base repositions zero-shot to make VLA waypoints reachable.
limitations: Bounded by the VLA's performance and deployable only in highly constrained movement spaces; cannot handle long-horizon tasks without a task-planning module.
notes: CVPR 2025. Only generates base/arm trajectories at the end of the navigation phase (OVMM Nav and Gaze use baseline modules). Real platform: Hexman Echo Plus base + RM65 arm, RealSense T265 for pose, Grounding SAM masks. Abstract's '4.2% higher success rate' = 15.8% vs 11.6% overall SR. Failure analysis: 72.09% of failures are 'Orient to place'. Real-world latency ~580-592 ms. Using Detic-style predicted masks instead of GT drops overall SR to 1.7%.

keyEquations.meaning: Plan base/EE trajectory between consecutive VLA waypoints minimizing feasibility cost.

symbols.meaning: i-th VLA waypoint in world frame
base pose (world) and EE pose (base frame)

keyEquations.meaning: Total cost: reachability (IK iterations), smoothness, collision (ESDF margin).

symbols.meaning: N_{IK}/N_{max}, or large C_0 if unreachable

keyEquations.tex: J_{up} = \sum_{x_e\in M} O(x^j_b, x_e) + \alpha\sum_{x_e\in N} O(x^j_b, x_e)
keyEquations.meaning: Upper level scores a base pose by expected and top-k arm-candidate costs.

algorithmSteps: VLA predicts next EE waypoint Q_i from RGB, proprioception and instruction.
Transform to world frame; initialize trajectory by linear interpolation (step size 0.05).
Upper level: Dual Annealing updates base poses, scoring each by sampled arm candidates (J_up).
Lower level: search EE/arm poses minimizing O given base poses.
Solve arm joints with Pinocchio IK; repeat until EE within tolerance of Q_i.
Execute and query VLA for the next waypoint.
ablations: Remove reachability cost: overall SR 13.1% vs 15.8% (largest drop); smoothness 13.8%; collision 15.3%.
Direct (non-bi-level) Dual Annealing: SR 14.1% and latency 742.9 vs bi-level 15.8% and 693.1.
Predicted instance masks instead of ground truth: overall SR 1.7%.
hyperparams: lambda1=10.0, lambda2=1.0, lambda3=0.6; safety margin eps0=0.1; interpolation step 0.05; Dual Annealing + SLSQP; OpenVLA-7B LoRA, 200 sim demos / 50 real samples.

name: χ0
resolvedTitle: χ0: Resource-Aware Robust Manipulation via Taming Distributional Inconsistencies
org: Kinetix AI (with HKU / OpenDriveLab / MMLab authors)
authorsShort: Yu et al. (alphabetical; leads Chonghao Sima, Li Chen)
topicName: Deformable, bimanual, mobile and soft manipulation
problem: Long-horizon garment manipulation fails not mainly from lack of scale but from mismatches among the demonstration distribution (P_train), the policy's learned bias (Q_model) and the executed trajectory distribution (P_test), which compound over multi-stage tasks.
keyIdea: A post-training recipe on top of π0.5 with three modules: Model Arithmetic (weight-space merging of checkpoints trained on data subsets, weights tuned on OOD DAgger validation data), Stage Advantage (a stage-conditioned pairwise advantage estimator for advantage-weighted BC), and Train-Deploy Alignment (heuristic DAgger, spatio-temporal augmentation, temporal chunk-wise smoothing).
architecture: Full-parameter fine-tuned π0.5 (PaliGemma VLM + flow-matching action expert) as the policy; a VLM-based advantage estimator takes pairs of images plus a stage label and predicts relative progress; an inference-side chunk buffer blends consecutive action chunks.
inputs: Three RGB views (one head, two wrist; RealSense D435i 640×480 at 30 Hz), proprioception, language/task; stage label for the advantage estimator
outputs: Action chunks of joint commands for two 6-DoF arms + 1-DoF grippers per bimanual station
actionRepr: chunk of K=50 joint actions via flow matching (π0.5), executed at 100 Hz with temporal chunk-wise smoothing; absolute joint control (delta joint also ablated)
trainingData: ~20 h expert demonstrations per task (2668 episodes Task A, 3519 Task B, 2988 Task C, incl. DAgger), collected at 30 Hz on Agilex Piper and ARX X5 dual-arm (ALOHA-style) stations; trained on 8×A100, 80k steps, batch 128
controlRateHz: 100 (execution frequency); low-level joint controllers 100–200 Hz; vision 30 Hz

headlineResults.value: 24 consecutive hours from arbitrary initial state

whatChangedVsParent: Instead of π*0.6-style value-difference advantages, χ0 predicts advantage directly and stage-conditioned, and adds weight-space merging plus deployment-side chunk smoothing on top of a fine-tuned π0.5.
limitations: Does not evaluate retention of pre-trained priors after post-training or extension to rigid-body tasks; unclear whether Model Arithmetic can merge distinct task policies; data-quality validation still needs costly training loops or replay checks.
notes: Code at github.com/OpenDriveLab/kai0; paper states code, data and model weights will be released (openWeights=true per stated release; verify). Name 'χ0' from 'KAI 0' = Kinetics Aligned to Intelligence. Other VLAs (GO-1, X-VLA, DexVLA, UniVLA, OpenVLA) reportedly achieved negligible success after fine-tuning on these tasks. Task definitions: A = T-shirt flatten+fold (180 s), B = conditional retrieval/sorting of T-shirt vs collared shirt, C = shirt hanging (from GR-3). MA uses 4 checkpoints. Exact per-task SR numbers are in bar-chart figures only, not tabulated.

keyEquations.meaning: Model Arithmetic: merge subset-trained checkpoints; α optimized on held-out (OOD DAgger) validation loss.

symbols.meaning: weights of policy trained on subset D_i

keyEquations.tex: A_{\text{stage}}(s, a, g) = f_\theta(s, s' \mid g)
keyEquations.meaning: Stage Advantage: directly predicts relative progress from s to s'=s_{t+Δ} within stage g.

symbols.meaning: state after random time span Δ

keyEquations.meaning: Binary optimality indicator used for advantage-weighted behavior cloning.

keyEquations.tex: \tilde a_i \leftarrow w_i a^{old}_i + (1-w_i) a^{new}_{rem,i},\quad w_i = 1 - i/\max(L-1,1)
keyEquations.meaning: Temporal chunk-wise smoothing: linearly cross-fade old buffer into new chunk over overlap L.

symbols.meaning: new chunk after dropping d stale steps

algorithmSteps: Collect ~20 h demos per task; add heuristic-DAgger recovery demos started from hand-designed failure states and flip/frame-skip augmentations.
Randomly split data into n subsets and fine-tune π0.5 on each (flow matching).
Merge checkpoints in weight space; choose α by minimizing loss on OOD DAgger validation set (greedy search best).
Train stage-conditioned pairwise advantage estimator on frame pairs from same episode.
Threshold advantages (ε=0.3) and train with advantage-weighted behavior cloning.
Deploy with asynchronous inference; drop stale actions (≤ d_max) and cross-fade new chunk into buffer.
ablations: All Model Arithmetic variants beat both the single-best subset checkpoint and the full-data (joint-trained) checkpoint; OOD (DAgger) validation is more robust than in-domain.
Stage Advantage gives more stable advantage signals (Smooth Frame Ratio, MSTD) than π*0.6-style value difference and reduces retry cost on Task B.
Temporal chunk-wise smoothing outperforms temporal ensembling and RTC in most settings; combining with RTC helps further; spatio-temporal augmentation gives no significant gain on Task A.
hyperparams: Chunk K=50; execution 100 Hz; 80k steps, batch 128, AdamW lr 2.5e-5; MA 4 checkpoints; SA ε=0.3; stages: 2 (A), 4 (B), 3 (C); RECAP baseline uses 50-step horizon.

name: H2O / OmniH2O
resolvedTitle: Learning Human-to-Humanoid Real-Time Whole-Body Teleoperation (H2O); OmniH2O: Universal and Dexterous Human-to-Humanoid Whole-Body Teleoperation and Learning
org: Carnegie Mellon University (OmniH2O also Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
problem: Real-time whole-body teleoperation of a full-size humanoid lacked a large feasible motion dataset and an RL tracker deployable with only real-world-available inputs; H2O still needed MoCap for velocity and lacked manipulation precision, which OmniH2O fixes.
keyIdea: Retarget AMASS to the humanoid, filter infeasible clips with a privileged imitator ('sim-to-data'), and train a goal-conditioned RL motion tracker with domain randomization; OmniH2O distills a privileged teacher into a history-based student that tracks only head+hand (3-point) kinematic goals, making kinematic pose a universal interface for VR, RGB, language (MDM), GPT-4o or learned policies.
architecture: H2O: MLP PPO policy on Unitree H1 (19 DoF) with proprioception + 8 keypoint goals, 200 Hz PD. OmniH2O: privileged RL teacher (913-d state) distilled via DAgger into an MLP student [512,256,128] with 25-step proprioceptive history (1665-d input) and 3-point goals; hands via IK to an off-the-shelf controller; Diffusion Policy on top for autonomy.
inputs: H2O: RGB-camera pose (HybrIK) → 8 keypoints + proprioception + MoCap root velocity. OmniH2O: head/hand 3D positions from VR (or RGB/MDM/GPT-4o) + 25-step proprioceptive history (no linear velocity)
outputs: 19-D joint target positions for PD control (plus hand joint targets via IK in OmniH2O)
actionRepr: single-step 19-D joint position targets at 50 Hz (tracker); OmniH2O LfD uses Diffusion Policy over motion goals
trainingData: AMASS (~40 h mocap): 13k sequences → 10k retargeted → ~8.5k feasible after sim-to-data (H2O); OmniH2O evaluates on 14k augmented sequences with standing/squatting variants; OmniH2O-6 teleop dataset (6 tasks, RGBD at 30 Hz)
whatChangedVsParent: Moves physics-based avatar motion imitation (PHC/PULSE) to a real humanoid via feasibility filtering, deployable state design and sim-to-real randomization; OmniH2O adds teacher-student DAgger distillation with history to drop MoCap velocity and track sparse VR inputs.
limitations: H2O: representation, embodiment and sim-to-real gaps; RGB pose-estimation latency/error; visual-only feedback to operator; required MoCap for linear velocity. OmniH2O (per summary): reliance on odometry for root tracking in some setups, difficulty on complex terrain like stairs.
notes: Merged card for two papers. OmniH2O arXiv 2406.08858 (CoRL 2024), url https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08858; H2O arXiv 2403.04436 (IROS 2024). OmniH2O releases the OmniH2O-6 dataset (claimed first humanoid whole-body loco-manipulation dataset). OmniH2O key reward addition: 'max feet height for each step' with curriculum; motion data biased toward standing/squatting.

keyEquations.meaning: Goal-conditioned RL objective: track motion goal from proprioception, optimized with PPO.
PD controller converts 19-D joint targets to torques.
OmniH2O DAgger distillation loss from privileged teacher to deployable student.

keyEquations.tex: s^{g\text{-real}}_t \triangleq (\tilde p^{real}_t - p^{real}_t,\ \tilde v^{real}_t - v^{real}_t,\ \tilde p^{real}_t)
keyEquations.meaning: OmniH2O student goal: 3-point (head, hands) position/velocity differences and targets.

algorithmSteps: Fit SMPL shape β' to H1 on 12 corresponding joints; retarget AMASS via IK position matching.
Train privileged imitator on all retargeted motions; drop clips it fails to track.
Train deployable tracker with PPO + domain randomization (H2O) or privileged teacher then DAgger student with 25-step history (OmniH2O).
At runtime estimate human pose (HybrIK RGB or VR headset) → keypoint goals.
Policy outputs 19-D joint targets at 50 Hz; PD at 200 Hz.
Optionally record teleop data and train Diffusion Policy to generate goals autonomously.
ablations: Sim-to-data filtering: 72.5% vs 67.9% success without it; richer goal state vs reduced: 72.5% vs 53.2% (H2O).
OmniH2O without DAgger (RL with 25-step history) collapses to 47.11% success vs 94.10% with DAgger.
3-point tracking (94.10%) is close to 22-point (94.72%); 25-step history best in real world (g-MPJPE 47.94 vs 83.26 with no history).
hyperparams: H2O: 8 keypoints, early termination at 0.5 m deviation, control delay 20–60 ms randomized; OmniH2O: 25-step history, MLP [512,256,128], PPO lr 1e-3, batch 64, γ 0.99, 3 keypoints (head+hands).

name: HumanPlus
resolvedTitle: HumanPlus: Humanoid Shadowing and Imitation from Humans
org: Stanford University
problem: Humanoids could not easily leverage human data because of perception/control complexity, human-robot morphology gaps, and the lack of a pipeline to learn autonomous skills from egocentric vision.
keyIdea: Train a task-agnostic low-level Humanoid Shadowing Transformer with RL on 40 h of AMASS, use it for single-RGB-camera real-time whole-body shadowing to collect data, then train a Humanoid Imitation Transformer (HIT) on binocular egocentric images with forward-dynamics feature prediction.
architecture: Two decoder-only transformers: HST (low-level, PPO in sim, context 8) maps proprioception + target pose to 19-D joint setpoints; HIT (ACT without encoder) uses ResNet features from two egocentric cameras + proprioception and predicts a 50-step chunk of target poses plus future image-feature tokens.
inputs: HST: root roll/pitch/angular velocity, joint pos/vel, last action, target pose (velocities, roll/pitch, yaw rate, joint angles). HIT: binocular egocentric RGB + proprioception
outputs: HST: 19-D body joint position setpoints (hands passed directly to PD). HIT: target body and hand poses
actionRepr: HIT: chunk of 50 target poses (fed asynchronously to HST); HST: single-step 19-D joint setpoints
trainingData: AMASS 40 h human motion (retargeted) for HST in simulation; 25–40 real shadowing demos per task for HIT
controlRateHz: HST 50; PD 1000; HIT 25; body pose estimation 25 fps, hand 10 fps

headlineResults.benchmark: Wear a Shoe and Walk (40 demos)

whatChangedVsParent: HIT removes ACT's encoder-decoder into a decoder-only transformer with binocular input and an L2 future-image-feature loss to stop overfitting to proprioception.
limitations: Hardware has fewer DoF than humans (1-DoF ankles, 5-DoF arms), fixed head cameras let hands leave view, fixed retargeting drops human joints, pose estimation fails under occlusion, and long-horizon navigation not addressed.
notes: Custom robot built on Unitree H1 with Inspire hands: 33 DoF total, 180 cm, two egocentric RGB cameras. HIT loss form 'L_action + λ L_feature' comes from the alphaXiv summary; paper text describes an L2 feature loss on predicted image features. Shadowing also demonstrated boxing, piano, table tennis, cabinet storage.

keyEquations.meaning: HST trained with PPO to maximize discounted return of pose-tracking rewards.

symbols.meaning: sum of velocity, joint, roll/pitch, energy, contact, slip, alive terms

keyEquations.meaning: Behavior-cloning loss on target poses plus L2 loss on predicted future image features.

symbols.meaning: L2 between predicted and actual future image-feature tokens

algorithmSteps: Retarget AMASS to humanoid (body joints, 1-DoF wrist, 6-DoF hands).
Train HST with PPO in sim with domain randomization; deploy zero-shot.
Operator shadows via single RGB camera (WHAM body 25 fps, HaMeR hands 10 fps).
Record binocular egocentric images + proprioception + target poses (25–40 demos/task).
Train HIT to predict 50-step target-pose chunk + future image features.
Deploy HIT at 25 Hz sending targets asynchronously to HST at 50 Hz.
ablations: Monocular HIT fails Wear-a-Shoe (0% vs 60% binocular) and drops Fold Clothes to 40% vs 100%.
ACT overfits to proprioception: 0% on Wear-a-Shoe and Type 'AI' vs 60% and 80% for HIT.
Low-level policy recovers in 1.2 s vs 15 s for H1 default; enables 0.35 m jump vs 0 m.
hyperparams: HST context length 8, 50 Hz; HIT chunk 50 target poses, 25 Hz, ResNet image encoder; domain rand. payload ±3 kg, friction 0.3–0.9, delay 0.02–0.04 s.

name: ExBody2
resolvedTitle: ExBody2: Advanced Expressive Humanoid Whole-Body Control
org: UC San Diego, UC Berkeley, MIT
problem: Whole-body motion trackers either trade expressiveness for stability or break on infeasible human motions; global keypoint tracking (H2O/OmniH2O) drifts and fails on non-stationary motions.
keyIdea: Automatically curate mocap by lower-body tracking error of a base policy (feasibility–diversity principle), train a generalist tracker, fine-tune specialists per motion group, and decouple local keypoint tracking from velocity-based global tracking; deploy via teacher–student DAgger distillation.
architecture: MLP teacher trained with PPO in IsaacGym using privileged info (root velocity, body link positions, physics params); MLP student distilled with DAgger from a 10-step proprioceptive history plus motion targets; outputs 23-D PD targets on Unitree G1.
inputs: Proprioception history (75-D × 10: DoF pos/vel, last action, root ang. vel., roll/pitch/yaw) + tracking target (23 DoF pos, 36-D local keypoints, root vel/ang. vel, roll/pitch/yaw, height)
outputs: 23-D joint position targets for PD controllers
actionRepr: single-step 23-D joint position targets at 50 Hz
trainingData: CMU mocap (retargeted), automatically filtered at τ=0.15; specialist sets (e.g., dancing), ACCAD as OOD test
whatChangedVsParent: Tracks full body (not just upper body like ExBody) with automated feasibility filtering, local-frame keypoints plus velocity tracking instead of OmniH2O's global keypoints, and generalist→specialist fine-tuning.
limitations: Specialist policies cannot yet be seamlessly recombined for dynamic transitions across diverse motion types; filtering trades a slight increase in velocity-tracking error.
notes: Also demonstrated RGB (HybrIK) teleoperation and CVAE motion synthesis in appendix. Filtering threshold chosen by greedy search over τ ∈ {0.075..0.175}. Evaluated on G1; summary mentions H1 not verified.

keyEquations.meaning: Lower-body tracking error of base policy per motion sequence, used for data curation.
Pick filter threshold whose trained policy performs best on the full dataset.

symbols.meaning: policy trained on filtered subset D_τ

keyEquations.meaning: DAgger distillation of student toward privileged teacher actions.

algorithmSteps: Retarget mocap to G1.
Train base policy on unfiltered data; compute lower-body error e(s) for each clip.
Sweep thresholds τ, train policies on D_τ, pick τ* (0.15) maximizing full-set performance.
Train privileged teacher with PPO on D_τ* using local keypoints + velocity tracking rewards.
Optionally fine-tune on a motion group (e.g., dance) to get a specialist.
Distill student with DAgger from 10-step proprioceptive history; deploy at 50 Hz.
ablations: Filtering improves MPJPE 0.1355 → 0.1079 (sim) and 0.1361 → 0.1074 (real) vs no filter, with slight velocity error increase (0.2787 → 0.2930).
Removing DAgger distillation: MPKPE 0.1150 vs 0.1000, Evel 0.4195 vs 0.2930.
History 10 best overall; history 0 gives Evel 0.4151, history 100 gives MPJPE 0.1225.
hyperparams: τ*=0.15; student history 10; policy 50 Hz; action 23-D; reward weights: DoF pos 3.0, keypoint 2.0, linear vel 6.0, vel direction 6.0.

name: WoCoCo
resolvedTitle: WoCoCo: Learning Whole-Body Humanoid Control with Sequential Contacts
org: Carnegie Mellon University (LeCAR Lab), ETH Zurich
problem: RL for humanoid tasks with prescribed contact sequences (jumping, loco-manipulation, climbing) needs task-specific rewards and state machines and struggles with sparse contacts and long-horizon exploration.
keyIdea: Decompose a task into contact stages (contact goal + task goal) and use task-agnostic rewards: dense contact reward, stage-count reward, and count-based curiosity via a random-network hash, plus a 3-phase sim-to-real curriculum; only 1–2 task terms per task.
architecture: End-to-end MLP actor and critic [512,256,128] trained with PPO + symmetry augmentation in Isaac Gym; curiosity hash network with one 32-unit hidden layer and 16-D output.
inputs: Proprioception (joint pos/vel, previous actions stacked 3 steps, base lin/ang velocity, projected gravity) + goal representations (current, and for parkour next two, contact/task goals from motion capture)
outputs: Joint target positions for low-level PD controllers
actionRepr: single-step joint position targets
trainingData: Pure RL in simulation; no motion priors or demonstrations

headlineResults.value: parkour jumping, box loco-manipulation, clap-and-tap dancing, cliffside climbing without motion priors

headlineResults.comparedTo: below 0.6 when DR merged into phase 1

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces task-specific rewards/state machines with stage-based task-agnostic rewards and replaces RND with hash count-based curiosity on task-agnostic observations.
limitations: No prediction of when the controller will fail; contact sequences are heuristically predefined; stage switching needs explicit contact feedback; goals come from motion capture rather than onboard sensing.
notes: Robot: Unitree H1 per project (verify; paper text says 'humanoid'). Ablation results are qualitative (behaviors and learning curves): 0-1 contact reward → robot does not jump; no stage count → avoids fulfilling contact goals; no curiosity → under-exploration; RND → leans backward riskily. Reward weights table: e.g., parkour w_con 120, w_stage 160, w_curi 20000.

keyEquations.meaning: Total reward: task-agnostic WoCoCo + regularization + 1–2 task terms.

keyEquations.tex: r_{con} = n_{corr} - n_{con}\, n_{wrong}\cdot \mathbb{1}(n_{stage}>0) + 2 n_{con}^2 F_{con} F_{task}
keyEquations.meaning: Dense contact reward: reward correct contacts, penalize wrong ones, bonus for stage fulfillment.
