Count-based curiosity with random-network hash buckets.

nodes: Curriculum: no DR → DR → heavier regularization
edges: Curriculum: no DR → DR → heavier regularization

algorithmSteps: Define contact stages with contact and task goals for the task.
Phase 1: train with PPO without domain randomization, curiosity on, until convergence.
Phase 2: resume with domain randomization until convergence.
Phase 3: raise regularization weights 20% per 2000 iterations until doubled.
Deploy; advance stage when sensors/human confirm contact+task goal, after a delay.
ablations: 0-1 contact rewards instead of dense: humanoid never jumps, just tracks upper-body posture.
Without stage-count reward: robot deliberately avoids fulfilling contact goals.
Merging DR into phase 1: parkour progress converges below 0.6 vs >0.75; skipping phase 3 yields aggressive behaviors that fail in real world.
hyperparams: MLP [512,256,128]; 3-step history stacking; hash net 32 hidden, 16-D output; control delay U(0,20) ms; regularization ramp +20%/2000 iters to 2×.

name: Real-world humanoid locomotion (Radosavovic)
resolvedTitle: Real-World Humanoid Locomotion with Reinforcement Learning
org: UC Berkeley
problem: Classical humanoid controllers are hard to generalize to new environments, and fully learned controllers had not been shown for full-sized humanoids outdoors.
keyIdea: A causal transformer over the history of proprioceptive observations and actions, trained with large-scale model-free RL plus annealed KL imitation of a privileged teacher in randomized simulation, adapts in-context and transfers zero-shot to the Digit humanoid.
architecture: Causal transformer: 4 blocks, embedding 192, 4 heads, MLP ratio 2, context 16 tokens (observation-action pairs), 1.4M parameters; MLP teacher [512,512,256,128] on full state.
inputs: History of proprioceptive observations (joint encoders, IMU) and past actions; velocity commands
outputs: PD setpoints for 16 actuated joints and PD gains for 8 leg joints
actionRepr: single-step joint PD setpoints + predicted gains at 50 Hz
trainingData: Isaac Gym RL on thousands of randomized environments across four A100 GPUs; terrains smooth/rough planes and slopes up to 10% grade

headlineResults.value: no falls over one week of full-day outdoor testing
reaches 1 m/s from rest within 1 s

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces MLP/TCN/LSTM locomotion policies with a causal transformer and combines RL with annealed KL teacher imitation rather than pure imitation.
limitations: Policy not perfectly symmetric (better lateral left than right), imperfect velocity tracking, and can fall under excessive disturbances such as a very strong cable pull.
notes: Science Robotics 2024. Robot: Agility Digit (1.6 m, 45 kg, 30 DoF). Emergent arm swing, gait change on slopes, and foot-trapping recovery; hidden states cluster by terrain. Closed kinematic chains simulated with virtual springs. Validation in Agility's high-fidelity simulator before hardware. Locomotion-only; cited in manipulation surveys as foundation for humanoid WBC.

keyEquations.meaning: Student trained with PPO loss plus KL to teacher state policy; λ annealed to 0 by mid-training.
Causal transformer predicts next action from observation-action history of length l=16.

algorithmSteps: Train teacher MLP with PPO on full state in randomized Isaac Gym.
Train transformer student on observation-action history with PPO + λ·KL to teacher, annealing λ to 0.
Validate policy in Agility simulator to filter unsafe policies.
Deploy zero-shot on Digit: policy at 50 Hz, PD at 1 kHz.
ablations: Transformer beats MLP, TCN and LSTM in mean success across slopes, steps, unstable ground (30 trials; figure only).
Larger context length improves velocity tracking on slopes.
Joint RL + teacher-imitation objective beats either alone.
hyperparams: Context 16; 4 blocks, dim 192, 4 heads; 1.4M params; policy 50 Hz; action = 16 joint setpoints + 8 leg PD gains.

name: FLAM
resolvedTitle: FLAM: Foundation Model-Based Body Stabilization for Humanoid Locomotion and Manipulation
org: Harbin Institute of Technology; Peng Cheng Laboratory
problem: RL for humanoid whole-body tasks relies on task rewards alone and rarely considers body stability explicitly, which slows learning on high-DoF humanoids.
keyIdea: Map robot poses to an SMPL-X human, run a pretrained diffusion human-motion reconstruction model (RoHM) to get a 'stabilized' pose, and reward the robot when its pose is close to the reconstruction; add this stabilizing reward to the task reward for TD-MPC2.
architecture: Stabilizing reward function (robot→SMPL-X mapping F_M, RoHM reconstruction F_R, joint-similarity F_S) + basic policy TD-MPC2 (encoder, latent dynamics, reward, terminal value, policy prior).
inputs: Robot state trajectory segments (for reward); simulator state for policy
outputs: Joint actions for Unitree H1 with dexterous hands (61 DoF) in simulation
actionRepr: TD-MPC2 MPC-planned continuous actions
trainingData: Online RL in HumanoidBench (2M environment steps reported); RoHM pretrained on human motion; no human motion dataset used for the policy

headlineResults.value: state of the art on Walk, Stand, Run, Sit-Hard, Pole
outperforms baselines on all tasks, but no method completes the tasks

whatChangedVsParent: Adds a foundation-model-derived stabilizing reward to TD-MPC2 without changing its architecture.
limitations: Favors static/low-speed stability, does not teach recovery after losing balance (fails Hurdle, Slide), inaccurate on non-planar terrain since RoHM trained on planar motion, and uses a simple fixed reward combination.
notes: Simulation-only (no real robot). Results are learning-curve figures without tabulated numbers, so no numeric headline values given. Negligible effect on Reach, Crawl, Hurdle, Balance-Hard; small gains on Maze, Stair, Slide.

keyEquations.meaning: Map robot pose to human pose; reconstruct stable human trajectory with RoHM.

keyEquations.tex: F_S(s_h,\hat s_h) = \sum_{i=0}^{N}\Gamma(s_h^i,\hat s_h^i),\ \Gamma = r_j \text{ if } \lVert s_h^i - \hat s_h^i\rVert_2^2 \le t_j \text{ else } 0
keyEquations.meaning: Count joints whose pose matches the reconstruction.

keyEquations.tex: R_S(s_r) = F_S(s_h,\hat s_h) \text{ if } F_S \ge t_s \text{ else } 0
keyEquations.meaning: Stabilizing reward given only when enough joints match.
Combine task and stabilizing rewards scaled by expected per-step return.

algorithmSteps: Roll out policy for l_s=145 steps to collect a trajectory segment.
Map robot poses to SMPL-X and reconstruct with RoHM.
Compute per-step stabilizing reward from joint similarity.
Combine with task reward, store in replay buffer.
Update TD-MPC2 l_s times from sampled batches.
ablations: Removing the stabilizing reward reduces FLAM to TD-MPC2, which it outperforms on Walk, Stand, Run, Sit-Hard, Pole.
Walk, Stand, Door are not very sensitive to λ; smaller λ significantly improves Run.
hyperparams: segment l_s=145; r_j=0.1; t_j=0.1; t_s=1.5; λ ∈ [0.5,1.0] (0.5 for Crawl/Sit); q=750 locomotion, 350 manipulation; l_e=1000.

name: Reactive Diffusion Policy (RDP)
resolvedTitle: Reactive Diffusion Policy: Slow-Fast Visual-Tactile Policy Learning for Contact-Rich Manipulation
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Tsinghua University IIIS; Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute; Shanghai AI Laboratory; Shanghai Innovation Institute
problem: Action-chunking IL policies (Diffusion Policy, ACT, pi0) execute each chunk open-loop, so they cannot react to real-time tactile/force feedback mid-chunk; most teleoperation systems also give no fine-grained tactile feedback, limiting data quality for contact-rich tasks.
keyIdea: A slow-fast hierarchy: a slow latent diffusion policy predicts latent action chunks at 1-2 Hz, and a fast asymmetric tokenizer decodes them autoregressively at 20-30 Hz conditioned on the latest tactile/force signal, acting like a learnable impedance controller. Paired with TactAR, a low-cost AR teleoperation system that renders tactile/force as a 3D deformation field.
architecture: Fast policy = Asymmetric Tokenizer (AT): 1D-CNN encoder compresses the action chunk to a latent chunk; GRU decoder reconstructs actions from [latent chunk, high-frequency tactile PCA features / 6-D wrench]. Slow policy = Latent Diffusion Policy (LDP): CNN-based Diffusion Policy (1D U-Net, FiLM conditioning) that denoises latent action chunks from low-frequency image+tactile+proprio observations.
inputs: Wrist RGB (and external RGB for bimanual), tactile PCA embedding (15-dim from GelSight Mini / MCTac marker deformation) or 6-D wrench from joint torque sensors, proprioception
outputs: Relative end-effector trajectory (action chunk) with gripper
actionRepr: Latent action chunk (32 steps @24 Hz, downsample ratio 4, latent dim 4 or 8) sampled by DDPM, decoded step-by-step at 24 Hz into relative end-effector poses using latest tactile/force input
trainingData: Own TactAR teleop demos: 60 (Peeling), 80 (Wiping), 50 (Bimanual Lifting); PCA tactile dataset: 30 min random interaction (GelSight Mini) + 40 min (MCTac) with 20 objects
controlRateHz: Slow policy 1-2 Hz; fast policy 24 Hz (limited by GelSight 25 FPS); actions interpolated to >500 Hz
whatChangedVsParent: Moves Diffusion Policy into a latent action space and adds a fast tactile-conditioned decoder so actions within a chunk are corrected closed-loop instead of executed open-loop.
limitations: TactAR intuitiveness and latency could improve; not yet extended to multi-fingered hands; fast policy only uses tactile/force (no high-frequency vision); integration with VLA models left for future work.
notes: Code for TactAR and RDP released at reactive-diffusion-policy.github.io. Ablations: temporal ensembling and small chunk sizes trade off reactivity vs getting stuck (grasp rate can drop from 100% to 20% with small chunks, per report). Simply adding tactile to DP observations did not help (Q1). Uses shear+torsion info; only-normal-force (like 3D-ViTac) drops Peeling 0.95 -> 0.48.

keyEquations.meaning: Fast tokenizer loss: L1 action reconstruction plus tiny KL penalty to smooth latent space.
Slow policy: DDPM noise-prediction loss on latent action chunks Z^0 = E(A^0).
Asymmetric tokenizer: tactile enters only the decoder, so latent holds high-level strategy.

algorithmSteps: Stage 1: train AT encoder/decoder on demo action chunks with L1 + KL (tactile only in decoder)
Stage 2: freeze encoder, encode chunks to latents, train LDP with DDPM loss
Inference: every chunk (1-2 Hz) LDP samples a latent chunk from 2 frames of observation
Discard first steps to match inference/execution latency
At each 24 Hz tick, feed latest tactile/force + latent chunk into GRU decoder
Decoder outputs next relative EE pose; interpolate and send at >500 Hz
ablations: Only normal force instead of full shear/torsion: Peeling 0.95 -> 0.48
Symmetric tokenizer (tactile also into encoder): Peeling 0.95 -> 0.58
Training RDP on data from traditional VR teleop (no tactile feedback) drops performance by >30% across perturbation settings
hyperparams: AT: horizon 32 @24 Hz, downsample 4, hidden 32, latent dim 4 (peeling) / 8 (wiping, lifting), KL 1e-6; LDP: obs horizon 2 @12 Hz, 100 train / 8 inference diffusion iters, image 240x320; tactile PCA d=15; chunk ~0.67 s

name: ForceVLA
resolvedTitle: ForceVLA: Enhancing VLA Models with a Force-aware MoE for Contact-rich Manipulation
org: Fudan University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Shanghai Innovation Institute; Shanghai AI Lab; NUS; Shanghai University; Xi'an Jiaotong University; Noematrix Intelligence
problem: VLA models rely on vision and language and struggle in contact-rich tasks (insertion, peeling, wiping) especially under occlusion; naive force concatenation barely helps.
keyIdea: Treat 6-axis external wrench as a first-class modality injected after the VLM (late fusion) via FVLMoE, a force-aware Mixture-of-Experts that fuses VL tokens with a force token and adds the result into pi0's flow-matching action expert.
architecture: pi0 backbone (PaliGemma/SigLIP VLM + flow-matching action expert). FVLMoE: linear force projection to a token (6 -> 2048), concatenated with VL features; one transformer encoder block (8 heads) then sparse MoE with 4 MLP experts, top-1 routing, residual; linear projection to action-expert width (1024); last H tokens added element-wise to the action expert's state/noisy-action suffix.
inputs: Base + wrist RGB, language instruction, proprio (TCP pose xyz + Euler + gripper width, 7-D), estimated external wrench (6-D)
outputs: Action chunk of target TCP pose and gripper width
actionRepr: Chunk of H continuous target TCP poses + gripper width via conditional flow matching (pi0 action expert, 32-D padded action)
trainingData: ForceVLA-Data: 244 teleop trajectories, 140k synchronized timesteps, 5 tasks (~50 demos per task), Flexiv Rizon 7-DoF + Dahuan gripper, Quest 3 VR teleop

headlineResults.comparedTo: pi0-base w/ F 40.2%; pi0-base w/o F 37.3%; pi0-fast w/o F 31.0%
pi0-fast w/o F 52.78%; pi0-base w/o F 38.93%

whatChangedVsParent: Adds a post-VLM force token and a 4-expert top-1 MoE fusion block whose output is added into pi0's flow-matching action expert, instead of feeding force as extra state.
limitations: Uses estimated external wrench values rather than direct high-fidelity measurements; authors point to better sensors/calibration and adapting to lower-cost platforms.
notes: Paper states 'code and data will be released'. '23.2% improvement' is absolute (60.5 vs 37.3). CONFLICT (internal): text calls 37.3% 'pi0-base without force feedback (pi0-base w/ F)' - figure shows 37.3% = pi0-base w/o F and 40.2% = w/ F. Multi-task joint training avg 67.5% vs pi0-base w/ F 42.5%. Router analysis: Expert 0 handles ~half of tokens (general-purpose); others phase-specific. Training: 10k steps single-task (1 GPU, ~9h), 30k multi-task, lr 2.5e-5.

keyEquations.meaning: Sparse MoE output: gate picks top-k experts (k=1 here) and weights their outputs.
Force is linearly projected to one token and appended after VLM features.
Policy maps base/wrist images, state, wrench and instruction to an H-step action chunk.

algorithmSteps: Encode base/wrist images and instruction with the pretrained VLM
Project current 6-D wrench to a force token
Concatenate VL tokens with force token; apply one transformer encoder block
Route each token to 1 of 4 expert MLPs; add residual; project to action-expert width
Take final H fused tokens and add element-wise to state/noisy-action embeddings
Run flow-matching denoising to produce H-step TCP pose + gripper chunk
Execute chunk, read new force, repeat
ablations: Fusion placement (plug insertion): MoE before VLM 0%, linear before VLM 55%, concat after VLM 60%, FVLMoE after VLM 80% (baseline 45%)
Naive force concat into pi0-base: 37.3% -> 40.2% avg; ForceVLA 60.5%
pi0-fast degrades with naive force (31.0% -> 14.2%)
hyperparams: 4 experts, top-1 routing, D_model 2048, 8 heads, action expert width 1024, action dim 32; Adam lr 2.5e-5 -> 2.5e-6, 10k steps single-task / 30k multi-task, bf16

name: FoAR
resolvedTitle: FoAR: Force-Aware Reactive Policy for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
problem: Vision-only policies cannot tell contact from non-contact, while naive force fusion injects noisy F/T readings during non-contact phases (reaching, grasping) and hurts performance.
keyIdea: A future-contact predictor gates the force feature: fused = [scene; phi*force + (1-phi)*learnable neutral embedding]. At deployment, the same contact probability drives a reactive rule that nudges position targets when predicted contact but force is insufficient, so simple position control suffices.
architecture: Built on RISE: sparse 3D point-cloud encoder (MinkowskiEngine, 5 mm voxels) + transformer -> 512-D scene feature; F/T encoder: per-step 3-layer MLP tokens + transformer over 200-step history -> 512-D force feature; future contact predictor: ResNet18 on RGB + MLP on F/T -> linear -> phi; CNN diffusion action head (DDIM).
inputs: Single-view RGB-D point cloud, RGB image (for predictor), 100 Hz F/T history (2 s)
outputs: End-effector action trajectory + future contact probability phi
actionRepr: Chunk of 20 end-effector (pose + gripper width) actions via CNN diffusion head, 20 DDIM inference steps; temporal ensembling with separate contact / non-contact buffers
trainingData: Haptic-teleop demos: 50 (Wiping, Peeling), 40 (Chopping); Flexiv Rizon + Dahuan AG-95 + OptoForce F/T
controlRateHz: Actions ~10 Hz (T_a horizon described at lower frequency like 10 Hz); F/T sensed at 100 Hz
whatChangedVsParent: Adds a force/torque transformer encoder, a separate future-contact predictor that gates force features, and a contact-aware reactive position-correction rule on top of RISE.
limitations: Relies on static force/torque thresholds that may not suit more varied environments; uses simple position control, which may limit nuanced compliance; not yet extended to dual-arm, humanoid or dexterous hands.
notes: Project site tonyfang.net/FoAR/. Also robust to disturbances (Rewrite / Move / Rewrite+Move) in Wiping (General): 100% grasp and wipe ASR, scores 0.800-0.850 (from report). Contact labels auto-extracted from demos by F/T threshold within [t-2s, t+2s].

keyEquations.meaning: Contact probability blends force feature with a learnable neutral embedding before concatenation with scene feature.
Diffusion action L2 loss plus BCE contact-prediction loss (alpha = 0.1).
Reactive correction: if phi>0.9 but force<8 N and torque<5 N·m, push along predicted motion by epsilon.

algorithmSteps: At each inference step, perceive point cloud, RGB, 2 s F/T history, EE pose
Run FoAR: predict phi and 20-step action chunk
If phi < 0.9: add chunk to non-contact temporal-ensemble buffer
Else if current force < 8 N and torque < 5 N·m: shift chunk positions by 6 mm toward mean of next 5 predicted steps
Add (possibly corrected) chunk to contact buffer
Retrieve a_t from buffer matching current phase and send to EE position controller
ablations: Wiping: 100 Hz F/T + predictor + reactive 0.875 vs no reactive 0.650, vs 10 Hz 0.800, vs 2 Hz 0.625
Sharing the 3D encoder for the contact predictor (FoAR 3D-cls) collapses: Wiping 0.175 vs 0.875 (worse than RISE 0.500)
Peeling: MLP F/T encoder 0.426 vs transformer 0.588 (RISE 0.293)
hyperparams: T_o=200 F/T steps @100 Hz; T_a=20 actions; 100 train / 20 DDIM inference steps; features 512-D; alpha=0.1; delta_phi=0.9, delta_f=8 N, delta_t=5 N·m, epsilon=0.006 m, T_f=5; batch 240, lr 3e-4

name: Adaptive Compliance Policy (ACP)
resolvedTitle: Adaptive Compliance Policy: Learning Approximate Compliance for Diffusion Guided Control
org: Stanford University; Toyota Research Institute
problem: Visuomotor policies output only positions with fixed or uniform stiffness, but contact-rich tasks need compliance that varies spatially and temporally; estimating full stiffness from a single human demo is ill-posed.
keyIdea: Label demos with an approximate compliance profile: low stiffness along the measured force direction and high stiffness elsewhere (proved to avoid contact-constraint violation). A diffusion policy predicts reference pose, virtual target pose and a stiffness scalar, executed by a low-level admittance controller.
architecture: Diffusion Policy head conditioned on: CLIP-pretrained ViT-B/16 image features (2 frames), force encoded either by FFT spectrograms (6x30x17) into a ResNet-18 with CoordConv, or by 5-layer causal conv over 32 steps; transformer encoder layer fuses image+force; concatenated with 3 frames of EE poses.
inputs: Fisheye GoPro RGB (past 2 frames), EE poses (past 3), wrist F/T (1 s @7000 Hz for FFT variant; 32 frames @250 Hz for temporal variant)
outputs: Per arm 19-D vector: 9-D reference pose, 9-D virtual target pose, 1-D stiffness in low-stiffness direction
actionRepr: Receding-horizon diffusion over sequences of 19-D per-arm actions (reference pose, virtual target pose, stiffness), 3D translational compliance
trainingData: Kinesthetic teaching with UR5e + ATI mini-45 + GoPro: 230 episodes over 15 items (flipping); 200 demos (bimanual vase wiping)
controlRateHz: Robot pose commands at 500 Hz (low-level); policy rate not stated in retrieved text

headlineResults.comparedTo: ACP w.o. FFT 95%; Compliant policy (k=500 N/m) 23%; Stiff policy 14%
ACP w.o. FFT 81.25%; Compliant 43.75%; Stiff policy broke tool

whatChangedVsParent: Extends Diffusion Policy's action space from position targets to position + virtual target + stiffness, with auto-computed compliance labels and FFT force encoding.
limitations: Relies on assumptions (contact force dominates inertia/friction/gravity, nonzero contact forces, no pinching contacts); uses pre-selected mass/damping and only 3D translational compliance in experiments; stiffness magnitude parameters set per hardware.
notes: Claims 'over 50% performance improvement' vs SOTA visuomotor policies. Uses admittance control (Maples & Becker). Wrench labels filtered with 1 s moving average, giving hindsight about upcoming contact. Limitations sentence is compiled from stated assumptions; paper has no explicit limitations section.

keyEquations.meaning: Spring-mass-damper compliance model implemented by the admittance controller.
Stiffness: low along force direction (first column of S = f/|f|), high elsewhere.

symbols.meaning: orthonormal basis with first column f/|f|

keyEquations.tex: k_{low} = \begin{cases} k_{max}, & |f| < f_{min} \\ k_{max} - (k_{max}-k_{min})\frac{|f|-f_{min}}{f_{max}-f_{min}}, & f_{min}\le |f| \le f_{max} \\ k_{min}, & |f| > f_{max}\end{cases}
keyEquations.meaning: Low stiffness decreases linearly with force magnitude between thresholds.
Theorem 1: leaving velocity free along force direction satisfies contact constraints Jv >= 0.

nodes: Stiffness label K = S K0 S^-1
edges: Stiffness label K = S K0 S^-1
Stiffness label K = S K0 S^-1

algorithmSteps: Collect kinesthetic demos with a soft admittance controller (low stiffness, damping, mass)
Filter wrench with 1 s moving average
Compute stiffness direction/magnitude from force (Eq. 6-7), k_high if |f| small
Compute virtual target pose so tracking it at that stiffness yields the reference force
Train diffusion policy to predict reference pose, virtual target, stiffness
At inference rebuild K from the ref->virtual direction and predicted scalar
Send K and virtual target to admittance controller
ablations: FFT vs temporal-conv force encoding: similar on flipping (96% vs 95%) but FFT better on wiping (93.75% vs 81.25%)
Uniform compliance k=500 N/m: flipping 23%, wiping 43.75%
Stiff position-only policy: flipping 14%; broke the tool in wiping
hyperparams: N=3 translational compliance; 2 RGB frames (224x224), 3 pose frames; force: 32 steps via 5-layer causal conv (768-D) or 1 s @7000 Hz to 6x30x17 spectrogram; 300 training epochs (flipping); 19-D action per arm

name: 3D-ViTac
resolvedTitle: 3D-ViTac: Learning Fine-Grained Manipulation with Visuo-Tactile Sensing
org: Columbia University; UIUC; University of Washington
problem: Optical tactile sensors are bulky/rigid or expensive and cheap ones are sparse; visual and tactile signals are hard to fuse because touch is local while vision is global.
keyIdea: Low-cost (~$20/pad) flexible piezoresistive 16x16 tactile arrays on soft fin grippers; each taxel is placed in 3D via forward kinematics and merged with the visual point cloud into one visuo-tactile point cloud that conditions a diffusion policy.
architecture: PointNet++ backbone encodes the unified point cloud (512 FPS-sampled visual points + 256 tactile points per finger, 4-D with value channel, plus one-hot modality flag); conditional denoising diffusion policy outputs joint-space action sequences.
inputs: Multi-view RGB-D point cloud (cropped, FPS to 512 points), tactile pad readings (256 per finger, 2 or 4 fingers) positioned by FK, robot joint states
outputs: Sequence of robot joint states (bimanual)
actionRepr: Sequence of joint-state targets generated by a conditional denoising diffusion model (ALOHA-style bimanual teleop setup)
trainingData: Own bimanual teleop demos at 10 Hz: 30 (Egg Steaming), 30 (Fruit Preparation), 30 (Hex Key Collection), 50 (Sandwich Serving)
controlRateHz: Data collected at 10 Hz; tactile readout up to ~32.2 FPS

headlineResults.comparedTo: PC only 0.55; RGB only 0.50; PC w/ tactile image 0.70
PC only 0.45; RGB w/ tactile image 0.70
PC only 0.65; RGB w/ tactile image 0.75

whatChangedVsParent: Instead of separate tactile-image branches, tactile readings become 3D points in the same frame as the visual point cloud.
limitations: Real multi-modal data collection is expensive; no simulation of the custom tactile sensor, limiting randomization and data scaling.
notes: CoRL 2024. Authors commit to releasing code and hardware. Sensor senses normal pressure only (piezoresistive Velostat); RDP paper contrasts this by noting 3D-ViTac uses only normal force. Tactile feedback visualized to teleoperators improved demo speed for new users. All policies trained 2,000 epochs with 3 cameras.

keyEquations.meaning: Unified observation: union of visual and tactile point clouds in robot base frame.

symbols.meaning: 256 x N_finger tactile points with reading as 4th channel

keyEquations.meaning: Visuo-tactile policy maps observations to actions via conditional denoising diffusion.

algorithmSteps: Merge multi-view depth into one cloud, crop to workspace, FPS to 512 points, transform to base frame
Compute each taxel's 3D position from joint states by forward kinematics
Attach tactile reading as feature channel; visual points get empty channel
Concatenate clouds with one-hot modality flag
Encode with PointNet++ and condition diffusion policy
Denoise Gaussian noise into joint-state action sequence and execute
ablations: Tactile resolution: continuous 16x16 slightly beats 8x8 and clearly beats 4x4 and binary 16x16
Tactile points only (no vision): Egg whole task 0.10, Hex Key 0.15
Single camera + tactile (0.80 egg / 0.70 hex key) beats multi-camera vision only (0.55 / 0.65)
hyperparams: N_vis=512, 256 taxels per pad (3 mm^2 each), N_finger=2 (single arm) / 4 (bimanual), 10 Hz data, 2,000 training epochs

name: UniT
resolvedTitle: UniT: Data Efficient Tactile Representation with Generalization to Unseen Objects
org: Purdue University; University of Arkansas
problem: Existing tactile representations need large or diverse datasets and do not transfer zero-shot across objects and downstream tasks for GelSight sensors.
keyIdea: Train a VQGAN autoencoder on GelSight images of a single simple object (Allen key or small ball, under 20 min of data); the frozen encoder's quantization-regularized latent generalizes to unseen objects and plugs into perception and diffusion policies.
architecture: VQGAN: CNN encoder E, CNN decoder G with quantization layer, patch-based discriminator D, trained self-supervised by reconstruction. After training, decoder/discriminator are discarded; frozen encoder feeds task heads built from Conv2D + GroupNorm + SEBlock blocks.
inputs: GelSight Mini (with markers) tactile image, e.g. 3x128x160
outputs: Latent tactile representation z (e.g. 3x16x20); downstream: pose, class, or diffusion-policy actions
actionRepr: (Downstream policy) Diffusion Policy outputting 7-DoF (single arm) or 14-DoF (bimanual) ALOHA joint angles + gripper, 10 Hz, 24 denoising steps
trainingData: Representation: 10,854 Allen-key images or 4,831 small-ball images at 10 Hz; policies: 200 (Chicken Legs), 180 (Chips), 170 (Allen Key) demos on ALOHA; sim peg insertion 30 demos (TacSL)

headlineResults.comparedTo: T3 Medium 0.279; ResNet34 pretrain 0.293; MAE best 0.247

headlineResults.benchmark: Real ALOHA policies, Allen Key Insertion

whatChangedVsParent: Repurposes VQGAN (a generative image compressor) as a discriminative tactile encoder trained on one object, frozen for downstream use.
limitations: Does not transfer across tactile sensor types with very different image characteristics (only across units of the same type); future work: train on more diverse, finely textured objects.
notes: Open-source repo github.com/ZhengtongXu/UniT (code; checkpoint release not confirmed from paper text). VQGAN loss follows Esser et al. and is not restated in the retrieved text, so it is not given verbatim here. Freezing the encoder performs comparably to fine-tuning. Chicken Legs: one leg 13/15, two legs 9/15 vs vision 9/15, 6/15.

keyEquations.tex: z = E(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times w\times c},\quad x\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times 3}
keyEquations.meaning: Tactile representation is the VQGAN encoder output; decoder with quantizer reconstructs x.
Downstream pose loss: quaternion angular error (plus MSE on position for 6D).

algorithmSteps: Record GelSight Mini images at 10 Hz while pressing one simple object with varying contact and force (<20 min)
Train VQGAN (encoder, quantized decoder, patch discriminator) self-supervised on reconstruction
Discard decoder and discriminator; freeze encoder
Attach small Conv2D/GroupNorm/SEBlock head for perception tasks, or plug encoder into Diffusion Policy
Train only the head / policy on downstream data
ablations: Removing VQ worsens 3D pose MAE (Allen key 16x20: 0.189 w/o VQ vs 0.128 UniT)
Removing discriminator: 0.156 vs 0.128 (Allen key 16x20)
Single-object UniT (e.g. bleach cleanser 91.0% frozen) beats MAE/T3 trained on more data in zero-shot classification
hyperparams: Latent 16x20 (or 8x10) from 128x160 images; representation data 10,854 (Allen key) / 4,831 (ball) images; policy 10 Hz, 24 denoising steps

name: FuSe
resolvedTitle: Beyond Sight: Finetuning Generalist Robot Policies with Heterogeneous Sensors via Language Grounding
org: UC Berkeley (BAIR)
problem: Generalist policies (Octo, VLAs) are pretrained on vision+proprio only; touch/audio datasets with actions are scarce, and naive finetuning makes the policy ignore the new sensors.
keyIdea: Finetune a pretrained generalist policy with new-modality encoders and two auxiliary language-grounding losses: a CLIP-style multimodal contrastive loss and a generative loss that describes observations in language for every modality combination.
architecture: Octo transformer backbone (also a 3B PaliGemma-based VLA); tactile images (2 DIGIT) via pretrained TVL encoder; audio spectrograms via ResNet26; observation embedding via multi-head attention pooling for contrastive loss; a single transformer generative head for language generation (in the VLA, the LM head itself).
inputs: Third-person and wrist RGB, 2 DIGIT tactile images (background-subtracted), 1 s audio spectrogram, proprioception, language instruction
outputs: Delta end-effector position commands (plus language descriptions from generative head)
actionRepr: Delta EE position commands at 5 Hz via Octo action head trained with MSE (L_BC)
params: 3B (PaliGemma VLA variant); Octo size not stated in paper
trainingData: 26,866 teleop trajectories (Meta Quest 2) on WidowX 250 with vision, touch, audio, IMU, proprio, actions, templated language; ChatGPT rephrasings (20 templates per modality combination); pretrained on OXE

headlineResults.value: increases success by over 20% vs all baselines
headlineResults.comparedTo: Octo Vision FT, Octo scratch, ResNet scratch

whatChangedVsParent: Adds touch/audio encoders and contrastive + language-generation auxiliary losses during finetuning so the pretrained visuomotor policy actually uses the new modalities.
limitations: Extra modalities increase training cost, limiting observation history to 0.4 s; longer context could improve reasoning over sparse tactile signals.
notes: Authors open-source data, code and models; claim VLA FuSe is the first open-source VLA finetuned on non-visual sensory inputs. Per-task success numbers are shown only in bar charts (Fig. 5), not transcribed here. Shopping-bag (occluded) task shows the largest gain over vision-only finetuning. Training: 50k steps, v5e-128 TPU, batch 1024, peak lr 3e-4, beta=lambda=1.

keyEquations.meaning: Finetuning objective: MSE action loss plus language-generation and multimodal contrastive losses.

symbols.meaning: cross-entropy of generated instruction per modality combination
CLIP-style loss averaged over modality-combination instructions

algorithmSteps: Start from generalist policy pretrained on OXE (Octo or PaliGemma VLA)
Tokenize vision, touch (TVL), audio (spectrogram ResNet26) and language
Compute BC loss on delta EE actions
For each modality combination, pool an observation embedding and apply CLIP-style loss vs matching templated instruction
Feed same embeddings to generative head to predict the modality-specific instruction
Optimize L_BC + L_gen + L_contrast; augment instructions with LLM rephrasings
At test time prompt with free-form multimodal language; optionally use generative head to describe touch/sound
ablations: Removing generative loss, contrastive loss, or both lowers shopping-bag success, especially on unseen objects (bar chart, Fig. 7)
Octo trained from scratch on the multimodal dataset performs poorly, showing pretraining is necessary
Vision-only finetune is competitive on tabletop/buttons but clearly worse in occluded shopping-bag task
hyperparams: Observation history 0.4 s; 5 Hz control; 1 s audio at 44.1 kHz; 50k steps, batch 1024, cosine lr peak 3e-4, 2000 warmup; beta=1, lambda=1; 20 rephrase templates per modality combination

name: Tactile-VLA
resolvedTitle: Tactile-VLA: Unlocking Vision-Language-Action Model's Physical Knowledge for Tactile Generalization
org: Tsinghua University; UESTC; Shanghai Jiao Tong University
problem: VLAs know what to do but not how hard to do it: tactile/force signals are usually a side input and never directly drive force-level action generation in contact-rich tasks.
keyIdea: Fuse a tactile token into the pi0 VLM prefix and extend the action expert to output both target position and target contact force, executed by a hybrid position-force controller; the VLM's latent physical knowledge then maps words like 'gently' to force magnitudes and generalizes zero-shot.
architecture: pi0-initialized model: pretrained VLM (Gemma 2.6B, ViT image encoder) with a non-causal token prefix of image, language and one MLP-encoded tactile-history token; a randomly initialized tactile-aware action expert (300M) outputs position + force targets. Tactile-VLA-CoT variant uses the VLM decoder to generate chain-of-thought failure analysis at fixed intervals.
inputs: Last H RGB frames, language instruction, H-step tactile history (normal + shear from dual gripper tactile sensors), proprioceptive state
outputs: Augmented action: target end-effector position P_target and target contact force F_target (net external force via Cartesian position, grasp force via gripper width); CoT variant also outputs text reasoning and a corrected instruction
actionRepr: Continuous action chunks (position + force targets) generated with conditional flow matching (pi0-style)
trainingData: VLA-T dataset collected with a UMI handheld gripper augmented with dual tactile sensors (100 Hz tactile, 20 Hz vision, downsampled to align). USB task: 100 'soft' + 100 'hard' demos; charger: 100 demos (motion only); grasping: 50 demos per object (6 training objects); wiping: 100 successful + 100 failed whiteboard demos.
whatChangedVsParent: Adds a tactile token to pi0's prefix, puts target force into the action space, and executes via a threshold-gated hybrid position-force controller, plus a tactile chain-of-thought replanning variant.
limitations: No explicit limitations section; evaluation is on three real tasks with small demo sets and 20-trial-scale evaluations, and CoT reasoning is triggered at fixed intervals rather than adaptively.
notes: CoT variant: when wiping chalk zero-shot, the default 3.5 N failed; after reasoning it raised force to 6.7 N (34% above the 5 N seen on whiteboard training data). Positions itself against FuSe (auxiliary losses) and ForceVLA (MoE routing). Limitations field is reader inference, not paper text (paper has no limitations section).

keyEquations.meaning: Token-level fusion prefix: H image tokens, language tokens, one tactile-history token.

symbols.meaning: input prefix sequence at time t

keyEquations.tex: P_{hybrid} = P_{target} + \begin{cases} K\cdot\Delta F & \|\Delta F\| > \tau \\ 0 & \|\Delta F\| \le \tau \end{cases},\quad \Delta F = F_{target}-F_{measured}
keyEquations.meaning: Hybrid controller shifts the position command by a gain times force error when above a threshold.

algorithmSteps: Collect force-guided demos with a tactile-augmented UMI gripper; sync 100 Hz tactile to 20 Hz video.
Initialize shared weights from pi0; tactile encoder and modified action expert start random.
Fine-tune end-to-end with conditional flow matching penalizing both kinematic and force dimensions.
At inference, encode images, instruction and tactile history into the prefix.
Action expert outputs target position and target force.
Hybrid controller adds K*dF to the position command when force error exceeds threshold; PID tracks it.
(CoT variant) at fixed intervals, VLM judges success, diagnoses force cause from tactile feedback, and emits a corrected instruction.
ablations: Force-word transfer: trained 'softly'/'hard' produced 0.51 N / 2.57 N on USB and transferred to the charger task that had no force-language training.
Removing CoT: on the unseen blackboard, Tactile-VLA reaches 15% vs 80% for Tactile-VLA-CoT.
Removing tactile fusion (pi0 baselines): USB success 5%/0% vs 35%.
hyperparams: Gemma 2.6B VLM + 300M action expert; tactile history of H frames compressed to 1 token; tactile 100 Hz downsampled to 20 Hz video rate; hybrid controller force-error threshold tau and gain K (values not stated).

name: TacDiffusion
resolvedTitle: TacDiffusion: Force-domain Diffusion Policy for Precise Tactile Manipulation
org: Technical University of Munich (MIRMI); CeTI; MBZUAI; Nanjing University
problem: Learned policies usually act in the motion domain, which cannot reach the sub-millimeter precision and zero-shot transfer that tight-clearance insertion needs; diffusion policies had not been applied to force-domain actions.
keyIdea: A DDPM generates a 6D feed-forward wrench from wrench/velocity observations, imitating a behavior-tree expert insertion skill, and a second-order dynamic-system filter upsamples the 50-500 Hz diffusion output into a smooth 1 kHz command for impedance control with feed-forward force.
architecture: Small residual MLP noise estimator (hidden width N in {128,256,512,1024}) conditioned on current and previous observations and diffusion step; exported to ONNX. Output feeds a dynamic-system filter and a Cartesian impedance controller with feed-forward wrench, embedded in a behavior tree after approach and contact primitives.
inputs: 18-D observation (current + previous): external wrench, internal wrench, end-effector velocity
outputs: 6-D feed-forward wrench F_df (force + torque)
actionRepr: Single-step 6-D wrench sampled by 50-step DDPM, filtered to 1 kHz feed-forward force
trainingData: 1500 expert demonstrations of Cuboid peg insertion (0.1 mm clearance) on a Franka Panda, generated by the authors' earlier behavior-tree insertion skill from varied initial poses; recorded at 1000 Hz; 80/20 train/val split.
controlRateHz: 1000 (controller); diffusion inference 51.2-503.8 Hz depending on model size (DF3: 141.8 Hz)

headlineResults.benchmark: Zero-shot insertion on 4 novel objects (Key, Cyl-S, Cyl-L, Prism)

parents: 1 kHz behavior tree for self-adaptable tactile insertion (Wu et al. 2024)
whatChangedVsParent: Moves diffusion-policy generation from motion space into the force domain (6-D wrench) and replaces the behavior tree's hand-designed insertion sub-tree with the learned policy.
limitations: Trade-off between model size and inference speed: the largest model (51.2 Hz) degrades because of misalignment with the 1 kHz loop; evaluated only on peg-in-hole insertion variants, with extension to other assembly tasks and more modalities left to future work.
notes: 'Tactile' here means force/torque (wrench) sensing from the Franka, not a vision-based tactile sensor. Code: github.com/popnut123/TacDiffusion. Model sweep: DF1 (N=128) 503.8 Hz / 77.5% novel avg; DF2 (256) 297.5 Hz / 87.5%; DF3 (512) 141.8 Hz / 95.7%; DF4 (1024) 51.2 Hz / 81.5%.

keyEquations.meaning: Noise-prediction loss on wrench actions conditioned on current+previous observations.

symbols.meaning: noised wrench action at step tau

keyEquations.meaning: DDPM denoising step from Gaussian noise to a wrench over T=50 steps.
Second-order filter interpolating low-rate diffusion output to 1 kHz feed-forward force.

keyEquations.tex: \tau_m(t) = J(q)^T\big[F_{ff}(t) + K(t)e + D\dot{e} + M(q)\ddot{x}_d\big] + C(q,\dot{q})\dot{q} + g(q)
keyEquations.meaning: Cartesian impedance control law with feed-forward wrench.

nodes: Observation o (ext/int wrench, EE velocity; current+prev)

Observation o (ext/int wrench, EE velocity; current+prev)

algorithmSteps: Run expert behavior-tree insertion skill 1500 times on the Cuboid task, logging 18-D observations and 6-D wrench at 1 kHz.
Train a residual-MLP DDPM noise estimator (T=50) on (observation pair, wrench).
At run time, approach and contact primitives bring the peg to the hole.
Sample a wrench by denoising from Gaussian noise conditioned on current+previous observations.
Filter/interpolate the wrench to 1 kHz with the second-order dynamic system.
Apply via impedance control with feed-forward force toward the hole pose; repeat until inserted.
ablations: Model width: N=512 (DF3, 141.8 Hz) is best at 95.7% novel-object success; N=1024 (51.2 Hz) drops to 81.5% due to rate misalignment.
Removing the dynamic-system filter lowers success by 9.15% on average (filter wins 16 of 20 cases).
Only DF3 beats the baseline on both demonstrated and novel tasks (+129.5% overall efficiency).

name: M3L
resolvedTitle: The Power of the Senses: Generalizable Manipulation from Vision and Touch through Masked Multimodal Learning
org: UC Berkeley; KAIST
problem: Vision and touch are usually studied separately in RL manipulation; there was no systematic way to fuse high-resolution tactile maps with vision to improve sample efficiency and generalization.
keyIdea: Jointly train a PPO policy and a multimodal masked autoencoder whose single ViT encoder reconstructs both pixels and taxels, so visual and tactile tokens attend to each other; the learned representation even helps vision-only policies at test time.
architecture: Early CNNs for image and for tactile force maps, 2D sin-cos positional and learnable modality embeddings, shared ViT encoder (masked for reconstruction, unmasked for policy), ViT decoder; actor and critic each a transformer layer + global average pooling + MLP. PPO gradients also flow into the encoder.
inputs: 4 stacked frames of 64x64 RGB image and tactile force maps (e.g. two 32x32 taxel grids with 2 shear + 1 pressure channel) in simulation
outputs: Continuous action distribution mean (PPO Gaussian policy) and value
actionRepr: Single-step continuous action from a PPO Gaussian policy
trainingData: Online RL in three MuJoCo simulated environments with touch-grid sensors: tactile insertion (18 training pegs, Robotiq 2F-85), door opening (Robosuite), in-hand cube rotation (Gym-Robotics hand); up to ~3M, ~1M and ~20M environment steps respectively (from learning curves).

headlineResults.benchmark: Zero-shot generalization (unseen pegs, randomized door, heavier cube)
headlineResults.value: M3L consistently matches or beats end-to-end and all representation baselines (bar plot, 5 seeds)
M3L is the only method consistently best in-task on all three tasks
M3L (vision policy) substantially closes gap to M3L and beats Vision-only MAE

parents: multi-view MAE for RL (Seo et al.)
whatChangedVsParent: Extends masked autoencoding to a joint vision+touch token set with modality embeddings, trained simultaneously with the RL objective.
limitations: Inherits PPO's sample complexity and exploration difficulties; uses tactile data even when uninformative (no tactile gating); relies on scarce paired vision-touch data; results are simulation-only.
notes: Results reported only as bar plots/curves, no numeric tables in the main text, so headline values are qualitative. Code and environments at sferrazza.cc/m3l_site. For the in-hand task, one RL step is taken every n=16 representation steps instead of summing losses.

keyEquations.meaning: Joint objective: representation learning plus RL.
Masked reconstruction of both image pixels and tactile taxels.
Standard PPO actor-critic objective with entropy bonus.

algorithmSteps: Initialize MAE and PPO parameters.
Collect rollouts: encode latest visual + tactile frames without masking to get z; act with current policy; store raw inputs.
Repeat until the PPO buffer is full.
Update: train MAE (masked reconstruction of pixels and taxels) and PPO on the rollouts for M epochs, backpropagating PPO gradients into the encoder.
Repeat until the interaction budget is reached.
ablations: Frame stacking: 4 stacked frames clearly outperform 1 frame on tactile insertion (frames act as contact memory).
Sequential (no cross-modal attention) is competitive on insertion and hand but degrades considerably on door opening due to training instability.
Vision-only deployment of the multimodal encoder retains much of M3L's generalization, far above a vision-only MAE.
hyperparams: Masking ratio 95%; tactile weight beta_T=10; 8 parallel PPO envs; batch 512; PPO buffer 32768 (insertion, hand) / 4800 (door); 10 PPO epochs; lr 1e-4; 4 stacked frames; n=16 representation steps per RL step for hand.

name: ViTaL
resolvedTitle: Touch begins where vision ends: Generalizable policies for contact-rich manipulation
org: NYU Shanghai; New York University; Honda Research
problem: Imitation learning needs many hard-to-collect demos for millimeter-precision tasks, while RL policies are precise but brittle to scene changes; neither generalizes spatially and visually for contact-rich manipulation.
keyIdea: Decompose into a VLM-guided global reaching phase and a scene-agnostic local visuotactile policy (egocentric wrist camera + skin tactile), trained with semantic background augmentation via BC and refined with residual RL, so a policy learned once in a canonical setting transfers via localize-then-execute.
architecture: Base policy: randomly initialized ResNet-18 image encoder + 2-layer MLP for 15-D AnySkin tactile, minGPT transformer, MLP action head predicting 10-step chunks with temporal ensembling. Residual actor (1-layer MLP) and critic (2-layer MLP) trained with n-step DDPG (DrQ-v2 style) on frozen encoders. Molmo VLM marks the target point for reaching.
inputs: Egocentric wrist RGB (128x128), AnySkin tactile reading (15-D), in end-effector frame; language query to VLM for reaching
outputs: Relative end-effector actions (base chunk + residual offset)
actionRepr: Chunk of 10 relative end-effector actions (MLP head, temporal ensemble m=0.01) plus residual RL offset capped at 20% of max action
trainingData: 32 VR-teleoperated demonstrations per task (collected at 30 Hz, subsampled to 6 Hz) against a green screen with fixed target position, plus ~45 min (~16k steps) online residual RL per task; 4 tasks (plug in socket, USB insertion, card swiping, key in lock).

headlineResults.benchmark: VLM-guided reaching, novel positions + distractors: Plug in Socket

whatChangedVsParent: Combines ViSk-style visuotactile BC with segmentation-based semantic augmentation, residual RL that keeps augmentations during online training, and VLM-based reaching for spatial generalization.
limitations: Spatial variation only on horizontal surfaces; VLM navigation assumes obstacle-free paths; evaluated in controlled lab conditions rather than real homes.
notes: Name casing in paper: VITAL / ViTaL. Datasets, training and evaluation code released (vitalprecise.github.io); trained weights not explicitly mentioned. Segmentation pipeline: human keypoints on one frame -> DIFT correspondence -> SAM 2 -> XMem tracking. Reward = human binary success + dense L1 distance to goal.

keyEquations.tex: a = a_b + a_r,\quad a_b \sim \pi_b(z),\; a_r \sim \pi_r(z, a_b)
keyEquations.meaning: Residual policy adds a learned offset to the frozen BC action.
Residual actor maximizes the critic's Q over replay data.
Temporal-ensemble weights over past chunk predictions.

algorithmSteps: Collect 32 teleop demos per task near a fixed target against a green screen, in the end-effector frame.
Segment task objects (keypoints, DIFT, SAM 2, XMem) and replace backgrounds procedurally.
Train visuotactile BC transformer with 10-step action chunks (MSE).
Freeze encoders; train residual actor-critic online (~45 min) with augmentations, offsets capped at 20% of max action.
At deployment, prompt Molmo to point at the target and move the gripper near it.
Execute local policy (temporal-ensembled base + residual) from wrist camera and tactile at 6 Hz.
ablations: Removing tactile input reduces success by ~40% on average.
Semantic augmentation is required for novel-scene generalization for both visual (BAKU) and visuotactile (ViSk) BC.
Without VLM reaching, ViSk scores 0/25 at novel positions on all three tasks.
hyperparams: Chunk length 10; temporal ensemble m=0.01; image 128x128; batch 256; lr 1e-4; hidden 256; obs history 1; residual offset scale 20% of max |action|; exploration std linear(0.25, 0.1, 5000); UTD 16; 6 Hz policy.

name: TA-VLA
resolvedTitle: TA-VLA: Elucidating the Design Space of Torque-aware Vision-Language-Action Models
org: Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence (BAAI); Tsinghua AIR; Nanyang Technological University
problem: VLAs ignore subtle physical feedback such as joint torque, which distinguishes e.g. failed vs successful insertion, and there was no systematic study of where and how to inject torque into pretrained VLAs.
keyIdea: Systematically explore the design space and find that torque should enter the action decoder (not the VLM encoder), as a single token summarizing the torque history, and that jointly predicting future torque alongside actions as an auxiliary diffusion/flow target further helps.
architecture: Built on pi0 (PaliGemma encoder + action expert). Torque history is encoded by an MLP adapter into one token prepended to the action expert's state input (DePost); the output linear layer predicts concatenated action and torque chunks with a shared denoiser. Also applied to RDT.
inputs: Multi-view RGB (3 cameras), language instruction, joint angles, joint-torque history (estimated from motor currents, all 7 joints)
outputs: Action chunk plus (auxiliary) future torque chunk
actionRepr: pi0-style action chunk of 50 via conditional flow matching with 10 integration steps, jointly denoised with a torque chunk
trainingData: Real-world teleop data on a dual-arm Cobot Magic ALOHA (7-DoF per arm) over 10 tasks (5 contact-rich, 5 regular); models fine-tuned from public pretrained weights. Cross-embodiment test on ROKAE SR arm.
whatChangedVsParent: Adds a single decoder-side torque-history token and an auxiliary future-torque prediction loss to pi0 (and RDT), with negligible training/inference overhead.
limitations: Depends on torque estimated from motor currents, which is sensitive to calibration, noise and thermal drift; unclear scalability to other modalities (tactile, temperature) under shared token budgets; needs more diverse real-world evaluation.
notes: Joint torque computed as tau = k_t * i from motor currents, no external F/T sensor. HSIC analysis: torque features correlate 0.957 with joint-angle features vs 0.300 with image features, motivating decoder placement. Inference 93.96 ms vs 90.70 ms for pi0 (RTX 4090). Published at CoRL 2025.

keyEquations.meaning: Joint torques encode external end-effector wrench via the Jacobian transpose.
Actions and future torques are noised together as one joint token.
Flow-matching loss on action slice plus weighted loss on torque slice.

algorithmSteps: Estimate joint torques from motor currents (tau = k_t i) for all joints.
Summarize the torque history into one token with an MLP adapter.
Prepend the torque token to the action expert's state input alongside joint angles.
Concatenate action and future-torque chunks; noise them jointly.
Train with flow-matching loss on actions plus beta-weighted torque loss via a single shared output layer.
At inference, integrate the vector field to get actions (torque predictions discarded).
ablations: Placement: decoder post-concat 12/20 vs encoder 8/20 on Charger Plugging (pi0 0/20); button pushing 10/20 vs 7/20.
History: single decoder history token 16/20 vs H decoder tokens 7/20 on Charger Plugging; Button 15/20 vs 9/20.
Aggregator: MLP 15/20 vs RNN 7/20 vs attention 13/20 (pi0+obs, button pushing); beta=0.1 gives 18/20 for obs+obj.
hyperparams: pi0 action chunk 50, 10 flow integration steps; torque from 7 joints; single-token MLP history aggregation; beta=1 for pi0+obj, beta=0.1 for pi0+obs+obj.

name: DeLaN
resolvedTitle: Deep Lagrangian Networks: Using Physics as Model Prior for Deep Learning
org: Technische Universität Darmstadt; Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
problem: Black-box learned dynamics models need lots of data and extrapolate poorly beyond training trajectories, while analytic models need precise physical parameters; model errors can damage the robot.
keyIdea: Impose the Euler-Lagrange equation on a deep network: learn a Cholesky factor L(q) of the mass matrix and the gravity term g(q) from joint positions only, and compute the inverse dynamics analytically, guaranteeing a symmetric positive-definite inertia matrix and physically plausible, extrapolating models.
architecture: Shared ReLU feed-forward network with three heads: diagonal of L (non-negative activation + positive offset b), off-diagonal of L (linear), and g(q). Derivatives dH/dt and d(q'Hq')/dq are computed analytically in a single forward pass so the model runs inside a real-time control loop.
inputs: Joint positions, velocities and accelerations (q, q_dot, q_ddot); only q enters the networks
outputs: Joint torques (inverse model), or accelerations (forward model); also decomposed inertial, Coriolis/centrifugal and gravity torques
trainingData: Learned online from random initialization using samples read from the control loop: 20 single-stroke character trajectories (2-DoF simulated robot) and cosine joint-space trajectories on simulated and physical 7-DoF Barrett WAM (4 lower joints learned).

headlineResults.value: Lower than FF-NN at all training-set sizes; with 8 training characters executes all 20, comparable to the analytic model (plot)

headlineResults.benchmark: Cosine trajectories, velocity extrapolation (sim + real WAM)
headlineResults.value: Degrades much more slowly than FF-NN; beats analytic RNE on simulated WAM at all velocity scales (plot)
Slightly better than analytic RNE but worse than FF-NN (cable-drive dynamics outside rigid-body prior)

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces hand-derived, embodiment-specific Newton-Euler features with a generic deep network constrained only by the Lagrangian structure, learned end-to-end.
limitations: Inherits the physics prior's model class: cannot represent non-rigid effects such as the WAM's cable drives or other non-conservative forces (friction), so an unconstrained network fits training trajectories better on the real robot.
notes: ICLR 2019. Results are presented as plots (no numeric tables in main text), so headline values are qualitative. Canonical 'physics prior' for learned robot dynamics; later Lagrangian/Hamiltonian NN work builds on it. Can be used as forward model since H=LL^T is invertible.

keyEquations.meaning: Euler-Lagrange equations of motion for a mechanical system.
Cholesky parameterization guarantees a valid inertia matrix.

symbols.meaning: lower-triangular network output with positive diagonal

keyEquations.meaning: Fit predicted inverse-dynamics torque to measured torque with L2 weight penalty.
Tracking control: low-gain PD plus DeLaN feed-forward torque.

algorithmSteps: Randomly initialize DeLaN; start PD control loop at 500 Hz.
Compute feed-forward torque tau_ff = f^-1(q_d, q_d_dot, q_d_ddot) at 200 Hz.
Log joint states and applied torques from the control loop.
In a separate process, fit L(q) and g(q) by minimizing torque prediction error + L2 penalty.
Periodically swap the updated model into the control loop.
Evaluate tracking error on held-out trajectories and higher velocities.
ablations: Training-set size sweep (1-20 characters): DeLaN's advantage over FF-NN in offline test MSE grows as training data shrinks.
Velocity scaling (1x to ~2.5x): FF-NN tracking error rises quickly while DeLaN extrapolates because L and g depend only on q.
Decomposition: trained only on summed torques, DeLaN recovers inertial, Coriolis/centrifugal and gravity components that match ground truth (2-DoF sim).
hyperparams: Three-head ReLU network sharing parameters between L and g; positive diagonal via ReLU/Softplus + offset b; L2 weight penalty lambda; control 500 Hz, feed-forward update 200 Hz (compute <= 1/200 s).

name: Hamiltonian Neural Networks
resolvedTitle: Hamiltonian Neural Networks
org: Google Brain; PetCube; Uber AI Labs
problem: Neural networks that predict dynamics directly learn only approximate conservation laws, so long rollouts drift to higher or lower energy.
keyIdea: Parameterize the scalar Hamiltonian H(q,p) with a neural network and obtain dynamics from its symplectic gradient via Hamilton's equations, so the model exactly conserves a learned energy-like quantity and is time-reversible.
architecture: 3-layer fully connected network (200 hidden units, tanh) outputting a scalar H; an in-graph gradient w.r.t. inputs gives (dq/dt, dp/dt). For pixels, a fully connected autoencoder (4 layers, residual, ReLU) with 2-D latent feeds the HNN.
inputs: Canonical coordinates (q, p), or latent coordinates from an autoencoder over two stacked 28x28 frames
outputs: Scalar Hamiltonian; time derivatives (dq/dt, dp/dt) integrated with RK4 for rollouts
trainingData: Mass-spring and ideal pendulum: 25 train + 25 test noisy trajectories of 30 observations; real pendulum data from Schmidt & Lipson; two-body: 1000 near-circular trajectories (200 trajectories of 50 observations used, 80/20 split); pixel pendulum: 200 trajectories of 100 frames from OpenAI Gym Pendulum-v0.
whatChangedVsParent: Learns the Hamiltonian itself with a neural network instead of hand-crafting it or regressing the vector field directly.
limitations: Assumes a conserved quantity exists, so it cannot model friction or other dissipation without separate modeling; both HNN and baseline struggle on the chaotic three-body problem.
notes: Code at github.com/greydanus/hamiltonian-nn. On real pendulum HNN has higher train/test loss (9.2/6.0 vs 2.7/2.2 x1e3) but far better energy MSE, because the real system has friction. Not a robot-control method itself; a physics-prior building block (later extended to Lagrangian NNs, dissipative variants).

keyEquations.meaning: Hamilton's equations: dynamics are the symplectic gradient of H.

keyEquations.tex: \mathcal{L}_{HNN} = \Big\|\frac{\partial H_\theta}{\partial p} - \frac{\partial q}{\partial t}\Big\|^2 + \Big\|\frac{\partial H_\theta}{\partial q} + \frac{\partial p}{\partial t}\Big\|^2
keyEquations.meaning: Train the network so its input gradients match observed time derivatives.
Rollouts by integrating the learned vector field (RK4).
Auxiliary latent loss making autoencoder latents behave like canonical coordinates.

algorithmSteps: Collect (q, p) states and their time derivatives (analytic or finite differences).
Forward pass: network outputs scalar H_theta(q, p).
Take in-graph gradient of H_theta w.r.t. inputs.
Form predicted derivatives (dH/dp, -dH/dq) and minimize L2 to observed derivatives (Adam, lr 1e-3).
For pixels, jointly train autoencoder reconstruction + HNN loss + latent canonical-coordinate loss.
Roll out by RK4 integration of the learned symplectic vector field.
ablations: Across tasks HNN ties baseline on train/test loss but cuts energy MSE by orders of magnitude (e.g. mass-spring 0.38 vs 170 x1e3).
Three-body: energy MSE 4.2 vs 1.1e4 (x1e2), though both models fit poorly.
Pixel pendulum: weight decay (1e-5) had a significant impact on results, unlike coordinate tasks.
hyperparams: 3 layers, 200 hidden units, tanh; Adam lr 1e-3; full-batch on small tasks; 2000 steps (tasks 1-3), 10000 steps with batch 200 (two-body); weight decay 1e-4 (tasks 1-3), 1e-5 (pixel); RK4 tolerance 1e-9; latent dim 2.

name: Lagrangian Neural Networks
resolvedTitle: Lagrangian Neural Networks
org: Princeton University; Oregon State University; Google Research; DeepMind; Flatiron Institute
problem: Neural nets struggle to learn conservation laws; Hamiltonian Neural Networks need canonical coordinates (q,p), which are often unknown or hard to compute, and DeLaN restricts kinetic energy to a quadratic form.
keyIdea: Parameterize an arbitrary Lagrangian L(q, qdot) with a neural net and obtain accelerations by numerically solving the Euler-Lagrange equation via autodiff Hessians, yielding energy-conserving dynamics in arbitrary coordinates.
architecture: MLP outputting scalar Lagrangian (4-layer, 500 hidden units, softplus activation chosen because second derivatives matter); accelerations computed with JAX Hessian + pseudoinverse. Lagrangian Graph Network variant sums a learned Lagrangian density over graph/grid neighbourhoods.
inputs: Coordinates q and velocities qdot (arbitrary, non-canonical allowed)
outputs: Scalar Lagrangian; accelerations qddot via Euler-Lagrange, integrated for trajectories
trainingData: Double pendulum: 600,000 random initial conditions (instantaneous accelerations); relativistic particle with random g; 1D wave equation on 100-point periodic grid

headlineResults.benchmark: Double pendulum (40 initial conditions x 100 steps)
headlineResults.metric: mean energy discrepancy (% of max potential energy)

whatChangedVsParent: Unlike HNN it needs no canonical momenta, and unlike DeLaN it does not assume T = qdot^T M qdot, learning an unrestricted Lagrangian.
limitations: Requires inverting the Hessian of the network w.r.t. velocities, O(d^3) in number of coordinates; needs a special initialization scheme and smooth activations (ReLU unusable).
notes: Code released at github.com/MilesCranmer/lagrangian_nns (code, not pretrained weights). Not a robot policy; a dynamics-model prior. Custom initialization fitted by symbolic regression (Eq. 16).

keyEquations.meaning: Vectorized Euler-Lagrange equation governing the path of the system

symbols.meaning: Lagrangian T - V (here a neural net)

keyEquations.tex:
\ddot q = (
abla_{\dot q}
abla_{\dot q}^{	op}L)^{-1}[
abla_q L - (
abla_q
abla_{\dot q}^{	op}L)\dot q]
keyEquations.meaning: Accelerations from a black-box Lagrangian via Hessian inverse; trained against true accelerations

algorithmSteps: Sample state (q, qdot) from data
Evaluate scalar L_theta(q, qdot)
Compute grad_q L, Hessian wrt qdot, mixed Jacobian via autodiff
Solve Eq. 6 with pseudoinverse to get qddot
Regress qddot to ground truth (MSE) and backprop through second derivatives
At test time integrate qddot forward to roll out trajectories
ablations: Activation search (ReLU^2, ReLU^3, tanh, sigmoid, softplus) on double pendulum: softplus performed best
Energy error 0.4% (LNN) vs 8% (baseline) of max potential energy at similar final loss
hyperparams: 4-layer MLP, 500 hidden units, softplus, lr 1e-3 decaying, batch 32, custom init sigma = (1/sqrt(n)) * {2.2 first, 0.58i hidden, n output}

name: Neural ODE
resolvedTitle: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
org: University of Toronto; Vector Institute
problem: Discrete-layer models (ResNets, RNNs, normalizing flows) have memory cost linear in depth, fixed computation, and handle irregularly-sampled time series poorly; flows need expensive log-determinants.
keyIdea: Parameterize the derivative of the hidden state dh/dt = f(h,t,theta) with a neural net, compute outputs with a black-box ODE solver, and backpropagate with the adjoint sensitivity method at constant memory.
architecture: Any neural net f defines a vector field; ODESolve replaces stacked residual blocks. Variants: ODE-Net (MNIST classifier), continuous normalizing flows (CNF), latent ODE (RNN encoder -> z_t0 -> ODE -> decoder) for time series.
inputs: Initial state h(0)/z(t0) (input features or encoded latent), time points
outputs: State h(T) or states at requested times; CNF densities
trainingData: MNIST; toy 2D densities; synthetic bi-directional spiral time series (irregular 30/50/100 of 100 points)
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces discrete residual updates h_{t+1}=h_t+f(h_t) with a continuous-depth ODE solved adaptively and differentiated by an adjoint ODE.
limitations: Minibatching can increase function evaluations; user must set solver error tolerances for forward and reverse passes; reverse-time reconstruction can add numerical error (checkpointing mitigates); uniqueness needs Lipschitz dynamics.
notes: Code: torchdiffeq (github.com/rtqichen/torchdiffeq). Foundational for Hamiltonian/Lagrangian/port-Hamiltonian neural ODEs used in robot dynamics learning. Not a robot policy.

keyEquations.meaning: Hidden state dynamics parameterized by a neural network; output is ODE solution at T
Adjoint ODE solved backward in time to get loss gradients
Parameter gradient via integral of vector-Jacobian products
Instantaneous change of variables for continuous normalizing flows

algorithmSteps: Forward: solve z(t1)=ODESolve(z(t0), f, t0, t1, theta)
Compute loss and dL/dz(t1)
Build augmented state [z(t1), dL/dz(t1), 0]
Solve augmented dynamics [f, -a^T df/dz, -a^T df/dtheta] backward to t0
Return dL/dz(t0) and dL/dtheta; update theta
ablations: Backward pass needs roughly half the function evaluations of forward pass
NFE increases during training (model adapts complexity)
Tolerance could be reduced to 1e-3 (classification) and 1e-5 (density) without degrading performance
