trainingData: No training; 3 fixed example programs in the prompt. VirtualHome dataset of 70 household tasks created for evaluation.
parents: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners (Huang et al.)
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces natural-language plan generation plus action matching with program-structured prompts that constrain outputs to available actions/objects and add assertion-based state feedback.
limitations: Assertions may not cover all failure cases and no action-success feedback is given; plans can be cut short by API length caps; real-robot runs had no closed-loop assertions; evaluation against a single ground-truth goal state penalizes valid alternatives.
notes: Ablations show both comments and assertion feedback help (GPT-3 SR 0.34 with both vs 0.18 with neither). Real Franka Panda: 4 tabletop tasks, near-perfect plan success with distractors.

name: Text2Motion
resolvedTitle: Text2Motion: From Natural Language Instructions to Feasible Plans
org: Stanford University
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: LLM planners like SayCan and Inner Monologue act myopically, checking only the feasibility of the next skill, and fail on long-horizon tasks with geometric dependencies across skills.
keyIdea: Use Q-functions of a learned skill library as feasibility heuristics and run geometric feasibility planning (STAP) over whole LLM-proposed skill sequences, combining shooting (full-sequence proposals) with greedy search fallback, and terminating via LLM-predicted symbolic goals.
architecture: LLM (text-davinci-003 for shooting, code-davinci-002 otherwise) proposes goals and skills; skill library of Pick, Place, Pull, Push parameterized primitives with policies, Q-function ensembles (OOD detection) and dynamics models; STAP optimizes skill parameters.
inputs: Natural language instruction, symbolic/geometric scene state (object poses from perception)
outputs: Sequence of parameterized skills (grasp poses, placements, push/pull parameters) verified to reach the goal
actionRepr: Parameterized manipulation primitives (e.g. grasp pose, placement pose, push/pull position-direction-distance)
trainingData: Skills trained per primitive in simulation (contextual bandit); LLM used with few-shot prompts, no finetuning.
whatChangedVsParent: Adds sequence-level geometric feasibility planning and a priori goal prediction on top of SayCan-style LLM skill scoring.
limitations: Assumes a closed world with known task-relevant objects and poses from perception; no task-level replanning during execution; open-world extension left to future work.
notes: Myopic baselines complete 50-80% of subgoals but stay under 20% success on geometric-dependency tasks. Published in Autonomous Robots (2023).

name: CoPa
resolvedTitle: CoPa: General Robotic Manipulation through Spatial Constraints of Parts with Foundation Models
org: Tsinghua University (IIIS), Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai AI Lab
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: Foundation-model approaches to low-level control (e.g. VoxPoser, Code as Policies) have only coarse object-level scene understanding and rely on heavy prompt engineering, failing on tasks needing part-level physical understanding and rotation control.
keyIdea: Split manipulation into task-oriented grasping and task-aware motion planning; use GPT-4V with coarse-to-fine Set-of-Mark part grounding to pick grasp parts and to state spatial constraints (e.g. colinear vectors, point offsets) between task-relevant parts, then solve for 6-DoF post-grasp poses.
architecture: GraspNet grasp proposals filtered by VLM-grounded part mask; SoM + GPT-4V coarse object then fine part grounding; parts modeled as vectors or surfaces; nonlinear constraint solver for SE(3) poses; motion planning (e.g. RRT*) between poses.
inputs: Language instruction, RGB-D images from calibrated cameras
outputs: Sequence of 6-DoF end-effector target poses (grasp + post-grasp)
actionRepr: Sequence of 6-DoF end-effector poses solved from VLM-generated spatial constraints
trainingData: No additional training; 3 prompt examples (vs 85 for VoxPoser).

headlineResults.benchmark: Ablation: w/o foundation model / w/o coarse-to-fine / w/o constraints

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces VoxPoser's object-level value maps and discrete rotations with part-level grounding and constraint-based continuous 6-DoF pose solving.
notes: Integrates with high-level planners for long-horizon tasks (make pour-over coffee, set up romantic table). Limitations section not in retrieved pages; left empty.

name: RT-Trajectory
resolvedTitle: RT-Trajectory: Robotic Task Generalization via Hindsight Trajectory Sketches
org: Google DeepMind, UC San Diego, Stanford University, Intrinsic
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: Language- and goal-image-conditioned policies fail to generalize to new tasks even when the needed arm motion resembles training motions (e.g. folding vs pick-and-place), because the task is out of distribution in language space.
keyIdea: Condition the policy on a coarse 2D trajectory sketch of the end-effector path (with color-coded time/height and gripper open/close markers) drawn on the camera image; training labels come for free by projecting recorded end-effector poses in hindsight.
architecture: RT-1 backbone (EfficientNet-B3 tokenizer over 6-image history + Transformer) with the trajectory sketch concatenated channel-wise to each image; FiLM language conditioning removed.
inputs: Head-camera RGB history, 2D or 2.5D trajectory sketch image (human drawing, human video, LLM code, or image-generation model)
outputs: Discretized arm and base actions (RT-1 action space)
actionRepr: RT-1 style tokenized (bucketized) end-effector and base actions
trainingData: RT-1 dataset: ~73K real teleoperated demonstrations across 542 seen tasks (8 skills, 17 objects) on Everyday Robots mobile manipulators.

headlineResults.benchmark: Trajectories from human videos: Pick / Fold Towel
Trajectories from LLM (Code as Policies): Pick / Open Drawer

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces RT-1's language conditioning with a motion-centric trajectory sketch image, enabling generalization to new motions.
limitations: Assumes a calibrated camera and stationary robot base/camera within an episode; sketches must be supplied at test time and performance depends on 'prompt engineering' the trajectory.
notes: Enables 'visual prompt engineering': changing the sketch changes behavior reproducibly. RT-Sketch paper notes RT-Trajectory sketches are motion-centric, whereas RT-Sketch is scene/goal-centric.

name: RT-Sketch
resolvedTitle: RT-Sketch: Goal-Conditioned Imitation Learning from Hand-Drawn Sketches
org: Stanford University, Google DeepMind, Intrinsic
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: Language goals are ambiguous for spatial arrangements and goal images over-specify (backgrounds, distractors) and are hard to provide at test time.
keyIdea: Specify goals with a hand-drawn sketch of the desired final scene; train on RT-1 data hindsight-relabeled with synthetic sketches from an image-to-sketch GAN, with augmentations spanning line sketches, colorized sketches, Sobel edges and raw goal images.
architecture: RT-1 Transformer with the goal sketch concatenated to the 6-image history before EfficientNet-B3 tokenization (no FiLM language path); Pix2Pix cGAN image-to-sketch network trained on Contour Drawing dataset + 500 manually drawn robot-scene sketches.
inputs: Goal sketch (or goal image / edge map), history of RGB observations
outputs: Bucketized actions: 7-D end-effector, 3-D base, mode flag
actionRepr: RT-1 discretized (bucketized) actions
trainingData: ~80K RT-1 teleoperated trajectories relabeled with synthetic goal sketches.

headlineResults.benchmark: Move Near spatial precision, line sketch

whatChangedVsParent: Swaps RT-1's language goal for a visual sketch goal, trained via automatic hindsight sketch relabeling.
limitations: Image-to-sketch network fine-tuned on sketches from a single annotator; policy shows biases toward trained skills and sometimes performs the wrong skill; sketches can be ambiguous when details are omitted.
notes: Evaluated on 6 skills with human Likert ratings (62 raters). Performs comparably to RT-1 and RT-Goal-Image in straightforward settings.

name: VRB (affordances from human video)
resolvedTitle: Affordances from Human Videos as a Versatile Representation for Robotics
org: Carnegie Mellon University; Meta AI
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: Visual affordance models learned from human video were evaluated only on static datasets, and it was unclear how to represent and use them on real robots.
keyIdea: Learn a robot-centric affordance, contact-point heatmap plus post-contact trajectory, from egocentric human video, mapping labels back to a human-free frame via homography, and plug it into four robot learning paradigms.
architecture: ResNet-18 encoder (from R3M) with deconvolutional heads + spatial softmax predicting 5 GMM contact-point means; 6-layer transformer encoder predicting a 5-waypoint post-contact trajectory; hand-object detector (100DOH) and skin segmentation for labels.
inputs: RGB image crop of the scene (no human present)
outputs: Contact point distribution and post-contact 2D trajectory, projected to 3D for robot execution
actionRepr: Contact point + short post-contact waypoint trajectory (pixel space, lifted to 3D with calibrated depth camera)
trainingData: EPIC-KITCHENS-100 videos, ~54K image-trajectory-contact tuples.

headlineResults.benchmark: BC on frozen encoder (Franka Kitchen sim): microwave / slide-door / door-open

headlineResults.value: 10 tasks, 4 environments, 2 robots (Franka, Hello Stretch), >200 hours

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces human-centric hand-pose/heatmap outputs with robot-first contact point + trajectory affordances usable across imitation, exploration, goal-reaching and action-space parameterization.
limitations: Future work: multi-stage tasks and incorporating force/tactile information; relies on a calibrated camera and fixed primitive (move to contact, grasp, follow trajectory).
notes: CVPR 2023. Name 'VRB' = Vision-Robotics Bridge. Card topic is B5 (planning) though VRB is an affordance/representation method.

name: SpatialVLM
resolvedTitle: SpatialVLM: Endowing Vision-Language Models with Spatial Reasoning Capabilities
org: Google DeepMind; Google Research
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: VLMs lack quantitative 3D spatial reasoning (metric distances, sizes), which the authors attribute to missing spatial data rather than architecture.
keyIdea: Automatically synthesize Internet-scale metric 3D spatial VQA by lifting real 2D images to 3D with off-the-shelf detection, segmentation, captioning (FlexCap) and metric depth (ZoeDepth), then co-train a VLM on it.
architecture: PaLM-E architecture with PaLM 2-S backbone, co-trained on the PaLM-E mixture plus 5% spatial-reasoning tokens; optional LLM (text-davinci-003) orchestration for chain-of-thought spatial reasoning.
inputs: Image and spatial question
outputs: Natural-language answers including metric distance/size estimates
trainingData: 10 million images and 2 billion synthetic spatial VQA pairs (50% qualitative, 50% quantitative; 38 question types) from WebLI and VQA images.
whatChangedVsParent: Same PaLM-E recipe, but adds a large synthetic metric-3D spatial VQA dataset to the training mixture.
limitations: Inherits biases of the expert vision models in the data pipeline (best on objects 1-10 m away, where metric depth is reliable); question templates are finite and involve at most two objects.
notes: Robotics use: dense reward annotation, e.g. monotonically decreasing gripper-to-can distance estimates. Does not hurt general VQA (comparable OKVQA, slightly better VQA-v2).

name: Where2Act
resolvedTitle: Where2Act: From Pixels to Actions for Articulated 3D Objects
org: Stanford University; Facebook AI Research
topicName: High-level planning with LLMs and VLMs (new)
problem: Semantic perception (labels, part segmentation) does not tell an agent where and how to interact with articulated objects.
keyIdea: Dense per-pixel prediction, for each action primitive, of an actionability score, candidate gripper orientations, and their success likelihoods, learned purely by interacting in simulation with an online adaptive sampling strategy.
architecture: Backbone UNet (ResNet-18 encoder) for RGB-D images or PointNet++ for partial point clouds producing 128-D per-pixel features; three MLP heads: actionability scorer, conditional action proposal (6D rotation from noise), action scorer.
inputs: Single RGB-D image or partial 3D point cloud of an articulated object
outputs: Per-pixel actionability, SE(3) gripper interaction proposals and success scores for 6 primitives (push, push-up, push-left, pull, pull-up, pull-left)
actionRepr: Pre-programmed short primitive trajectories parameterized by starting gripper pose in SE(3)
trainingData: SAPIEN simulation with PartNet-Mobility: 972 shapes over 15 categories (10 train categories, 5 held-out); ~10,000 positive offline trajectories per primitive plus 50/50 random/adaptive online samples.
whatChangedVsParent: Moves from coarse affordance classification or planar grasping to dense per-pixel actionable information with low-level 6-DoF interaction proposals for articulated parts.
limitations: Single-frame input is ambiguous about part mobility; limited to six hard-coded primitives; does not explicitly model part segmentation or motion axes.
notes: ICCV 2021. Generalizes to unseen categories and shows qualitative transfer to real scans/images. Quantitative F-score and sample-success-rate tables were not in the retrieved pages, so headline numbers are omitted.

name: TD-MPC
resolvedTitle: Temporal Difference Learning for Model Predictive Control
org: UC San Diego
problem: Model-based RL either plans expensively over long horizons or propagates model bias into policies, and reconstruction-based world models waste capacity modeling task-irrelevant details.
keyIdea: Learn a Task-Oriented Latent Dynamics (TOLD) model jointly with a terminal Q-function via TD learning (reward, value and latent-consistency losses, no reconstruction), and plan short horizons with MPPI using the value for long-term return.
architecture: Deterministic MLPs: encoder h, latent dynamics d, reward R, twin Q, policy pi (2-layer 512-unit MLPs; 4-layer CNN encoder for pixels); MPPI planning with horizon 5, 512 samples, 5% policy-guided samples.
inputs: State vectors or stacked 84x84 RGB frames
outputs: Continuous action (first action of planned sequence, receding horizon)
actionRepr: Continuous actions from MPPI trajectory optimization in latent space
trainingData: Online RL interaction; evaluated on 92 tasks from DMControl and Meta-World v2.

headlineResults.benchmark: DMControl Humanoid and Dog locomotion (up to 38-D actions)
headlineResults.comparedTo: SAC, LOOP, MPC with ground-truth simulator

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces pixel/state reconstruction with reward-, value- and latent-consistency-driven model learning and combines short-horizon MPC with a learned terminal value.
limitations: Learned policy alone is inferior to planning on complex tasks; planning cost and inference time grow with horizon and iterations.
notes: ICML 2022. Code at nicklashansen.github.io/td-mpc; solves most tasks in about an hour on one GPU. Specific numeric returns are in figures only. Parent of MoDem and TD-MPC2.

name: MoDem
resolvedTitle: MoDem: Accelerating Visual Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with Demonstrations
org: Meta AI; UC San Diego
problem: Visual model-based RL is bottlenecked by exploration on sparse-reward manipulation, and naively appending a few demonstrations to the replay buffer barely helps.
keyIdea: Three phases on top of TD-MPC: (1) BC policy pretraining on demos, (2) seeding world model and critic with rollouts of the pretrained policy, (3) interactive finetuning with aggressive, annealed demo oversampling and data augmentation.
architecture: TD-MPC (TOLD latent dynamics, reward, Q, policy; MPPI planning) with image encoder; inputs are 2 stacked 224x224 RGB frames plus proprioception.
inputs: Third-person RGB images (224x224, 2 frames) + proprioceptive state
outputs: Continuous actions via planning
actionRepr: Continuous actions from TD-MPC MPPI planning
trainingData: 5 demonstrations per task (human teleop for Adroit; MPC-generated for Meta-World/DMControl) + 100K online interaction steps; 21 tasks (3 Adroit, 15 Meta-World, 3 DMControl).
whatChangedVsParent: Adds BC pretraining, policy-driven seeding and demo oversampling to TD-MPC instead of simply appending demos to the buffer.
limitations: Policy pretraining alone gives limited benefit (likely catastrophic forgetting during finetuning); evaluated in simulation only.
notes: Code at github.com/facebookresearch/modem. Abstract states 160-250% more successful than prior approaches; conclusion states 250-350% (internal inconsistency in the paper). 100K interactions is about one hour of real-robot time in Adroit.

name: Dreamer 4
resolvedTitle: Training Agents Inside of Scalable World Models
org: Google DeepMind
problem: Earlier world models (e.g. Dreamer 3's RSSM) cannot fit complex data distributions, while large controllable video models mispredict object interactions and are too slow for imagination training.
keyIdea: A scalable transformer world model (causal tokenizer + block-causal dynamics trained with a shortcut forcing objective) fast enough for real-time single-GPU inference, in which a policy is trained by RL purely in imagination from offline data.
architecture: Causal tokenizer (masked autoencoding, 400M) + interactive dynamics transformer (1.6B) with space layers and temporal attention every 4 layers, GQA, register tokens; x-space prediction with ramp loss weight; policy, reward and value heads added via task tokens; imagination RL with PMPO and KL to the BC prior.
inputs: Video frames (Minecraft 360x640), low-level mouse and keyboard actions, task embeddings
outputs: Predicted future frames; policy actions, rewards, values
actionRepr: Keyboard as 23 binary variables + mouse as 121-way categorical (foveated discretization) for Minecraft; 7-D relative end-effector actions in SOAR robotics experiments
trainingData: VPT contractor dataset, 2,541 hours of Minecraft gameplay at 20 FPS (no online interaction); also SOAR robotics (180 h) and Epic Kitchens (100 h) for world-model experiments.
controlRateHz: 21 FPS world-model inference on one H100 (Minecraft runs at 20 FPS)
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces Dreamer 3's RSSM with a 2B transformer world model trained by shortcut forcing, and learns from offline data only instead of online interaction.
limitations: World model has short memory (9.6 s context) and imprecise inventory predictions, so it is far from a full game clone.
notes: First agent to obtain Minecraft diamonds purely offline; uses 100x less data than VPT. Shortcut forcing with 4 sampling steps approaches diffusion forcing with 64 steps. Action conditioning learned from a small amount of action-labeled video. Robotics (SOAR) generations shown qualitatively only.

name: iVideoGPT
resolvedTitle: iVideoGPT: Interactive VideoGPTs are Scalable World Models
org: Tsinghua University; Huawei Noah's Ark Lab; Tianjin University
problem: Recurrent world models are interactive but do not scale, while large video generators scale but only offer trajectory-level (not step-level) action control.
keyIdea: A GPT-style autoregressive transformer over tokens of observations, actions and rewards, using compressive tokenization: context frames get 16x16 tokens, future frames only 4x4 tokens conditioned on context via a conditional VQGAN.
architecture: Conditional VQGAN with dual encoders/decoders (cross-attention to context features); LLaMA-architecture transformer at GPT-2 size (138M main; 436M for scaling study); slot tokens for optional action embeddings and a reward head.
inputs: Context video frames, optional per-step actions
outputs: Next-frame tokens (decoded to video) and rewards
trainingData: Action-free pretraining on 35 Open X-Embodiment datasets plus Something-Something-v2 (95 classes, 15% weight), over one million trajectories; finetuned on BAIR, RoboNet, VP2, Meta-World.

headlineResults.value: outperforms FitVid world model on 5 of 6 tasks

whatChangedVsParent: Unlike VideoGPT's non-causal spatiotemporal tokenizer or IRIS's per-frame tokens, uses context-conditioned compressive tokens and step-wise autoregression so actions can be injected at every step.
limitations: Limited diversity in public robot data; compressive tokenization assumes initial frames provide enough context, which may fail for long videos with large camera motion; benefits of larger models not yet shown on real-robot control.
notes: NeurIPS 2024. Code and pretrained models at thuml.github.io/iVideoGPT. Action conditioning improves BAIR FVD by almost 20% (exact FVD table not in retrieved pages). Asymptotic 16x token reduction. Visual MBRL training ~4 h vs IRIS 7 days for 100K env steps.

name: DreamDojo
resolvedTitle: DreamDojo: A Generalist Robot World Model from Large-Scale Human Videos
org: NVIDIA (GEAR), HKUST, UC Berkeley, UW, Stanford, KAIST, UofT, UCSD, UT Austin
problem: Robot video world models are confined to observed setups because robot data has limited coverage and action labels are scarce, so they generalize poorly to unseen objects/environments and respond weakly to counterfactual actions.
keyIdea: Pretrain an action-conditioned video world model on 44k hours of egocentric human video, using self-supervised continuous latent actions as unified proxy action labels, then post-train on a small target-robot dataset and distill to a real-time autoregressive model.
architecture: Initialized from Cosmos-Predict2.5 (latent video DiT, WAN2.2 tokenizer, flow matching); actions injected per latent frame as 4-step chunks via an MLP added to timestep embeddings in AdaLN. A 700M spatiotemporal-Transformer VAE latent action model (32-dim latent) provides proxy actions; a Self-Forcing-style distillation converts it to a causal, 4-step student.
inputs: Initial frame(s) + action sequence (latent actions during pretraining; relative robot joint actions after post-training); empty text prompt
outputs: Future video frames at 640x480 (autoregressive, 10.81 FPS after distillation)
trainingData: Pretraining on 44,711 h of human video: In-lab (55 h), EgoDex (829 h), DreamDojo-HV (43,827 h, crowdsourced, ~1.135M trajectories, 6,015 tasks, 9,869+ scenes) sampled 1:2:10; post-training on target robot data (GR-1, Unitree G1, AgiBot, YAM). 140k steps on 256 H100s for pretraining.

headlineResults.value: 15x longer duration, 96x more skills, 2,000x more scenes

whatChangedVsParent: Extends a pretrained video generator with continuous latent-action conditioning learned from massive human video, relative/chunked action injection, a temporal-consistency loss, and real-time autoregressive distillation.
limitations: Struggles with uncommon actions (slapping, fast waving); policy-eval success rates in DreamDojo are often higher than real (fails to generate nuanced failures); no native multi-view simulation; retention of pretrained knowledge during post-training not studied.
notes: Applications shown: live teleoperation, policy evaluation (positive correlation with real-world), model-based planning / test-time policy steering. Temporal consistency loss lambda=0.1.

name: LeWorldModel
resolvedTitle: LeWorldModel: Stable End-to-End Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture from Pixels
org: Mila & Université de Montréal, NYU, Samsung SAIL, Brown University
problem: JEPA latent world models are prone to representation collapse and rely on fragile heuristics (EMA, stop-gradient, frozen pretrained encoders, many-term losses).
keyIdea: Train encoder and predictor end-to-end from pixels with only two losses: next-embedding MSE and SIGReg, a regularizer that pushes embeddings toward an isotropic Gaussian via random 1-D projections and the Epps-Pulley normality test.
architecture: ViT-Tiny encoder (~5M, patch 14, CLS token + BN projector) and a 6-layer transformer predictor (~10M) with AdaLN action conditioning and causal masking; planning with CEM-based MPC in latent space.
inputs: 224x224 RGB frames + actions (frame-skip 5 action blocks)
outputs: Predicted next latent embeddings; actions via latent MPC toward a goal-image embedding
trainingData: Offline reward-free trajectories per environment (e.g., PushT 20k expert episodes; TwoRoom 10k episodes); trainable on a single GPU in a few hours
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces PLDM's seven-term VICReg-style objective (and DINO-WM's frozen encoder) with a two-term loss, reducing tunable loss hyperparameters from six to one.
limitations: Planning limited to short horizons; needs offline data with sufficient coverage; SIGReg struggles in low-intrinsic-dimension environments (worse on Two-Room); still needs action labels.
notes: Code released (paper links website and code). Also shows physical-quantity probing and violation-of-expectation surprise detection. Two-Room: LeWM 87% vs 97-100% for baselines.

name: GWM (Gaussian world model)
resolvedTitle: GWM: Towards Scalable Gaussian World Models for Robotic Manipulation
org: Tsinghua University, BIGAI, Nanyang Technological University
problem: Image-based world models lack robust 3D geometric understanding, while per-scene 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction is too slow for world modeling and model-based RL.
keyIdea: Represent world state as feed-forward 3D Gaussian splats (from unposed images) compressed by a 3D Gaussian VAE, and learn action-conditioned dynamics with a latent diffusion transformer that predicts future Gaussians.
architecture: Splatt3R (MASt3R-based) feed-forward 3DGS -> 3D Gaussian VAE (FPS to fixed set, cross-attention encoder; 2048 -> 512 latent points) -> DiT with EDM preconditioning, AdaLN timestep, action cross-attention; optional reward head for MBRL; features after first denoising step used as encoder for BC-transformer/Diffusion Policy.
inputs: Single or two-view unposed RGB images + robot action
outputs: Future 3D Gaussian splats (renderable video); features for policy; predicted reward (RL)
trainingData: RoboCasa (Human-50 and MimicGen Generated-3000; 24 atomic tasks), Meta-World (50 tasks), real Franka pick-and-place (30 demos)

headlineResults.comparedTo: image-based DiT WM 4%, GS without 3D VAE 18%

whatChangedVsParent: Moves DIAMOND-style diffusion world modeling from image space to a latent 3D Gaussian representation for geometric consistency.
notes: Evaluated on 31 tasks across 3 domains. Limitations not explicitly listed in the retrieved pages.

name: PIN-WM
resolvedTitle: PIN-WM: Learning Physics-INformed World Models for Non-Prehensile Manipulation
org: National University of Defense Technology, Wuhan University, Shenzhen University
problem: Non-prehensile manipulation (pushing, flipping) is highly sensitive to friction/restitution; purely data-driven world models need much data and generalize poorly, and prior physics identification is gradient-free, 2D, or needs state estimation.
keyIdea: Identify 3D rigid-body physics parameters end-to-end from RGB via a differentiable LCP physics simulator plus differentiable 2D Gaussian Splatting rendering loss, then perturb the identified twin into physics-aware 'digital cousins' to train robust RL policies for zero-shot sim-to-real.
architecture: World model = differentiable rigid-body dynamics g (velocity-based LCP with mass/inertia, restitution, friction) composed with 2D Gaussian Splatting renderer; policy trained with PPO across randomized cousins (delta=0.1).
inputs: Multi-view RGB images (for rendering params) + few-shot task-agnostic push trajectories (video)
outputs: Identified physics and rendering parameters; rendered next images; RL policy outputting end-effector translations
trainingData: Few-shot, task-agnostic real interaction trajectories (e.g., straight-line pushes)
whatChangedVsParent: Makes 3D physics identification differentiable and observation-driven (rendering loss, no state estimation) and replaces naive domain randomization with physics-aware perturbations around identified values.
limitations: Robot-induced shadows distort the rendering loss and physics estimates; limited to rigid-body dynamics (no deformables).
notes: Without PADC: 65% push / 60% flip real success.

name: PointWorld
resolvedTitle: PointWorld: Scaling 3D World Models for In-The-Wild Robotic Manipulation
org: Stanford University, NVIDIA
problem: Physics simulators need curated scene-specific modeling, learned dynamics models rely on domain-specific priors, and video models lack explicit action conditioning and physical consistency; no single 3D dynamics model generalizes in the wild.
keyIdea: Unify state and action as 3D point flows: given a full-scene point cloud from RGB-D and robot actions rendered as gripper point flows (via URDF forward kinematics), predict per-point 3D scene displacements over a chunk, enabling embodiment-agnostic pretraining at scale.
architecture: Point Transformer V3 backbone over concatenated scene + time-stacked robot points; scene points featurized with frozen DINOv3, robot points with temporal embeddings; shared MLP head predicts per-point displacements for H=10 steps (0.1 s each) in one pass; loss = movement-weighted Huber with aleatoric uncertainty. Used inside MPPI-based MPC.
inputs: One or few calibrated RGB-D images + robot joint-space action sequence + URDF
outputs: Full-scene 3D point flows over a 1 s horizon
trainingData: ~2M trajectories / ~500 h curated from DROID (real, single-arm Franka, 3D flows pseudo-labeled via metric depth, pose estimation, point tracking) and BEHAVIOR-1K (sim, bimanual humanoid)

headlineResults.value: ~0.1 s per batched forward pass (PTv3-1B ~0.12 s)
Drawer 90%, Scarf 80%, Tissue box 70%, Duster/Broom 60%, Pillow 40%, Microwave 30%, Book 20%
roughly log-linear gains from 50M to 1B params

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces graph-based particle dynamics with a scalable point-cloud transformer trained on large real+sim data, with actions expressed as robot point flows rather than joint or end-effector vectors.
notes: Paper states code, dataset, and checkpoints 'will be' open-sourced (openWeights=true is per that promise). Gripper-only point flows outperform whole-body flows and low-dim EEF/joint actions. Limitations section not retrieved.

name: Robotic World Model (Li, Krause, Hutter)
resolvedTitle: Robotic World Model: A Neural Network Simulator for Robust Policy Optimization in Robotics
org: ETH Zurich
problem: Learned world models accumulate errors over long autoregressive rollouts and usually rely on domain-specific inductive biases, so policies trained in them rarely transfer to hardware.
keyIdea: Train a GRU world model with self-supervised autoregressive (multi-step, own-prediction-fed) training and a dual-autoregressive mechanism, then optimize policies with PPO over long imagined rollouts (MBPO-PPO).
architecture: GRU-based model predicting Gaussian mean/std of next observation plus privileged info (e.g., contacts); inner autoregression over history (M=32) and outer autoregression over forecast (N=8); MBPO/Dyna-style loop with PPO.
inputs: History of proprioceptive observation-action pairs
outputs: Distribution over next observations and privileged info; imagined rollouts for policy training
trainingData: Simulation data from Isaac Lab across manipulation and locomotion tasks (pretraining uses 6M state transitions); ANYmal D hardware trajectories for prediction evaluation

headlineResults.value: succeeded on ANYmal D and Unitree G1
headlineResults.comparedTo: SHAC and DreamerV3 failed to produce deployable policies

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces teacher-forced single-step model training with autoregressive multi-step training so PPO can optimize over hundreds of imagined steps.
limitations: Still below well-tuned model-free RL on high-fidelity simulators; world model pretrained in sim because training from scratch is unstable (policy exploits model errors); safe online learning on hardware remains challenging.
notes: Mostly locomotion (quadruped, humanoid); manipulation tasks (Reach, Lift-Cube, Open-Drawer, Repose-Cube Allegro) appear only in prediction-error benchmark. MBPO-PPO training time 5 min after 50 min pretraining.

name: Hierarchical latent world models (Zhang et al.)
resolvedTitle: Hierarchical Planning with Latent World Models
org: FAIR at Meta, New York University, Mila, Brown University
problem: Flat planning with latent world models fails on non-greedy and long-horizon tasks due to non-monotone goal costs, compounding prediction error, and exponential search; prior hierarchies need task-specific policies/rewards or known low-dim dynamics.
keyIdea: HWM: learn world models at multiple temporal scales in a shared latent space; the high-level model plans over learned latent macro-actions and its first predicted latent becomes the subgoal for low-level MPC, all zero-shot from a goal image.
architecture: Low-level model = existing latent WM (VJEPA2-AC, DINO-WM, or PLDM); high-level model predicts waypoint latents conditioned on 4-D macro-actions from a transformer action encoder; CEM/MPPI at both levels with receding horizon.
inputs: Current and goal RGB images (+ end-effector pose on Franka)
outputs: End-effector delta poses (Franka) / primitive actions via hierarchical MPC
trainingData: ~130 h unlabeled real robot data from DROID and RoboSet (Franka); DINO-WM Push-T dataset; PointMaze (25 layouts)
whatChangedVsParent: Adds a coarser-timescale latent world model and macro-action encoder on top of flat latent WM planners, coupling levels through latent subgoal matching instead of hierarchical policies.
limitations: Failures mainly from perceptual imprecision (depth errors) and near-misses; coarse high-level subgoals can lose details needed for precise low-level guidance.
notes: Name resolution uncertain: survey label 'Hierarchical latent world models (Zhang et al.)' matched to HWM (Wancong Zhang, Meta/NYU). An alternative candidate is MIND-V (Ruicheng Zhang et al., 2512.06628, hierarchical video world model with VLM planner + CogVideoX-5B generator + GRPO physics reward). Code: github.com/kevinghst/HWM_PLDM.

name: LaDi-WM
resolvedTitle: LaDi-WM: A Latent Diffusion-based World Model for Predictive Manipulation
org: National University of Defense Technology, Peking University, Shenzhen University
problem: Pixel-level world models predict robot-object futures poorly and generalize weakly, while existing latent world models use reconstruction-optimized latents lacking geometric and semantic structure.
keyIdea: Predict future latent states in pretrained VFM spaces (DINO for geometry, SigLIP for semantics) with an interactive latent diffusion process that cross-attends between the two, then feed imagined futures to a diffusion policy that iteratively refines its actions.
architecture: Diffusion-transformer world model with interactive diffusion between DINO and SigLIP latent codes (clean-component decomposition); transformer diffusion policy conditioned on instruction, end-effector states, historical and imagined latents; 2 refinement iterations at inference.
inputs: Historical DINO/SigLIP latents from two camera views + action sequence (WM); plus instruction and EEF state (policy)
outputs: Future latent states (WM); action chunks (policy)
actionRepr: action chunk from a diffusion policy; real robot uses delta OSC pose
trainingData: World model on task-agnostic clips (LIBERO-90; half of CALVIN tasks); policy on LIBERO-LONG with 10 demos/task; real CR10 arm with 10 demos/task
whatChangedVsParent: Extends DINO-WM-style latent prediction with a diffusion model over combined geometric+semantic latents and uses imagined states to iteratively refine a diffusion policy.
limitations: Limited scale of world-model training data; longer-horizon predictions suffer from compounding error (memory mechanisms suggested).
notes: CoRL 2025. Code promised at github.com/GuHuangAI/LaDiWM.

name: Vid2World
resolvedTitle: Vid2World: Crafting Video Diffusion Models to Interactive World Models
org: Tsinghua University, Chongqing University
problem: Pretrained video diffusion models are non-causal (bidirectional, full-sequence) and lack frame-level action conditioning, so they cannot serve directly as interactive autoregressive world models.
keyIdea: Causalize a pretrained video diffusion model (causal temporal attention masks plus extrapolative weight transfer for temporal convolutions, Diffusion-Forcing-style per-frame noise) and add frame-level action injection with causal action guidance (classifier-free guidance on the latest action).
architecture: Base: DynamiCrafter (U-Net latent video diffusion, SD VAE, CLIP image conditioning); causalized temporal layers; per-frame independent noise levels; action dropout during training enables guidance scale lambda at sampling.
inputs: Context frames + per-frame actions
outputs: Autoregressively generated future frames (320x512)
trainingData: RT-1 (robot manipulation; 100k steps, ~7 days on 4x A100), CS:GO game data, RECON open-world navigation

headlineResults.value: best among transfer methods in both NAR and AR settings
headlineResults.comparedTo: AVID, ControlNet, action/language-conditioned fine-tuning, classifier guidance

whatChangedVsParent: Unlike AVID-style adapters on a frozen non-causal model, it converts the model itself to causal autoregressive generation with per-frame action guidance.
limitations: Limited to a relatively lightweight base model due to compute; training remains time-consuming.
notes: ICLR 2026. Code and models released. Parameter count stated inconsistently in paper (1.4B in intro, 1.1B trainable in appendix).

name: GigaWorld-0
resolvedTitle: GigaWorld-0: World Models as Data Engine to Empower Embodied AI
org: GigaAI
problem: VLA training is bottlenecked by expensive real-world data; generated data must be simultaneously photorealistic, geometrically consistent, physically plausible and controllable.
keyIdea: A world-model 'data engine' combining a video branch (MoE video foundation model plus appearance, view, and human-to-robot mimic transfer) with a 3D branch (3D asset generation, 3DGS background reconstruction, differentiable physics system identification, motion planning) to synthesize VLA training data.
architecture: GigaWorld-0-Video-Dreamer: flow-matching IT2V DiT with sparse (neighborhood) attention and MoE FFN (4 routed experts, top-2), 3D-VAE (4x8x8 compression, 16 channels), T5 text encoder, 3D-RoPE; post-trained control branches (channel-concat control latents) for AppearanceTransfer, ViewTransfer, MimicTransfer; an IDM recovers joint actions. 3D suite: -3D-FG, -3D-BG (3DGS), -3D-Phys, -3D-Act. Trained with GigaTrain (FP8, sparse attention), step distillation.
inputs: Image + text (+ depth/normal, camera extrinsics, rendered arm video, or egocentric human video for transfer models)
outputs: Embodied manipulation videos (multi-view) and inferred robot actions; 3D scenes with executable trajectories
trainingData: Large-scale corpus of embodied interaction data (scale not stated in retrieved pages)
whatChangedVsParent: Unifies video-generation transfer models and a physically grounded 3D generation pipeline into one data engine, with MoE + sparse attention + FP8 for efficiency rather than parameter scaling.
notes: Paper says models and data pipeline 'will' be open-sourced. Claims VLA (GigaBrain-0) trained on GigaWorld-0 data improves real-robot success without real-world interaction during training; specific numbers not retrieved.

name: WoW
resolvedTitle: WoW: Towards a World omniscient World model Through Embodied Interaction
org: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics, Peking University, HKUST
problem: Video models trained on passive observation (e.g., Sora) show brittle physical intuition and produce physically inconsistent outcomes; physical intuition should come from large-scale causally rich interaction data.
keyIdea: Train a 14B video world model on 2M real robot interaction trajectories, refine generations with a VLM solver-critic loop (SOPHIA) that iteratively rewrites prompts, and close the loop to action with a Flow-Mask Inverse Dynamics Model.
architecture: DiT video generation world model (variants on Cosmos1, Cosmos2, Wan bases) with integrated self-supervised (DINO) feature alignment; Refiner agent + fine-tuned VLM Dynamic Critic team; FM-IDM (fine-tuned SAM on masked frame + CoTracker3 optical flow + DINO features -> MLP) predicts 7-DoF end-effector delta actions.
inputs: Initial image + text instruction
outputs: Future robot video; 7-DoF end-effector actions via FM-IDM
actionRepr: 7-DoF end-effector delta action inferred by inverse dynamics from generated frames
trainingData: 2.03M clips, >7,300 h, ~633M frames at 24 fps, 12 robot embodiments (Franka FR3 dual-arm, UR5e single/dual, Panda, ARK, AgileX, Tienkung), 5,275 tasks; ~75% raw data filtered out. IDM: 646k image-action pairs across 219 tasks.

headlineResults.benchmark: VLM planning with WoW as sandbox

whatChangedVsParent: Post-trains video foundation models on large real interaction data and adds an agentic critic-refiner loop plus an inverse dynamics model to turn imagined futures into actions.
limitations: Physics understanding is stochastic, with physical hallucinations; hard physical-reasoning tasks remain challenging and demand further scaling.
notes: Paper states models, data, benchmark will be open-sourced. Real robot deployment: WoW-cosmos2 with fine-tuning scores 0.64 real-world success score. Survey P03 classifies WoW as not action-conditioned (planning use).

name: UnifoLM-WMA-0
resolvedTitle: UnifoLM-WMA-0: A world-model-action (WMA) framework under UnifoLM family
org: Unitree Robotics
notes: No arXiv paper; software release cited as 'Unitree, 2025' in P03 (2605.00080), which lists it under foundation video world models as task-conditioned and action-conditioned, main use = simulation. GENERAL KNOWLEDGE (unverified): open-source GitHub/Hugging Face release by Unitree (~Sept 2025) of a world-model-action architecture for Unitree robots, with a video world model that can run in a 'simulation' mode (action-conditioned video generation for synthetic data / policy evaluation) and a 'decision-making' mode (predicting future frames to guide an action head); reportedly built on a pretrained video diffusion backbone (DynamiCrafter-style) fine-tuned on Open-X and Unitree datasets. Verify against the repo before stating on the site.

name: Gen2Act
resolvedTitle: Gen2Act: Human Video Generation in Novel Scenarios enables Generalizable Robot Manipulation
org: Google DeepMind, Carnegie Mellon University, Stanford University
problem: Robot policies fail to generalize to unseen object types and novel motions, and scaling robot data to cover everyday diversity is impractical.
keyIdea: Generate a human video of the task zero-shot with an off-the-shelf web-trained video model (no fine-tuning), then execute with a closed-loop policy conditioned on the generated video, trained with an auxiliary point-track prediction loss.
architecture: Pre-trained video generator (VideoPoet) conditioned on first frame + language; policy: ViT features for generated video and robot history, Perceiver-Resampler transformer encoders (64 tokens each), track-prediction transformers (training-only aux loss using BootsTAP/CoTracker tracks), BC head with 256-bin discretized actions and cross-entropy loss.
inputs: Scene image + language goal (video gen); generated human video + last k robot observations (policy)
outputs: Robot action chunks
actionRepr: discretized actions, 256 bins per dimension, predicted as a chunk a_t:t+h
trainingData: Offline robot demonstration dataset paired with automatically generated human videos (from first frames), plus ~400 additional diverse teleoperated trajectories for co-training; an order of magnitude less robot data than the video model's training data

headlineResults.value: Stowing apple 60%, Cleaning table 40%, Making coffee 20%, Heating soup 20%

whatChangedVsParent: Instead of predicting tracks or masks from web video with intermediate models, conditions the policy on a full zero-shot generated human video, with tracks only as an auxiliary training loss.
limitations: Bounded by video-generation quality (e.g., unrealistic hands), limiting very dexterous tasks; implausible generated videos cause failures at higher generalization levels.
notes: CoRL 2025. Uses Gemini to decompose long-horizon activities.

name: Im2Flow2Act
resolvedTitle: Flow as the Cross-Domain Manipulation Interface (Im2Flow2Act)
org: Stanford University, Columbia University, J.P. Morgan AI Research, Carnegie Mellon University
problem: Learning from human videos suffers an embodiment gap and learning from simulation suffers a sim-to-real gap plus task-specific environment design; existing flow-based methods still need real robot teleop data or heuristic policies.
keyIdea: Use object-centric flow (tracked keypoints on the manipulated object only) as the interface: a flow generator trained on human videos produces the complete task flow from image + language, and a flow-conditioned policy trained only on task-agnostic simulated play data executes it, with no real robot training data.
architecture: Flow generator: Grounding DINO box -> grid keypoints -> TAPIR tracks formed into 'flow images', compressed by the Stable Diffusion autoencoder, generated by AnimateDiff (SD + motion modules, LoRA). Policy: transformer state encoder over current keypoints + initial 3D coords, temporal alignment module predicting remaining task flow latent, diffusion action head; online point tracking at run time.
inputs: Initial RGB frame + task description (flow gen); generated task flow + tracked keypoints + proprioception (policy)
outputs: Object flow; robot action sequence
actionRepr: sequence of L actions: 6-DoF end-effector pose + 1-DoF gripper, from a diffusion action head
trainingData: Real-world human hand demonstration videos per task (flow generator); simulated UR5e exploration data from predefined random action primitives across rigid, articulated, deformable objects (policy)
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces ATM's embodiment-contaminated next-step grid flow with complete object-centric task flow, letting the policy train entirely on simulated play data instead of real teleop.
limitations: Assumes calibrated camera viewpoint matching between sim and test; flow abstraction drops action details (limits dexterous/in-hand tasks); depends on accurate object detection; does not apply when state changes are not visible as object motion.
notes: CoRL 2024. Performance drops ~15% on average from sim to real.

name: Dreamitate
resolvedTitle: Dreamitate: Real-World Visuomotor Policy Learning via Video Generation
org: Columbia University, Toyota Research Institute, Stanford University
problem: Behavior cloning policies generalize poorly to new visual environments and need ground-truth robot actions; generated human videos are hard to transfer due to the embodiment gap, and robot video data is scarce.
keyIdea: Fine-tune an internet-pretrained video diffusion model to generate stereo videos of a human using a trackable tool to do the task; track the tool's 6-DoF pose in the generated video and have the robot (holding the same tool) execute that trajectory.
architecture: Stable Video Diffusion fine-tuned per task (frozen VAE encoder/decoder, spatial/temporal attention fine-tuned) to output stereo (two-view) videos; Megapose CAD-based 6D tool tracking on 768x448 frames; stereo resolves 3D pose; inverse kinematics for the rest of the arm.
inputs: Stereo image pair of the scene (two calibrated cameras 45 degrees apart)
outputs: Generated stereo video -> SE(3) tool trajectory executed open-loop
actionRepr: SE(3) 6-DoF tool pose per generated frame (open-loop trajectory)
trainingData: Per-task human tool-use demonstrations: Rotation 371, Scooping 368, Sweeping 356, Push-Shape 727; test objects disjoint from training
whatChangedVsParent: Uses the video model as the policy itself (generate then track a tool) rather than as a simulator or inverse-dynamics input, bridging embodiment via shared tools.
limitations: Limited to visually trackable tool actions; fails under heavy end-effector occlusion; rigid tools limit fine-grained control; video generation cost makes real-time closed-loop control infeasible.
notes: Paper says code and data will be released. Separate model trained per task.

name: Video Language Planning (VLP)
resolvedTitle: Video Language Planning
org: Google DeepMind, MIT, UC Berkeley
problem: LLM/VLM planners reason over text and struggle with physical dynamics, while text-to-video models capture dynamics but only over short horizons; long-horizon visual planning needs both.
keyIdea: Tree search over video and language: a VLM policy proposes next text actions, a text-to-video model rolls out each as short videos, a VLM heuristic scores progress, and the best beams are extended into a long video plan executed by goal-conditioned policies.
architecture: PaLM-E-based VLM policy (prompted or fine-tuned) and VLM heuristic (predicts steps-to-goal); text-to-video diffusion dynamics model (UniPi-style); parallel hill-climbing beam search (A text branches x D video branches x B beams), discarding over-optimistic videos; short-horizon goal-conditioned policy converts each frame subgoal into actions.
inputs: Current image + long-horizon language goal
outputs: Long multimodal (video + language) plan; low-level actions via goal-conditioned policy
trainingData: Language Table, 7-DoF mobile manipulator (RT-1 style) data, 14-DoF bimanual ALOHA, plus co-training on internet-scale data for generalization

headlineResults.benchmark: Language Table 'make a line' plan synthesis

headlineResults.comparedTo: PaLM-E planning, RT-2 fine-tuned for long horizon, UniPi

whatChangedVsParent: Extends UniPi's single text-to-video plan into a forward tree search combining VLM policy/value with video dynamics, so plan quality scales with compute.
limitations: Images are an incomplete world-state representation (no full 3D, no physics/mass); video dynamics model sometimes makes objects appear or teleport.
notes: Execution success-rate numbers per task were not retrieved; see paper Table 2.

name: TesserAct
resolvedTitle: TesserAct: Learning 4D Embodied World Models
org: UMass Amherst, HKUST, Harvard University
problem: Video world models operate in 2D pixels, lacking depth and pose information and producing inconsistent object sizes/shapes, which hurts precise manipulation.
keyIdea: Fine-tune a video diffusion model to jointly generate RGB, depth, and normal (RGB-DN) videos from an image and text instruction, reconstruct temporally consistent 4D point clouds via normal-integrated depth optimization with flow-based consistency losses, and use them with a 3D inverse dynamics model.
architecture: CogVideoX backbone with frozen 3D VAE encoding RGB, depth, normal separately; separate input projectors summed, zero-initialized Conv3D DN output branch; 4D reconstruction with normal integration + consistency and regularization losses (RAFT flow masks); PointNet-based inverse dynamics + text embedding -> MLP -> 7-DoF action.
inputs: Initial RGB (+ depth, normal) image + text instruction
outputs: RGB-DN video; 4D point cloud scene; 7-DoF actions
actionRepr: 7-DoF action from a point-cloud inverse dynamics model between consecutive predicted 4D states
trainingData: RLBench 80k (sim, GT depth), RT-1 Fractal 80k, Bridge 25k, Something-Something V2 100k videos per Table 1 (depth via RollingDepth, normals via Marigold); text describes the dataset as about 200k data points

headlineResults.value: outperforms video-diffusion and image BC baselines on most tasks

whatChangedVsParent: Extends 2D video world models to jointly predict depth and normals, enabling 4D reconstruction and 3D-aware inverse dynamics.
limitations: RGB-DN only captures a single visible surface; a more complete 4D model would need multi-view RGB-DN generation.
notes: RLBench per-task numbers not retrieved; worse than baseline on open microwave and weighing off.

name: Vidar
resolvedTitle: Vidar: Embodied Video Diffusion Model for Generalist Manipulation (earlier title: ...for Generalist Bimanual Manipulation)
org: Tsinghua University, Shengshu Tech
problem: Each new robot embodiment needs large homogeneous demonstrations, and end-to-end pixel-to-action policies degrade under background and viewpoint shifts.
keyIdea: Factor the policy through video: an internet-pretrained video diffusion model is continually pretrained on 750K multi-view bimanual episodes in a unified observation space (robot, camera, task text + aggregated views), fine-tuned with ~20 min of target-robot demos, and decoded to actions by a Masked Inverse Dynamics Model that learns action-relevant pixel masks without labels.
architecture: Rectified-flow video diffusion (Vidu 2.0 for real-world, Wan2.2 5B for simulation; HunyuanVideo 13B also in code); test-time scaling picks the best of K=3 rollouts with GPT-4o; MIDM = U-Net mask predictor + ResNet action regressor with L1 mask sparsity (straight-through).
inputs: Multi-view images + text describing robot, cameras, and task
outputs: Generated multi-view video (60 frames at 8 fps, open-loop) -> joint-position actions via MIDM
actionRepr: per-frame bimanual joint positions + gripper from inverse dynamics on generated video (open-loop)
trainingData: Pretraining on 746,533 episodes from AgiBot-World, RoboMind (Franka, Aloha), RDT (+EgoDex for sim); fine-tuning on 20 min / 232 episodes / 81 tasks on an unseen Aloha setup; RoboTwin 2.0 with 20 or 50 episodes per task
whatChangedVsParent: Adds embodied continual pretraining in a unified multi-view observation space, test-time scaling, and a masked IDM to UniPi's video-then-inverse-dynamics recipe.
notes: Claims SOTA on RoboTwin 2.0 multi-task vs pi0.5 (numbers not retrieved). Generating one 60-frame video takes ~25 s on 8 GPUs. Reported gains in abstract: +58% over VPP and +40% over UniPi. Limitations not retrieved.

name: VidMan
resolvedTitle: VidMan: Exploiting Implicit Dynamics from Video Diffusion Model for Effective Robot Manipulation
org: Sun Yat-sen University, Pengcheng Laboratory, Huawei Noah's Ark Lab
problem: Robot data is small, and directly fitting action data without modeling the observation-action relationship underuses it; GPT-style next-frame policies are slow.
keyIdea: Two-stage training inspired by dual-process theory: first pretrain Open-Sora as a video diffusion model on OXE to predict future frames, then add a layer-wise self-attention adapter so the same network acts as an implicit inverse dynamics model that predicts actions in one pass (no iterative denoising of video).
architecture: Open-Sora video diffusion transformer (12 blocks), history latents channel-concatenated with noisy future latents; stage 2 feeds pure noise, learnable action queries attend through Flamingo-style gated layer-wise adapters, diffusion action head (100 steps).
inputs: History frames (third-person + wrist camera) + language instruction (+ proprioception on CALVIN)
outputs: Action chunk (12 steps on OXE, 10 on CALVIN)
actionRepr: chunk of 10-12 continuous end-effector actions via diffusion action head
trainingData: Stage 1: 25 OXE datasets (Octo mixture), 4-frame clips (2 history + 2 future, interval 3) at 256x256; Stage 2: OXE and CALVIN (language-annotated subset)
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces GR-1's GPT-style next-frame pretraining with multi-frame video diffusion pretraining and repurposes the same backbone as an implicit IDM via adapters.
notes: NeurIPS 2024. Co-training video+action in stage 2 degrades CALVIN to 2.70 (vs 3.42 action-only). Limitations section not retrieved.

name: ARDuP
resolvedTitle: ARDuP: Active Region Video Diffusion for Universal Policies
org: University of Maryland, UT Austin, Caltech, NVIDIA
problem: Video-planning policies (UniPi) generate all pixels uniformly and often focus on wrong regions, e.g., manipulating the wrong object and then recoloring it.
keyIdea: Decompose video planning: first generate the 'active region' (objects to be interacted with) from image + text, then generate latent video conditioned on it, and decode actions directly from latents with a latent inverse dynamics model; active-region labels come automatically from CoTracker motion + SAM.
architecture: Latent active-region diffusion model (T5-XXL text, modified UNet) + latent video diffusion (Stable Diffusion VAE latents 128x128x4, AVDC-style temporal modules, H=6 frames) + convolutional latent IDM producing 7-D actions; open-loop execution.
inputs: Initial frame + task text
outputs: Active-region latent, latent video plan, 7-D action sequence
actionRepr: 7-dim action per frame transition from a latent inverse dynamics model (open-loop)
trainingData: CLIPort: 110k demos over 11 tasks (evaluated on 3 unseen tasks); BridgeData v2 for real-world video plans
whatChangedVsParent: Adds active-region conditioning and moves video planning and inverse dynamics into latent space instead of RGB.
limitations: Pseudo active-region quality depends on CoTracker, which may struggle with long-horizon tasks or complex backgrounds.
notes: UniPi* is the authors' reproduction; Bridge results are qualitative video plans.

name: This&That
resolvedTitle: This&That: Language-Gesture Controlled Video Generation for Robot Planning
org: University of Michigan, University of Washington
problem: Language-only video planners are ambiguous in cluttered scenes (which object, where), and translating video plans into actions is under-explored.
keyIdea: Condition a fine-tuned video diffusion model on deictic language plus 2D pointing gestures (e.g., 'put this there'), then execute with DiVA, a behavior-cloning transformer that cross-attends live observations to the generated video frames.
architecture: Stable Video Diffusion fine-tuned with language conditioning and a ControlNet-like gesture branch (first-frame latents + noisy frames + Gaussian-dilated gesture maps concatenated); gestures auto-annotated by tracking gripper/objects. DiVA: ResNet-18 + TokenLearner (16 tokens/frame), transformer encoder-decoder (ACT-like) outputting action chunks.
inputs: First frame + language + 1-2 gesture points (VDM); generated video plan + live image + EE pose (DiVA)
outputs: Video plan; chunk of robot actions
actionRepr: action chunk a_t:t+k from an ACT-style transformer decoder
trainingData: Bridge V1+V2: 25,767 videos for fine-tuning, 14,735 with gesture annotation; Isaac Gym block pick-and-place demos (scripted) for BC
whatChangedVsParent: Adds sparse gesture conditioning to language-conditioned video planning and replaces inverse dynamics/flow extraction with a video-conditioned BC policy.
limitations: Object shapes can change over time (no 3D constraints); limited to short modular tasks; gesture alone can be 3D-ambiguous; policy experiments only in simulation (no real robot).

name: GR-MG
resolvedTitle: GR-MG: Leveraging Partially-Annotated Data via Multi-Modal Goal-Conditioned Policy
org: Institute of Automation CAS (NLPR/MAIS), UCAS, ByteDance Research
problem: Fully annotated robot data (actions + text) is scarce, while partially annotated data (human videos without actions, robot play without text) is abundant but hard to use; prior goal-image methods ignore task progress and rely solely on possibly wrong generated goals.
keyIdea: Generate a subgoal image with a progress-guided image-editing diffusion model (task progress appended to the text) and condition a GPT-style policy on both the text and the generated goal image, so each module can train on a different kind of partially annotated data.
architecture: Goal generator: InstructPix2Pix with T5-Base text encoding including discretized progress (10 bins), regenerated every n steps; policy: GR-1-style GPT transformer (Ego4D video-pretrained) with MAE goal-image tokens, [PROG]/[OBS]/[ACT] query tokens, and a cVAE action-trajectory head.
inputs: Text instruction, static + wrist camera image history, robot state history (6-DoF EE pose + gripper)
outputs: Action trajectory (k steps), task progress, future images
actionRepr: action trajectory of k steps (end-effector pose + gripper) decoded by a cVAE transformer head
trainingData: CALVIN ABC (~18k annotated trajectories + unlabeled play, 1M frames without text); real Kinova Gen-3: 18k demos over 37 tasks; goal generator additionally uses Something-Something-V2 and RT-1 videos
whatChangedVsParent: Adds progress-conditioned goal-image generation to SuSIE and conditions a GR-1-style policy on both text and goal image, enabling training on text-less and action-less data.
limitations: Few-shot novel skills bottlenecked by the policy (goal images are accurate but policy fails to follow); two modules trained independently; no depth information.
notes: RA-L 2024. Code and checkpoints released on project page.

name: 3DFlowAction
resolvedTitle: 3DFlowAction: Learning Cross-Embodiment Manipulation from 3D Flow World Model
org: South China University of Technology, Tencent Robotics X, HKUST, Pazhou Laboratory
problem: Robot datasets use inconsistent action spaces in simple scenes, and video world models are not object-centric and plan only in 2D, hurting generalization and 3D motions like rotations.
keyIdea: Learn a 3D object-flow world model from large human and robot video data (ManiFlow-110k), verify predicted flow by rendering the predicted final object state and asking GPT-4o, then solve robot actions by optimization that makes object keypoints follow the predicted 3D flow.
architecture: AnimateDiff-style flow generator (SD v1.5 with LoRA + motion module trained from scratch; CLIP encodes image/text, sinusoidal encoding of initial points; 3D flow input bypasses the VAE); SVD rigid transform for flow-guided rendering; GPT-4o + AnyGrasp task-aware grasp selection with IK reachability; Dual Annealing + SLSQP optimization for SE(3) end-effector actions.
inputs: RGB(-D) observation + language instruction + initial object points
outputs: 3D object flow (T x H x W x 4: u, v, depth, visibility); chunk of end-effector SE(3) poses
actionRepr: chunk of end-effector SE(3) poses solved by constrained optimization on predicted 3D flow (no learned action head)
trainingData: ManiFlow-110k: 110k 3D flow instances auto-extracted (Grounding-SAM2, CoTracker3, DepthAnythingV2) from BridgeV2 (27%), RH20T-Human (27%), RT-1 (18%), DROID (13%), AgiBot-World (8%), LIBERO (4%), HOI4D (3%); 10-30 human-hand demos per downstream task

headlineResults.benchmark: 4 real tasks (pour tea, insert pen, hang cup, open drawer), 10 trials each
headlineResults.comparedTo: w/o closed-loop rendering 50.0%, w/o large-scale pretraining 30.0%

whatChangedVsParent: Moves Im2Flow2Act-style flow generation from 2D to 3D, pretrains on a large multi-source flow dataset, and replaces the learned policy with flow-constrained optimization plus VLM verification.
limitations: 3D flow struggles with flexible/deformable objects (occlusion, complex motion); non-rigid deformation can prevent the action optimizer from producing valid actions.
notes: Compared against AVDC, ReKep, Im2Flow2Act*, pi0; baseline numbers not retrieved. Claims cross-embodiment transfer without hardware-specific training. Flow model trained ~2 days on 64 V100s.

name: NovaFlow
resolvedTitle: NovaFlow: Zero-Shot Manipulation via Actionable Flow from Generated Videos
org: Robotics and AI Institute, Brown University
problem: Zero-shot manipulation methods either assume in-distribution tasks or need embodiment-matched fine-tuning data; VLAs face a data bottleneck and trained flow generators generalize less than internet video models.
keyIdea: Generate a task video with an off-the-shelf video model, distill it into actionable 3D object flow with pretrained perception (depth, 3D tracking, grounding), then convert flow to actions: Kabsch rigid transforms + grasp for rigid/articulated objects, or particle-dynamics MPC tracking for deformables. No demonstrations or robot training.
architecture: Video generator (Wan2.1 or Veo) -> MegaSaM monocular video depth (calibrated to initial depth) -> TAPIP3D 3D point tracking -> Grounding DINO + SAM2 object grounding; VLM (Gemini) rejection sampling over candidate flows; GraspGen grasp proposals; trajectory optimization (PyRoki); PhysTwin-style particle model for deformables.
inputs: Single RGB-D observation + task description (optional goal image)
outputs: 3D object flow; end-effector trajectory tracked open-loop
actionRepr: end-effector SE(3) trajectory from object flow via Kabsch + grasp transform, then trajectory optimization (open-loop)
trainingData: None for the task (zero-shot); uses pretrained video and perception models

headlineResults.value: highest among zero-shot methods and above DP trained on 10-30 demos
headlineResults.comparedTo: AVDC*, VidBot, Diffusion Policy (10/30 demos), UniPi IDM

headlineResults.benchmark: Block insertion (Wan2.1 with goal image / without; Veo without)

parents: Robotic Manipulation by Imitating Generated Videos (Patel et al.)
whatChangedVsParent: Uses large pretrained (internet) video models instead of self-trained flow/video models and lifts to 3D object flow with off-the-shelf perception, extending to deformables via particle dynamics.
limitations: Main bottleneck is physical execution (grasping, unexpected dynamics) under an open-loop plan; runtime dominated by video generation and 3D lifting.
notes: Evaluated on Franka tabletop and Spot mobile manipulator; tasks: hang mug, insert block, cup on saucer, water plant, open drawer, straighten rope. Per-task success numbers are in a figure, not retrieved as text.

name: Dream2Flow
resolvedTitle: Dream2Flow: Bridging Video Generation and Open-World Manipulation with 3D Object Flow
org: Stanford University
problem: Off-the-shelf video generators synthesize plausible (mostly human-hand) interactions, but translating those pixels into low-level robot actions is hard because of the embodiment gap and different action spaces.
keyIdea: Use 3D object flow reconstructed from a generated video as the interface: manipulation becomes object-trajectory tracking, separating what state change should happen from how a given embodiment achieves it.
architecture: Zero-shot pipeline of off-the-shelf models: image-to-video generator (Veo 3, Wan2.1, Kling 2.1 compared) -> SpatialTrackerV2 video depth (scale/shift aligned to real depth) -> Grounding DINO + SAM 2 mask -> CoTracker3 point tracks lifted to 3D. Actions come from trajectory optimization (random shooting with a learned particle dynamics model for Push-T; PyRoki with rigid-grasp dynamics and AnyGrasp/HaMeR-guided grasp in the real world) or RL (SAC with 3D-flow reward).
inputs: Language instruction + initial RGB-D observation with known camera calibration
outputs: Robot action sequence (push primitives, absolute end-effector poses, or delta EE/joint commands from an RL policy)
actionRepr: No learned policy head; actions obtained by optimizing to track a 3D object flow (T x n x 3 point trajectories)
trainingData: No task-specific demonstrations or training for the video/perception stack; a particle dynamics model is learned for simulated Push-T and SAC policies are trained in simulation for door opening.

headlineResults.value: 12 video-generation failures, 4 flow-extraction failures, 4 robot-execution failures

whatChangedVsParent: Instead of tracking a 6D object pose or learning a flow-conditioned policy, it reconstructs dense 3D object flow from a generated video and tracks it with a planner or RL, covering rigid, articulated, deformable and granular objects.
limitations: Bottlenecks are video artifacts (object morphing, hallucinated objects), occlusion/rotation-induced tracking dropouts, and grasp-selection mismatches; video models not fine-tuned on robots give implausible interactions when the robot is in frame, so the robot is removed from the initial image.
notes: Real-world tasks: Put Bread in Bowl, Open Oven, Cover Bowl (10 trials each with Veo 3); simulated Push-T and Robosuite Open Door. Per-task real-world success numbers are in Table I, which was not in the retrieved pages. Veo 3 produced fewer articulation-direction errors than Kling 2.1 / Wan2.1.

name: RIGVid
resolvedTitle: Robotic Manipulation by Imitating Generated Videos Without Physical Demonstrations
org: UIUC; UC Irvine; Columbia University
problem: Learning from video usually needs large datasets with domain gaps or carefully matched demonstrations; prior video-generation-for-robotics work still relies on robot data or task-specific training.
keyIdea: Generate a task- and scene-conditioned video with an off-the-shelf video diffusion model, filter it with a VLM, extract the object's 6D pose trajectory, and retarget it to the robot — no physical demonstrations or robot training.
architecture: Video diffusion model (Kling etc.) -> GPT-4o filter on 4 sampled frames (up to 5 regenerations) -> monocular depth per frame with scale alignment -> FoundationPose 6D object tracking (needs object mesh) -> grasp then object-to-end-effector retargeting with real-time closed-loop re-tracking.
inputs: Initial RGB-D image + free-form language command
outputs: 6-DoF end-effector trajectory
actionRepr: Retargeted 6D object pose trajectory assuming a fixed end-effector-to-object transform
trainingData: None (zero robot data; uses pretrained models only)
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces sparse point tracks/optical flow/feature fields (Gen2Act, Track2Act, AVDC, 4D-DPM) with model-based 6D pose tracking on a VLM-filtered generated video, and drops all behavior cloning.
limitations: Video generation is computationally expensive; FoundationPose needs a precomputed object mesh (mesh-free alternatives too slow for real time); a fixed grasp transform is assumed.
notes: Four main real tasks: pour water, lift lid, place spatula, sweep trash. Paper claims filtered generated videos are as effective as real demonstrations and that success improves with generation quality; it outperforms ReKep and the trajectory-extraction baselines (Fig. 9, numbers only in the figure). Preliminary extensions: wiping, mixing, ironing, bimanual shoe placement.

name: LVP
resolvedTitle: Large Video Planner Enables Generalizable Robot Control
org: MIT; UC Berkeley; Harvard
problem: VLAs transfer MLLM knowledge to actions asymmetrically on scarce robot data and generalize poorly to new tasks; the paper explores video pretraining as the primary modality for a robot foundation model.
keyIdea: Train a foundation-scale video model as a generative planner that produces zero-shot video plans (human hands doing the task) from an image and instruction, then extract and retarget hand motion to robots.
architecture: Latent video diffusion: temporally causal 3D VAE + Diffusion Forcing Transformer initialised from Wan 2.1 14B, trained with flow matching, per-frame noise levels (random 0–6 latent context frames), History Guidance plus text CFG. Action extraction: HaMeR hand pose + MegaSaM 4D reconstruction + Dex-Retargeting + cuRobo IK.
inputs: One or a few observation frames + text instruction
outputs: Video plan; after post-processing, robot wrist SE(3) trajectories and finger joint trajectories
actionRepr: Wrist pose trajectory + dexterous-hand joint angles retargeted from generated human hand motion (also parallel-jaw gripper retargeting); executed open-loop
trainingData: Curated open internet-scale dataset of human activity and robot task-demonstration videos (released).
whatChangedVsParent: Fine-tunes Wan 2.1 into a Diffusion-Forcing video planner with history guidance on embodied-decision data, emphasizing physical consistency and instruction following over content creation.
limitations: A single video plan takes several minutes on one A100 (not real-time); 4D reconstruction and hand-pose estimation errors cause failures; retargeting to low-DoF grippers is hard; execution is open-loop.
notes: Model, dataset and training code released. Real-robot comparisons vs pi0 and OpenVLA (gripper tasks only) in Table 8, not retrieved. Hunyuan baseline listed as 'Hunyuan I2V 14B' in the table but '13B' in the text.

name: UD-VLA
resolvedTitle: Unified Diffusion VLA: Vision-Language-Action Model via Joint Discrete Denoising Diffusion Process
org: HKUST (Guangzhou); Westlake University; Zhejiang University; Monash University
problem: Unified VLAs that also predict future images either use external expert encoders/decoders or treat image generation and action prediction as separate processes, limiting synergy between foresight and action.
keyIdea: Jointly denoise future-image tokens and action tokens in a single synchronous discrete (masked) diffusion trajectory (JD3P), so actions are iteratively refined under guidance of the evolving predicted future image.
architecture: Single transformer over a unified discrete token space (Emu3-style text tokens, VQ image tokens, FAST action tokens) with hybrid attention: bidirectional within the future-image block and within the action block, causal across blocks (action attends to image, not vice versa). Two-stage training: world-model post-training on future-image prediction, then JD3P fine-tuning on robot data. Inference uses KV-cache, prefilled special tokens, modality-restricted decoding and confidence-based decoding.
inputs: Language instruction + current image
outputs: Future image tokens + action tokens
actionRepr: Variable-length FAST discrete action tokens, decoded by masked discrete diffusion jointly with future-image tokens
trainingData: Stage (i) video/future-image post-training; stage (ii) robot action datasets (CALVIN, LIBERO, SimplerEnv-Bridge); real world 200 trajectories per task category recorded at 15 Hz.
whatChangedVsParent: Unlike UniVLA/WorldVLA which only decode actions at inference, UD-VLA explicitly generates future images and actions together in one joint discrete diffusion process.
limitations: Generated future frames lack visual fidelity (arm and background details) due to no large-scale generative pretraining and few image tokens.
notes: ICLR 2026. Ablation: no visual generation 4.21 vs future image 4.64 avg len on CALVIN. Real world: UR5e + Inspire 6-DoF hand, >80% success, beats GR00T N1 and UniVLA. Backbone likely Emu3 (text tokenization 'same design as Emu3'), but parameter count not stated in retrieved pages.

name: RynnVLA-002
resolvedTitle: RynnVLA-002: A Unified Vision-Language-Action and World Model
org: DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group; Hupan Lab; Zhejiang University
problem: Standard VLAs have actions only on the output side, no imagination of how the world evolves and no explicit physics; world models predict the future but cannot output actions.
keyIdea: An 'action world model': one autoregressive backbone with a shared token space trained on both VLA data (predict actions) and world-model data (predict next image from image+action), so the two capabilities mutually improve.
architecture: Initialized from Chameleon; separate image (VQ-GAN), text, state and action tokenizers sharing one vocabulary. Discrete action chunks use an action attention mask (each action attends only to text/vision, not prior actions); a lightweight continuous Action Transformer head with learnable action queries outputs whole chunks in parallel (L1 loss). Evolution of the authors' WorldVLA.
inputs: Language goal, proprioceptive state, observation history (M=2 frames; wrist + front cameras)
outputs: Action chunk (discrete tokens or continuous) or, when queried as world model, next image
actionRepr: Chunk of K=5 or 10 delta EE actions [Δx, Δθ, ΔGrip]; discrete tokens with action attention masking, or continuous via Action Transformer head
trainingData: LIBERO demos (filtered, no robot-data pretraining); real world: LeRobot SO100 teleop demos (248 block-in-circle, 249 strawberries-in-cup).
controlRateHz: Continuous head up to 48.20 Hz inference frequency (chunk 10, no wrist cam, no history); 15.78 Hz with wrist cam + history

headlineResults.benchmark: Real SO100 'place block in circle', multi-target

whatChangedVsParent: Over WorldVLA it adds a continuous Action Transformer head (smoother, faster, better real-world generalization) on top of discrete joint modeling with action attention masking.
limitations: The purely discrete autoregressive variant rarely succeeds in the real world (overfits on small data, jerky chunks, slow inference); model is queried separately as VLA or world model and does not roll out images for control.
notes: Code at github.com/alibaba-damo-academy/RynnVLA-002. Abstract claims the integrated world model boosts real-world success by 50%. Parameter count not stated in retrieved pages (Chameleon base; WorldVLA used 7B Chameleon).

name: DreamVLA
resolvedTitle: DreamVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Dreamed with Comprehensive World Knowledge
org: SJTU; EIT Ningbo; Tsinghua; Galbot; PKU; UIUC; USTC
problem: VLAs that forecast future images waste capacity on redundant pixels and lack explicit spatial (3D) and high-level semantic knowledge of future states.
keyIdea: Forecast a compact 'world embedding' of comprehensive future knowledge — dynamic regions (optical flow), depth, and DINOv2/SAM semantics — via learnable <dream> queries, then use it for inverse-dynamics action generation with a diffusion transformer.
architecture: Frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 text encoder, MAE ViT-B visual encoder with Perceiver Resampler, MLP state encoder; GPT-2 Medium (~345M) backbone with <dream> and <action> queries; block-wise structured attention to keep dynamic/depth/semantic queries disentangled; lightweight ViT decoders for each knowledge type (training only); DiT action head (10 diffusion steps).
inputs: Language instruction, RGB (static + wrist views), proprioceptive state
outputs: n-step action sequence (future-knowledge heads used only in training)
actionRepr: n-step chunk of 7-D continuous actions (6-D EE displacement + gripper) via DiT diffusion head
trainingData: Pretrained on language-free CALVIN split and full DROID; LIBERO-90 pretraining for LIBERO; then fine-tuning per target dataset.
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces pixel-level future-frame prediction (Seer/GR-1/UP-VLA) with forecasting of dynamic regions, depth and semantic features, plus structured attention and a DiT action head.
limitations: Mainly parallel-gripper manipulation, RGB-centric data, limited geometric and material diversity in training scenes.
notes: Paper links code and Hugging Face. Ablation: dynamic-region prediction gives the largest gain; depth or semantics alone can hurt. 'openWeights' true based on HF link on title page.

name: UniVLA (Wang et al.)
resolvedTitle: Unified Vision-Language-Action Model
org: CASIA; BAAI; Tsinghua; HKISI
problem: Language-centric VLAs map static images to actions via late fusion, missing the temporal and causal structure of visual observations and unable to exploit large-scale video.
keyIdea: Represent vision, language and action as discrete tokens in one vocabulary and model interleaved sequences autoregressively; post-train as a world model on robot videos (vision-token loss only) before action fine-tuning.
architecture: Encoder-free 8.5B autoregressive transformer identical to Emu3; VQ image tokenizer (8x spatial compression); FAST (DCT) action tokenizer with 1024-token vocab replacing last 1024 language IDs; boi/eoi/boa/eoa delimiters.
inputs: Instruction + interleaved image observations (third-person + wrist)
