outputs: Action tokens (also future vision tokens / text in other tasks)
actionRepr: FAST DCT-compressed discrete tokens for action chunks (chunk 10 on CALVIN/LIBERO, 5 on SimplerEnv), relative actions
trainingData: Post-training on 622K robot videos (world model, no actions), then fine-tuning on CALVIN, LIBERO, Bridge-WidowX; also ALOHA real robot and driving.
whatChangedVsParent: Moves from VLM late fusion to a native unified token space and shows world-model post-training on video is the most effective post-training for downstream policy learning.
notes: Distinct from UniVLA (Bu et al., 'Learning to Act Anywhere with Task-centric Latent Actions', 2505.06111). Only action tokens are decoded at inference (UD-VLA paper notes this). Limitations not retrieved.

name: VLA-JEPA
resolvedTitle: VLA-JEPA: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Model with Latent World Model
org: USTC; Zhongguancun Academy; SJTU; Tsinghua; EIT Ningbo; UCAS; Nankai
problem: Latent-action pretraining from video stays anchored to pixel variation: biased toward appearance, vulnerable to camera/nuisance motion, prone to future-information leakage, and needs fragile multi-stage pipelines.
keyIdea: Leakage-free JEPA-style state prediction: the VLM sees only the current observation and emits latent-action tokens; a latent world model must predict V-JEPA2 embeddings of future frames (future used only as target), giving a two-stage recipe (JEPA pretraining, then action-head fine-tuning).
architecture: Qwen3-VL-2B backbone with <latent_i> and <action> tokens; V-JEPA2 encoder as world-state encoder (multi-view concatenation); 12-layer autoregressive time-causal latent world model; flow-matching DiT-B action head (16 layers, 4 denoising steps).
inputs: Multi-view images (2 views), language instruction, 8-D state
outputs: Latent actions (pretraining) and continuous robot actions
actionRepr: Chunk of 7 future 7-D actions (EE delta position + delta axis-angle + gripper) via flow matching
trainingData: Human videos (action-free) plus DROID (76K trajectories) for pretraining; fine-tuning on LIBERO (~2K demos), Fractal and BridgeV2 for SimplerEnv, 100 real demos over 3 tasks.
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces frame-difference latent actions (LAPA/UniVLA) that see future frames with JEPA latent-state prediction where future frames are targets only.
notes: Code, project page and Hugging Face weights released (huggingface.co/ginwind/VLA-JEPA). Claims best average on LIBERO, best Google Robot average and second-best WidowX on SimplerEnv, best on 5/7 LIBERO-Plus perturbations; exact main-table numbers not in retrieved pages. Closely related author group to DreamVLA (Zhang, Qi, Jin).

name: JEPA-VLA
resolvedTitle: JEPA-VLA: Video Predictive Embedding is Needed for VLA Models
org: Tsinghua University; Huawei Noah's Ark Lab
problem: VLAs have low sample efficiency and weak generalization, which the authors trace to image-pretrained visual encoders (DINO, SigLIP) that capture task-relevant state poorly and provide no policy prior about how scenes evolve.
keyIdea: Plug frozen V-JEPA 2 video-predictive embeddings into existing VLAs; probing shows they encode task-relevant state and future state changes better while ignoring nuisance lighting/background.
architecture: Frozen V-JEPA 2 encoder on the two most recent frames; fused either by early fusion (projected tokens concatenated to the VLA sequence, for VLAs without robot pretraining) or Flamingo-style gated cross-attention inserted every 8 decoder layers (for robot-pretrained VLAs such as OpenVLA-OFT).
inputs: Language instruction, third-person image(s), proprioception, V-JEPA 2 features of recent frames
outputs: Action chunk (depends on host VLA)
actionRepr: Inherits host VLA: 256-bin discrete tokens (Chameleon-based basic VLA) or continuous chunks with L1 regression (OpenVLA-OFT)
trainingData: LIBERO (1/10 of data for basic-VLA experiments; full for OpenVLA-OFT), RoboTwin2.0 (50 clean trajectories/task), real Piper arm pick-and-place (22 trajectories = 1/5 subset, and full).
whatChangedVsParent: Adds video-predictive V-JEPA 2 features to an existing VLA (no world-model training data) instead of relying only on image-pretrained encoders.
limitations: Fusion strategy is simple; more principled mechanisms for integrating predictive embeddings remain unexplored.
notes: Not a generative world model: uses a frozen predictive encoder as representation. Also reports CortexBench: V-JEPA 2 ViT-L 90.4% MetaWorld avg vs VC-1 88.8%.

name: DUST
resolvedTitle: Dual-Stream Diffusion for World-Model Augmented Vision-Language-Action Model
org: KAIST; RLWRLD
problem: World-model-augmented VLAs either force actions and images into one joint diffusion latent (modality mismatch) or use one-way causal conditioning that blocks bidirectional knowledge transfer.
keyIdea: A dual-stream multimodal diffusion transformer keeps separate action and future-vision-embedding streams that meet only in shared attention, trained with independent per-modality noise levels and decoupled flow-matching losses; asynchronous sampling gives more denoising steps to vision for test-time scaling.
architecture: Frozen Eagle-2 VLM (layer-12 features) conditions a diffusion action expert of 12 MMDiT blocks + 4 modality-specific DiT blocks per stream; world-model target is SigLIP-2 future-image embedding (256 tokens pooled to 64); built on GR00T-N1.5 design.
inputs: Current image, task instruction, robot state
outputs: Action chunk + predicted future observation embedding
actionRepr: Chunk of 16 action tokens via flow matching (Euler, N_A=4 steps); real Franka uses joint positions + binary gripper
trainingData: RoboCasa (100/300/1000 demos per task, 24 tasks), GR-1 humanoid (300/1000 demos per task), 60 real Franka demos per task; transfer with BridgeV2 action-free video pretraining and GR-1 + EgoDex (46k episodes) joint training.
whatChangedVsParent: Versus FLARE's implicit alignment and PAD's single joint diffusion, DUST explicitly diffuses future embeddings in a separate stream with independent noise, enabling bidirectional forward/inverse-dynamics learning.
notes: ICML 2026. Asynchronous sampling adds 2–5% (abstract) / 2–6% (intro). Positions itself as orthogonal to video-backbone WAMs (Cosmos Policy, Fast-WAM, DreamZero). CALVIN/LIBERO results in appendix, not retrieved.

name: FRAPPE
resolvedTitle: FRAPPE: Infusing World Modeling into Generalist Policies via Multiple Future Representation Alignment
org: Zhejiang University; Westlake University; HKUST (GZ); SCUT; ShanghaiTech; Tsinghua
problem: World-modeling policies over-emphasize pixel reconstruction (hurting semantics and OOD generalization) and suffer error accumulation when relying on predicted future observations at inference; single-encoder representation alignment carries that encoder's inductive bias.
keyIdea: Implicit world modeling by aligning learnable future-prefix tokens with future-observation embeddings from multiple visual foundation models, via two stages: mid-training against a distilled Theia-style teacher, then parallel 'Mixture-of-Prefix-and-LoRA' experts each aligned to a different VFM and merged by a router.
architecture: RDT-1B diffusion transformer backbone (SigLIP vision, T5 language); learnable future prefixes with cosine alignment loss; post-training adds M=3 prefix+LoRA experts aligned to CLIP (400M), DINOv2 (142M) and ViT (300M), a router with load-balance loss and label smoothing, shared MLP action head. No VFMs used at inference.
inputs: Current observation, language instruction, proprioception
outputs: Action chunk
actionRepr: Diffusion-denoised action chunk (RDT action space)
params: RDT-1B base (only prefixes and LoRAs trainable in post-training)
trainingData: RoboTwin 2.0: 50 Easy-setting trajectories per task, 15k mid-training + 5k post-training steps; real world: robot teleop plus action-free egocentric human data (task-specific and 1k+ hours web-scale).
whatChangedVsParent: Extends FLARE-style single-target future representation alignment to multiple VFM targets with parallel LoRA experts on a diffusion policy.
notes: Model on Hugging Face (hhhJB/frappe) and code released. Claims highest average success on RoboTwin 2.0 Easy vs DP, VPP, RDT, pi0, pi0.5 and 10–15% gain from human videos when teleop data is scarce; table numbers not in retrieved pages. Same group as UD-VLA.

name: LDA-1B
resolvedTitle: LDA-1B: Scaling Latent Dynamics Action Model via Universal Embodied Data Ingestion
org: Peking University; Galbot; CASIA; BAAI; Tsinghua; Sun Yat-sen; NVIDIA
problem: Behavior-cloning foundation models discard the dynamics knowledge in heterogeneous, mixed-quality embodied data; Unified World Model approaches use data coarsely, lack large standardized datasets, and predict in pixel space.
keyIdea: Scale a Unified-World-Model-style latent dynamics action model by assigning data roles by quality (expert data trains everything, low-quality trajectories train dynamics/forecasting, actionless video trains visual forecasting) and predicting future DINO latents rather than pixels.
architecture: Frozen Qwen3-VL for conditioning and frozen DINO encoder for targets; multimodal diffusion transformer (MM-DiT) with separate action and visual experts sharing self-attention, language cross-attention, AdaLN task embeddings for 4 objectives (policy, forward dynamics, inverse dynamics, visual forecasting) and register tokens; flow-matching loss.
inputs: Egocentric RGB observation, language instruction
outputs: Action chunk and/or future DINO latent features depending on task embedding
actionRepr: Hand-centric chunk: delta wrist pose + gripper width or finger keypoints; actions at 10 Hz, visual latents at 3 Hz
trainingData: EI-30k: >30k hours — 8.03k h real robot, 8.6k h simulated robot, 7.2k h human demos with actions, 10k h actionless human video; 4,608 H800 GPU-hours pretraining.
whatChangedVsParent: Versus UWM, it predicts DINO latents instead of VAE pixels, uses an MM-DiT with task embeddings, and ingests 30k hours of quality-labeled heterogeneous data at 1B scale.
limitations: Relies on fixed DINO visual features and predominantly egocentric camera viewpoints, which may limit generalization to new viewpoints and other sensory modalities.
notes: Code and data at pku-epic.github.io/LDA. Abstract: up to 21%/48%/23% gains over pi0.5 on contact-rich/dexterous/long-horizon tasks, +10% from using 30% low-quality trajectories. The '1B' refers to trainable parameters; Fig. 1 says 1.6B parameters.

name: DiT4DiT
resolvedTitle: DiT4DiT: Jointly Modeling Video Dynamics and Actions for Generalizable Robot Control
org: Mondo Robotics; HKUST (GZ); HKUST
problem: VLA representations come from static image-text pretraining, leaving physical dynamics to be learned from limited action data; prior uses of video models are multi-stage rather than end-to-end.
keyIdea: Cascade a video Diffusion Transformer and an action Diffusion Transformer end-to-end: intermediate denoising features of the video DiT (hooked at a fixed flow timestep) condition the action DiT, trained jointly with a dual flow-matching objective and decoupled 'tri-timestep' scheme.
architecture: Video DiT initialized from Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B (causal video VAE, Cosmos-Reason1 text embeddings) used as feature extractor via forward hooks; action DiT adapted from GR00T-N1 (AdaLN, cross-attention to video features, proprioception, learnable future tokens). Tri-timestep: uniform τ_v for video loss, fixed τ_f for feature extraction, Beta-sampled τ_a for actions.
inputs: Current observation frame(s) (single egocentric camera in real world), language goal, proprioceptive state
outputs: Action trajectory (future frames generated optionally)
actionRepr: Continuous action chunk (joint positions / EEF pose) via flow matching
trainingData: Trained from scratch on benchmark data (LIBERO, RoboCasa-GR1 24 tasks), real Unitree G1 demonstrations; no external action data.
whatChangedVsParent: Unlike mimic-video (frozen video backbone + separate decoder at a fixed flow time), video and action DiTs are trained jointly end-to-end so the action model learns which generative features to use.
limitations: Video backbone lowers control rate to 6 Hz on an A100 (vs 13 Hz for GR00T-N1.5).
notes: Abstract states code and models released at dit4dit.github.io. Real-world G1 tasks also: Stack Cup 60% vs 25%, Move Spoon 40% vs 15%, Drawer Interaction 90%, Box Packing 50%.

name: GigaWorld-Policy
resolvedTitle: GigaWorld-Policy: An Efficient Action-Centered World–Action Model
org: GigaAI
problem: World-action models that roll out future video at inference are slow (iterative video sampling) and propagate video-prediction errors into action decoding.
keyIdea: Action-centered WAM: one causal diffusion transformer predicts actions from the current context and, in the same model, action-conditioned future frames as dense training supervision; at inference the video branch is optional, so actions can be decoded alone.
architecture: Wan 2.2 5B DiT backbone; three camera views composited into one image; shared transformer blocks for all tokens with type-specific positional encodings; blockwise causal mask (actions attend to state+obs only; future-video tokens attend to state, obs and actions); KV cache; curriculum: web-video init → embodied pretraining (robot + egocentric human video, video loss only) → target-robot post-training.
inputs: Multi-view RGB (left/front/right), language instruction, proprioceptive state
outputs: Action chunk; optionally sparse future frames
actionRepr: Chunk of p=48 continuous actions via flow matching; future frames predicted every Δ=12 steps (training supervision)
trainingData: Wan 2.2 web-video init; embodied pretraining on real robot recordings + large-scale egocentric human video; RoboTwin 2.0: 2,500 clean + 25,000 randomized demos over 50 tasks.
controlRateHz: 360 ms per inference on A100 (action-only mode)
whatChangedVsParent: Makes future-video generation a training-only regularizer with a causal mask so actions never depend on generated frames, giving ~9x lower latency than Motus.
notes: CONFLICT (internal): RoboTwin average reported as 0.87 clean in main Table 2 but 0.86 in appendix Table 8. Claims 95% relative improvement over pi0.5 at matched speed on RoboTwin 2.0.

name: X-WAM
resolvedTitle: Unified 4D World Action Modeling from Video Priors with Asynchronous Denoising
org: Tsinghua University; Xiaomi Robotics; Peking University; CASIA
problem: Unified world action models (UWM, Motus, etc.) are confined to 2D pixel space without 3D geometry, and decoupled per-modality noise sampling mismatches training and asynchronous inference.
keyIdea: A unified 4D world action model that jointly predicts multi-view RGB-D video, states and actions from a video-diffusion prior, adding depth via a lightweight branch of replicated final DiT blocks and using Asynchronous Noise Sampling (actions decoded in few steps; coupled training noise so t_video ≥ t_action).
architecture: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B DiT with causal VAE; MLP state/action projectors; learnable view embeddings; final M blocks replicated as an interleaved depth branch with unilateral cross-attention (depth reads RGB branch, not vice versa); wrist-camera pose derived from predicted end-effector pose; UniPC schedulers with separate step sizes per modality.
inputs: Multi-view RGB observation (1 frame), initial proprioceptive state, language instruction
outputs: 8 future RGB and depth frames, 8 future states, 32 future actions
actionRepr: Chunk of K=32 delta end-effector pose + gripper actions (dual-arm interface) via flow matching, decoded in few asynchronous steps (5 in ablations)
trainingData: Pretrained on >5,800 hours of real and simulated robot data; RoboTwin 2.0: 50 clean + 500 randomized trajectories on 50 tasks.
controlRateHz: ~300 ms per action chunk with 8 denoising steps
whatChangedVsParent: Adds explicit depth/4D prediction and replaces independent per-modality noise sampling with coupled asynchronous noise sampling.
limitations: Fixed-length context without history or autoregressive rollout (weak for long-horizon task-progress tracking); higher inference latency than dedicated policies or lightweight WAMs like Fast-WAM.
notes: Real-world dual-arm earphone packing vs XR-0: e.g., pack 2 earphones 93.8% vs 79.1% progress.

name: BagelVLA
resolvedTitle: BagelVLA: Enhancing Long-Horizon Manipulation via Interleaved Vision-Language-Action Generation
org: Tsinghua University; ByteDance Seed
problem: VLAs typically use either linguistic planning or visual forecasting in isolation, which underperforms on multi-stage long-horizon manipulation; full image generation for foresight is slow.
keyIdea: Interleave textual subtask planning, keyframe visual forecasting and action generation in one Mixture-of-Transformers model initialized from Bagel; Residual Flow Guidance starts keyframe denoising from the current observation and conditions actions on a single denoising step.
architecture: MoT with understanding and generation experts (Qwen2.5-7B architecture, from Bagel; SigLIP2 ViT for understanding, FLUX VAE for generation) plus a ~2B action expert (Qwen2.5-style with 1/5 MLP width); dual flow matching for keyframe and actions; KV-cache and asynchronous action generation.
inputs: Global instruction, current multi-view observation, proprioception
outputs: Subtask text, predicted keyframe image, action chunk
actionRepr: Continuous action chunks via flow matching conditioned on single-step (RFG) keyframe features
trainingData: Stage 1: 2.98M VQA pairs, 310k human-hand episodes, 146k + 297k open-source robot episodes, 75k self-collected robot episodes (subtask/keyframe annotated, partly by Seed-1.5-VL); Stage 2 action fine-tuning; real Aloha-AgileX: 3,000 basic + 1,500 long-horizon demos.
whatChangedVsParent: Adds explicit textual subtask planning on top of visual-foresight VLAs and replaces full keyframe synthesis with one-step residual flow guidance.
notes: Distinct from WorldBagel (Georgia Tech, 2607.03461), which also builds on BAGEL but adds action-conditioned world modeling and Fourier action tokens. RoboTwin table numbers not in retrieved pages.

name: CoVAR
resolvedTitle: CoVAR: Co-generation of Video and Action for Robotic Manipulation via Multi-Modal Diffusion
org: University of Freiburg; LMU Munich / MCML; TU Munich; Huawei Heisenberg Research Center (Munich)
problem: Video diffusion models lack paired action labels; two-stage video-then-IDM pipelines limit cross-modal sharing, while joint single-DiT models must re-learn a joint latent space and underperform with limited data.
keyIdea: Attach a dedicated parallel action DiT to a pretrained video DiT and let them exchange information through Bridge Attention (separate Q/K/V per modality, joint attention over concatenated tokens), co-generating text-conditioned video–action pairs.
architecture: OpenSora-1.2 video DiT (1.1B) + new action modules (0.3B): MLP action encoder, action DiT with text cross-attention, Bridge Attention, UNet action decoder; multi-modal rectified flow; optional transformer action-refinement model for low-resolution datasets.
inputs: Initial image, initial robot joint states, text instruction
outputs: 35-frame video and paired action/joint-state sequence
actionRepr: Sequence of T joint-state actions (T×L) co-generated with video via rectified flow; open-loop, interpolated to 100 Hz on the real robot
trainingData: CALVIN (~20k demos, ABCD), LIBERO-90 (50 demos per task), 1K self-collected real UR5 demos; refinement model fine-tuned on 450 LIBERO pairs.
controlRateHz: ~4 s to generate a 35-frame sequence (30 steps); actions interpolated to 100 Hz

headlineResults.benchmark: CALVIN drawer / cabinet / light / pick / push
Real UR5 nut / screw / dowel picking

whatChangedVsParent: Keeps the pretrained video DiT intact and adds a separate action DiT with Bridge Attention instead of adapting one joint DiT (PAD/UVA/UWM) or using a one-way two-stage pipeline.
limitations: Operates only on monocular video, limiting 3D scene understanding.

name: AdaWorldPolicy
resolvedTitle: AdaWorldPolicy: World-Model-Driven Diffusion Policy with Online Adaptive Learning for Robotic Manipulation
org: The University of Hong Kong; Beihang University
problem: Unified world-action models are trained offline and cannot adapt to visual and physical (force) domain shifts at deployment without new demonstrations.
keyIdea: Use the world model's prediction error as a self-supervised test-time signal: the network alternates between Action Generation and Future Imagination modes, and the gap between imagined and real next observation (and force) drives online LoRA updates (AdaOL).
architecture: Three flow-matching DiTs linked by multi-modal self-attention: world model from Cosmos-Predict2 2B (multi-view tokens concatenated in time), lightweight action model (0.4–0.6B) and force predictor (0.4B); T5-XXL text, state and noise level via adaLN; mode switch via input masks; LoRA for online updates.
inputs: Static and gripper camera histories, force-torque readings, text, robot state
outputs: Action chunk; in imagination mode, future frames and forces
actionRepr: Chunk of T_a actions (8–32 depending on benchmark) via flow matching
params: Cosmos-Predict2 2B world model + 0.4–0.6B action model (+0.4B force predictor in real world)
trainingData: Benchmark data (PushT, CALVIN ABC→D, LIBERO-10) and real INOVO arm demos with force sensing; no extra pretraining data.
whatChangedVsParent: Turns the world model from an offline auxiliary or evaluator into an online supervisor for test-time adaptation, and adds force prediction.
notes: Claims SOTA on LIBERO-10 (numbers not in retrieved pages), >5% OOD gain and ~1% in-domain gain from AdaOL; online learning is ~5% slower than without adaptation.

name: PhysGen
resolvedTitle: Learning Physics from Pretrained Video Models: A Multimodal Continuous and Sequential World Interaction Models for Robotic Manipulation
org: Sun Yat-sen University; X-Era AI Lab; Guangdong University of Technology
problem: LLM-based VLAs suffer a text–action modality gap; discrete tokenization of images and actions in autoregressive world-action models introduces resolution errors that accumulate.
keyIdea: Repurpose a pretrained non-quantized autoregressive video generator (NOVA) as a physics simulator: frames and action chunks become shared continuous 'physical tokens' predicted autoregressively and de-tokenized by diffusion heads.
architecture: NOVA causal transformer (frozen Phi text encoder, frozen 3D-VAE) with MLP action tokenizer; frame diffusion head and lightweight Action-DiT de-tokenizer (MAR-style diffusion loss); causal mask where actions attend to frame tokens (implicit inverse kinematics); Lookahead Multi-Token Prediction (3 tokens); LoRA fine-tuning; KV cache.
inputs: Language instruction, past images (multi-view concatenated), past action chunks
outputs: Next visual frame and next action chunk
actionRepr: Continuous action chunks of L=8 via per-token diffusion; lookahead of 3 future tokens
trainingData: No action pretraining (video-generation pretraining only); LIBERO ~400 demos per suite, ManiSkill 1,000 demos per task, real Franka 80–100 demos per task; fine-tuning ≤60 A100 GPU-hours.

headlineResults.comparedTo: MolmoAct 87%; pi0-FAST 86%; WorldVLA (no act. pretrain) 82%; OpenVLA 77%

whatChangedVsParent: Unlike WorldVLA's discrete tokens, frames and actions share continuous tokens modeled with diffusion heads on a video-pretrained autoregressive backbone.
limitations: Underperforms pi0-FAST on LIBERO-Spatial, attributed to limited spatial perception of the underlying video model.
notes: Name collision: 'PhysGen' is also an ECCV 2024 physics-grounded image-to-video generation paper (Liu et al.) unrelated to robot policies; this card assumes the WAM-survey citation refers to the robotics paper (2603.00110). Verify against survey reference list.

name: S-VAM
resolvedTitle: S-VAM: Shortcut Video-Action Model by Self-Distilling Geometric and Semantic Foresight
org: HKUST (Guangzhou); Huawei Foundation Model Department
problem: Video-action models either generate future video with slow multi-step denoising or use noisy, entangled one-step diffusion features (as in VPP), so they cannot have both real-time inference and high-fidelity foresight.
keyIdea: Self-distillation: lightweight decouplers learn to map one-step video-diffusion features to DPAv3 (geometry) and DINOv2 (semantics) features extracted from the model's own multi-step generated videos, giving high-fidelity foresight in one forward pass.
architecture: Stable Video Diffusion backbone (~1.5B, embodied-pretrained from VPP) → multi-layer up-sampling features from first denoising step → geometric and semantic spatio-temporal transformer decouplers (~100M, anchored on current-frame VFM features) → Uni-Perceiver (Q-Former-style) token condensation → DiT diffusion policy with CLIP text conditioning. Three-stage training.
inputs: Monocular third-view RGB observation, task description
outputs: Action chunk (foresight features internal)
actionRepr: Chunk of 8 actions via DiT diffusion policy
trainingData: CALVIN ABC, MetaWorld (50 demos per task, 50 tasks), real AgileX Cobot ~50 demos per task (4 tasks).
controlRateHz: 25 Hz effective (307.6 ms per forward pass, chunk of 8, RTX 3090)
whatChangedVsParent: Versus VPP's raw one-step features, S-VAM distills them into disentangled geometric and semantic foresight supervised by the model's own multi-step generations, at 15.8% extra latency.
notes: Same HKUST(GZ) group (Haoang Li) as UD-VLA and FRAPPE.

name: Video Policy
resolvedTitle: Video Generators are Robot Policies
org: Columbia University; Toyota Research Institute
problem: Visuomotor behavior-cloning policies generalize poorly under perceptual/behavioral shifts and are limited by demonstration data size; prior video-to-policy methods use hand-crafted decoders or data-hungry learned decoders.
keyIdea: Use video generation as a proxy for policy learning: a video diffusion model generates the robot rollout while a small action U-Net decodes actions from its intermediate features, so the video model effectively is the policy.
architecture: Image-to-video Stable Video Diffusion U-Net with CLIP text cross-attention; hidden features from 5 decoder layers (9, 14, 17, 20, 23) → CNN adapter → 1D CNN action U-Net adapted from Diffusion Policy; action loss gradients stopped from flowing into the video U-Net; 3 camera views concatenated in time.
inputs: Initial observation (multi-view) + text task description
outputs: Generated video (8 frames per view) + action sequence
actionRepr: 7-D end-effector action sequence (6-DoF pose + gripper) via action diffusion U-Net, jointly denoised with video
trainingData: RoboCasa (50 human demos per task, 24 tasks; also 300 MimicGen demos), LIBERO-10 (50 demos per task), real-world robot demos; supports action-free video for video training.
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces Dreamitate's hand-crafted tracking decoder with a learned action head on video-diffusion features while keeping the video model as the main carrier of the policy.
limitations: Limited scale of simulation benchmarks and a single real embodiment; only one video model family (SVD) explored; video diffusion compute cost is a deployment bottleneck.
notes: Paper says code and models will be released (videopolicy.cs.columbia.edu). Two-stage training (video first, then frozen features for action head) outperformed end-to-end joint training.

name: HMA
resolvedTitle: Learning Real-World Action-Video Dynamics with Heterogeneous Masked Autoregression
org: MIT; UIUC; Meta FAIR
problem: Interactive video world models for robotics must handle heterogeneous action spaces across embodiments and run in real time; full-sequence diffusion video models are too slow.
keyIdea: Heterogeneous Masked Autoregression: per-embodiment action stems/heads around a shared spatial-temporal transformer trunk, trained with masked autoregression on video (VQ or diffusion 'soft' tokens) and actions, unifying forward dynamics, policy and full dynamics.
architecture: HPT-style modular design: embodiment-specific MLP action encoders ('stems') and decoders ('heads'), shared spatial (bidirectional) and temporal (causal) attention trunk with per-domain modulation; discrete variant with 1XGPT/MAGVIT2 VQ tokens (CE loss) or continuous MAR variant with diffusion heads on SVD-VAE latents.
inputs: Past video frames and past action sequences
outputs: Future video frames and/or future actions
actionRepr: Embodiment-specific continuous actions chunked to 2 Hz in pretraining (original frequency in post-training), predicted by per-embodiment heads (MSE or diffusion)
trainingData: Over 3 million trajectories (>2.5B frames) from 40 datasets: 35 real robot (mainly Open X-Embodiment), 3 human egocentric video, 2 simulation.
controlRateHz: Up to 22.72 FPS (HMA-Base MaskGIT) on RTX 4080

headlineResults.benchmark: Language Table video simulation (200 held-out traj.)
Robomimic synthetic data (10 real + 90 generated traj.)

whatChangedVsParent: Extends HPT's heterogeneous stems/heads from policies to full action-video dynamics, and uses masked autoregression instead of IRASim-style full-sequence diffusion for ~15x faster simulation.
limitations: Controllability imperfect with limited data; policy performance when used for action generation is limited.
notes: Primarily an action-conditioned world model / learned simulator (policy evaluation, synthetic data), with policy use secondary.

name: 4DGen
resolvedTitle: Geometry-aware 4D Video Generation for Robot Manipulation
org: Stanford University; Toyota Research Institute
problem: Video generators for robotics trade off temporal coherence against 3D multi-view consistency, producing flicker/deformation or being limited to simple scenes, which degrades trajectories extracted from them.
keyIdea: Generate 4D (RGB + pointmap) videos with DUSt3R-style cross-view pointmap supervision: predict a second view's future pointmaps in the reference view's frame, learning a shared 3D scene representation; then track the gripper's 6DoF pose in the generated RGB-D video to get actions.
architecture: Stable Video Diffusion U-Net fine-tuned to jointly generate RGB and pointmap latents (pointmap VAE initialized from SVD VAE); two pointmap decoders with multi-view cross-attention; actions from FoundationPose gripper tracking (SAM2 mask, gripper CAD model) plus finger-distance gripper open/close rule.
inputs: RGB-D observations from two camera views (no camera poses needed at inference)
outputs: Future RGB videos per view + future pointmaps in reference frame; derived end-effector SE(3) trajectory
actionRepr: End-effector 6DoF pose trajectory recovered by pose tracking on generated 4D video, executed open-loop per inference
trainingData: LBM simulator (Drake): 3 tasks × 25 demos × 16 camera views (12 train / 4 test views); real: 4 bimanual Franka tasks × 20 demos with 2 D415e cameras.
controlRateHz: ~30 s to generate 10 future frames on one RTX 4090

headlineResults.benchmark: LBM sim, 3 tasks, novel camera views

whatChangedVsParent: Versus Dreamitate (RGB stereo video + MegaPose), it generates geometry-consistent RGB-D/pointmap video, improving pose-tracking accuracy and novel-view generalization.
limitations: Needs multi-view RGB-D training data (hard to collect in the real world, depth quality issues); slow video generation makes closed-loop control difficult.
notes: ICLR 2026. 'Pixel (decoded) ∧ Geometric, post-prediction head, open-loop' in P04's census (dated 2025.07). Resolution by matching P04's description (pose tracking) and date; not the graphics paper '4DGen: Grounded 4D Content Generation' (2312.17225). Project page robot4dgen.github.io; code/models promised.

name: TraceGen
resolvedTitle: TraceGen: World Modeling in 3D Trace-Space Enables Learning from Cross-Embodiment Videos
org: University of Maryland, College Park; New York University
problem: Learning new tasks on new robots from a handful of demos is hard; abundant human/other-robot videos differ in embodiment, camera and scene, while pixel-space video world models are slow and waste capacity on appearance.
keyIdea: Model the world in a compact 3D 'trace-space' of scene-level point trajectories (robot and objects), learned from 123K cross-embodiment videos converted by the TraceForge pipeline, then execute predicted traces on a robot.
architecture: Flow-based (stochastic interpolant, linear ODE) trace decoder adapted from CogVideoX 3D transformer over a 20×20 keypoint grid × 32 future steps (2×2 patches); Prismatic-style fusion of frozen DINOv3, SigLIP and SigLIP-depth encoders plus frozen T5 text; predicts per-step 3D increments. TraceForge: camera pose/depth estimation, 3D point tracking, world-to-camera alignment, speed retargeting, VLM instructions.
inputs: Single RGB-D frame + language instruction
outputs: Future 3D trace (20×20 keypoints × 32 steps)
actionRepr: Scene-level 3D point trajectories converted to joint commands via inverse kinematics / tracking controller
trainingData: TraceForge-123K: 123K videos, 1.8M observation–trace–language triplets from human, single-arm and bimanual robot datasets; warm-up with 5 target robot or 5 handheld human videos.

headlineResults.benchmark: Real Franka 4 tasks, 5 robot warm-up videos
Real Franka 4 tasks, 5 human phone videos (Human→Robot)

headlineResults.comparedTo: Video-generation world models (e.g., Veo 3.1 via API, NovaFlow)

whatChangedVsParent: Versus 2D-trace or object-only 3D-flow methods (Im2Flow2Act, 3DFlowAction), predicts scene-level 3D traces including the robot, trained on ~15x more data without object detectors.
limitations: No control over which trajectory mode is sampled for ambiguous tasks; noisy source demonstrations; zero-shot generation not fully reliable on novel embodiments/environments; traces may lack detail for fine-grained manipulation.
notes: Real tasks: Clothes, Ball, Brush, Block on Franka Research 3. With 15 warm-up videos: 82.5%.

name: VILP
resolvedTitle: VILP: Imitation Learning with Latent Video Planning
org: Purdue University
problem: Video-planning policies (e.g., UniPi) are too slow for real-time closed-loop control, are usually open-loop, and do not handle multi-view, multi-modal robot data well.
keyIdea: Generate short, time-aligned multi-view future videos with a latent video diffusion model fast enough for receding-horizon replanning, then map consecutive generated frames to action chunks with a small goal-conditioned low-level policy.
architecture: Per-view latent video diffusion U-Nets (DDIM sampling) with global conditioning on fused multi-view observation embeddings; low-level policy of two CNN encoders + MLP head mapping pairs of adjacent predicted frames to action sequences.
inputs: Current multi-view RGB observations (optionally low-dim state)
outputs: Predicted future frames (e.g., 5-6 frames, 96x160) and an action sequence
actionRepr: Continuous action sequences regressed from pairs of adjacent generated frames; executed receding-horizon (first N_e steps)
trainingData: Task-specific video datasets (e.g., 610 and 200 video episodes for Arrange-Blocks and Nut-Assembly) plus small action-labeled sets (e.g., 10-16 demos, 'Hybrid' adds off-target demos); 220 human demos for real Franka task
controlRateHz: ~14 Hz full policy inference (0.073 s per inference, Arrange-Blocks-Hybrid, VILP-4)
whatChangedVsParent: Moves UniPi-style video planning into latent space with global multi-view conditioning, making it ~real-time so it can be run closed-loop.
limitations: Generated videos sometimes contain minor artifacts; very long video planning horizons are impractical due to training/inference cost; models are single-task/single-dataset.
notes: Code open-sourced at github.com/ZhengtongXu/VILP (weights not stated). Claims to be first real-time video-generation robot policy.

name: InternVLA-A1
resolvedTitle: InternVLA-A1: Unifying Understanding, Generation and Action for Robotic Manipulation
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory (InternVLA-A1 Team)
problem: MLLM-based VLAs understand semantics but lack physical-dynamics reasoning; video-prediction world-model policies lack semantic grounding and are brittle to prediction errors.
keyIdea: A Mixture-of-Transformers with three experts (understanding, visual-foresight generation, action) sharing a unified masked self-attention, so action generation is conditioned on both semantic context and predicted future latent images.
architecture: Understanding expert = InternVL3 or Qwen3-VL; generation expert uses Cosmos CI8x8 VAE latents compressed to 16 tokens/image (3 views x 2 timesteps = 96 tokens) with parallel decoding; action expert produces actions via flow matching. All experts decoder-only transformers.
inputs: Multi-view images (head + two wrist) at t and t-15, language instruction, proprioception
outputs: Predicted future images (latent) and action chunk
actionRepr: Continuous action chunk a_{t:t+k} via flow matching (Euler ODE integration)
params: 1.8B (2B variant: InternVL3-1B + Qwen2.5 experts) and 3.2B (3B variant: Qwen3-VL-2B + Qwen3 experts)
trainingData: Heterogeneous pre-training over real robot data, synthetic simulation data (InternData-A1) and egocentric human videos, >692M frames; 700K pre-training steps, then task post-training
whatChangedVsParent: Adds a lightweight single-pass visual-foresight generation expert (replacing F1's iterative next-resolution generation) inside a pi0-style MoT VLA.
limitations: Understanding expert not co-trained with large-scale VQA data, weakening semantic reasoning/instruction following; foresight image fidelity was sacrificed for inference speed.
notes: Homepage lists Code, Model and Data (InternData-A1) releases. Fig.1 reports absolute numbers for ours vs pi0.5 (e.g., 86.9, 89.5/86.7, 75.1/70.7, 60.0) but mapping to benchmarks was not unambiguous in extracted text, so only deltas are recorded.

name: CoWVLA
resolvedTitle: Chain of World: World Model Thinking in Latent Motion
org: Harbin Institute of Technology; Li Auto; BAAI; UNSW; Peking University
problem: World-model VLAs waste capacity reconstructing redundant background pixels, while latent-action VLAs model only frame-pair transitions and lack temporally continuous dynamics and world knowledge.
keyIdea: Use a pretrained structure/motion-disentangled video VAE to extract a continuous latent motion chain; pretrain the VLA to infer this latent motion and the terminal frame from instruction + initial frame, then co-fine-tune jointly with discrete action tokens over sparse keyframes.
architecture: Latent motion extractor = VidTwin video VAE (fine-tuned on 237k robot videos) producing structure latent and directional motion latents (D_m=1792); VLA decoder follows UniVLA on Emu3 (8.5B) autoregressive VLM with VQGAN image tokens, a learnable motion query Q + MLP head, FAST action tokens.
inputs: Language instruction, initial frame (and sparse keyframes during fine-tuning)
outputs: Latent motion vector, terminal/keyframe tokens, discrete action tokens
actionRepr: FAST-tokenized discrete action chunks (chunk length 10 on LIBERO, 5 on SimplerEnv), decoded autoregressively
trainingData: Pretraining on 237k robot videos (16 frames each); fine-tuning on LIBERO (OpenVLA-curated mix) and BridgeData V2
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces UniVLA-style full-frame future prediction with prediction of a disentangled continuous latent motion chain plus only the terminal keyframe.
limitations: Latent motion space depends on quality and domain coverage of the pretrained video VAE; relies on a large VLA backbone and substantial compute.
notes: Project site fx-hit.github.io/cowvla-io. Evaluated only in simulation (LIBERO, SimplerEnv).

name: World4RL
resolvedTitle: World4RL: Diffusion World Models for Policy Refinement with Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Manipulation
org: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences; UCAS; Zhongguancun Academy; Tsinghua University
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Imitation-learned manipulation policies are limited by scarce expert data; real-robot RL is costly/unsafe and simulator RL suffers sim-to-real gap.
keyIdea: Pre-train a diffusion world model on multi-task data, then refine a BC-initialized policy with PPO entirely inside the frozen world model, using a learned binary success classifier as reward.
architecture: EDM-style diffusion transition model with 2D U-Net conditioned on 4-frame history and two-hot encoded actions (K=21 bins); ResNet18 reward classifier; Gaussian policy + value network trained with PPO with clipped std (sigma <= e^0).
inputs: Image observation history + actions (world model); image observation (policy)
outputs: Next-frame prediction; sparse success reward; refined policy actions
actionRepr: Gaussian continuous actions from the policy; two-hot encoded per-dimension for world-model conditioning
trainingData: Meta-World: per task 50 expert demos + 150 BC-policy rollouts + 30 random rollouts (50 steps each), six tasks; real-robot tasks

headlineResults.comparedTo: best baselines (BC, DP, TD3+BC, IQL, IRASim, DiWA, TD-MPC2); abstract claims +16% absolute in sim

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces DiWA's RSSM latent world model with a pixel-space diffusion world model and two-hot action encoding for sharper, more stable imagined rollouts.
limitations: Moderate visual resolution and model capacity due to compute limits may limit fidelity of imagined rollouts.
notes: World model pretraining 20 h on 4 A800; single-task refinement ~6 h on one A800.

name: World-Gymnast
resolvedTitle: World-Gymnast: Training Robots with Reinforcement Learning in a World Model
org: New York University; NYU Shanghai; UC Berkeley
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: SFT is bottlenecked by expert data and software-simulator RL suffers a sim-to-real gap; it is unclear whether RL inside a learned video world model yields better real-robot performance.
keyIdea: RL-fine-tune a VLA (GRPO) by rolling it out in an action-conditioned video world model (WorldGym) and scoring rollouts with a VLM (GPT-4o) binary success reward; enables training from any frame, novel instructions, distractor-edited images, test-time training and Dyna-style world model updates.
architecture: World model: WorldGym DiT (16 layers, hidden 1024) over SD3 VAE latents at 256x256, 20-frame context, with KV caching; policy: OpenVLA-OFT (OpenVLA 7B) with LLaMA-2 LM head for action probabilities; reward: GPT-4o.
inputs: Single initial frame + language instruction
outputs: Refined VLA policy actions
actionRepr: Tokenized 7-DoF actions (6-DoF EE pose + gripper) via LM head, chunks of 5
trainingData: World model pretrained on Open X-Embodiment (580k steps); policy SFT on BridgeData V2; RL on 17 Bridge-style tasks, rollouts up to 40 steps

headlineResults.benchmark: AutoEval real Bridge: put eggplant into blue sink
AutoEval: put eggplant into yellow basket

whatChangedVsParent: Uses WorldGym (previously a policy evaluator) as an RL training environment for a VLA, with VLM rewards.
limitations: Cannot generalize to initial frames far from the world model's training distribution; relies on a VLM success judge that can hallucinate.
notes: Close-the-drawer: SIMPLER-RL 74% beat World-Gymnast 62% (the one task where it did not win). Test-time training overfits to the single task.

name: PlayWorld
resolvedTitle: PlayWorld: Learning Robot World Models from Autonomous Play
org: Princeton University
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Action-conditioned video world models trained on success-biased human demonstrations hallucinate in contact-rich interactions due to poor coverage of interaction dynamics.
keyIdea: Train the world model on autonomously collected robot play: a VLM proposes perturbed tasks and a VLA executes them (with safety filter/resets) for hours unattended, giving broad coverage of contacts and failures; train with a difficulty curriculum.
architecture: Stable Video Diffusion backbone with factorized spatial/temporal attention and per-frame action conditioning (following Ctrl-World), jointly predicting three camera views; initialized from DROID-pretrained weights.
inputs: Multi-view images, proprioception, action sequence
outputs: Predicted future multi-view video
trainingData: Autonomous play on a DROID setup (up to 8 h continuous, overnight); scaled to 30 hours; trained on 8x H200 for two days

headlineResults.comparedTo: world model trained on human-collected data

headlineResults.benchmark: Real-world RL fine-tuning in world model (DSRL)

whatChangedVsParent: Keeps Ctrl-World-style architecture but replaces human demonstration training data with autonomous VLM/VLA play data plus curriculum.
limitations: Collection is not sample-efficient and produces redundant trajectories; depends on a capable play policy; hallucinations not eliminated (open-loop drift, fixed action horizon); scaling beyond lab setting open.
notes: World model is not a policy (actionRepr empty). RL via DSRL latent-noise steering with a learned progress reward.

name: RISE
resolvedTitle: RISE: Self-Improving Robot Policy with Compositional World Model
org: CUHK; Kinetix AI; HKU (OpenDriveLab); Shanghai Innovation Institute; Horizon Robotics; Tsinghua University
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: VLAs are brittle in contact-rich/dynamic manipulation, and on-policy real-world RL is limited by safety, hardware cost, serial execution and resets.
keyIdea: Do on-policy RL in imagination with a Compositional World Model: an action-controllable multi-view video dynamics model plus a separate progress value model; advantages from imagined rollouts drive advantage-conditioned policy improvement (RECAP-style).
architecture: Dynamics model initialized from Genie Envisioner GE-Base (LTX-Video based) with a lightweight action encoder, 4 input / 25 predicted frames, 3 views, pretrained with Task-Centric Batching; value model initialized from pi0.5 and trained with progress regression + TD learning; policy pi0.5 conditioned on discretized advantage, trained with flow matching.
inputs: Multi-view images, language instruction, candidate action chunk
outputs: Imagined future multi-view frames, value/advantage, improved policy action chunks
actionRepr: Flow-matching action chunks of 50 steps, 14-dim (dual 7-DoF arms, absolute joint control), advantage-conditioned
trainingData: Dynamics pretraining on AgiBot World + Galaxea (16 H100, ~7 days), task fine-tuning (8 H100, ~3 days); task-specific expert demos + policy rollouts (success/failure) + some DAgger data
whatChangedVsParent: Moves RECAP's advantage-conditioned policy improvement from off-policy real data to on-policy imagined rollouts from a learned dynamics + value world model.
limitations: Effectiveness bounded by world model accuracy/coverage; can still produce physically implausible transitions in rare or underrepresented scenarios.
notes: Code at github.com/OpenDriveLab/RISE. Robot: dual 7-DoF AgileX arms. World model used only during training (zero inference overhead). GE generates 25 multi-view frames in <2 s vs >10 min for Cosmos (paper's claim).

name: RehearseVLA
resolvedTitle: RehearseVLA: Simulated Post-Training for VLAs with Physically-Consistent World Model
org: Sun Yat-sen University; AMap, Alibaba Group
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: VLAs trained by imitation degrade in data-scarce regimes, real-world RL is non-resettable/unsafe, and VLAs lack a task-completion signal, causing redundant post-success actions.
keyIdea: Post-train a VLA with RL entirely inside a physically-consistent video world simulator, with a VLM-guided 'instant reflector' that gives continuous success-probability rewards and triggers early termination.
architecture: World simulator: U-Net video diffusion conditioned on projected action maps (via forward kinematics) + memory-bank history, with geometry-aware VGGT features and CLIP features injected by cross-attention; reflector: frozen LLaVA + trainable reward head; policy: OpenVLA-OFT with added Laplace scale head, optimized with LOOP (RLOO + PPO), LoRA rank 32.
inputs: RGB observation, proprioceptive state, language instruction
outputs: Continuous actions; imagined next frames; reward/termination signal
actionRepr: Continuous 7-DoF actions (6D EE pose + gripper) from OpenVLA-OFT regression head, sampled from a Laplace distribution for exploration
trainingData: LIBERO with only 5 expert demos per task, augmented with OpenVLA-OFT self-exploration rollouts in the LIBERO simulator for world model training; 8 H20 GPUs ~48 h
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces the physics simulator used by RIPT-VLA-style RL with a learned world simulator plus a learned VLM reward/termination model.
limitations: World simulator and reflector need large-scale diverse data for fidelity; policy optimization is slower than concurrent methods due to simulator-based rollout cost.
notes: Code at github.com/amap-cvlab/world-env (earlier arXiv versions titled 'World-Env'). Small real-world test: e.g., 'put orange toy' 50% vs OpenVLA-OFT 20%.

name: ProphRL
resolvedTitle: Reinforcing Action Policies by Prophesying
org: Fudan University; Shanghai Innovation Institute; Logos Robotics
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Imitation-trained VLAs are brittle; real-robot RL is expensive and simulators transfer poorly; existing world models are single-scene and not practical RL backends; RL on flow-based action heads is unstable.
keyIdea: Pretrain a general action-to-video world model (Prophet) on 31M+ trajectories, few-shot adapt it to new scenes, then RL-post-train VLAs inside it with FA-GRPO (Flow-GRPO ratios at environment-action level) plus FlowScale (noise-schedule-based per-step gradient reweighting).
architecture: Prophet: Cosmos-Predict2-2B Video2World DiT with Wan2.1 video autoencoder, history buffer (60 frames) and dual action conditioning (action vectors + optional rendered action frames); generates 20 frames per 20-step action chunk. Reward: frozen Qwen2.5-VL judge. Policies: VLA-Adapter-0.5B, pi0.5-3B, OpenVLA-OFT-7B.
inputs: Initial frame + history + action chunk (world model); image + instruction (policy)
outputs: Future video rollouts; RL-improved VLA actions
actionRepr: World-model action: per-step 7-dim per end-effector (3D delta translation, 3D delta Euler rotation, gripper open ratio), up to 2 arms; policies use flow-matching action heads
trainingData: Pretraining on AgiBot, DROID, LIBERO and curated Open-X subsets (>31M sampled trajectories), 64 H200; fine-tuning on BRIDGE, LIBERO and 800 self-collected UR30e trajectories (4 tasks)
whatChangedVsParent: Adapts Flow-GRPO to flow-based VLA heads (action-level ratios + FlowScale reweighting) and trains in a large pretrained, few-shot-adaptable world model rather than a single-scene one.
limitations: Computationally demanding: closed-loop rollouts through the 2B Prophet dominate RL cost and limit iterations.
notes: Project page LogosRoboticsGroup.github.io/ProphRL. Introduces an optical-flow-guided evaluation protocol for action fidelity of world models. Also compares to VLA-RFT, WMPO and RIPT-VLA-style RL (FA-GRPO+FlowScale gains 12.1 overall vs lower for those on pi0.5).

name: World-VLA-Loop
resolvedTitle: World-VLA-Loop: Closed-Loop Learning of Video World Model and VLA Policy
org: Show Lab, National University of Singapore
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Action-conditioned video world models follow actions imprecisely (hallucinating success on near-miss failures) and lack native reward signals; a static simulator drifts out of alignment as the policy changes during RL.
keyIdea: Train a state-aware video world model on Success-And-Near-Success (SANS) data that jointly predicts future frames and binary rewards from diffusion latents, use it for GRPO post-training of the VLA, and feed new policy rollouts back to refine the world model in a co-evolving loop.
architecture: Cosmos-Predict 2 DiT with action-embedder MLP added to timestep embeddings and a lightweight MLP reward head on denoised latents (joint flow-matching + reward loss); policy OpenVLA-OFT trained with SimpleVLA-RL GRPO pipeline inside the world model.
inputs: First h frames + T-step action chunk (6-DoF EE pose + gripper)
outputs: Future frames + per-step reward; RL-refined policy
actionRepr: OpenVLA-OFT continuous action chunks (6-DoF EE pose + binary gripper)
trainingData: SANS: 35k ManiSkill video-action pairs over 23 tasks for pretraining; ~50 success + 50 failure trajectories per LIBERO/real task (80-100 per task for WM fine-tuning, ~50 successes for policy SFT)

headlineResults.benchmark: Outcome alignment (reward head vs Qwen3-VL-8B judge), LIBERO-Object T2

whatChangedVsParent: Moves reward prediction inside the world model (latent reward head) instead of an external VLM/reward model, and adds near-success data plus iterative world-model/policy co-training.
limitations: Autoregressive video models have limited context memory and quality drift, degrading long-horizon tasks (>300 frames, e.g., LIBERO-100 not evaluated); sparse final-state rewards.
notes: Concurrent with WoVR and VLAW, which also co-evolve world model and VLA. Evaluated only 2 tasks per LIBERO suite.

name: WoVR
resolvedTitle: WoVR: World Models as Reliable Simulators for Post-Training VLA Policies with RL
org: Tsinghua University; Institute of Automation, CAS; UCAS; Zhongguancun Academy; Infinigence AI
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Closed-loop imagined rollouts hallucinate and accumulate errors, so RL in world models exploits model inaccuracies (spurious success) rather than genuine task progress.
keyIdea: Regulate hallucination at three levels: a rollout-stable action-controllable video world model, Keyframe-Initialized Rollouts (KIR) with masked GRPO to shorten effective error depth, and PACE low-frequency world-model/policy co-evolution.
architecture: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B video diffusion backbone converted to action-conditioned generator via dual-channel action injection (AdaLN-Zero modulation + cross-attention with action embeddings), first-frame anchored context with noisy-context training, rectified flow objective, 5 diffusion steps; lightweight binary reward classifier; policy OpenVLA-OFT trained with masked GRPO on RLinf.
inputs: Reference frame + memory frames + action chunk
outputs: Future frames, sparse success reward, RL-refined policy
actionRepr: OpenVLA-OFT chunked actions
trainingData: Per LIBERO suite 2,500 real-environment trajectories budget: 1,500 base-policy rollouts to train WM_Base + 1,000 evolved-policy rollouts for WM_Evo; real robot: 150 base-policy rollouts
whatChangedVsParent: Unlike World-Env/WMPO that treat the world model as a drop-in simulator, adds explicit hallucination controls (anchoring, keyframe starts, success masking, co-evolution).
limitations: Reduces but does not eliminate hallucination, especially in very long-horizon or highly contact-sensitive settings; relies on learned reward modeling and limited real-data refinement.
notes: Released via Hugging Face collection RLinf/wovr and github.com/RLinf/RLinf (open weights inferred from HF collection link). Base policy is one-trajectory SFT OpenVLA-OFT, hence low 39.95% start.

name: DiWA
resolvedTitle: DiWA: Diffusion Policy Adaptation with World Models
org: University of Freiburg; University of Technology Nuremberg
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: RL fine-tuning of diffusion policies (e.g., DPPO) needs millions of environment interactions and ground-truth signals, impractical for real robots.
keyIdea: Learn a latent world model once from unlabeled play data, then fine-tune a diffusion policy fully offline with PPO inside a 'Dream Diffusion MDP' that embeds the denoising chain into imagined latent rollouts, with a learned success classifier reward and BC regularization.
architecture: DreamerV2-style RSSM (1024-d deterministic + 32x32 categorical stochastic latent, two camera encoders fused) following LUMOS; diffusion policy conditioned on world-model latents; binary success classifier on latents; DPPO-style two-level PPO with denoising-step discount and BC regularizer.
inputs: Static + gripper camera RGB encoded into world-model latents
outputs: Continuous robot actions
actionRepr: Continuous actions from a K-step diffusion denoising chain (Gaussian per denoising step)
trainingData: CALVIN env D: ~6 h play (~500k transitions) + 50 demos per skill; real Franka: 4 h teleoperated play (~450k transitions) + 50 demos per skill

headlineResults.comparedTo: base 59.14; DPPO needs ~345,600 env steps to match

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces DPPO's online environment MDP with a learned latent world model so diffusion-policy PPO fine-tuning needs no real interaction.
limitations: World model frozen after offline training, so its errors persist and can be exploited; improvements in imagination do not guarantee real success, requiring real-world checkpoint evaluation.
notes: CoRL 2025. Parameter count 40M is from World4RL's comparison table, not DiWA's own paper. World4RL criticizes DiWA's RSSM for blurry, compounding generations. Real-world tasks: open/close drawer, push slider right (zero-shot transfer).

name: EnerVerse-AC
resolvedTitle: EnerVerse-AC: Envisioning Embodied Environments with Action Condition
org: AgiBot; SJTU; MMLab-CUHK
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Evaluating manipulation policies requires costly real-robot deployment or hand-built 3D simulators; existing video world models are driven by language rather than the agent's actions.
keyIdea: An action-conditioned multi-view video world model (EVAC) that generates future observations from predicted robot actions, usable both as a policy evaluator and a data engine, trained with mined failure trajectories.
architecture: UNet video diffusion (DynamiCrafter-style, following EnerVerse) with multi-level action injection: end-effector projection action maps (CLIP-encoded, channel-concatenated) + delta-action cross-attention; spatial cross-attention across views; ray-map encoding of (moving) wrist cameras; sparse memory of 4 frames, chunk size 16.
inputs: Initial multi-view observation, memory frames, 7-dim (or 14-dim bimanual) EE action trajectory
outputs: Multi-view future video chunks
trainingData: AgiBot World (>210 tasks, 1M trajectories) plus mined and auto-collected failure trajectories; 32 A100 for 2 days (single-view) / 8 days (multi-view)

headlineResults.benchmark: Data engine: take-a-bottle task (GO-1 policy, 20 demos)

headlineResults.value: e.g., Take a Toast 90% EVAC vs 100% real; Take a Leaf 50% vs 55%

whatChangedVsParent: Adds action conditioning (action maps + delta-action attention) and ray maps for moving wrist cameras to the language-conditioned EnerVerse world model.
limitations: Unit-circle gripper encoding may not generalize to dexterous hands; wrist-camera background noise limits multi-view generation to ~10 chunks vs 30 for single view; RL integration unexplored.
notes: Code, checkpoints and datasets released (project page annaj2178.github.io/EnerverseAC.github.io). Success judged by human evaluators watching generated videos. WoVR reports EVAC at 2.7 FPS.

name: Veo world simulator (Gemini Robotics)
resolvedTitle: Evaluating Gemini Robotics Policies in a Veo World Simulator
org: Google DeepMind (Gemini Robotics Team)
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Generalist policies need broad evaluation (nominal, OOD, safety) that hardware testing cannot cover, and video models had been used mainly for in-distribution evaluation.
keyIdea: Fine-tune the Veo 2 video model for robot-pose-conditioned, multi-view (tiled 4-camera) generation, and combine it with generative image editing (NanoBanana) plus multi-view completion to evaluate policies in nominal, OOD and safety-critical scenes.
architecture: Veo 2 latent diffusion (autoencoder + transformer denoiser) fine-tuned on large-scale robot data, conditioned on the current image and a sequence of future robot poses, generating 4 tiled camera views; separate Veo2 fine-tune for single-to-multi-view synthesis; Gemini 2.5 Flash Image for scene edits.
inputs: Initial multi-view frames (possibly edited), future robot pose sequence from the policy
outputs: Multi-view predicted video (8-second closed-loop episodes), human-scored for success
trainingData: Large-scale robotics dataset of diverse manipulation tasks (ALOHA 2 platform); evaluated on 1600+ real-world trials of 8 Gemini Robotics On-Device checkpoints over 5 tasks
whatChangedVsParent: Extends video-model policy evaluation from in-distribution to OOD generalization and closed-loop semantic-safety red teaming via image editing.
limitations: Contact-rich interactions with small objects still hallucinate (objects appear spontaneously); only 8-second episodes; relies on human scoring; absolute predicted success rates are lower than real; inference cost.
notes: Evaluator only (no policy training). Policy evaluated (GROD) predicts 1-second chunks of continuous actions at 50 Hz. Veo model not released (proprietary).

name: World-in-World
resolvedTitle: World-in-World: World Models in a Closed-Loop World
org: Johns Hopkins University; Peking University; Princeton; MIT; Harvard
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: World-model benchmarks are open-loop and focus on visual quality, leaving unanswered whether world models actually help embodied agents succeed at tasks.
keyIdea: A closed-loop benchmark wrapping heterogeneous world models with a unified action API (text / camera trajectory / low-level actions) and a proposal-simulation-revision online planning loop, ranking world models by task success.
architecture: Benchmark platform: proposal policy (VLM, heuristic or 3D diffusion policy) samples M candidate plans; world model rolls each out; revision policy scores and selects; plus a post-training recipe that fine-tunes video generators on action-observation data.
inputs: Egocentric observation + candidate action plans
outputs: Task success metrics across 4 tasks (Active Recognition, A-EQA, ImageNav, RLBench manipulation)
trainingData: Post-training sets of 400 to 80K action-observation instances; evaluates SVD, LTX-Video, Hunyuan, Wan2.1/2.2, Cosmos-Predict2, NWM, PathDreamer, SE3DS, Runway Gen4
whatChangedVsParent: Evaluates world models by closed-loop embodied task success rather than open-loop visual metrics.
limitations: Gains small for manipulation since contact-rich dynamics are poorly modeled; long-horizon planning hard due to weak spatiotemporal memory; performance floor set by proposal/revision policies; transfer to novel environments limited.
notes: ICLR 2026. Benchmark, not a policy. Key findings: visual quality does not guarantee task success (controllability matters more); scaling action-conditioned post-training beats upgrading the pretrained generator; inference-time compute helps. Code github.com/World-In-World.

name: DreamPlan
resolvedTitle: DreamPlan: Efficient Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Planners via Video World Models
org: USC Physical Superintelligence Lab; Toyota Research Institute
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Zero-shot VLM planners lack physical grounding for deformable-object manipulation, and RL fine-tuning of VLMs on real robots is too expensive and unsafe.
keyIdea: Collect exploratory data with the zero-shot VLM, train an action-conditioned video world model on it, then fine-tune the VLM planner offline using Best-of-K world-model rollouts turned into preference pairs optimized with ORPO.
architecture: World model: CogVideoX-5B image-to-video with a ControlNet branch injecting rendered robot-arm trajectory videos, predicting object-only cropped videos; planner: Qwen3-VL-8B choosing keypoint pairs; GPT-4o selects best predicted outcome vs goal image to form preferences.
inputs: Current image + goal image with keypoint overlays
outputs: Discrete keypoint-pair manipulation command (grasp point, place point) executed by a fixed pick-and-place primitive
actionRepr: Discrete keypoint-based action (source keypoint, target keypoint) mapped to a scripted grasp-transport-release primitive
trainingData: 2,056 autonomously collected trajectories (about four hours of robot interaction) on a bimanual Franka FR3 setup

headlineResults.benchmark: Real deformable tasks (rope, cloth, toy arm), 10 trials each
Inference cost vs explicit WM verification (N=8)

whatChangedVsParent: Targets deformable manipulation with a VLM planner and replaces online RL in the world model with offline Best-of-K preference optimization so no world-model queries are needed during policy updates.
limitations: Paper does not state an explicit limitations section; single-step primitive evaluation over 10 trials per task; video diffusion inference ~1 min per action sequence.
notes: Project page psi-lab.ai/DreamPlan. Name could collide with other 'DreamPlan' works; resolved by topic (world model as data engine/RL environment).

name: VLA-Reasoner
resolvedTitle: VLA-Reasoner: Empowering Vision-Language-Action Models with Reasoning via Online Monte Carlo Tree Search
org: Nanyang Technological University; Tsinghua University; BUPT
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: VLAs predict short-sighted next actions and accumulate incremental deviations on long-horizon tasks.
keyIdea: Plug-in test-time scaling: run MCTS over candidate actions (seeded by the VLA, expanded via a KDE action prior) with a world model simulating future states and a learned visual value model scoring them; blend the searched action with the VLA action.
architecture: World model: iVideoGPT-style action-aware model (600M) fine-tuned on task data plus some failure demos; value model: frozen ResNet-34 + 2-layer MLP trained on progress labels; KDE over offline actions; UCB selection; action injection a = alpha*a_VLA + (1-alpha)*a_reasoner.
inputs: Current observation, instruction, VLA proposal
outputs: Refined action at test time
actionRepr: Same as wrapped VLA (OpenVLA/Octo single-step actions; SpatialVLA 4-action chunks), blended with MCTS-selected action
params: World model 600M; wraps OpenVLA 7B, Octo-Small 27M, SpatialVLA 4B
trainingData: Same public LIBERO/SimplerEnv datasets used to fine-tune the VLA, plus a small set of failure rollouts for the world model
whatChangedVsParent: Adds world-model-based MCTS look-ahead to frozen VLAs at test time instead of retraining them.
limitations: Still requires task-specific training (world model, value model, KDE) before deployment; performance bounded by world-model fidelity and value-estimation quality.
notes: Best injection strength alpha around 0.4-0.6. Also real-world tests on top of pi0-FAST and another VLA (5 tasks), numbers not extracted.

name: WorldPlanner
resolvedTitle: WorldPlanner: Monte Carlo Tree Search and MPC with Action-Conditioned Visual World Models
org: New York University; FAIR at Meta
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Behavior cloning needs costly goal-directed demonstrations with resets and transfers poorly to new tasks.
keyIdea: Learn an action-conditioned diffusion world model, a diffusion action prior and reward models from a few hours of unstructured play; plan long action sequences with MCTS (tree edges sampled from the play prior to avoid world-model hallucination) and track the plan with a zeroth-order CEM-style MPC.
architecture: DIAMOND-style EDM diffusion U-Net world model (3 denoising steps, multi-view channel stacking, action via adaptive group norm); diffusion-policy action prior (LeRobot); rewards: geometric tracker, masked DINOv2 embedding distance, or ViT progress reward trained with Bradley-Terry (Rank2Reward).
inputs: Camera images, goal image or geometric goal
outputs: MCTS plan executed by image-space MPC
actionRepr: Desired Cartesian end-effector velocities; MPC optimizes spline knot points, executes 0.4 s chunks (2 steps)
trainingData: About four hours of teleoperated unstructured play on a Flexiv Rizon-10S 7-DoF arm; world model trained ~3 days on one RTX 4090

headlineResults.benchmark: Push-T (100 random inits in world model), <=2.5 cm

whatChangedVsParent: Uses a small play-trained DIAMOND-style world model with a diffusion play prior to discretize MCTS for long-horizon real-robot planning instead of short-horizon MPC.
limitations: Planning is slow (plans take under five minutes on average, MPC steps a couple of seconds); Push-T quantitative comparison run inside the world model; future work needed for foundation models and zero-shot tasks.
notes: Tasks: push-T, push-cubes, push-chain (deformable). BC baselines trained on <100 goal-directed demos vs MCTS world model on play data. World model rollouts stay consistent up to 64 steps (11.28 s).

name: M³PC
resolvedTitle: M³PC: Test-time Model Predictive Control for Pretrained Masked Trajectory Model
org: ETH Zurich; KU Leuven; HKU; CMU
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Bidirectional masked trajectory models trained for offline RL are used with a single mask (e.g., return-conditioned BC) at inference, leaving their world-model and reward-prediction abilities unused.
keyIdea: Use the same pretrained masked trajectory transformer as policy, forward dynamics and reward/return predictor via different masks, performing sample-based MPC at test time (forward M3PC) or path inference + inverse dynamics for goal reaching (backward M3PC), without extra training.
architecture: Encoder-decoder bidirectional transformer over tokenized states, actions, returns-to-go and rewards, trained with random + causal masking and uncertainty-aware (NLL) action reconstruction with an entropy constraint; test-time masks RCBC, FD, RP, ID, PI; TD(lambda) utility and softmax selection.
inputs: State-based trajectories (not pixels)
outputs: Selected action
actionRepr: Continuous low-dimensional actions sampled from a reconstructed action distribution
trainingData: D4RL locomotion (hopper, walker2d, halfcheetah; medium and medium-replay) and RoboMimic (can-pair, square-mh, lift-mg, custom can-lim, real can-real)
whatChangedVsParent: Turns a pretrained masked trajectory model into its own test-time MPC planner by ensembling masks, instead of using a single RCBC mask.
limitations: Limited to state-based observations (no pixels); unclear whether scaling transformer capacity improves test-time planning.
notes: ICLR 2025. Code github.com/wkh923/m3pc. Not a VLA; low-dimensional state setting. Survey listing under world-models-as-planners.

name: SRPO
resolvedTitle: SRPO: Self-Referential Policy Optimization for Vision-Language-Action Models
org: Fudan University; Tongji University; Shanghai Innovation Institute (OpenMOSS)
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: GRPO-style VLA RL suffers from sparse binary rewards that waste failed trajectories, while hand-crafted process rewards need expert demos or task engineering.
keyIdea: Use the model's own in-batch successful trajectories as references and score failed trajectories by distance to them in a pretrained world model's latent space (V-JEPA 2), giving progress-wise rewards for GRPO-style optimization.
architecture: Policy OpenVLA* (OpenVLA with action chunking of 8 and parallel decoding); reward: V-JEPA 2 trajectory embeddings, DBSCAN clustering of successful ones, L2 distance to nearest center normalized and squashed; GRPO-style clipped objective with KL; built on siiRL.
inputs: Third-view image + language instruction
outputs: Action chunks
actionRepr: OpenVLA-style tokenized actions with chunks of 8 and parallel decoding
trainingData: One demonstration per task for SFT on LIBERO, then online RL in LIBERO simulator (~200 RL steps); LIBERO-Plus for robustness; real X-ARM 7 offline RL on 5 tasks
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces GRPO's binary outcome reward with a self-referential latent-world-model progress reward for failed trajectories.
limitations: No explicit limitations section found in retrieved text; progress reward weight needs tuning (0.8 best); online RL relies on a simulator.
notes: Code github.com/sii-research/siiRL and HF collection Sylvest/srpo. World model used only as a latent encoder for rewards, not as a simulator. Real world (offline RL): average gains reported as +66.8% (pi0) and +86.7% (pi0-FAST) relative.

name: NORA-1.5
resolvedTitle: NORA-1.5: A Vision-Language-Action Model Trained using World Model- and Action-based Preference Rewards
org: Nanyang Technological University; Lambda Labs; SUTD
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: VLAs trained by SFT inherit demonstration bias and lack reliability across embodiments; RL via simulated rollouts is expensive and hard to scale.
keyIdea: Add a flow-matching action expert to the autoregressive NORA VLA, then post-train with DPO on preference pairs ranked by a world-model goal reward (V-JEPA2-AC predicted embedding vs goal/subgoal image) plus a ground-truth-action distance heuristic.
architecture: NORA backbone (Qwen-2.5-VL-3B, FAST+ action tokens) whose layer KV feed a flow-matching action expert transformer (layer-wise attention, pi0-style); reward world model: V-JEPA2 encoder + trained action-conditioned predictor (1.3B V-JEPA2-AC); DPO adapted to flow matching.
inputs: Image observation + language instruction
outputs: Action chunk (horizon N=5) via flow matching or FAST+ tokens (-FAST variant)
actionRepr: Chunk of 5 continuous actions via flow-matching expert (or FAST+ discrete tokens for NORA-1.5-FAST)
params: ~3B backbone (Qwen-2.5-VL-3B) plus action expert; reward WM 1.3B
trainingData: Open X-Embodiment pretraining; SFT on SimplerEnv/LIBERO data; 1,000 teleoperated Galaxea A1 episodes (9 tasks, ~50K frames) for real robot
whatChangedVsParent: Adds a flow-matching action expert to NORA and uses world-model-based preference rewards with DPO for post-training.
limitations: Flow-matching expert underperforms autoregressive decoding in low-data real-robot settings (Galaxea A1); WM reward is noisy due to limited action-conditioned training data and ignores implicit safety constraints (degraded Move Near when used alone).
notes: Code github.com/declare-lab/nora-1.5 (weights released per project page; flag if unverified). World model used as reward/evaluator, not simulator. Real-robot numbers on Galaxea A1 not extracted.

name: IRL-VLA
resolvedTitle: IRL-VLA: Training an Vision-Language-Action Policy via Reward World Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
org: Bosch Corporate Research; Shanghai University; SJTU; Tsinghua AIR
topicName: World models as simulator, evaluator and data engine
problem: Driving VLAs trained by open-loop imitation copy recorded behavior, and closed-loop RL needs costly high-fidelity sensor simulators with sim-to-real gaps.
keyIdea: Pretrain a driving VLA by imitation, learn a lightweight Reward World Model via inverse RL that predicts NAVSIM EPDMS sub-scores from trajectories and BEV features, then fine-tune the VLA's diffusion planner with PPO using the RWM instead of a simulator.
architecture: VLA: Senna-VLM-based semantic reasoning + BEV 3D reasoning (V2-99 backbone, detection and map tokens) + anchor-based diffusion planner; RWM: per-metric MLP heads on trajectory features from BEV space; PPO over the denoising chain with group-standardized advantages and BC regularization.
inputs: Multi-view camera images (256x704), ego status, navigation command
outputs: Future driving trajectory waypoints (x, y, heading)
actionRepr: Multimodal trajectory of waypoints from an anchored diffusion planner
trainingData: NAVSIM (navtrain 1,192 scenes; navhard 136 eval scenes) with simulator-scored diverse trajectories for RWM
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces simulator-based RL rewards with a learned reward world model trained by inverse RL.
limitations: No explicit limitations section in retrieved text; Extended Comfort metric excluded from RWM since it needs two simulations per scene.
notes: CONFLICT/SCOPE: this is an autonomous-driving paper, not manipulation; the 'world model' is a reward model, not a visual simulator. Cited by manipulation surveys under world models as evaluators.

name: RH20T
resolvedTitle: RH20T: A Comprehensive Robotic Dataset for Learning Diverse Skills in One-Shot
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
problem: Existing robot datasets are small, skill-limited (mostly push/pick-place), vision-only and seldom contact-rich, hindering one-shot and foundation-model manipulation learning.
keyIdea: Collect a large, real-world, multi-robot, multi-modal (vision, force/torque, audio, proprioception, some tactile) contact-rich dataset via intuitive haptic teleoperation with force feedback, pairing each robot episode with a human demonstration video and language description.
architecture: Dataset (not a model). Platforms: robot arm + wrist F/T sensor + gripper, 1-2 in-hand cameras, 8-10 calibrated global cameras, 2 microphones, haptic device and pedal; 7 configurations from 4 arms (Flexiv, UR5, Franka, Kuka), 4 grippers, 3 F/T sensor types.
trainingData: Over 110,000 robot sequences + 110,000 paired human demo videos; 147 tasks (48 RLBench, 29 MetaWorld, 70 self-proposed) spanning 42 skills; over 40M robot image frames (50M+ total); RGB/depth 10 Hz, F/T 100 Hz, tactile 200 Hz; about 20 TB
controlRateHz: 10 Hz (RGB, joint, gripper recording); F/T at 100 Hz

headlineResults.benchmark: Real block-to-weight task, ACT, 75 demos, 750 epochs

whatChangedVsParent: Adds force/torque, audio, tactile and paired human video to a large multi-robot real-world dataset focused on contact-rich skills.
limitations: Data collection is expensive; potential of robotic foundation models not yet evaluated on the dataset.
notes: Dataset publicly available at rh20t.github.io. Success:failure ratio about 10:1 with 0-9 quality ratings. CONFLICT: RoboMIND's comparison table lists RH20T as 13k trajectories, 140 tasks, 33 skills, whereas the RH20T paper reports >110k sequences, 147 tasks, 42 skills (RH20T's own Table I lists 110k trajectories, 42 skills, 4 robots).

name: RoboMIND
resolvedTitle: RoboMIND: Benchmark on Multi-embodiment Intelligence Normative Data for Robot Manipulation
org: Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics (X-Humanoid); Peking University; BAAI
problem: Robot datasets lack a unified collection standard and sufficient high-quality data across tasks, scenarios and embodiments (Open X-Embodiment aggregates heterogeneous lab data).
keyIdea: A multi-embodiment teleoperation dataset collected on one standardized platform and protocol, with quality filtering, failure demonstrations with causes, fine-grained language annotations and an Isaac Sim digital twin.
architecture: Dataset (not a model). Embodiments: Franka Emika Panda, UR5e (single-arm, GELLO-style teleop), AgileX Cobot Magic V2.0 (dual-arm), X-Humanoid Tien Kung humanoid with dexterous hands (VR/motion capture); H5 storage; cloud data platform for collection, filtering, classification, annotation.
trainingData: 107k demonstration trajectories (305.5 hours), 479 tasks, 96 object classes, 38 skills; per embodiment: Franka 26,856 real, Tien Kung 15,187, AgileX 10,269, UR5e 25,170, simulation 30,035; plus 5k failure trajectories and 10k frame-level language-annotated trajectories

headlineResults.benchmark: Sim vs real correlation, 5 Franka tasks
