trainingData: Online RL; baselines run ~48 h each (e.g. 2M steps TD-MPC2, 10M DreamerV3); low-level reaching pretrained 2-4B steps on 32,768 MJX envs
whatChangedVsParent: First benchmark pairing a real-hardware humanoid model with dexterous hands and a broad whole-body manipulation + locomotion task suite.
limitations: State-based setting only benchmarked; forearm-less Shadow Hands are not a realistic model; flat RL (DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, SAC, PPO) fails most tasks; hierarchical gains limited on package task.
notes: RSS 2024. Open-source code (humanoid-bench.github.io). Results are learning curves only, no verbatim numeric tables retrieved. Runs 1000+ FPS on one CPU (550 FPS with tactile). CONFLICT: P01 Table 2 lists HumanoidBench modalities as 'RGB, LiDAR'; the paper describes egocentric RGB cameras and whole-body tactile sensing (448 taxels), with no LiDAR mentioned in retrieved pages.

name: SIMPLE
resolvedTitle: SIMPLE: Simulation-Based Policy Learning and Evaluation for Humanoid Loco-manipulation
org: USC Physical Superintelligence (PSI) Lab
problem: Humanoid foundation models are evaluated mostly in costly, irreproducible real-world tests; existing simulation benchmarks target tabletop or wheeled robots, not whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation.
keyIdea: A dual-simulator testbed coupling MuJoCo contact physics with Isaac Sim photorealistic rendering, with 60 whole-body tasks, motion-planning and VR-teleop data pipelines, and a standardized 3-level domain-randomization protocol for benchmarking VLAs and world-action models.
architecture: Benchmark: MuJoCo physics synced to Isaac Sim ray-traced rendering; decoupled control where the high-level policy outputs upper-body targets + locomotion commands executed by lower-body trackers (AMO / SONIC / GR00T WBC); Gym API; LeRobot-format export.
inputs: Egocentric RGB, language, 32-D proprioception (14 hand, 14 arm, waist rpy, base height)
outputs: 36-D action: 32-D upper-body targets + 4-D locomotion command (vx, vy, vyaw, qyaw)
trainingData: 60 tasks, 50 HSSD indoor scenes, 1,000+ objects (Objaverse, GraspNet-1B); 6,000+ rendered episodes from cuRobo motion planning and PICO VR teleop at 50 Hz
whatChangedVsParent: Extends simulation-as-proxy evaluation (SimplerEnv style) from tabletop/wheeled robots to whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation with a hybrid physics/rendering stack.
limitations: Ray-traced rendering is slow (~4 FPS per GPU); rigid-body only, so no cloth, rope or food.
notes: Confirmed as P01 ref [137] (arXiv 2606.08278); P01 Table 2 lists it as MuJoCo + Isaac Sim, 1.5K+ objects, 60 tasks, 6K demos, Unitree G1. P09 (Jan 2025) predates it, so the citation comes from P01 only. Authors say codebase will be open-sourced.

name: HumanoidArena
resolvedTitle: HumanoidArena: Benchmarking Egocentric Hierarchical Whole-body Learning
org: HKUST (Guangzhou); Beijing Univ. of Technology; HIT Shenzhen; Shenzhen MSU-BIT Univ.; JD Explore Academy
problem: Existing humanoid benchmarks rarely evaluate the interface between a high-level policy and a low-level general motion tracker (GMT), so it is unclear whether intermediate whole-body actions are executable, robust to shifts, and transferable across trackers.
keyIdea: A simulation-first benchmark that fixes a shared hierarchical interface: a high-level policy maps egocentric RGB, proprioception and instruction to a compact 40-D intermediate whole-body action, executed by a swappable low-level GMT (TWIST2 or SONIC); evaluated on 7 leg-critical HOI/HSI tasks with perturbation- and GMT-conditioned protocols.
architecture: Benchmark (Isaac Lab, Unitree G1). Baseline high-level policies: ACT, Diffusion Policy, Flow Matching and pi0.5 (all via LeRobot); low-level GMTs: TWIST2 and SONIC. Data collected with GMT-based VR teleoperation in simulation.
inputs: Egocentric RGB, 64-D proprioceptive state, task instruction
outputs: 40-D intermediate whole-body action executed by a GMT
actionRepr: Chunks of 20 intermediate 40-D whole-body actions (baseline policies), tracked by a low-level GMT
trainingData: Simulated teleoperated demonstrations per task (7 tasks) collected with TWIST2 and SONIC GMTs; each baseline trained 100k gradient steps
whatChangedVsParent: Makes the policy–tracker interface itself the object of evaluation, including cross-GMT transfer, rather than evaluating a fixed end-to-end stack.
limitations: Paper reports that performance is strongly tracker-conditioned and cross-GMT transfer remains fragile; simulation-only benchmark.
notes: Benchmark paper, not a single method. Code and data at humanoidarena.github.io. Each config evaluated with 3 seeds x 20 rollouts. Main-text per-policy success tables were not retrieved; numbers above are from appendix Table S8 (merged-data transfer).

name: OASIS
resolvedTitle: OASIS: From Simulation Data Collection to Real-World Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
org: TeleAI (China Telecom); Fudan; ECUST; SJTU
problem: Real-robot humanoid teleoperation gives high-quality data but is slow, costly and fragile (resets, damage); a scalable yet embodiment-aligned data source is needed.
keyIdea: Collect whole-body demonstrations entirely in simulation: real-to-sim assets via Hunyuan3D + Qwen3-VL physics estimation, VR teleoperation in sim, then offline path-traced re-rendering with texture/lighting/camera randomization to expand each trajectory, and train a hierarchical policy deployed zero-shot on a real G1.
architecture: High-level Transformer flow-matching planner conditioned on CLIP text features, frozen DINOv2 features of three camera views, and an MLP over 2 frames of history; predicts 32 frames of 67-D reference motion commands. Low-level RL controller (Teleopit) tracks them as 29 body joint angles, plus 14 hand DoF.
inputs: Three-view RGB (head + two wrists), text instruction, reference-motion-command history (used as proprioception)
outputs: Whole-body reference motion commands -> 43-DoF joint angles
actionRepr: Chunk of 32 frames of 67-D reference motion commands via flow matching (10 Euler steps)
trainingData: 50 teleoperated sim trajectories per task, each re-rendered in 20 randomized environments

headlineResults.benchmark: Real G1, Kneel and Wipe Under Table
Data collection, Kneel and Wipe task (50 trajectories)

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces real-robot teleoperation with sim teleoperation plus decoupled offline photorealistic re-rendering for visual diversity.
limitations: Augmentation only randomizes appearance, not trajectories, so motion diversity is bounded by the operator; auto-generated assets may have inaccurate geometry/physics, widening the sim-to-real gap on contact-rich tasks.
notes: Sim-only data matched or beat real-robot data at equal 50-trajectory budget on most tasks; an equal sim+real mix was best (Fig. 5). Real G1 with 7-DoF three-fingered hands.

name: GRAIL
resolvedTitle: GRAIL: Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from 3D Assets and Video Priors
org: NVIDIA; UCLA
problem: Teleoperation and mocap for humanoid loco-manipulation data do not scale, and reconstructing 4D interactions from in-the-wild video is ambiguous in scale, camera and geometry.
keyIdea: Fully digital pipeline: specify the 3D scene, camera, scale and a robot-proportioned character first, use a video foundation model to generate the interaction, then reconstruct metric 4D human-object interaction within the known frame, retarget to G1, and train task-general trackers on SONIC.
architecture: Object-aware latent adaptor (3-layer MLP) injecting a 64-D latent residual into a frozen SONIC whole-body controller plus binary hand primitives; scene-aware tracker fine-tuning SONIC with an 11x11 height-map CNN encoder. Distilled into egocentric RGB visual policies that output SONIC latent tokens.
inputs: Tracker: proprioception, object reference (pose, hand-object transforms, contact forces, BPS shape code) or local height map; deployed policy: head-camera RGB + proprioception
outputs: SONIC latent tokens -> 29 body joint targets; binary open/close per hand mapped to 7 finger joints
actionRepr: Latent residual (64-D) on a pretrained FSQ-tokenized whole-body controller plus 2-D binary hand primitive
trainingData: Over 20,000 generated sequences from 1,000 object assets and 1,000 procedurally generated terrains (pick-up, whole-body manipulation, sitting, terrain traversal); PPO on 64 L40 GPUs, 30,000 iterations
controlRateHz: Visual policy inference 10 Hz on real G1
whatChangedVsParent: Generates interaction data from video priors inside a fully specified 3D scene instead of reconstructing unconstrained video, and trains task-general (not per-task) trackers.
limitations: Needs 3D assets, simulator-ready scenes and a VFM that follows the requested interaction; reconstruction degrades under occlusion, fast motion or inconsistent object appearance, and filtering discards a non-trivial fraction; trackers still need retraining when the motion family changes substantially.
notes: First alphaXiv resolution returned WEAVE (2609.16683), which cites GRAIL; resolved via that reference. Deployment streams from an RTX 5090 desktop to the G1.

name: FCLM
resolvedTitle: Learning Force Control for Legged Manipulation
org: MIT Improbable AI Lab; EPFL; UC San Diego
problem: Sim-to-real RL policies achieve forceful interaction only implicitly and cannot be commanded to exert a specific contact force, especially without force sensors.
keyIdea: Train a whole-body RL policy for a quadruped-with-arm that tracks commanded end-effector force (or position) by simulating a spring-damper external force field in training; forces are estimated from proprioception, enabling gravity compensation and impedance control for teleoperation.
architecture: MLP actor, critic and concurrent state estimator (predicting body velocity, gripper position and external gripper force) over a 30-step observation history; PPO with 4096 parallel envs in Isaac Gym.
inputs: Proprioception history (gravity vector, foot clock, joint pos/vel, previous action) plus commands: EE force, EE position, base velocity, force/position mode flag
outputs: 17-D joint position targets (12 leg joints + 5 arm joints) for PD control
actionRepr: Per-step joint position residuals around a default pose
trainingData: Simulation only (Isaac Gym), 4096 parallel environments

headlineResults.value: about 5 N at low targets, below 10 N across range

whatChangedVsParent: Adds explicit end-effector force commands and force-tracking rewards (with simulated contact field) to a whole-body loco-manipulation RL policy.
limitations: Tracking accuracy (about 5 cm position, about 5 N force) may be insufficient for highly precise tasks; low-frequency neural policy without force sensor.
notes: Name FCLM is the P10 survey's label (ref [2], ICRA 2024). Platform: Unitree B1 + Z1 arm. P10 describes FCLM as receiving teleoperation commands in Phase 2 rather than a learned high-level policy, consistent with the paper.

name: UPPFC
resolvedTitle: Learning a Unified Policy for Position and Force Control in Legged Loco-Manipulation
org: BIGAI; BUPT
problem: Visuomotor policies for legged manipulators learn either position or force control, and trajectory-only datasets omit contact information because robots lack force sensors.
keyIdea: A single RL policy trained with random combinations of position/force commands and external disturbances, built on an impedance formulation, estimates external force from state history and compensates by adjusting position/velocity; its force estimate is then used to collect force-aware demonstrations for a diffusion imitation policy.
architecture: Observation encoder over 32-step history, state estimator (external force, EE position, base velocity) and actor; two-stage PPO in Isaac Gym. High level: diffusion policy taking RGB, proprioception and estimated force, outputting position and force commands.
inputs: Low level: proprioception history + commands (base velocity, EE position, EE force, base force); high level: RGB (EE + base cameras), robot state, estimated force
outputs: Joint position residual targets for PD; high-level policy outputs EE position and force commands
actionRepr: Per-step joint residuals (low level, 50 Hz); diffusion-generated force + position commands (high level, 2 Hz)
trainingData: RL in simulation; 50 teleoperated trajectories for wipe-blackboard (30k diffusion training steps)

headlineResults.benchmark: 4 real contact-rich tasks (wipe blackboard, open/close cabinet, open drawer with occlusion)

parents: FCLM (Learning Force Control for Legged Manipulation)
whatChangedVsParent: Unifies force and position control in one policy (instead of switching modes) and uses the learned force estimator to supply force-aware imitation data.
limitations: Force estimation degrades in high-frequency interactions and at workspace edges; sim-to-real force accuracy varies by axis; only single-point force estimation.
notes: CoRL 2025. Platforms: Unitree B2-Z1 quadruped manipulator and Unitree G1 humanoid. Name UPPFC is the P10 survey label (ref [1]).

name: FORGE
resolvedTitle: FORGE: Force-Guided Exploration for Robust Contact-Rich Manipulation under Uncertainty
org: MIT; USC; NVIDIA; DEVCOM ARL
problem: Sim-to-real assembly policies can be too aggressive under pose uncertainty, causing part slip or damage, and their force behavior depends on careful controller gain tuning.
keyIdea: Condition an RL policy on a maximum allowable force threshold with an excess-force penalty, train under broad dynamics randomization (controller gains, friction, dead-zone), and add a success-prediction action for early termination and automatic threshold tuning.
architecture: Recurrent PPO with asymmetric actor-critic in Isaac Gym (Factory); outputs task-space impedance targets.
inputs: Noisy EE pose and velocity, estimated EE contact force, noisy fixed-part pose, previous action, force threshold
outputs: Relative (x, y, z, yaw) impedance control target plus early-termination (success) action
actionRepr: Per-step 4-D relative pose target for a task-space impedance controller
trainingData: Simulation only (Factory / IsaacGym); 3 seeds per task
whatChangedVsParent: Adds force observations, a tunable force threshold, dynamics randomization and success prediction to IndustReal-style sim-to-real assembly RL.
limitations: Main failures at high position-estimation error; training unstable with noise above sigma = 2.5 mm; nut orientation assumed known.
notes: RA-L 2025. Real Franka Panda; 855 real trials in the main table; handles up to 5 mm position error; snap-fit insertion needing 15 N shown via auto-tuned threshold. Authors say they plan to release code.

name: AdmitDiff
resolvedTitle: Admittance Visuomotor Policy Learning for General-Purpose Contact-Rich Manipulations
org: Southeast University (Nanjing)
problem: Diffusion visuomotor policies plan trajectories from images but pay little attention to force control and smooth transitions between contact stages in multi-stage contact-rich tasks.
keyIdea: A diffusion policy with multi-head outputs that jointly predicts end-effector pose, finger joints and desired contact force from vision, proprioception and wrist F/T; an admittance controller interpolates and tracks the force-position trajectory, and consistency distillation enables single-step denoising.
architecture: Diffusion Policy-style noise network with ResNet-18 image encoders, 3-layer MLP low-dim encoder, FiLM conditioning, multi-level feature fusion and multi-head conv prediction blocks; teacher (100 steps) distilled into a one-step consistency student. Low-cost teleoperation rig (T265 wrist tracking, Leap Motion hand retargeting, vibration-motor force feedback, under $400).
inputs: Global and palm camera RGB, proprioception, wrist F/T measurements (previous 2 steps)
outputs: EE pose, LEAP Hand finger joints, desired contact force
actionRepr: Chunk of 8 future steps of EE pose + finger joints + desired force, executed via admittance control
trainingData: 50 teleoperated demonstrations per task, 5 tasks; 400 epochs (about 8 h) per task

headlineResults.comparedTo: Diffusion Policy 60%, Consistency Policy 70%, w/o force control 73%

whatChangedVsParent: Predicts dynamic desired contact force (not controller stiffness as in Comp-ACT) and executes it through an admittance controller, with one-step consistency-distilled sampling.
limitations: Drawing task stayed low for all methods (45% best) due to spatial-understanding demands; future work targets finger-level admittance control and more complex tasks.
notes: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics 2025 (P10 ref [7]). Tasks: insertion, door opening, drawer dragging, wiping, drawing. Authors state code and design files will be public.

name: ForceMimic
resolvedTitle: ForceMimic: Force-Centric Imitation Learning with Force-Motion Capture System for Contact-Rich Manipulation
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
problem: Robot learning focuses on trajectory policies with little attention to force skills, and force-centric demonstrations are hard to collect (teleoperation with force feedback is slow and unnatural).
keyIdea: ForceCapture, a handheld robot-free device with a 6-axis F/T sensor and SLAM camera, records natural force-motion demonstrations; HybridIL predicts both pose and wrench and executes them with orthogonal hybrid force-position control primitives.
architecture: Modified Diffusion Policy with an MLP point-cloud encoder concatenated with TCP pose; switches between IK joint-position control (predicted force below 6 N) and a hybrid force-position controller (Flexiv RDK) that projects predicted force orthogonal to motion direction.
inputs: Point cloud (from L515 RGB-D, 10,000 points), robot TCP pose
outputs: Pose and wrench parameters for the next 20 steps
actionRepr: Chunk of 20 future pose + 6-D wrench targets via diffusion, executed by hybrid force/position primitives
trainingData: 15 zucchinis, 438 peeling skill segments, 30,199 action sequences; 500 epochs

headlineResults.comparedTo: Raw DP 55%, Force DP 10%, Force+Hybrid DP 20%
about 13 min force-feedback teleoperation; 2.9 min bare human

whatChangedVsParent: Adds wrench prediction and hybrid force-position execution to a diffusion policy, trained on robot-free handheld force-motion demonstrations.
limitations: Simple MLP representations; only two control primitives; demonstrated on a single peeling skill; feeding measured force as input hurt performance due to force distribution mismatch.
notes: ICRA 2025. Abstract states 54.5% relative success increase over pure-vision imitation learning. Hardware, code and data released on project site. Counterintuitive finding: Force DP (force as input) did worse than vision-only.

name: DIPCOM / Comp-ACT
resolvedTitle: Learning Diffusion Policies from Demonstrations For Compliant Contact-rich Manipulation (DIPCOM); baseline Comp-ACT = Learning Variable Compliance Control From a Few Demonstrations for Bimanual Robot with Haptic Feedback Teleoperation System
org: OMRON SINIC X; Osaka University
authorsShort: Aburub et al. (DIPCOM); Kamijo et al. (Comp-ACT)
problem: Rigid position-controlled robots struggle to sustain stable contact and consistent force; the earlier Comp-ACT (VAE/ACT-based compliance policy) fails on long-horizon repetitive contact tasks like powder grinding.
keyIdea: Replace Comp-ACT's CVAE-ACT policy with a diffusion policy that predicts absolute EE pose, gripper width and 6-D stiffness (diagonal) from images, F/T and proprioception, executed by a compliance controller, with long horizons and temporal ensembling.
architecture: Encoder-decoder transformer diffusion policy (DDIM) with ResNet-18 vision backbone (no pretraining); observations encoded with self-attention, noisy actions cross-attend in decoder; compliance controller (FDCC per P10) converts to joint commands.
inputs: RGB images (1-3 views), 6-D F/T reading, 9-D proprioception
outputs: Absolute EE pose (3-D position + 6-D rotation), gripper width, 6-D stiffness
actionRepr: Chunk of about 48 actions (pose + gripper + stiffness) via DDIM diffusion with temporal ensemble
trainingData: 40-60 VR-teleoperated demonstrations per task (from 3 demonstrators); two UR5e arms with wrist F/T
whatChangedVsParent: Swaps the CVAE-ACT generator of Comp-ACT for a transformer diffusion policy with longer horizons and 6-D rotation representation.
limitations: More sensitive to hyperparameters and computationally heavier than Comp-ACT, making control frequency vulnerable; trained on few demos, one policy per task.
notes: Combined card: P10 lists DIPCOM [13] (SII 2026) and Comp-ACT [14] (IROS 2024) separately; both predict EE pose + stiffness for a compliance controller on UR5e. Comp-ACT details here are only as described in the DIPCOM paper (CVAE decoder transformer, trained from few demonstrations with haptic-feedback teleoperation); Comp-ACT's own paper was not read. Comp-ACT arXiv id not confirmed.

name: FARM
resolvedTitle: Tactile-Conditioned Diffusion Policy for Force-Aware Robotic Manipulation
org: TU Darmstadt; DFKI; Hessian.AI
problem: Visuotactile imitation learning usually treats touch only as an extra observation, leaving grip force an uncontrolled side effect of gripper position commands.
keyIdea: FARM puts force into both observation and action: GelSight Mini images are converted to shear/normal force distributions (FEATS), and a diffusion policy jointly predicts pose, grip width and target grip force, executed by a dual-mode width/force gripper controller.
architecture: Diffusion Policy 1D temporal CNN with FiLM (LeRobot); separate ResNet-18 encoders for wrist RGB and the 3-channel force-distribution image; demos from a handheld UMI gripper with GelSight Mini, deployed on a matching Actuated UMI gripper on a Franka Research 3.
inputs: Wrist RGB (96x96), grip width, FEATS force-distribution image + total normal force, gripper pose (3-D position + 6-D rotation); 2-step history
outputs: Absolute EE pose, target grip width, target grip force
actionRepr: Prediction horizon 32, execution horizon 16 of pose + grip width + grip force via diffusion
trainingData: Robot-free handheld UMI demonstrations with GelSight Mini (counts not retrieved)
controlRateHz: Policy 7 Hz; gripper force loop 25 Hz; gripper motor about 50 Hz
whatChangedVsParent: Adds target grip force as an explicit action and high-dimensional force distributions as observation, versus UMI/DP position-only gripper control.
limitations: Paper lists future work: bimanual, anthropomorphic hands, flow-matching objective for reactivity; FEATS force estimates may deviate due to model assumptions.
notes: Tasks: plant insertion, grape picking, screw tightening. Paper reports FARM outperforms force-aware, tactile-aware and vision-only baselines, but the per-task success table was not retrieved in this pass. Code and design files open-sourced (tactile-farm.github.io). P10 ref [19].

name: TLA
resolvedTitle: TLA: Tactile-Language-Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
org: Samsung Research China - Beijing; CASIA; BAAI
problem: VLA models lack touch, and there are neither tactile-action instruction datasets nor tactile-language-action models for contact-rich manipulation.
keyIdea: Fine-tune Qwen2-VL on a 24k-pair simulated tactile-action instruction dataset for fingertip peg-in-hole, tiling a sequence of left/right tactile images into one composite image and predicting numeric actions as text tokens.
architecture: Qwen2-VL: frozen ViT as tactile encoder (8 tactile frames in a 3x3 grid, 616x616) + Qwen2 7B language model fine-tuned with LoRA; actions scaled to integers and decoded from text.
inputs: Sequence of GelStereo 2.0 tactile images (2 fingers x 4 timesteps), language instruction
outputs: 3-D corrective action (dx, dy, drz)
actionRepr: Single-step 3-D action emitted as text number tokens (beam search)
trainingData: 24k tactile sequence / action pairs from Isaac Gym FEM tactile simulation, 2.0 mm clearance only

headlineResults.benchmark: Insertion across clearances (2.0/1.6/1.0 mm), 50 trials each

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces vision with tactile image sequences as the VLM input to generate contact-correcting actions.
limitations: Temporal information encoded only by spatial tiling; rudimentary tactile representation and action de-tokenization; weaker on y-axis (perpendicular to gripper); experiments in simulation, real-world sim-to-real still to be tested.
notes: Evaluation in simulation (insertion trials in simulated environment). Authors release all data, models and code. P10 lists TLA as tactile + language input only.

name: FILIC
resolvedTitle: FILIC: Dual-Loop Force-Guided Imitation Learning with Impedance Torque Control for Contact-Rich Manipulation Tasks
org: Tsinghua University; HKUST (Guangzhou); DISCOVER Robotics
problem: Imitation policies are position-centric without force awareness, and wrist F/T sensors are costly for low-cost collaborative arms.
keyIdea: A dual-loop design: an ACT-style Transformer policy consumes images plus end-effector wrench estimated without sensors (Jacobian pseudo-inverse on joint torques minus a MuJoCo digital-twin prediction), and outputs pose targets tracked by a joint-space impedance torque controller.
architecture: ACT backbone (CVAE, 4 encoder / 7 decoder layers, hidden 512) with dual ResNet image encoders, MLP force encoder and cross-attention vision-force fusion; inner loop: IK + impedance (MIT-mode) torque control with gravity/Coriolis compensation from a synchronized MuJoCo twin.
inputs: Two RGB cameras, EE pose, estimated 6-D EE wrench
outputs: 6-DoF EE target pose sequence -> joint torques via impedance control
actionRepr: Chunk of 25 EE poses with temporal ensembling (ACT)
trainingData: Simulation: 150 trajectories (peg-in-hole) collected with vibro-haptic handheld controller; real tasks on AIRBOT Play (demo counts not retrieved)
controlRateHz: Policy 25 Hz; gravity compensation 250 Hz; impedance loop 2 kHz

headlineResults.benchmark: Real Plug / E-stop / Clamp / Cap (30 trials)

whatChangedVsParent: Adds sensorless estimated EE wrench as input and an impedance torque inner loop to an ACT policy.
limitations: Force reconstruction relies on modeled dynamics; fixed impedance parameters (variable impedance left to future work).
notes: Wrench estimator code open-sourced (mujoco-wrench-estimator). P10 classifies FILIC as ACT architecture with impedance control on AIRBOT Play.

name: ManipForce
resolvedTitle: ManipForce: Force-Guided Policy Learning with Frequency-Aware Representation for Contact-Rich Manipulation
org: GIST (Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology); KIMM
problem: Imitation learning relies on vision-only demos; handheld interfaces like UMI lack F/T, and prior RGB-F/T work downsamples high-frequency force to image rate and relies on point clouds.
keyIdea: ManipForce: a handheld dual-camera gripper with wrist F/T (ArUco pose tracking, gravity compensation); FMT, a transformer diffusion policy that tokenizes 30 Hz RGB and 200 Hz F/T with frequency- and modality-aware embeddings and fuses them via bi-directional cross-attention.
architecture: DINOv2-B image encoder for two wrist cameras, 1D CNN F/T encoder, learnable spatial/frequency/modality embeddings, bi-directional cross-attention, Time-series Diffusion Transformer policy head.
inputs: Two hand-eye RGB streams (2 frames), F/T window (8 samples at 200 Hz)
outputs: 6-DoF EE pose deltas + gripper
actionRepr: Action sequence via transformer diffusion (6-DoF delta poses)
trainingData: About 100 handheld demonstrations per task, 6 tasks
whatChangedVsParent: Adds high-rate F/T to a UMI-style handheld interface and fuses asynchronous RGB/F/T natively via frequency-aware embeddings instead of downsampling.
limitations: Paper plans extension to longer-horizon and more dexterous tasks; no other explicit limitations retrieved.
notes: Hardware and software released. Tasks: gear assembly, LAN plug insertion, box flipping, open lid, battery disassembly, battery insertion. The paper names the policy FMT; ManipForce is the data-collection system.

name: TACT
resolvedTitle: TACT: Humanoid Whole-body Contact Manipulation through Deep Imitation Learning with Tactile Modality
org: CNRS-AIST JRL; Tokyo University of Science; University of Tsukuba
problem: Humanoid whole-body contact manipulation (using arms and chest, not just hands) is hard to model and needs perception of broad-area contact.
keyIdea: Extend ACT with a tactile token (163 upper-body tactile/proximity cells, flattened and linearly projected) and combine the learned upper-body policy with model-based retargeting and biped locomotion control on a life-size humanoid.
architecture: CVAE transformer (ACT) with ResNet-18 image features plus a linear-projected tactile token fed to encoder and condition blocks; outputs human arm poses that are retargeted via IK; model-based ZMP/damping locomotion control.
inputs: Arm joint positions, head camera RGB, distributed tactile + proximity measurements (163 cells)
outputs: Target poses of elbows and wrists (human-arm pose space), retargeted to robot joints
actionRepr: Action chunks of arm (elbow/wrist) poses via CVAE transformer
trainingData: Teleoperation demos via upper-body pose trackers; e.g. 8 episodes per plastic-bag motion; 30 demos for simulated box reorientation

headlineResults.benchmark: Real RHP7 Kaleido: hold up paper boxes (14 trials)

whatChangedVsParent: Adds a distributed tactile/proximity token to ACT and couples it with model-based humanoid retargeting and walking control.
limitations: Small boxes failed due to large size variation in data; position-controlled robot limits stiff/heavy objects; locomotion controller must be improved for heavier loads; GCN tactile encoders did not help.
notes: RA-L 2025. Life-size humanoid RHP7 Kaleido; claims first whole-body contact loco-manipulation by imitation learning with visual + tactile input. P10 lists TACT with ACT Phase 1 and admittance-style model-based Phase 2.

name: TaF-VLA
resolvedTitle: Tactile-Force Alignment in Vision-Language-Action Models for Force-aware Manipulation
org: Beihang University; ShanghaiTech; BIGAI; HKU
problem: Tactile-augmented VLAs treat vision-based tactile images as extra visual texture (tactile-vision alignment), missing the link between surface deformation and interaction force.
keyIdea: Shift to tactile-force alignment: pretrain a TaF-Adapter (causal transformer over tactile sequences) contrastively against VQ-VAE-quantized 6-axis F/T and force-map codebooks on a 10M-frame dataset, then plug its force-aligned tokens into pi0.5.
architecture: TaF-Adapter: causal transformer tactile encoder + two VQ-VAE force codebooks aligned via InfoNCE; frozen and injected as tactile tokens into a pi0.5 VLA backbone whose action expert uses flow matching.
inputs: Scene RGB images, language (including force-aware instructions), proprioception, sequential vision-based tactile images
outputs: End-effector action chunks
actionRepr: Flow-matching action chunks (pi0.5 action expert, 10 integration steps)
trainingData: TaF-Dataset: over 10M synchronized tactile / 6-axis F/T / force-map frames from 6 VBTS sensors (automated rig, 100k frames/hour); policy fine-tuning on over 10,000 force-aware episodes across 20+ scenarios
whatChangedVsParent: Aligns tactile embeddings to measured force (not to images) before injecting them into the pi0.5 VLA.
limitations: Limitations section not retrieved in this pass.
notes: Abstract/intro claim an average 22% improvement over the SOTA tactile-vision-aligned baseline. Adapter is plug-and-play for ACT and DP. Intro mentions 7 tasks while Fig. 4 caption says 8; table reports 7.

name: Force Policy
resolvedTitle: Force Policy: Learning Hybrid Force-Position Control Policy under Interaction Frame for Contact-Rich Manipulation
org: Noematrix; Flexiv; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Zhejiang University; Shanghai Innovation Institute
problem: Monolithic force-aware policies entangle global visual decision-making with local contact refinement, and control-centric methods assume a known task structure or only learn controller gains.
keyIdea: Formalize a physically grounded interaction frame (recovered from demonstrations via power/dissipation residuals) and use a global-local design: a 5 Hz global vision policy guides free-space motion, and on contact a 50 Hz local force policy predicts the interaction frame, selection mask and reference wrench for hybrid force-position control.
architecture: Global: RISE-2 3D visuomotor policy (its diffusion-head condition used as a global feature). Local: wrist-image ResNet + proprioception GRU, FiLM-conditioned on the global feature, gated fusion, MIP head for motion chunk and MLP head for frame/mask/wrench. Dual-policy asynchronous scheduler with DTW chunk alignment.
inputs: Global: 3D scene (image + depth); local: wrist image, wrench and proprioceptive history
outputs: Interaction frame, selection mask, reference wrench, relative motion chunk; executed by hybrid force-position controller (Flexiv)
actionRepr: Local action = {interaction frame, 6-D selection mask, reference wrench, delta motion chunk}; global action chunks in free space
trainingData: Real teleoperated demonstrations (arm-to-arm force-feedback teleop); counts not retrieved
controlRateHz: Global 5 Hz; local and scheduler 50 Hz

headlineResults.benchmark: Push and Flip, unseen objects (6 objects x 5 trials)
headlineResults.comparedTo: RISE-2 best 3/5, pi0.5 best 3/5, TA-VLA best 3/5, RDP/FoAR/ForceVLA mostly 0/5

headlineResults.metric: success with its IF recovery vs wrench-only labels
headlineResults.comparedTo: Force Policy trained with wrench-only interaction frames

whatChangedVsParent: Explicitly predicts the interaction frame and force/motion subspace split (instead of only stiffness or single-axis force) and decouples a plug-and-play global vision policy from a fast local force policy.
limitations: IF theory limited to stable, topologically invariant contact (no fracture); evaluated on peg-in-hole and surface interaction classes; does not estimate the true contact point needed for torque control; force not used for high-level decisions.
notes: Main multi-task success table not retrieved in this pass; paper reports consistent gains over RISE-2, pi0.5, RDP, FoAR, ForceVLA and TA-VLA. P10 lists Force-Policy as DP-based with hybrid F/P on Flexiv Rizon.

name: FACTR
resolvedTitle: FACTR: Force-Attending Curriculum Training for Contact-Rich Policy Learning
org: Carnegie Mellon University
problem: Force information available on arms like Franka is rarely used; low-cost leader-follower teleop lacks force feedback, and policies given force input tend to ignore it and overfit to vision.
keyIdea: A low-cost bilateral leader-follower teleop that relays follower external joint torques to an actuated leader (with gravity compensation and null-space redundancy resolution), plus a curriculum that blurs/downsamples visual inputs with decreasing strength so the policy learns to attend to force.
architecture: Encoder-decoder transformer (ACT-style): pretrained ViT vision tokens + one MLP force token from external joint torques; action tokens cross-attend to regress joint-position chunks; curriculum operator applied in pixel or latent space.
inputs: RGB (front or wrist camera), external joint torques
outputs: Future joint position targets
actionRepr: Chunk of k joint position targets (MSE regression)
trainingData: 50 teleoperated demonstrations per task; 4 tasks (box lift, non-prehensile pivot, fruit pick-place, dough rolling)

headlineResults.benchmark: Box lift recovery after knock-down (test objects)

whatChangedVsParent: Adds a force token and a vision-corrupting curriculum to ACT, and force feedback to a GELLO-style leader arm.
limitations: External joint torque sensing is imprecise for subtle forces; assumes arms with joint torque sensors; curriculum hyperparameters can be task-dependent.
notes: RSS 2025. Codebases and instructions released at jasonjzliu.com/factr. Abstract states +43% generalization to unseen objects vs no curriculum; body says 40.0% average. Franka Panda with OpenManipulator-X grippers. CRAFT later replaces the blur curriculum with a variational information bottleneck.

name: ForceSight
resolvedTitle: ForceSight: Text-Guided Mobile Manipulation with Visual-Force Goals
org: Georgia Institute of Technology (Hello Robot)
problem: Deep models that output human-interpretable kinematic goals relegate force to low-level execution, even though force is critical for contact tasks.
keyIdea: A text-conditioned RGBD vision transformer predicts visual-force goals: a kinematic goal (gripper 3D position via affordance and depth maps, yaw, width) plus a force goal (applied force vector and grip force), executed by visual-force servoing through a sequence of action primitives.
architecture: ViT-Large (304M, ImageNet-21k init) with RGBD patch embedding and cross-attention to a frozen T5 text encoder at every block; convolutional decoders for affordance/depth maps; MLP heads for width, yaw, applied force, grip force.
inputs: Single eye-in-hand RGBD image (224x224), text prompt with appended action primitive
outputs: Visual-force goal: fingertip/goal location, yaw, gripper width, 3-D applied force, grip force
actionRepr: Keyframe goal (4-DoF pose + width + forces) tracked by a proportional visual-force servo controller
trainingData: Over 26,000 datapoints (about 10,000 demonstrations) from about 30 h of Stretch RE1 teleoperation
whatChangedVsParent: Adds explicit force goals (applied and grip force) to a text-conditioned keyframe goal predictor, instead of kinematic-only goals as in PerAct.
limitations: Depth prediction errors at distance; target must be in camera view; assumes constant pitch and roll; limited task scope; only tested on Stretch RE1.
notes: ICRA 2024. Code, dataset and trained models released. Mobile manipulator (Stretch RE1) with wrist ATI F/T sensor; grip force estimated by a small MLP.

name: CRAFT
resolvedTitle: CRAFT: Adapting VLA Models to Contact-rich Manipulation via Force-aware Curriculum Fine-tuning
org: Hunan University; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics; NUS
problem: When VLAs are fine-tuned with force, high-entropy vision/language inputs dominate and low-entropy but critical force signals get ignored.
keyIdea: Insert a variational information bottleneck on vision and language embeddings with a KL weight that starts high and is annealed, so fine-tuning first relies on joint-torque force signals and then gradually restores full multimodal information.
architecture: Plug-in VIB module after the VLM encoder of pretrained VLAs (pi0 and RDT); joint torque used as the proprioceptive/force state; Franka under impedance control with a homologous leader-follower teleop with force feedback.
inputs: Wrist + third-person RGB, language, joint torques
outputs: Action chunk over horizon H (backbone's native action space)
actionRepr: Backbone's action head (pi0 flow matching or RDT diffusion) action chunks
trainingData: Teleoperated demonstrations on 5 real tasks (counts not retrieved)
whatChangedVsParent: Replaces FACTR's heuristic image-blur curriculum with an annealed information bottleneck on vision-language embeddings inside pretrained VLAs.
limitations: No explicit limitations section retrieved.
notes: Tasks: USB insertion, shaft-to-hole insertion, flip carton, wipe whiteboard, rolling plasticine. Ablation: base 20.0%, +VIB 46.7%, +VIB & force 56.7%.

name: EquiContact
resolvedTitle: EquiContact: A Hierarchical SE(3) Vision-to-Force Equivariant Policy for Spatially Generalizable Contact-rich Tasks
org: UC Berkeley; Yonsei University
problem: Visuomotor policies like ACT and DP generalize poorly to new spatial configurations, and high-level equivariant planners lack the sub-millimeter precision contact tasks need.
keyIdea: Anchor a localized compliant policy on a globally estimated reference frame: Diff-EDF estimates SE(3) reference frames from point clouds, and G-CompACT outputs relative pose and admittance gains from local observations, executed by geometric admittance control, making the whole pipeline provably SE(3)-equivariant.
architecture: High level: Diffusion Equivariant Descriptor Fields (Diff-EDF) on scene point clouds. Low level: Geometric Compliant ACT (ACT with CLIP-RN50 vision, language-guided features) using geometrically consistent error vectors, F/T in EE frame and wrist RGB; geometric admittance controller.
inputs: Scene point cloud (high level); GCEV, EE-frame F/T, wrist RGB, text prompt (low level)
outputs: Reference frames (high level); relative desired pose + admittance gains (low level)
actionRepr: ACT action chunks of relative EE pose + admittance gains
trainingData: Teleoperated demos at a single fixed platform pose (with visual distractors); 20 demos for Diff-EDF
whatChangedVsParent: Makes CompACT equivariant by expressing observations/actions in a local frame anchored to an equivariantly estimated reference frame.
limitations: Fails near manipulator singularities (symmetry breaking); small datasets limit wiping/screwing; extreme transformations fail for wiping and screwing.
notes: P10 lists EquiContact with admittance control outputting action + stiffness K. Assumes peg aligned in gripper and hole yaw known within 90 deg.

name: MoDE-VLA
resolvedTitle: Towards Human-Like Manipulation through RL-Augmented Teleoperation and Mixture-of-Dexterous-Experts VLA
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Sharpa; Shanghai AI Lab; Zhongguancun Academy; NUS
problem: VLAs are confined to low-DoF grippers; extending them to bimanual dexterous in-hand manipulation faces a data bottleneck (63-DoF teleop), multi-skill learning, and heterogeneous force/tactile fusion.
keyIdea: IMCopilot, RL-trained in-hand skills (grasp maintenance, in-hand rotation), assists teleoperators via foot pedal and is later called by the VLA as a primitive; MoDE-VLA fuses arm joint torques and fingertip tactile wrenches via self-attention, sparse mixture-of-experts and residual injection into pi0's action expert.
architecture: pi0 backbone (SigLIP So400m/14 + PaliGemma Gemma-3B + Gemma-300M action expert) extended with a MoDE block: force (14-D arm torques) and tactile (60-D fingertip wrenches) tokens, self-attention with backbone tokens, top-k sparse MoE, modality-specific residual heads for arm vs hand actions; IMCopilot PPO skills (IsaacLab, teacher-student).
inputs: Head stereo RGB + wrist fisheye RGB, language, proprioception, arm joint torques, fingertip 6-D wrenches
outputs: Arm, hand and waist actions plus an IMCopilot trigger scalar
actionRepr: Flow-matching action chunks (horizon H) with residual force/tactile corrections; hand actions overridden by IMCopilot when trigger > 0.5
trainingData: Teleoperated bimanual demonstrations with exoskeleton, gloves, VR and IMCopilot assistance (counts not retrieved)

headlineResults.benchmark: 4 dexterous contact-rich tasks (gear assembly, charger plugging, tube rearranging, apple peeling)

whatChangedVsParent: Adds a separate force/tactile MoE pathway with residual injection (vs ForceVLA's force MoE on grippers) and an RL in-hand skill primitive callable by the VLA, for dual dexterous hands.
limitations: Not retrieved in this pass.
notes: Platform: SharpaNorth with dual 7-DoF arms and 22-DoF SharpaWave hands (63 active DoF). Claims first autonomous dual-dexterous-hand apple peeling. Per-task success table not retrieved; no total parameter count stated (components: Gemma-3B VLM + Gemma-300M action expert). P10 labels it VLA+RL on SharpaNorth.

name: ForceVLA2
resolvedTitle: ForceVLA2: Unleashing Hybrid Force-Position Control with Force Awareness for Contact-Rich Manipulation
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory; Tongji; SJTU; Shanghai Innovation Institute; Noematrix; ECNU; Zhongguancun Academy; NUS; Lumos Robotics
problem: Existing VLAs, including ForceVLA, use force only as a perceptual input and output position-only actions, lacking active closed-loop force regulation and stage-aware force reasoning.
keyIdea: Force prompts (text subtask/force state) give the VLM stage-aware force concepts, while a Cross-Scale MoE in the action expert fuses these with raw force (via a bypass path) to output hybrid force-position actions plus a subtask transition indicator.
architecture: pi0-style PaliGemma/SigLIP VLM + flow-matching action expert; multimodal encoder for EE pose and force tokens; force bypass to a Cross-Scale MoE; outputs pose delta, wrench and progress.
inputs: 3 RGB views (2 static + wrist), task prompt, force prompt, EE 6D pose, 6-D F/T
outputs: EE pose change (7-D), target contact force (6-D), subtask transition indicator
actionRepr: Flow-matching hybrid force-position action [delta pose 7-D; force 6-D] plus progress scalar
trainingData: ForceVLA2-Dataset: 1,000 trajectories (about 500K timesteps) over 5 tasks, force-feedback GELLO teleop on Flexiv Rizon 4s; F/T at 300 Hz

headlineResults.comparedTo: pi0 48%, pi0.5 35%, ForceVLA 31% (as stated in conclusion)

whatChangedVsParent: Moves from force-as-input (ForceVLA) to force-as-output hybrid force-position control with force prompts and a cross-scale MoE.
limitations: Limitations section not retrieved; ablation notes extra force tokens slightly hurt simple single-switch tasks.
notes: CONFLICT (internal): abstract says it outperforms pi0 and pi0.5 'by 48.0% and 35.0%', while the conclusion says pi0/pi0.5/ForceVLA obtain 48%/35%/31% on average; the text also says pi0 with naive force reaches 17%, 'similar to the base version'. Treat baseline numbers with care. Appendix calls the model Foca-VLA (earlier name).

name: ReTac-ACT
resolvedTitle: ReTac-ACT: A State-Gated Vision-Tactile Fusion Transformer for Precision Assembly
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications; SunHDex; University of Hamburg
problem: In the 'last millimeter' of precision assembly, vision fails from end-effector/workpiece occlusion, and naive vision-tactile fusion suffers modality imbalance.
keyIdea: Extend ACT with separate tactile encoder, bidirectional vision-tactile cross-attention, a proprioception-conditioned gate that shifts weight to touch on contact, and an auxiliary tactile reconstruction loss (plus contrastive alignment).
architecture: ACT CVAE transformer (4-layer encoder, 1-layer decoder, D=512); ResNet-18 visual encoders for 3 cameras; 5-layer CNN tactile encoder (196 tokens) with transposed-conv reconstruction decoder; 3-layer MLP gate on proprioception.
inputs: 3 RGB views (2 wrist + 1 third-person), 4 Xense optical tactile images, proprioception
outputs: 14-DoF bimanual joint targets + 2 gripper commands
actionRepr: Action chunk of k=100 (ACT CVAE decoder)
trainingData: Released dataset of over 5,000 VR-teleop demos (5 shapes x 4 clearances, NIST ATB M1); 50-100 demos per clearance level used for training

headlineResults.benchmark: NIST ATB M1 peg-in-hole, 3 mm clearance (20 trials)

whatChangedVsParent: Adds native tactile tokens with state-gated reciprocal fusion and a reconstruction objective to ACT.
limitations: Evaluated only on cylindrical pegs; other NIST shapes, sim-to-real tactile transfer and VLA integration left to future work.
notes: Bimanual Realman RM75-6F-V arms. Code and dataset stated to be released. P10 classifies it as ACT with position control.

name: TacVLA
resolvedTitle: TacVLA: Contact-Aware Tactile Fusion for Robust Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
org: Purdue University; Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia
problem: VLAs relying on vision and language struggle under occlusion and fine contact, and naively concatenating dense image-like tactile tokens adds cost and interference during non-contact phases.
keyIdea: Encode a compact 15x8 tactile array into 36 tokens and use a contact-aware gate that masks tactile tokens out of attention (and zeroes them) until a threshold-based contact flag fires, fine-tuning pi0.5 with LoRA.
architecture: pi0.5 (OpenPI) with SigLIP vision encoder, PaliGemma tokenizer, Gemma 2.6B VLM and flow-matching action expert; MLP tactile encoder with 2D sin-cos embeddings; contact-dependent attention mask.
inputs: Front + wrist RGB, language, proprioception, 15x8 tactile pressure map
outputs: Continuous robot action sequences
actionRepr: Flow-matching action chunk a_{t:t+H} (pi0.5 action expert)
trainingData: 50 teleoperated demos per task, 5 tasks (4 constraint-locked disassembly + in-box picking), 10 Hz; LoRA fine-tuning 10,000 steps per task
whatChangedVsParent: Adds compact tactile tokens with contact-gated attention to pi0.5 instead of always-on image-like tactile tokens.
limitations: Binary threshold gate (not learned); low spatial resolution tactile array; evaluated on short-horizon contact-centric tasks.
notes: Franka Panda; one task-specific model per task. Robustness demo shows recovery after human disturbance. Arxiv v4 (Sep 2026).

name: KineDex
resolvedTitle: KineDex: Learning Tactile-Informed Visuomotor Policies via Kinesthetic Teaching for Dexterous Manipulation
org: Tongji University; Tsinghua University; SJTU; HKU; Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute; Shanghai AI Lab
problem: Teleoperation and video retargeting for dexterous hands suffer kinematic mismatch and give the operator no real-time tactile feedback, so high-fidelity tactile demonstrations are hard to collect.
keyIdea: Hand-over-hand kinesthetic teaching: the operator 'wears' the robot hand via finger straps, so motions transfer directly and contact forces are felt; the human is inpainted out of the images, and the policy predicts fingertip forces as well as joint targets for force control at deployment.
architecture: Diffusion Policy (U-Net) with a multi-view visual encoder plus a tactile encoder (shared 1D conv per finger + 2-layer MLP); Grounded-SAM + ProPainter remove the operator from images before training; a modified PD controller converts predicted fingertip forces into force-informed target positions.
inputs: 2 RGB views (front + wrist, inpainted), 5x120x3 fingertip tactile arrays, arm TCP pose and hand joint positions
outputs: 23-D action: 6-DoF end-effector pose, 12 hand joint angles, 5 fingertip normal-force targets
actionRepr: chunk of 16 actions (23-D: pose + joints + fingertip normal forces) via diffusion, executed with force control
trainingData: ~100 kinesthetic demos per task for simpler tasks, ~150 for harder ones (toothpaste, syringe); 9 tasks; Franka + Robotera XHand1 (12 DoF, 120 taxels per finger)
controlRateHz: Interpolation controller: 100 Hz arm, 50 Hz hand

headlineResults.benchmark: 9 real contact-rich dexterous tasks (20 trials each)
headlineResults.comparedTo: 57.7% improvement over variant without force control

headlineResults.benchmark: Cap Twisting / Toothpaste Squeezing / Syringe Pressing

whatChangedVsParent: Versus DexForce, uses a higher-DoF tactile hand and inpainting instead of trajectory replay to get clean observations, enabling longer and harder tasks.
limitations: Inpainting may degrade under severe occlusion; two human hands are needed to drive one robot hand (thumb separately), limiting bimanual demos.
notes: Project page https://dinomini00.github.io/KineDex/. Force control is the dominant factor: without it success is 0/20 on 5 of 9 tasks.

name: OmniVTA
resolvedTitle: OmniVTA: Visuo-Tactile World Modeling for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
org: NUS; CASIA; Fudan; TARS Robotics; Tsinghua; Zhongguancun Academy; Beihang
problem: Visuo-tactile datasets are small and narrow, and existing methods treat touch as a passive observation executed open-loop in action chunks, so they cannot react to slip, misalignment or disturbances.
keyIdea: A slow-fast design: a visuo-tactile world model predicts short-horizon future tactile/visual latents that feed a contact-aware fusion policy, while a 60 Hz reflexive controller corrects deviations between predicted and observed touch.
architecture: Four modules: TactileVAE (spatio-temporal encoder + implicit neural decoder); two-stream spatio-temporal DiT visuo-tactile world model; Adaptive Visuo-Tactile Fusion Policy (Latent Tactile Differential encoder, contact-probability gating, 1D U-Net diffusion policy); Reflexive Latent Tactile Controller (3-layer MLP residual corrector).
inputs: 2 visual frames (15 Hz), 8 tactile frames (60 Hz, visuo-tactile sensors such as GelSight Mini/Tac3D/Xense/Daimon), 2 proprioceptive states
outputs: Relative-action chunks of 6 actions (15 FPS, interpolated to 60 Hz) plus 60 Hz residual corrections
actionRepr: chunk of 6 relative end-effector actions via diffusion (1D U-Net), with 60 Hz MLP residual correction
trainingData: OmniViTac: 21,879 visuo-tactile-action trajectories, 86 tasks, 100+ objects, 6 interaction patterns (wipe, peel, cut, grasp, assembly, in-hand adjustment); 150 trajectories per object for world-model/policy training; ~1.2M tactile samples for TactileVAE
whatChangedVsParent: Unlike RDP's slow-fast policy that only reacts to touch, OmniVTA predicts future contact with a visuo-tactile world model and uses the prediction-observation difference for fusion and reflexive control.
notes: Real-robot success-rate tables were not in the retrieved pages, so only world-model prediction metrics are listed. Authors state all data, models and code will be released. Platform: xArm7 + TacUMI handheld interface.

name: OmniVTLA
resolvedTitle: OmniVTLA: Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Models with Semantic-Aligned Tactile Sensing
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Paxini Tech
problem: VLA models ignore touch and fail in contact-rich tasks; prior tactile-VLA attempts feed tactile data as low-level signals without semantic alignment to vision and language.
keyIdea: Add a dual tactile encoder path (a pretrained vision ViT plus a semantically-aligned tactile ViT, SA-ViT, trained contrastively on tri-modal data) to a pi0-style VLA.
architecture: Built on pi0: PaliGemma tokenizer, SigLIP-400M image encoder, Gemma-2.6B backbone, flow-matching action expert; tactile signals stitched into 224x224 images and encoded by ViT + SA-ViT (256 tokens). SA-ViT trained with AnyTouch stage-2 alignment losses on ObjTac plus existing tactile datasets.
inputs: Third-view and wrist RGB, tactile images (gripper or 11-sensor dexterous hand), language instruction, proprioception
outputs: Action chunk: 10-D for gripper (3 rel. position, 6 rel. rotation, 1 gripper) or 25-D for four-finger hand (3+6+16 joints)
actionRepr: action chunk via flow matching (pi0-style)
trainingData: ObjTac: 135K tri-modal (text/vision/tactile) samples, 56 objects in 10 categories, Paxini Gen2 sensors; 40 teleoperated demos per object at 30 Hz for policy tasks
whatChangedVsParent: Adds a semantically-aligned tactile encoder path to pi0 so touch tokens share a vision-language embedding space.
limitations: Repeated-attempt training data was needed only for contact-rich tasks; no gain in messy clutter where success depends on visual navigation.
notes: ObjTac dataset released (homepage https://readerek.github.io/Objtac.github.io/). Paper v3 dated June 2026. Also reports a from-scratch DP variant: VTA 78.1% vs DP 59.4% on gripper pick-and-place.

name: ViTaS
resolvedTitle: ViTaS: Visual Tactile Soft Fusion Contrastive Learning for Visuomotor Learning
org: Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute; Harbin Institute of Technology; Tsinghua University; HKU; CMU
problem: Visuo-tactile methods mostly concatenate features or only align them, missing the complementarity of touch and vision, so they struggle under (self-)occlusion.
keyIdea: Soft fusion contrastive learning (top-K visually similar frames' tactile counterparts are positives, alternating modalities) plus a CVAE that reconstructs the image from fused visuo-tactile features.
architecture: Separate CNN encoders for vision and touch; soft-fusion contrastive loss (K=10, alternating schedule) and CVAE reconstruction loss added to the policy loss (PPO for RL or Diffusion Policy for IL); only the two encoders are kept at inference.
inputs: RGB image(s) and tactile maps (e.g., 32x32x3 in sim; 16x16 3D-ViTaC maps in real)
outputs: Actions from PPO policy or Diffusion Policy head
actionRepr: task-dependent: PPO continuous actions (sim) or Diffusion Policy action sequence (IL)
trainingData: 12 simulated tasks across 5 environments (RL, 3e6 steps; IL with 50 demos/task) and 3 real tasks with 100 teleop demos each on Galaxea-R1

headlineResults.comparedTo: DP w/ CNN 38.2, DP w/ Transformer 33.4

whatChangedVsParent: Extends CoCLR-style co-training contrastive learning to cross-modal visuo-tactile fusion and adds CVAE reconstruction for complementarity.
limitations: Highly dynamic precise tasks like real-world pen spinning remain hard (RL bottleneck in high dimensions); deformable-object manipulation not explored.
notes: Project page https://skyrainwind.github.io/ViTaS/. Real-robot DP with ViTaS uses only head camera + touch, while baseline DP uses 3 cameras.

name: VLA-Touch
resolvedTitle: VLA-Touch: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Models with Dual-Level Tactile Feedback
org: National University of Singapore
problem: VLAs cannot interpret tactile signals, and there are no large multimodal datasets to fine-tune them with touch.
keyIdea: Add touch at two levels without fine-tuning the base VLA: a tactile-language model (Octopi) turns touch into text for a VLM planner, and an interpolant diffusion controller (BRIDGeR) refines VLA action chunks using tactile force signals.
architecture: GPT-4o task planner + Octopi tactile-language model (planning); RDT as base VLA; BRIDGeR stochastic-interpolant controller conditioned on DINOv2 visual embeddings, proprioception and GelSight marker-tracking force vector (X, Y, M).
inputs: Scene and wrist RGB, GelSight Mini tactile images, proprioception, task goal
outputs: Refined end-effector action chunks; updated language instructions from the planner
actionRepr: RDT 64-step action chunk, first 48 steps refined by interpolant diffusion from the VLA action distribution
trainingData: Kinesthetic demos: Cup (40+60 episodes, ~8 min), Wipe (40+60, ~15 min), Peel (60+120, ~30 min) at 10 Hz; RDT first fine-tuned on unrelated Franka data (100k steps)
controlRateHz: Refinement and execution at up to 8 Hz
whatChangedVsParent: Wraps an unmodified VLA with tactile-language planning feedback and a tactile interpolant refiner instead of retraining the VLA with touch.
limitations: Modular, loosely coupled design adds redundancy and latency; Octopi is not trained for force, so a separate marker-tracking path is used.
notes: Code is open-sourced per the abstract. Claims up to 40% planning-efficiency gain and up to 35% higher manipulation success vs vision-only VLA.

name: 3DTacDex
resolvedTitle: Canonical Representation and Force-Based Pretraining of 3D Tactile for Dexterous Visuo-Tactile Policy Learning
org: Peking University (CFCS, PKU-Agibot Lab)
problem: Distributed 3D tactile data on dexterous hands is high-dimensional with no standardized datasets or pretrained backbones, and converting it to 2D images loses spatial structure.
keyIdea: Canonicalize each sensor's taxel coordinates into a unit frame (plus sensor pose) and pretrain a graph encoder with self-supervised masked local-force and net-force prediction on play data.
architecture: GraphMAE-style GNN over taxels (12-D per node: sensor 6D pose, canonical 3D position, 3D force; 4-neighbourhood edges); pretrained encoder plugged into Diffusion Policy with a DINOv2 vision backbone.
inputs: Single RGB camera, 3D tactile from PaXini sensors on LEAP Hand, arm pose + 16 hand joints
outputs: Target arm end-effector pose (3 translation + 4 quaternion) and 16 hand joint targets
actionRepr: Diffusion Policy action sequence of target (intended) actions
trainingData: Self-collected tactile play data (T-DEX protocol) for pretraining; teleoperated demos (HaMeR + DexPilot) for 4 tasks

headlineResults.benchmark: 4 real dexterous tasks (Open Box, Reorientation, Flip, Assembly), 10 runs each

headlineResults.value: 48% w/o pretraining; 0% w/o canonical rep. and pretraining

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces T-DEX's 2D tactile images + BYOL pretraining with a canonical 3D graph representation and force-prediction pretraining.
limitations: Limited generalization to objects with significantly different shapes and dynamics.
notes: Name '3DTacDex' comes from project site https://3dtacdex.github.io; paper title does not use it. Hardware: JAKA MiniCobo arm + LEAP Hand, 3x5 taxel arrays per sensor.

name: VTAO-BiManip
resolvedTitle: VTAO-BiManip: Masked Visual-Tactile-Action Pre-training with Object Understanding for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
org: Zhejiang University
problem: Single-hand visuo-tactile pretraining does not capture inter-hand coordination, object-state changes or composition of sub-skills needed for bimanual dexterous tasks like bottle-cap twisting.
keyIdea: MAE-style pretraining on human bimanual data over vision, binary touch and hand joints that also predicts future actions and object pose/size, followed by two-stage curriculum RL (fixed bottle, then free bottle).
architecture: Transformer MAE encoder over 196 image patch tokens, 40 tactile tokens, 48 joint tokens, a fusion token and 9 object mask tokens; decoders reconstruct image, touch, current action, predict 5 future actions and object 6-DoF pose + 3-D size. Frozen encoder's fusion token feeds a PPO policy.
inputs: Egocentric RGB (224x224), binarized tactile (20 sensors per hand), joint angles/velocities of both hands
outputs: Joint targets for two Shadow Hands (46-D action in sim)
actionRepr: per-step continuous joint actions from PPO
trainingData: 216 human bimanual trajectories with 26 bottles (61,684 aligned frames) captured with HoloLens2, tactile gloves and 16-camera mocap; RL in Isaac Gym with 15 ShapeNet bottles (10 seen, 5 unseen)
whatChangedVsParent: Extends single-hand masked visuo-tactile pretraining to bimanual hands by adding joint-action tokens, future-action prediction and object pose/size reconstruction.
limitations: Overall success stays around 60% given object variety and action dimensionality; object understanding relies on motion-captured bounding boxes.
notes: Real-world deployment on dual LEAP Hands + Unitree Z1 is shown qualitatively (video) only. Single-stage RL gave zero success. IROS 2025.

name: VTLA
resolvedTitle: VTLA: Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Model with Preference Learning for Insertion Manipulation
org: Institute of Automation, CAS; Samsung R&D Institute China-Beijing; BAAI
problem: VLA models lack touch and are limited to visually dominated tasks; the tactile-only TLA lacks global vision, and next-token classification loss mismatches continuous control.
keyIdea: Fine-tune a VLM on vision + temporally-enhanced tactile image tokens to output insertion actions as text, then apply DPO preference learning to give regression-like supervision.
architecture: Qwen2-VL 7B; tactile 4-frame sequences tiled as 2x2 images encoded by the ViT; vision tokens placed after tactile (vision-guided temporally enhanced tokens); SFT with frozen vision encoder/adapter, then DPO.
inputs: Left/right fingertip tactile image sequences, wrist camera image, language instruction
outputs: Action text [dx, dy, drz]
actionRepr: single-step 3-DoF corrective action (x, y, z-rotation) as text tokens
trainingData: 28,000 simulated peg-in-hole samples (Isaac Gym + visuotactile simulator), 5 peg shapes, 0.6-2.0 mm clearance, domain randomization; 1k-2.4k DPO preference pairs
whatChangedVsParent: Adds wrist vision to TLA and replaces pure next-token SFT with SFT + DPO preference learning.
limitations: Tactile inputs use an off-the-shelf vision encoder, possibly losing tactile-specific features; deeper vision-tactile fusion inside LLMs remains open.
notes: Trained only in simulation, zero-shot sim-to-real on UR3 + GelStereo 2.0 sensors. Name collision: VTLA is also used generically by OmniVTLA for the model class.

name: ARCH
resolvedTitle: ARCH: Hierarchical Hybrid Learning for Long-Horizon Contact-Rich Robotic Assembly
org: Stanford University; MIT; University of Michigan; Autodesk Research
problem: End-to-end imitation needs many demos and lacks assembly precision, while RL is sample-inefficient on long horizons with sparse rewards.
keyIdea: Adaptive Robotic Compositional Hierarchy: a high-level DiT policy, imitation-learned from ~10 keyboard-selected primitive demos, sequences and parameterizes a library of motion-planning primitives (grasp, place, move) and a sim-trained RL insertion primitive using force-torque feedback.
architecture: High-level Diffusion Transformer (4 blocks, hidden 128) with Robomimic observation encoder outputs primitive scores and continuous parameters; low-level library of MP primitives (lazyPRM) and a PPO insertion policy trained in IsaacLab with domain randomization; CPPF++ pose estimation with Chamfer refinement.
inputs: Object 6D pose from RGB-D pose estimation, robot proprioception; RL insert primitive uses EE pose, force-torque and pose relative to goal
outputs: Discrete primitive choice plus its parameters (object index, SE(3) poses); insert primitive outputs EE velocity
actionRepr: parameterized primitives (PAMDP): categorical primitive + continuous parameters; RL primitive outputs EE velocity
trainingData: 10 high-level demonstrations (half successful, half with recovery), collected by selecting primitives, no teleoperation; RL insertion trained in sim with 1,000 parallel envs; trained on a single object (Hexagon)

headlineResults.comparedTo: Luo et al. 25%, MimicPlay 20%, DP 0%, PPO 0%; human oracle 65%

parents: Luo et al. multi-stage cable routing
whatChangedVsParent: Versus hierarchical IL (Luo et al.), uses a hybrid MP + sim-trained RL primitive library and a DiT high-level policy trained from primitive-level demos.
limitations: High-level policy is task-specific; objects are manually labelled/indexed; assumes tasks decompose into a finite set of parameterized primitives and known CAD models.
notes: CoRL 2025. Force-torque is used only inside the RL insertion primitive, not by the high-level policy. P10 classifies ARCH as 'RL, MP' Phase-1 architecture.

name: TouchGuide
resolvedTitle: TouchGuide: Inference-Time Steering of Visuomotor Policies via Touch Guidance
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Xense Robotics; Sun Yat-sen University; Oxford; Shanghai AI Lab; USTC; UCSD
problem: Feature-level visuo-tactile concatenation lets vision dominate, and policy-level composition needs multiple policies and misses cross-modal correlation.
keyIdea: Fuse touch in action space at inference time: a task-specific Contact Physical Model scores (vision, touch, noisy action) feasibility and its gradient steers late denoising/flow-matching steps of a frozen visuomotor policy, like classifier guidance.
architecture: Base policy (Diffusion Policy or pi0.5 action expert) unchanged; CPM uses DINOv2 encoders for tactile and visual inputs, an N-layer Transformer encoder and an action encoder, trained with symmetric contrastive loss on noised actions. Also introduces TacUMI handheld collector (Vive tracker, Xense sensors, $720).
inputs: Visual observations, tactile images or force estimates (Xense sensors), proprioception
outputs: Steered action chunks
actionRepr: base policy's action chunk (relative EE poses) steered by CPM gradient during diffusion or flow-matching sampling
trainingData: Limited expert demos per task collected with TacUMI (e.g., only 20 demos for Lock Opening); 5 tasks on Bi-ARX5 and Flexiv Rizon4
whatChangedVsParent: Adds touch without retraining the base policy by steering its sampler with a contrastively trained contact-feasibility model.
limitations: The CPM is task-specific and must be trained per task, adding training time and cost.
notes: Derives a flow-matching form of classifier guidance (weight t/(1-t)). Tasks: shoe lacing, chip handover, cucumber peeling, vase wiping, lock opening.

name: Context-aware DeLaN
resolvedTitle: Context-Aware Deep Lagrangian Networks for Model Predictive Control
org: TU Darmstadt; Hessian.AI; DFKI; Robotics Institute Germany
problem: A single global physics-consistent model (DeLaN) cannot capture changing dynamics when a robot handles different, uncertain payloads.
keyIdea: Condition a residual DeLaN on a latent context inferred online by an LSTM from recent states and residual torques, and plug the resulting physically consistent model into nonlinear MPC (CaDeLaC).
architecture: Residual DeLaN (MLPs 30-20 neurons predicting Cholesky inertia and potential energy) on top of a nominal Pinocchio model, conditioned on a 10-D latent from a 5-layer LSTM; converted to CasADi via L4CasADi and solved with acados SQP-RTI (horizon 12).
inputs: Joint positions, velocities, accelerations; history of 15 (q, qdot, residual torque) samples
outputs: Residual joint torques / inverse dynamics used by MPC; MPC outputs joint torques
trainingData: Simulated MuJoCo data: 20 ten-second trajectories for each of 100 random payloads (0-4 kg) plus no-load, 1.01M samples at 50 Hz; applied zero-shot on a real Franka Panda

headlineResults.benchmark: Real Franka pick-and-place with changing loads

whatChangedVsParent: Adds a latent context input with online LSTM system identification and residual (nominal-model) learning to DeLaN for MPC.
limitations: Velocity tracking worsened on some joints; assumes dynamics constant over the MPC horizon; demonstrated only on a fixed-base 7-DoF arm (future: humanoids, underactuated systems).
notes: Method name in paper: CaDeLaC (Context-Aware Deep Lagrangian MPC).

name: FeLaN
resolvedTitle: Floating-Base Deep Lagrangian Networks
org: TU Darmstadt; University of São Paulo; Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia; Hessian.AI; DFKI
problem: Grey-box dynamics models like DeLaN ignore floating-base constraints (branch-induced sparsity, composite spatial inertia triangle inequality, constant total mass) of quadrupeds and humanoids.
keyIdea: A reordered-Cholesky parameterization of the floating-base inertia matrix that guarantees positive definiteness, branch-induced sparsity and full physical consistency, learned DeLaN-style by minimizing inverse-dynamics error.
architecture: Per-kinematic-branch networks predict blocks of the reordered Cholesky factor from that branch's joints; a shared network predicts first mass moment and base covariance terms; total mass is a trainable scalar; potential energy is computed from mass and first moment rather than a separate network. Implemented in JAX.
inputs: Generalized positions (base pose + joints), velocities, accelerations
outputs: Generalized torques / inverse dynamics; interpretable inertia matrix, mass and first mass moment
params: 106 inertia-parameterization outputs for 12-joint robots (Go2/Spot/HyQReal2), 199 for Talos (per paper Table I)
trainingData: Sim: 50k samples each for Go2 and Talos (MuJoCo XLA); real: HyQReal2 75k, Talos 125k, Spot 66k (force plates), Spot+Arm 45k samples; dataset released
whatChangedVsParent: Extends DeLaN from fixed-base to floating-base robots with a structured inertia parameterization enforcing sparsity and full physical consistency.
limitations: Not yet used for control; full FeLaN is slightly less accurate than the sparsity-only variant and DeLaN-PP on some data (accuracy traded for interpretability).
notes: Future work: locomotion and loco-manipulation with FeLaN as a model. Evaluated on Go2, Spot, Spot with arm, HyQReal2, Talos.

name: Controlled HNN
resolvedTitle: Symplectic ODE-Net: Learning Hamiltonian Dynamics with Control
org: Princeton University; Siemens Corporate Technology
problem: Hamiltonian/Lagrangian networks assume autonomous systems and need higher-order derivatives; they cannot learn controlled dynamics or handle embedded angle data.
keyIdea: SymODEN: learn inverse mass matrix, potential energy and input matrix networks that define controlled Hamiltonian dynamics, trained end-to-end through a differentiable ODE solver, then synthesize energy-shaping controllers from the learned model.
architecture: Three MLPs (M^-1(q) via Cholesky, V(q), g(q)) assembled into Hamiltonian dynamics with control, integrated by Neural ODE (RK4); angle-aware variant works on (cos q, sin q, qdot).
inputs: State trajectories (q, p or cos/sin q, qdot) under constant control inputs
outputs: Learned vector field / predicted trajectories; energy-based control law
params: 0.13M-0.51M depending on task (fewest among compared models)
trainingData: Simulated Pendulum, CartPole, Acrobot (OpenAI Gym with RK4), 16-1024 initial conditions x 5 constant controls, 20 steps each

headlineResults.benchmark: Pendulum swing-up via learned energy-shaping controller
headlineResults.value: max |u| 7.5 used vs 2.0 in training, still reaches inverted position
headlineResults.comparedTo: only SymODEN yields a usable potential energy

headlineResults.value: lower than naive and geometric baselines
headlineResults.comparedTo: naive baseline, geometric baseline, unstructured SymODEN

whatChangedVsParent: Adds an external control input map to HNNs and trains via ODE-solver rollouts without needing accelerations.
limitations: Validated only on low-DoF simulated systems; underactuated control needs kinetic energy shaping not provided; learned functions extrapolate poorly outside training range for non-embedded angles.
notes: Identified via P11 text: 'Zhong et al. (2020) extended HNNs to controlled Hamiltonian systems by introducing generalized forces through a learned input map' = SymODEN (ICLR 2020). Code at github.com/d-biswa/Symplectic-ODENet.

name: Forced VIN
resolvedTitle: Forced Variational Integrator Networks for Prediction and Control of Mechanical Systems
org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
problem: Variational Integrator Networks only model conservative systems, while real robots have damping and control inputs.
keyIdea: Use the discrete Lagrange-d'Alembert principle to build explicit forced variational integrators (Velocity-Verlet / Stormer-Verlet) as a network architecture, with learned potential, control-force and damping terms.
architecture: Three 2-layer MLP heads (100 units): potential gradient V, control forcing F_control(q,u), damping F_damping(q,qdot), combined in a Velocity-Verlet update; optional encoder/decoder to map observations to configurations; trained with multi-step open-loop rollout loss.
inputs: Configuration (or observations such as cos/sin angles), velocities, control inputs
outputs: Next-state prediction; used as model inside CEM-MPC
trainingData: Very few trajectories: 5-20 (pendulum) or 20-50 (cartpole) trajectories of 50 steps in simulation; 10 trajectories of 50 steps on a real Quanser Qube Servo 2
controlRateHz: CEM-MPC runs at about 3 Hz on a laptop CPU
whatChangedVsParent: Adds non-conservative forcing (control and damping) to VINs via the discrete Lagrange-d'Alembert principle.
limitations: Restricted to Euclidean configuration spaces and low-DoF systems; future work to scale to larger systems and real-time control.
notes: Real-system result is prediction only (Quanser Qube), where FVIN captures dissipation after control is turned off while the residual baseline overfits. CONFLICT: P11 says FVIN 'was applied on a real cartpole system using MPC'; the paper's real-system experiment is prediction on a rotary pendulum (Quanser Qube), and MPC control is only in simulation.

name: Lagrangian-SINDy
resolvedTitle: Discovering Interpretable Dynamics by Sparsity Promotion on Energy and the Lagrangian (Chu & Hayashibe, IEEE RA-L 2020)
org: Tohoku University
notes: Primary paper not found on arXiv via alphaXiv (search resolved to a 2025 follow-up, 'Differentiable Sparse Identification of Lagrangian Dynamics', arXiv 2511.10706). From P11 and that follow-up (not the primary): Lagrangian-SINDy discovers compact total-energy and Lagrangian expressions of multi-DoF systems by sparse regression, using prior knowledge from simpler subsystems; the follow-up describes it as treating total energy as a Koopman eigenfunction with zero eigenvalue and aligning its time derivative with net power input. Extension: xL-SINDy (Purnomo & Hayashibe 2023). Org 'Tohoku University' is from general knowledge (unverified).

name: EQLN
resolvedTitle: Learning and Extrapolation of Robotic Skills using Task-Parameterized Equation Learner Networks
org: University of Innsbruck; University of Trento
problem: Imitation-learning skill models interpolate well but produce unpredictable motions for task parameters outside the demonstrated range.
keyIdea: Task-Parameterized Equation Learner Network (TP-EQLN): a network with mixed analytic activations (identity, sin, cos, sigmoid, product, sech) fits closed-form trajectory expressions as a function of time and task parameters, so it extrapolates while preserving motion shape.
architecture: EQLN feed-forward layers with multiple activation types and a linear output layer; input is [task parameters, time]; three-phase training (no regularization, L1 lasso, final) plus a workspace-bound penalty term sampled in the extrapolation domain.
inputs: Time step and task parameters (e.g., obstacle height, goal point, cup size)
outputs: End-effector position (3-D) or pose with quaternion (7-D) at each time step
actionRepr: time-indexed Cartesian end-effector trajectory
trainingData: Small sets of demonstrations: synthetic parametric trajectories for 4 sim tasks, kinesthetic demos on a Franka Panda for pick-and-place (4 of 8 containers demonstrated) and pouring

headlineResults.value: lowest in most tasks (qualitative bar plots)

whatChangedVsParent: Adds task parameters as inputs, extra activations (sech) and an extrapolation-domain penalty to EQL for skill learning.
limitations: Too few hidden layers lose detail while too many produce highly nonlinear extrapolation; constant-factor errors grow away from the trained range.
notes: Results are reported as MSE plots without single headline numbers in the retrieved text, so no numeric values are given. Published in Robotics and Autonomous Systems (P11 cites as Perez-Villeda et al. 2023).

name: Neural time fields
resolvedTitle: NTFields: Neural Time Fields for Physics-Informed Robot Motion Planning
org: Purdue University
problem: Neural motion planners need expensive expert trajectories from classical planners, and grid-based Eikonal solvers (FMM) do not scale to high-dimensional configuration spaces.
keyIdea: Train a network to directly satisfy the Eikonal PDE (physics-informed, no expert paths) so it outputs a continuous arrival-time field between start and goal; plan by bidirectionally following time-field gradients.
architecture: C-space encoder (FC + ResNet blocks), workspace encoder (3D CNN on voxelized obstacles with trilinear interpolation at robot surface points), nonlinear symmetric max/min operator, time-field generator outputting factorized time tau in [0,1]; loss from the factorized Eikonal equation with a distance-based speed model.
inputs: Start and goal configurations, obstacle point cloud (voxel grid 128^3)
outputs: Arrival time field and its gradient; path via bidirectional gradient following
trainingData: Only randomly sampled start/goal configurations with speed labels; data generation 3.74 s per cluttered 3D env, 2.2 min for Gibson, ~60 s for manipulators

headlineResults.value: ~6x faster than MPNet and FMM, >10x faster than RRT*/LazyPRM*

whatChangedVsParent: Replaces EikoNet's factorization with a start-goal symmetric formulation, a collision-aware speed model and workspace encoding so it works for robot motion planning.
limitations: Only collision and speed constraints (no acceleration/dynamics); generalizes only to new start/goal in a given environment; not validated on real robots; occasional failures from PDE approximation error.
notes: ICLR 2023; code released at github.com/ruiqini/NTFields. P11 also groups follow-ups (progressive NTFields, Ren et al. 2025 manipulation extension, Liu et al. 2025a online fields).
