problem: The hypothesis that video generators are implicit world models has never been directly tested: visual benchmarks cannot distinguish a robot passing through a table from physically valid motion.
keyIdea: Treat simulated task success as the grounding signal: generate a manipulation video from scene image + prompt, lift the end-effector motion to 3D world-frame trajectories (monocular depth + known camera), infer gripper timing, and execute in robosuite/RoboCasa365; evaluate on visual, trajectory and execution tracks.
architecture: Five-step video-to-trajectory pipeline (region masks via sim segmentation or Grounding DINO + SAM2, tracking, depth lifting, gripper-event inference with task priors) -> delta 6-DoF actions + gripper commands replayed with robosuite OSC with checkpoint correction (5 mm / 0.03 rad tolerances).
inputs: Initial scene image + task description
outputs: Visual scores, trajectory similarity, checkpoint executability, task success rate
trainingData: 101 manually curated RoboCasa365 episodes at 3 difficulty levels (8 L1 / 42 L2 / 51 L3 per figure counts)
whatChangedVsParent: Closes the loop with a simulated robot controller rather than VLM/human plausibility judgments.
limitations: Depth estimation is a major bottleneck (GT depth substantially improves rollout-video upper bound); no base navigation; pipeline limits make it a lower bound on true executability.
notes: 8 models: Hailuo 2.3, Kling 3.0, Wan 2.7, SeedDance 2.0, Veo 3.1 (closed), Wan 2.2, LTX-Video (open), Cosmos Policy (robot-specific); also Wan 2.2 LoRA fine-tunes. Findings: visual quality poor predictor of executability; in-domain fine-tuning improves appearance not physics; failure modes object levitation, phantom grasp, kinematic breakdown. Code 'will be open-sourced' at github.com/showlab/Dream.exe.

name: RoboChallenge
resolvedTitle: RoboChallenge: Large-scale Real-robot Evaluation of Embodied Policies
org: Dexmal; Hugging Face
problem: VLAs need large-scale real-robot evaluation (many models x many tasks), but real tests suffer tester variance, lack scalability, and existing online systems host only a few tasks on one or two machines.
keyIdea: An online 'remote robot' service: users run inference on their own side and call asynchronous APIs for timestamped observations and an action queue; a controlled-tester protocol resets scenes by visually matching reference episode frames; first benchmark Table30 with success rate + progress score.
architecture: Fleet of 10 robots of 4 types (UR5 + Robotiq, Franka Panda, Cobot Magic Aloha bimanual, ARX-5) with RealSense RGBD main/wrist/side cameras; up to 1000 demo episodes per task hosted on Hugging Face (LeRobot conversion).
inputs: User-submitted policies via remote API
outputs: Per-task success rate and progress score (10 rollouts x 10 points)
trainingData: Table30: 30 tabletop tasks with provided demonstrations (up to 1000 episodes/task)
controlRateHz: Robots required to support cyclic position mode up to 100 Hz; UR5 RTDE up to 125 Hz
whatChangedVsParent: Scales hosted real-robot evaluation to a 10-machine fleet with user-side inference and visual scene-matching reset protocol.
limitations: Cannot verify that the user-side model is the claimed one (possible cheating/human-in-the-loop); fixed reference test cases could be overfit; lighting and camera drift uncontrolled.
notes: Showed tester type (experienced / ignorant / adaptive) changes measured success substantially ('sweet-spot effect'). Also evaluated OpenVLA-OFT per text. Results and videos public at robochallenge.ai.

name: PolaRiS
resolvedTitle: PolaRiS: Scalable Real-to-Sim Evaluations for Generalist Robot Policies
org: University of Washington, Princeton, UC Berkeley, Stanford, Toyota Research Institute, USC, Cornell, Physical Intelligence
problem: Simulated benchmarks correlate poorly with real performance of generalist VLAs, green-screen real-to-sim (SIMPLER) cannot support wrist cameras, and building realistic sim scenes is laborious.
keyIdea: Turn 2–5 minute phone video scans into interactive Isaac Sim environments via 2D Gaussian splatting (visuals) + TSDF meshes (physics) with articulated robot splats, then briefly co-finetune policies on a small sim dataset from disjoint scenes so they can be evaluated zero-shot in unseen PolaRiS scenes.
architecture: 2DGS scene and robot reconstruction (COLMAP, ChArUco scale), TRELLIS-generated object assets, mesh via marching cubes into IsaacSim, splats anchored to robot links for kinematic articulation; co-training mixes sim data with pretraining data under a BC loss.
inputs: Video scans of scene/robot/objects; policies on DROID platform (Franka + ZED wrist/external cameras)
outputs: Simulated progress scores correlated with real-world performance
trainingData: ~350 sim teleop demos over 15 co-training scenes; policies finetuned 1k steps; 50 sim rollouts per task; 20 real rollouts per policy per env for ground truth

headlineResults.comparedTo: MSE, Libero-Score and Ctrl-World video model all poorly correlated

whatChangedVsParent: 3D Gaussian-splat reconstructions (supporting wrist/novel views) plus policy-agnostic sim co-training instead of 2D green-screen overlays.
limitations: Only rigid-object tasks; simplistic system identification; visual gaps remain (co-training needed); does not replace real-world evaluation for deformable/complex contact.
notes: Policies tested: pi0, pi0-FAST, PaliGemma-binning, pi0.5. Tools, co-training dataset, environments and a sharing hub open-sourced. Hardware-in-the-loop shows visual mismatch is dominant error source.

name: RoboMME
resolvedTitle: RoboMME: Benchmarking and Understanding Memory for Robotic Generalist Policies
org: University of Michigan; Stanford University; Figure AI
problem: Memory-augmented VLAs are evaluated on narrow, non-standardized tasks; existing memory benchmarks (MemoryBench, MIKASA-Robo) are near-solved, short-horizon, or lack demonstrations for imitation learning.
keyIdea: 16 non-Markovian ManiSkill tasks in four cognitively-motivated suites — Counting (temporal), Permanence (spatial), Reference (object), Imitation (procedural) — plus MME-VLA, 14 memory variants on a common pi0.5 backbone comparing symbolic, perceptual and recurrent memory with context/modulator/expert integration.
architecture: ManiSkill tabletop with 7-DoF Franka; front + wrist 256x256 RGB; MME-VLA: symbolic subgoals from VLM (SimpleSG/GroundSG), perceptual memory (TokenDrop/FrameSamp), recurrent memory (TTT/RMT), integrated as memory-as-context, adaLN modulator, or separate memory expert.
inputs: Multi-view RGB, proprioception, language; some tasks start with a video of history
outputs: Robot actions
actionRepr: Absolute joint space (8-D: 7 joints + gripper) or absolute EEF space (7-D: xyz, Euler, gripper)
trainingData: 1,600 demonstrations (100 per task), ~770k timesteps, with 5% waypoint noise for recovery behaviour
whatChangedVsParent: First benchmark covering temporal, spatial, object and procedural memory with enough demos for VLA imitation, plus a controlled same-backbone comparison of memory designs.
limitations: Tabletop only with fixed assets; mainly one backbone (pi0.5); no mobile manipulation; memory representations complementary, none dominates.
notes: Finding: symbolic memory best for counting/short-horizon, perceptual for motion-centric/time-sensitive; perceptual+modulator best efficiency tradeoff (GroundSG ~3x pi0.5 compute, MemER ~5x). Code at robomme.github.io.
